Comment: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome is an unsatisfactory term describing lethal underdevelopment of the left ventricle (LV). It represents the more severe end of a spectrum of LV hypoplasia, mandating single-ventricle palliation or cardiac transplantation. Less severe borderline ventricular hypoplasia may instead allow various biventricular therapeutic strategies and better long-term outcomes.

Name: Type I truncus arteriosus
Def: Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) with a short pulmonary trunk arises from the truncus arteriosus, giving rise to both pulmonary arteries.
Comment: According to the Van Praagh classification (PMID:2856609). The Van Praagh classification additionally specifies the presence (subtype A) or absence (subtype B) of a ventricular septal defect.

Name: Gastrointestinal inflammation
Def: Inflammation of the alimentary part of the gastrointestinal system.

Name: Enterocolitis
Def: An inflammation of the colon and small intestine. However, most conditions are either categorized as Enteritis (inflammation of the small intestine) or Colitis (inflammation of the large intestine).

Name: Microcolon
Def: A colon of abnormally small caliber.

Name: Intestinal pseudo-obstruction
Def: A functional rather than mechanical obstruction of the intestines, associated with manifestations that resemble those caused by an intestinal obstruction, including distension, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, constipation or diarrhea, in an individual in whom a mechanical blockage has been excluded.

Name: Hamartomatous polyposis
Def: Polyp-like protrusions which are histologically hamartomas. These can occur throughout the gastrointestinal tract. Hamartomatous polyps are composed of the normal cellular elements of the gastrointestinal tract, but have a markedly distorted architecture.
Comment: Patients with Cowden-Syndrom for example often have multiple hamartomatous gastrointestinal polyps.

Name: Prune belly
Def: A kind of congenital defect of the anterior abdominal wall in which the intestines are evident through the thin, lax, and protruding abdominal wall in affected infants.
Comment: Wrinkly folds of skin covering the abdomen as a result of partial or complete lack of abdominal muscles.

Name: Malnutrition
Def: A deficiency in the intake of energy and nutrients.

Name: Poor appetite
Def: A reduced desire to eat.

Name: Ectopic anus
Def: Abnormal displacement or malposition of the anus.

Name: Peptic ulcer
Def: The term peptic ulcer refers to acid peptic injury of the digestive tract, resulting in mucosal break reaching the submucosa. Peptic ulcers are usually located in the stomach or proximal duodenum, but they can also be found in the esophagus or Meckel's diverticulum. Infection with Helicobacter pylori and the use of non steroidal antiinflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or aspirin are the main risk factors of both gastric and duodenal peptic ulcers.
Comment: Symptoms of peptic ulcer disease have limited predictive value because they are non-specific. Patients with duodenal ulcers typically feel hungry or have nocturnal abdominal pain. By contrast, patients with gastric ulcers have postprandial abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and weight loss. Patients with untreated peptic ulcer disease typically have relapsing symptoms because of spontaneous healing and relapse while the causal factor (eg, H pylori infection or NSAID use) persists.
Synonym: Sore in the lining of gastrointestinal tract

Name: Congenital pyloric atresia
Def: Congenital atresia of the pylorus.

Name: Abnormality of the pylorus
Def: An abnormality of the pylorus.

Name: Meconium ileus
Def: Obstruction of the intestine due to abnormally thick meconium.
Comment: Obstruction of the intestine is known as ileus.

Name: Abnormal nipple morphology
Def: An abnormality of the nipple.

Name: Abnormality of the sense of smell
Def: An anomaly in the ability to perceive and distinguish scents (odors).
Synonym: Abnormality of the sense of smell

Name: Hyposmia
Def: A decreased sensitivity to odorants (that is, a decreased ability to perceive odors).

Name: Deviated nasal septum
Def: Positioning of the nasal septum to the right or left in contrast to the normal midline position of the nasal septum.

Name: Abnormality of the pulmonary artery
Def: An abnormality of the pulmonary artery.

Name: Pulmonary artery stenosis
Def: An abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
Comment: Stenosis, or narrowing, of the branches of the pulmonary artery is a type of congenital heart disease that, if left untreated, may lead to significant complications. Ideally, interventions to treat stenosis occur before significant complications or long-term sequelae take place, often within the first 2 years of life.

Name: Intermittent claudication
Def: Intermittent claudication is a symptom of peripheral arterial occlusive disease. After having walked over a distance which is individually characteristic, the patients experience pain or cramps in the calves, feet or thighs which typically subsides on standing still.
Comment: Vascular intermittent claudication caused by peripheral arterial disease most often related to severe atherosclerosis.

Name: Thrombophlebitis
Def: Inflammation of a vein associated with venous thrombosis (blood clot formation within the vein).

Name: Recurrent thrombophlebitis
Def: Repeated episodes of inflammation of a vein associated with venous thrombosis (blood clot formation within the vein).

Name: Arterial thrombosis
Def: The formation of a blood clot inside an artery.

Name: Elevated systolic blood pressure
Def: Abnormal increase in systolic blood pressure.
Comment: Normal systolic blood pressure is less than 120 mmHg in adults.

Name: Biparietal narrowing
Def: A narrowing of the biparietal diameter (i.e., of the transverse distance between the protuberances of the two parietal bones of the skull).

Name: Cranium bifidum occultum
Def: Cranium bifidum occultum, also known as Catlin mark, is a congenital midline skull defect presenting as an enlarged posterior fontanelle in the upper posterior angle of the parietal bone close to the intersection of the sagittal and lambdoid sutures. Cranium bifidum occultum occurs due to a defect in intramembranous ossification, a process through which skull bones (frontal, parietal, squamous temporal and occipital bones superior to the mendosal suture) ossify under a vascularized membrane toward the midline to cover the brain. Unlike cranium bifidum cysticum, cranium bifidum occultum does not have herniation of intracranial contents. As the skull grows, the midline cranium bifidum occultum defect is separated into bilateral enlarged parietal foramina (EPF) by a midline osseous bridge.
Comment: Cranium bifidum tends to resolve into distinct enlarged parietal foramina over the first few years of life through the midline ossification of a central bridge of bone bisecting the defect.

Name: Flat forehead
Def: A forehead with abnormal flatness.

Name: Abnormal cheek morphology
Def: An abnormality of the cheek- one of two bilateral soft tissue facial structures in the region of the face inferior to the eyes and between the nose and the ear. \

Name: Elfin facies
Def: This is a description previously used to describe a facial form characterized by a short, upturned nose, wide mouth, widely spaced eyes, and full cheeks. Because of the imprecision in this definition it is preferable to describe these features precisely. This term is retained because it was often used in the past, but it should not be used for new annotations.

Name: Recurrent viral infections
Def: Increased susceptibility to viral infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of viral infection.

Name: Severe combined immunodeficiency
Def: A type of primary immune deficiency that is characterized by a more severe defect in both the T- and B-lymphocyte systems.

Name: Reduced circulating complement concentration
Def: An immunodeficiency defined by the absent or suboptimal functioning of one of the complement system proteins.

Name: Agammaglobulinemia
Def: A lasting absence of total IgG and total IgA and total IgM in the blood circulation, whereby at most trace quantities can be measured.

Name: Secretory IgA deficiency
Def: Deficiency of secretory IgA (polymers of 2-4 IgA monomers are linked by two additional chains) and is the primary antibody response at the mucosal level, where it forms immune complexes with pathogens and allergens.

Name: Decreased circulating complement C8 concentration
Def: Concentration of the complement component C8 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
Comment: The eighth component of complement (C8) plays an important role in the function of membrane attack complex (MAC) that is generated on target cells upon activation of the complement system. MAC is generated by sequential addition of C5b, C6, C7, C8, and C9 molecules, which results in the transmembrane pore and eventual cell lysis. Individuals with C8 deficiency tend to have recurrent neisserial infections.

Name: Cranial hyperostosis
Def: Excessive growth of the bones of cranium, i.e., of the skull.

Name: Hyperostosis frontalis interna
Def: Bony overgrowth of the internal (endosteal) surface of the frontal bone.
Synonym: Enlargement of the inner surface of the frontal bone
Excessive growth of inner surface of the frontal bone
Hyperostosis of the internal surface of the frontal bone
Hypertrophy of the internal surface of the frontal bone
Increased ossification of the internal surface of the frontal bone
Overgrowth of the inner surface of the frontal bone
Overgrowth of the inside of the frontal bone
Thick inner surface of the frontal bone
Thick internal surface of the frontal bone

Name: Craniofacial dysostosis
Def: A characteristic appearance resulting from defective ossification of craniofacial bones.
Comment: Note: This term is used in the medical literature to describe an appearance of the face of patients with Crouzon syndrome (also called craniofacial dysostosis), which is characterized by acrocephaly, exophthalmos, hypertelorism, strabismus, parrot-beaked nose, and hypoplastic maxilla. This is thus probably mainly used as a bundled term and should be replaced by better descriptions in the future.

Name: Coronal craniosynostosis
Def: Premature closure of the coronal suture of skull.

Name: Sagittal craniosynostosis
Def: A kind of craniosynostosis affecting the sagittal suture.
Synonym: Early closure of midline skull joint

Name: Lambdoidal craniosynostosis
Def: A kind of craniosynostosis affecting the lambdoidal suture.

Name: Spherocytosis
Def: The presence of erythrocytes that are sphere-shaped.
Comment: Erythrocytes are normally biconcave rather than spherical.

Name: Elliptocytosis
Def: The presence of elliptical, cigar-shaped erythrocytes on peripheral blood smear.
Comment: Elliptocytes (ovalocytes) are abnormal erythrocytes ranging from slightly oval to elongated cigar-shaped forms.

Name: Stomatocytosis
Def: The presence of erythrocytes with a mouth-shaped (stoma) area of central pallor on peripheral blood smear.

Name: Poikilocytosis
Def: The presence of abnormally shaped erythrocytes.
Comment: General description for abnormally shaped erythrocytes.

Name: Fulminant hepatic failure
Def: Hepatic failure refers to the inability of the liver to perform its normal synthetic and metabolic functions, which can result in coagulopathy and alteration in the mental status of a previously healthy individual. Hepatic failure is defined as fulminant if there is onset of encephalopathy within 4 weeks of the onset of symptoms in a patient with a previously healthy liver.

Name: Preauricular skin furrow
Def: A groove of the skin immediately in front of the ear.
Synonym: Skin groove in front of the ear
Skin sulcus in front of the ear

Name: Postauricular skin tag
Def: A rudimentary tag of ear tissue often containing a core of cartilage and located just in back of the auricle (outer part of the ear).

Name: Abnormality of the middle ear ossicles
Def: An abnormality of the middle-ear ossicles (three small bones called malleus, incus, and stapes) that are contained within the middle ear and serve to transmit sounds from the air to the fluid-filled labyrinth (cochlea).

Name: Overfolding of the superior helices
Def: A condition in which the superior portion of the helix is folded over to a greater degree than normal.

Name: Dilatated internal auditory canal
Def: The presence of a dilated inner part of external acoustic meatus.

Name: Exostosis of the external auditory canal
Def: A benign bony growth projecting outward from a bone surface within the external auditory canal.

Name: Congenital earlobe sinuses
Def: Pits in the earlobes at the location where ears are typically pierced for earrings.

Name: Absent brainstem auditory responses
Def: Lack of measurable response to stimulation of auditory evoked potentials.

Name: Postauricular pit
Def: Benign congenital lesion of the postauricular soft tissue consisting of a blind-ending narrow tube or pit.

Name: Delayed brainstem auditory evoked response conduction time
Def: An abnormal increase (delay) in the conduction time of the brainstem auditory-evoked response.

Name: Preauricular pit
Def: Small indentation anterior to the insertion of the ear.
Comment: Preauricular cysts and sinuses are ectodermal remnants from an aberrant development of the auditory tubercles, tend to be bilateral and are localized anterior to the tragus of the ear. The preauricular sinus is a benign congenital lesion of the preauricular soft tissue consisting of a blind-ending narrow tube or pit. It is also known as preauricular pit, preauricular fistula, preauricular tract and preauricular cyst. It can be asymptomatic or present as an infected and discharging sinus. It presents as a small pit adjacent to the external ear usually located at the anterior margin of the ascending limb of the helix. The preauricular sinus is variably also termed a preauricular pit, preauricular fistula, preauricular tract and preauricular cyst.
Synonym: Pit in front of the ear

Name: Anomalous tracheal cartilage
Def: An abnormality of the C-shaped rings of hyaline cartilage, normally 16 to 20 in number, that occupy the anterior two-thirds of the circumference of the trachea (the posterior portion of the ring is completed by fibrous and smooth muscle tissue).

Name: Chronic bronchitis
Def: Chronic inflammation of the bronchi.

Name: Atretic occipital cephalocele
Def: A congenital defect in the occipital region of the skull, covered by skin of the scalp and containing meninges or remnants of glial or neural tissues.

Name: Aplasia cutis congenita over the scalp vertex
Def: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin on the scalp vertex, often just lateral to the midline.

Name: Mandibular hyperostosis
Def: Hyperostosis (bony overgrowth) of the mandible.
Comment: This bundled term will be made obsolete in future versions of the HPO.

Name: Persistent open anterior fontanelle
Def: The anterior fontanelle generally ossifies by around the 18th month of life. A persistent open anterior fontanelle is diagnosed if closure is delayed beyond this age.

Name: Aplasia cutis congenita over parietal area
Def: A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin on the scalp in the parietal area.
Synonym: Absent cutis congenita over parietal area

Name: Progressive macrocephaly
Def: The progressive development of an abnormally large skull.

Name: Relative macrocephaly
Def: A relatively mild degree of macrocephaly in which the head circumference is not above two standard deviations from the mean, but appears dysproportionately large when other factors such as body stature are taken into account.

Name: Craniofacial asymmetry
Def: Asymmetry of the bones of the skull and the face.

Name: Cessation of head growth
Def: Stagnation of head growth seen as flattening of the head circumference curve.

Name: Acrobrachycephaly
Def: An abnormality of head shape characterized by the presence of a short, wide head as well as a pointy or conical form of the top of the head owing to premature closure of the coronal and lambdoid sutures.

Name: Macrocephaly at birth
Def: The presence of an abnormally large skull with onset at birth.
Synonym: Head circumference large for gestational age

Name: Calvarial hyperostosis
Def: Excessive growth of the calvaria.
Comment: The calvaria (skull cap) is made up of the frontal, occipital, right and left parietal, right and left temporal, sphenoid, and ethmoid bones, and thus comprises the upper dome-like part of the skull and does not include the lower jaw.

Name: Large posterior fontanelle
Def: An enlargement of the posterior fontanelle relative to age-dependent norms.

Name: Widely patent fontanelles and sutures
Def: An abnormally increased width of the cranial fontanelles and sutures.
Comment: This term indicates that both the fontanelles and the sutures are widely patent and thus represents a severe form of delay in closure of the fontanelles/sutures.

Name: Craniofacial hyperostosis
Def: Excessive growth of the craniofacial bones.
Synonym: Excessive bone growth of the skull and face

Name: Chronic rhinitis due to narrow nasal airway
Synonym: Chronic nasal inflammation due to narrow nasal airway

Name: Bilateral choanal atresia
Def: Bilateral absence (atresia) of the posterior nasal aperture (choana).
Synonym: Bilateral blockage of the rear opening of the nasal cavity
Bilateral obstruction of the rear opening of the nasal cavity

Name: Pancreatic islet-cell hyperplasia
Def: Hyperplasia of the islets of Langerhans, i.e., of the regions of the pancreas that contain its endocrine cells.
Comment: The islets of Langerhans contain the alpha cells (producing glucagon), beta cells (insulin and amylin), delta cells (somatostatin),PP cells (pancreatic polypeptide), and the epsilon cells (ghrelin).

Name: Long eyebrows
Def: Increased length of the hairs of the eyebrows.

Name: Temporal hypotrichosis
Def: Reduced or lacking hair growth in the temporal region (i.e., around the temples on the side of the skull).
Synonym: Reduced hair growth in temporal region

Name: Large clumps of pigment irregularly distributed along hair shaft
Synonym: Large clumps of pigment irregularly distributed along hair shaft

Name: Generalized hypotrichosis
Def: Reduced or lacking hair growth in a generalized distribution.

Name: Sacral hypertrichosis
Def: Excessive, increased hair growth located in the sacral region.

Name: Anterior cervical hypertrichosis
Def: Anterior cervical hypertrichosis (ACH) or 'hairy throat' refers to the presence of a tuft of terminal hair on the anterior neck, just above the laryngeal prominence.

Name: Congenital, generalized hypertrichosis
Def: A confluent, generalized overgrowth of silvery blonde to gray lanugo hair at birth.
Comment: Hypertrichosis refers to excessive, abnormal hairiness.

Name: Scarring alopecia of scalp
Synonym: Hair loss on scalp from scarring condition

Name: Generalized hypertrichosis
Def: Generalized excessive, abnormal hairiness.

Name: Cervical platyspondyly
Def: A flattened vertebral body shape with reduced distance between the vertebral endplates affecting the cervical spine.

Name: Increased spinal bone density
Def: Increased bone density affecting the bones of the spine (vertebral column).

Name: Pear-shaped vertebrae
Def: Bulbous appearance of the anterior vertebral bodies, such that the vertebral bodies have the greatest vertical height anteriorly as well as bulbous anterior superior-inferior contours.

Name: Beaking of vertebral bodies
Def: Anterior tongue-like protrusions of the vertebral bodies.

Name: Increased vertebral height
Def: Increased top to bottom height of vertebral bodies.

Name: Anterior wedging of T11
Def: An abnormality of the shape of the thoracic vertebra T11 such that it is wedge-shaped (narrow towards the front).
Synonym: Anterior wedging of the 11th thoracic vertebra

Name: Sclerotic vertebral endplates
Def: Sclerosis (increased density) affecting vertebral end plates.

Name: Anterior scalloping of vertebral bodies
Def: An excessive concavity of the anterior surface of one or more vertebral bodies.
Comment: One cause of anterior scalloping is an aortic aneurysm, which because of its pulsatile pressure can cause a convex defect along the anterior surface of an adjacent vertebra body. The defect may have a sclerotic margin.

Name: Biconcave vertebral bodies
Def: Exaggerated concavity of the anterior or posterior surface of the vertebral body, i.e., the upper and lower vertebral endplates are hollowed inward.
Comment: This finding has been called fish or codfish vertebra because of the characteristic biconcave form of fish vertebral bodies.

Name: Thoracic platyspondyly
Def: A flattened vertebral body shape with reduced distance between the vertebral endplates affecting the thoracic spine.

Name: Hump-shaped mound of bone in central and posterior portions of vertebral endplate
Supernumerary vertebral ossification centers
Def: Three ossification sites are present in typical vertebral bodies (C3-L5): a single ossification center in the vertebral body, and one each in the two neural arches. This term applies if there are additional vertebral ossification centers present during the development and maturation of the spine.

Name: Absent or minimally ossified vertebral bodies
Spina bifida occulta at L5
Def: The closed form of spina bifida with incomplete closure of the vertebra L5 with intact overlying skin.

Name: Cervical C2/C3 vertebral fusion
Def: Fusion of cervical vertebrae at C2 and C3, caused by a failure in the normal segmentation or division of the cervical vertebrae during the early weeks of fetal development, leading to a short neck with a low hairline at the back of the head, and restricted mobility of the upper spine.

Name: Absent vertebral body mineralization
Def: A lack of bone mineralization of the vertebral bodies.

Name: Unossified vertebral bodies
Def: A lack of ossification of the vertebral bodies.

Name: Anterior beaking of lower thoracic vertebrae
Def: Anterior tongue-like protrusions of the lower thoracic vertebral bodies.

Name: Anteriorly placed odontoid process
Def: Anterior mislocalization of the dens of the axis.

Name: Lumbar spinal canal stenosis
Def: An abnormal narrowing of the lumbar spinal canal.
Comment: Symptoms of lumbar spinal canal stenosis include pseudoclaudication (pain, numbness,, or weakness induced by walking and relieved by rest; the prefix pseudo is used to differentiate this manifestation from claudication, which has similar symptoms but is caused by peripheral artery disease).

Name: Spina bifida occulta at S1
Def: The closed form of spina bifida with incomplete closure of S1 with intact overlying skin.

Name: Cleft vertebral arch
Def: A discontinuity of the vertebral arch, i.e., of the posterior part of a vertebra.

Name: Butterfly vertebral arch
Def: Butterfly vertebrae have a cleft through the body of the vertebrae and a funnel shape at the ends.

Name: Enlarged vertebral pedicles
Def: Increased size of the vertebral pedicle.
Comment: The vertebral pedicles are the two short, thick processes, which connect the body of the spinal vertebra to the arch.

Name: Progressive intervertebral space narrowing
Def: A progressive form of decreased height of the intervertebral disk.

Name: Biconvex vertebral bodies
Def: Presence of abnormal convexity of the upper and lower end plates of the vertebrae, i.e., an exaggerated bulging out of the upper and lower vertebral end plates.
Comment: Note that biconvex vertebral bodies can be a normal finding in newborns.

Name: Small cervical vertebral bodies
Def: Reduced size of cervical vertebrae.

Name: Anterior beaking of thoracic vertebrae
Def: Anterior tongue-like protrusions of thoracic vertebral bodies.

Name: Decreased cervical spine flexion due to contractures of posterior cervical muscles
Synonym: Inability to touch chin to chest

Name: Cervical segmentation defect
Def: An abnormality related to a defect of vertebral separation of cervical vertebrae during development.

Name: Lower thoracic kyphosis
Def: Over curvature of the lower thoracic region, leading to a round back or if sever to a hump.

Name: Cervical C5/C6 vertebrae fusion
Def: Fusion of the C5 and C6 cervical vertebrae.

Name: Elevated amniotic fluid alpha-fetoprotein
Def: An elevation of alpha-feto protein measured in the amniotic fluid.
Comment: This feature can be found in pregnancies with fetuses affected by a range of abnormalities including for instance encephalocele.
Synonym: Elevated amniotic fluid alpha fetal protein
Elevated amniotic fluid alpha foetal protein

Name: Hypoplasia of the nasal bone
Def: Underdevelopment of the nasal bone.

Name: Hypoplasia of facial musculature
Def: Underdevelopment of one or more muscles innervated by the facial nerve (the seventh cranial nerve).

Name: Frontalis muscle weakness
Def: Reduced strength of the frontalis muscle (which is located on the forehead).

Name: Facial midline hemangioma
Def: Hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, occurring in the midline region of the face.

Name: Decreased facial expression
Def: A reduced degree of voluntary and involuntary facial movements involved in responded to others or expressing emotions.

Name: Deep longitudinal plantar crease
Def: Narrow, paramedian longitudinal depressions in the plantar skin of the forefoot.

Name: Talipes valgus
Def: Outward turning of the heel, resulting in clubfoot with the person walking on the inner part of the foot.
Comment: The phrase talipes valgus is derived from the Latin words talus (ankle), pes (poot), and valgus (outward angulation of the distal segment of a bone).

Name: Short third metatarsal
Def: Underdevelopment of the Third metatarsal bone leading to a short (hypoplastic) third metatarsal bone.

Name: Short fourth metatarsal
Def: Short fourth metatarsal bone.

Name: Thickened Achilles tendon
Def: An abnormal thickening of the Achilles tendon.

Name: 2-3 toe syndactyly
Def: Syndactyly with fusion of toes two and three.
Synonym: Syndactyly of second and third toes

Name: 4-5 toe syndactyly
Def: Syndactyly with fusion of toes four and five.

Name: Calcaneal epiphyseal stippling
Def: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in the epiphysis of the calcaneus.

Name: Osteoporotic metatarsal
Def: Decrease in mass and density of the metatarsal bones.

Name: Short fifth metatarsal
Def: Short (hypoplastic) fifth metatarsal bone.
Synonym: Hypoplasia of the fifth metatarsal bone

Name: Renal malrotation
Def: An abnormality of the normal developmental rotation of the kidney leading to an abnormal orientation of the kidney.
Comment: The final kidney position in the renal fossa results from the rotation of the kidney with an orientation of the renal pelvis to the medial and the renal calyces to the lateral. Malrotation of the kidney can lead to orientation of the renal pelvis anteriorly, posteriorly and laterally. In most cases, renal malrotation does not cause any symptoms, but, hydronephrosis or stone formation can be observed as complications of renal malformation.

Name: Reversible renal failure
Def: Acute renal failure with resolution of manifestations.

Name: Axial malrotation of the kidney
Def: An abnormality of the normal developmental rotation of the kidney leading to an abnormal axial orientation of the kidney.

Name: Hyperechogenic kidneys
Def: An increase in amplitude of waves returned in ultrasonography of the kidney, which is generally displayed as increased brightness of the signal.
Comment: Normal renal parenchyma is similar (isoechoic) or slightly darker (hypoechoic) compared with liver and includes the cortex and medulla. The thickness of the renal cortex is measured from the outer border of the medullary pyramids (yellow line) or from the arcuate arteries to the renal capsule. The medullary pyramids (white arrow) contain fluid in parallel tubules, which is anechoic (black) and appear as regularly spaced dark pools at the inner margin of the parenchyma (arrow). Because fat is echogenic, the central renal sinus appears bright.
Synonym: Increased echogenicity of the renal parenchyma

Name: Thickened glomerular basement membrane
Def: Prominent glomerular basement membrane (GBM), reflecting an increase in thickness (subjective estimate) of the basal lamina of the glomerulus of the kidney.
Comment: This finding is demonstrated on renal biopsy.

Name: Calcium nephrolithiasis
Def: The presence of calcium-containing calculi (stones) in the kidneys.
Comment: The overwhelming majority of renal calculi contain calcium.

Name: Impaired renal concentrating ability
Def: A defect in the ability to concentrate the urine.
Comment: An impairment in renal concentrating ability can be easily recognized by the maximum concentrating ability (Umax) as determined by the urine osmolality reached after a fixed period of dehydration. Inability to maximally concentrate the urine is related to one or both of two basic tubular defects: 1) a failure of maximal free-water generation by the diluting segment in the ascending limb of Henle's loop; and 2) a failure of the distal tubular epithelium to achieve maximum permeability to water during water deprivation.

Name: Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis
Def: Acute inflammation of the kidney affecting the interstitium of the kidneys surrounding the tubules.

Name: Impaired renal uric acid clearance
Def: A reduction in the ability of the kidneys to remove uric acid from the serum.

Name: Renal cortical microcysts
Def: Cysts of microscopic size confined to the cortex of the kidney.

Name: Crossed fused renal ectopia
Def: A developmental anomaly in which the kidneys are fused and localized on the same side of the midline. This anomaly is thought to result from disruption of the normal embryologic migration of the kidneys.

Name: Global glomerulosclerosis
Def: Obliteration of the glomerular capillary lumen by increased collagenous matrix, with or without hyalinosis or foam cells. Sclerosis involves 100% of the glomerular tuft. Relative to other patent glomeruli in the sample, glomerular size is preserved, or increased/decreased by no more than 50%.
Comment: Glomerular changes can be focal (only in some glomeruli) or diffuse (in all or almost all the glomeruli), and segmental (only a part of the glomerulus) or global (the entire glomerulus).

Name: Abnormal renal collecting system morphology
Def: An abnormality of the renal collecting system.
Synonym: Abnormality of the renal collecting system

Name: Chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis
Def: Chronic inflammation of the kidney affecting the interstitium of the kidneys surrounding the tubules.

Name: Glomerular subendothelial electron-dense deposits
Def: Electron dense deposits at the glomerular basement membrane,
Comment: Subendothelial electron-dense deposits are a characteristic feature of dense-deposit disease.

Name: Atrial flutter
Def: A type of atrial arrhythmia characterized by atrial rates of between 240 and 400 beats per minute and some degree of atrioventricular node conduction block. Typically, the ventricular rate is half the atrial rate. In the EKG; atrial flutter waves are observed as sawtooth-like atrial activity. Pathophysiologically, atrial flutter is a form of atrial reentry in which there is a premature electrical impulse creates a self-propagating circuit.
Comment: Atrial flutter can lead to palpitations, fatigue, dyspnea, and chest pain. Atrial flutter can be paroxysmal or persistent.

Name: Paroxysmal ventricular tachycardia
Def: Episodes of ventricular tachycardia that have a sudden onset and ending.

Name: Congenital atrioventricular dissociation
Def: A form of atrioventricular (AV) dissociation (i.e., the atria and the ventricles are under the control of two separate pacemakers) with congenital onset.

Name: Permanent atrial fibrillation
Def: Atrial fibrillation (AF) that cannot be successfully terminated by cardioversion, and longstanding (more than 1 year) AF, where cardioversion is not indicated or has not been attempted, is termed permanent.
Comment: The natural history of atrial fibrillation (AF) is characterized by a gradual worsening with time. AF itself produces changes in atrial function and structure. Note there is no precise definition of the duration of AF required to be regarded as chronic.

Name: Supraventricular tachycardia
Def: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) is an abnormally increased heart rate (over 100 beats per minute at rest) with origin above the level of the ventricles.
Comment: A narrow complex (QRS width less than 120 milliseconds) reflects rapid activation of the ventricles via the normal conduction pathway, i.e. His-Purkinje system, which in turn suggests that the tachycardia originated above the AV node and is thus supraventricular.

Name: Ventricular tachycardia
Def: A tachycardia originating in the ventricles characterized by rapid heart rate (over 100 beats per minute) and broad QRS complexes (over 120 ms).
Comment: Ventricular tachycardia (VT) is a potentially life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia that presents as a wide QRS complex tachycardia, and is defined as three or more consecutive QRS complexes with a duration longer than 120 milliseconds (ms) and a rate of 100 beats per minute or more, whereby the complexes have a ventricular origin. VT can be subdivided as follows: (i) sustained VT persists for 30 seconds or more; (ii) non-sustained VT lasts less than 30 seconds; (iii) monomorphic VT displays a uniform QRS morphology; and (iv) polymorphic VT displays QRS morphologies that variy from beat to beat. VT is observed most commonly in individuals with structural heart disease or acute myocardial infarction (MI). VT may also be observed in in the setting of drug toxicity or electrolyte abnormalities or in individuals with Mendelian disease.

Name: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
Def: Episodes of atrial fibrillation that typically last for several hours up to one day and terminate spontaneously.

Name: Effort-induced polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
Def: Polymorphic ventricular arrhythmias of varying morphologythat do not exist under resting conditions but appear only upon physical exercise or catecholamine administration.

Name: obsolete Nodular calcific aortic valve disease
Hypoplasia of right ventricle
Def: Underdevelopment or reduced size of the heart right ventricle, often due to a reduced number of cells.

Name: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia
Def: An episodic form of supraventricular tachycardia with abrupt onset and termination.
Comment: PSVT is a term used to denote intermittent supraventricular tachycardia other than atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter and multifocal atrial tachycardia (AT). The major causes are atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVNRT), atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT), and sinoatrial node reentrant tachycardia (SNRT).

Name: Myxomatous mitral valve degeneration
Def: Myxomatous mitral valve is defined as the presence of excess leaflet tissue and leaflet thickening greater than 5 mm, resulting in a prolapse greater than 2 mm into the left atrium on parasternal long axis view.

Name: Sparse anterior scalp hair
Def: Decreased number of head hairs per unit area on the anterior region of the scalp.
Synonym: Sparse scalp hair at front of head
Thin scalp hair at front of head

Name: Brittle scalp hair
Def: Fragile, easily breakable scalp hair.

Name: Elbow hypertrichosis
Def: Excessive, increased hair growth located in the elbow region.

Name: Duodenal polyposis
Def: Presence of multiple polyps in the duodenum.

Name: Juvenile gastrointestinal polyposis
Def: The presence of multiple juvenile polyps in the stomach and intestine. The term juvenile polyps refer to a special histopathology and not the age of onset as the polyp might be diagnosed at all ages. The juvenile polyp has a spherical appearance and is microscopically characterized by overgrowth of an oedematous lamina propria with inflammatory cells and cystic glands. Juvenile polyps are a specific type of hamartomatous polyps.

Name: Malrotation of colon
Def: An anatomical anomaly that results from an abnormal rotation of the gut as it returns to the abdominal cavity during embryogenesis.

Name: Fulminant hepatitis
Def: Acute hepatitis complicated by acute liver failure with hepatic encephalopathy occurring less than 8 weeks after the onset of jaundice.
Comment: Note that different definitions of fulminant hepatitis are used in the medical literature.

Name: Intestinal lymphedema
Def: Fluid retention and edema in the intestine caused by a compromised lymphatic system.

Name: Lactose intolerance
Def: An inability to digest lactose.

Name: Hypoplasia of the small intestine
Def: Underdevelopment of the small intestine.

Name: Esophageal ulceration
Def: Defect in the epithelium of the esophagus, essentially an open sore in the lining of the esophagus.

Name: Rectoperineal fistula
Def: The presence of a fistula between the perineum and the rectum.

Name: Malrotation of small bowel
Def: A deviation from the normal rotation of the midgut during embryologic development with mislocalization of the small bowel.
Comment: Malrotation results not only in the malposition of the bowel but also in the malfixation of the mesentery. The normally broad mesenteric attachment is shortened to a narrow pedicle that predisposes the patient to the complication of midgut volvulus.

Name: Hamartomatous stomach polyps
Def: Polyp-like protrusions which are histologically hamartomas located in the stomach.

Name: Multiple small bowel atresias
Def: The presence of multiple areas of atresia affecting the small intestine.

Name: Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract
Def: Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract.
Synonym: Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract
Recurrent infection of the GI tract

Name: Episodic hemolytic anemia
Def: A form of hemolytic anemia that occurs in repeated episodes.

Name: Congenital hemolytic anemia
Def: A form of hemolytic anemia with congenital onset.

Name: Acute myeloid leukemia
Def: A form of leukemia characterized by overproduction of an early myeloid cell.

Name: Neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia
Def: Low platelet count associated with maternal platelet-specific alloantibodies.
Comment: Neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia occurs following fetomaternal transfusions leading to generation of alloreactive antiplatelet antibodies.

Name: Congenital hypoplastic anemia
Def: A type of hypoplastic anemia with congenital onset.
Comment: In this condition, hematopoiesis must have been inadequate in fetal life. Affected infant have marked pallor and reticulocytopenia or absence of red blood cell precursors in an otherwise normally cellular bone marrow. This term does not refer to a particular diagnosis or etiology (or which several are known) but to the phenotypic feature.

Name: B Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
Def: A type of ALL characterized by elevated levels of B-cell lymphoblasts in the bone marrow and the blood.

Name: Post-transfusion thrombocytopenia
Def: Sudden onset of thrombocytopenia (reduced platelet count) within 5-10 days of the transfusion of blood products. The clinical presentation is post-transfusion purpura (PTP), wigth severe thrmbocytopenia, epistaxis, and hemorrhages.
Comment: Post-transfusion thrombocytopenia is thought to be related to platelet-specific alloantibody from prior transfusion/pregnancy.

Name: Fava bean-induced hemolytic anemia
Def: A kind of hemolytic anemia that is induced by the ingestion of fava beans.
Comment: Persons with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency are susceptible to fava bean-induced hemolytic anemia because of the oxidative stress induced by compounds in Fava beans (thought to be vicine and isouramil). The same underlying defect can make affected persons susceptible to hemolysis induced by a number of mediciations.
Synonym: Hemolytic anaemia following ingestion of fava beans
Hemolytic anemia following ingestion of fava beans

Name: Drug-sensitive hemolytic anemia
Def: A form of hemolytic anemia that is triggered by ingestion of certain drugs.

Name: Normocytic hypoplastic anemia
Def: A type of hypoplastic anemia in which the erythrocytes have a normal cell volume (the mean corpuscular volume is within normal limits).

Name: Acute myelomonocytic leukemia
Def: An acute leukemia characterized by the proliferation of both neutrophil and monocyte precursors.

Name: Hypersegmentation of neutrophil nuclei
Def: An excessive division of the lobes of the nucleus of a neutrophil.
Comment: Neutrophils usually display 3-4 nuclear lobes. Hypersegmented neutrophile nuclei display 5 or more lobes. This feature can be seen in vitamin B12 or folate deficiency or with other etiologies.
Synonym: Hypersegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in peripheral blood

Name: Anisopoikilocytosis
Def: A type of poikilocytosis characterized by the presence in the blood of erythrocytes of varying sizes and abnormal shapes.

Name: Increased hemoglobin oxygen affinity
Def: An abnormal increase in the binding affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen.

Name: Folate-unresponsive megaloblastic anemia
Def: A type of megaloblastic anemia that does not improve upon administration of folate. Since vitamin B12 acts by promoting recycling of folate, administration of vitamin B12 also does not improve this type of anemia.

Name: Refractory anemia with ringed sideroblasts
Def: A type of myelodysplastic syndrome characterized by less than 5% myeloblasts in the bone marrow, but with 15% or greater red cell precursors in the marrow being abnormal iron-stuffed cells called ringed sideroblasts.

Name: Recurrent thromboembolism
Def: Repeated episodes of obstruction of blood flow due to an embolus, i.e., blood clot that has traveled from its point of origin within the blood stream.

Name: Microspherocytosis
Def: The presence of erythrocytes that are sphere-shaped and reduced in size.

Name: Acute promyelocytic leukemia
Def: A type of acute myeloid leukemia in which abnormal promyelocytes predominate.

Name: Pyropoikilocytosis
Def: A form of severe hemolytic anemia characterized by erythrocyte morphology reminiscent of that seen in patients after a thermal burn.

Name: Hypochromic microcytic anemia
Def: A type of anemia characterized by an abnormally low concentration of hemoglobin in the erythrocytes and lower than normal size of the erythrocytes.

Name: Reduced factor XII activity
Def: Decreased activity of coagulation factor XII. Factor XII (fXII) is part of the intrinsic coagulation pathway and binds to exposed collagen at site of vessel wall injury, activated by high-MW kininogen and kallikrein, thereby initiating the coagulation cascade.

Name: Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia
Def: A type of hemolytic anemia in which the Coombs test is positive.
Comment: The Coombs test measures a coating of immunoglobulin or complement on the red cell surface.

Name: Acute monocytic leukemia
Def: The accumulation of transformed primitive hematopoietic blast cells, which lose their ability of normal differentiation and proliferation.

Name: Prolonged bleeding after surgery
Def: Bleeding that persists longer than the normal time following a surgical procedure.

Name: Ph-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia
Def: A subset of acute lymphoblastic leukemia that results from a reciprocal translocation between the ABL-1 oncogene and a breakpoint cluster region (BCR), resulting in a fusion gene, BCR-ABL, that encodes an oncogenic protein with constitutively active tyrosine kinase activity.

Name: Recurrent deep vein thrombosis
Def: Repeated episodes of the formation of a blot clot in a deep vein.

Name: Folate-responsive megaloblastic anemia
Def: A type of megaloblastic anemia (i.e., anemia characterized by the presence of erythroblasts that are larger than normal) that improves upon the administration of folate.

Name: Reduced leukocyte alkaline phosphatase
Def: Decreased alkaline phosphatase measured within leukocytes.

Name: Intermittent thrombocytopenia
Def: Reduced platelet count that occurs sporadically, i.e., it comes and goes.

Name: Reduced protein S activity
Def: An abnormality of coagulation related to a decreased concentration of vitamin K-dependent protein S. Protein S is a cofactor of protein C.
Comment: Protein S functions as a cofactor to Protein C in the inactivation of Factors Va and VIIIa in the coagulation pathway. Therefore, a defect in protein S is associated with an increased risk of thrombosis.

Name: Normochromic microcytic anemia
Def: A type of anemia characterized by an normal concentration of hemoglobin in the erythrocytes and lower than normal size of the erythrocytes.

Name: Hyperchromic macrocytic anemia
Def: A type of anemia characterized by abnormally large erythrocytes with abnormally high amounts of hemoglobin.

Name: Amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia
Def: Thrombocytopenia related to lack of or severe reduction in the count of megakaryocytes.

Name: Thiamine-responsive megaloblastic anemia
Def: A type of megaloblastic anemia (i.e., anemia characterized by the presence of erythroblasts that are larger than normal) that improves upon the administration of thiamine.

Name: Elevated bone marrow ring sideroblast count
Def: Count of ring sideroblasts in the bone marrow above the upper limit of normal. Ring sideroblasts are nucleated erythroblasts with a pathologic accumulation of iron granules in the mitochondrial matrix. They can be detected by Prussian blue staining as blue perinuclear aggregates in bone marrow aspirate erythroblasts.
Comment: Sideroblastic anemia includes a group of inherited and acquired anemias of ineffective erythropoiesis characterized by an accumulation of ring sideroblasts in the bone marrow and decreased production of mature red blood cells. Additionally, refractory anemia with ring sideroblasts is a type of myelodysplastic syndrome that is characterized by anemia and the presence of at least 15 percent ring sideroblasts in the marrow.

Name: Impaired ADP-induced platelet aggregation
Def: Abnormal platelet response to ADP as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of ADP.

Name: Chronic hemolytic anemia
Def: An chronic form of hemolytic anemia.

Name: Perineal fistula
Def: The presence of a fistula between the bowel and the perineum.
Comment: The perineum is the diamond-shaped region of the body between the pubic arch and the anus.

Name: Incisional hernia
Def: An abdominal hernia that occurs at a site of weakness in the abdominal wall resulting from an incompletely-healed surgical wound.

Name: Spontaneous neonatal pneumothorax
Def: Pneumothorax occurring neonatally without traumatic injury to the chest or lung.

Name: Intercostal muscle weakness
Def: Lack of strength of the intercostal muscles, i.e., of the muscle groups running along the ribs that create and move the chest wall.

Name: Intermittent hyperventilation
Def: Episodic hyperventilation.

Name: Respiratory infections in early life
Def: Increased susceptibility to respiratory infections in early life, as manifested by recurrent episodes of respiratory infections.

Name: Respiratory failure requiring assisted ventilation
Def: A state of respiratory distress that requires a life saving intervention in the form of gaining airway access and instituting positive pressure ventilation.

Name: Intermittent episodes of respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness
Elevated pulmonary artery pressure
Def: An abnormally elevated blood pressure in the circulation of the pulmonary artery.

Name: Recurrent infections due to aspiration
Def: Increased susceptibility to infections due to aspiration, as manifested by recurrent episodes of infections due to aspiration.

Name: Stress/infection-induced lactic acidosis
Def: A form of lactic acidemia that occurs in relation to stress or infection.

Name: Persistent lactic acidosis
Def: A continuous form of lactic acidemia.

Name: Severe lactic acidosis
Def: A severe form of lactic acidemia.

Name: Exercise-induced lactic acidemia
Def: A form of lactic acidemia that occurs following exercise or exertion.

Name: Congenital lactic acidosis
Def: A form of lactic acidemia with congenital onset.

Name: Maturity-onset diabetes of the young
Def: The term Maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY) was initially used for patients diagnosed with fasting hyperglycemia that could be treated without insulin for more than two years, where the initial diagnosis was made at a young age (under 25 years). Thus, MODY combines characteristics of type 1 diabetes (young age at diagnosis) and type 2 diabetes (less insulin dependence than type 1 diabetes). The term MODY is now most often used to refer to a group of monogenic diseases with these characteristics. Here, the term is used to describe hyperglycemia diagnosed at a young age with no or minor insulin dependency, no evidence of insulin resistance, and lack of evidence of autoimmune destruction of the beta cells.
Synonym: Maturity onset diabetes of the young

Name: Reduced circulating vitamin A concentration
Def: Concentration of vitamin A below the lower limit of normal in the blood circulation.

Name: Episodic metabolic acidosis
Def: Repeated transient episodes of metabolic acidosis, that is, of the buildup of acid or depletion of base due to accumulation of metabolic acids.

Name: Intermittent lactic acidemia
Def: An intermittent (discontinuous) form of lactic acidemia.

Name: Recurrent infantile hypoglycemia
Def: Recurrent episodes of decreased concentration of glucose in the blood occurring during the infantile period.
Synonym: Recurrent low blood sugar in infant

Name: Impairment of galactose metabolism
Def: An impairment of galactose metabolism.

Name: Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis
Def: A form of metabolic acidosis with increased serum chloride levels.

Name: Abnormal magnesium concentration
Def: An abnormality of magnesium ion homeostasis.

Name: Hyperphenylalaninemia
Def: An increased concentration of L-phenylalanine in the blood.

Name: Abnormal oral glucose tolerance
Def: An abnormal resistance to glucose, i.e., a reduction in the ability to maintain glucose levels in the blood stream within normal limits following oral administration of glucose.

Name: Chronic lactic acidosis
Def: A chronic form of lactic acidemia.

Name: Orthostatic hypotension due to autonomic dysfunction
Pulmonary artery dilatation
Def: An abnormal widening of the diameter of the pulmonary artery.

Name: Abnormality of the pulmonary vasculature
Synonym: Abnormality of the lung blood vessels

Name: Arteriosclerosis of small cerebral arteries
Def: Arteriosclerosis (increased thickness, increased stiffness, loss of elasticity) of the small arteries of the brain.
Synonym: Hardened artery wall in small cerebral arteries

Name: Ascending aortic dissection
Def: A separation of the layers within the wall of the ascending aorta. Tears in the intimal layer result in the propagation of dissection (proximally or distally) secondary to blood entering the intima-media space.
Comment: According to the Stanford classification, type A aortic dissection affects the ascending aorta and arch.

Name: Vascular calcification
Def: Abnormal calcification of the vasculature.

Name: Pulmonary artery atresia
Def: A congenital anomaly with a narrowing or complete absence of the opening between the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery.
Comment: Pulmonary artery atresia means that unoxygenated blood in the right ventricle can not be effectively pumped into the lung for oxygenation.

Name: Venous thrombosis
Def: Formation of a blood clot (thrombus) inside a vein, causing the obstruction of blood flow.

Name: Pulmonary artery aneurysm
Def: An aneurysm (severe localized balloon-like outward bulging) in the pulmonary artery.

Name: Tortuous cerebral arteries
Def: Excessive bending, twisting, and winding of a cerebral artery.

Name: Generalized arterial calcification
Def: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts, affecting arteries distributed throughout the body.

Name: Extrahepatic portal hypertension
Def: Increased pressure in the pre-hepatic portal vein.
Comment: Hypertension in the portal venous tree proper. previous def: 'has part' some ('increased pressure' and ('inheres in' some ('arterial blood' and ('part of' some 'Pre-hepatic portal vein (adult human)'))) and ('has modifier' some abnormal))

Name: Aortic aneurysm
Def: Aortic dilatation refers to a dimension that is greater than the 95th percentile for the normal person age, sex and body size. In contrast, an aneurysm is defined as a localized dilation of the aorta that is more than 150 percent of predicted (ratio of observed to expected diameter 1.5 or more). Aneurysm should be distinguished from ectasia, which represents a diffuse dilation of the aorta less than 50 percent of normal aorta diameter.
Comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe (pathological) form of dilatation of a segment of a blood vessel. In clinical practice, dilatation and aneurysm are occasionally used interchangeably. In this subhierarchy, we therefore use aneurysm as the primary label and list dilatation as a broad synonym.
Synonym: Bulge in wall of large artery that carries blood away from heart

Name: Accelerated atherosclerosis
Def: Atherosclerosis which occurs in a person with certain risk factors (e.g., SLE, diabetes, smoking, hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, family history of early heart disease) at an earlier age than would occur in another person without those risk factors.

Name: Dilatation of the cerebral artery
Def: The presence of a localized dilatation or ballooning of a cerebral artery.
Comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.

Name: Extracranial internal carotid artery dissection
Def: A separation (dissection) of the layers of the extracranial portion of the internal carotid artery wall.

Name: Arteriovenous fistula
Def: An abnormal connection between an artery and vein.

Name: Vascular tortuosity
Def: Abnormal twisting of arteries or veins.

Name: Peripheral arterial stenosis
Def: Narrowing of peripheral arteries with reduction of blood flow to the limbs. This feature may be quantified as an ankle-brachial index of less than 0.9, and may be manifested clinically as claudication.
Comment: The ankle-brachial index (ABI; the ratio of systolic blood pressure in the ankle to that in the arm), is a measure of occlusion of peripheral arteries in the leg. Peripheral arterial stenosis may be observed with atherosclerosis and with increased intima media thickness as seen in diseases such as pseudoxanthoma elasticum. The most common cause of peripheral arterial stenosis in patients over 40 years of age is atherosclerosis. Cerebral and coronary arteries are by definition not included in peripheral artery disease.

Name: Pulmonary arteriovenous fistulas
Def: A rare vascular anomaly with a direct communication between pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein without an intervening capillary bed.

Name: obsolete Dilatation of the descending aorta
Generalized arterial tortuosity
Def: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of arteries affecting most or all arteries.

Name: Descending thoracic aorta aneurysm
Def: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the descending thoracic aorta.
Synonym: Dilatation of the descending thoracic aorta

Name: Absent pulmonary artery
Def: A congenital defect with aplasia (absence) of one of the right or left pulmonary artery.
Comment: This is a rare feature that has been observed in recessive lethal osteogenesis imperfecta with mutation in CRTAP.

Name: Pulmonary artery sling
Def: An anomalous origin of the left pulmonary artery, such that it arises from the posterior aspect of the right pulmonary artery and passes between the trachea and esophagus to reach the left hilum.

Name: Thoracic aorta calcification
Def: An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall in the thoracic aorta.

Name: Calcification of the aorta
Def: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the aorta.
Comment: Note that the phrase "aortic calcification" is mainly used to describe calcification of the aortic valve rather than of the aorta itself.

Name: Pulmonary arterial medial hypertrophy
Def: Increase in mass of the tunica media of the arteries in the pulmonary circulation.
Synonym: Hypertrophy of the pulmonary artery wall

Name: Medial calcification of large arteries
Def: Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the tunica media of large (conduit) arteries.
Comment: GitHub issue: https://github.com/obophenotype/human-phenotype-ontology/issues/6877

Name: Recurrent cerebral hemorrhage
Def: Recurrent bleeding into the parenchyma of the brain.

Name: Peripheral pulmonary artery stenosis
Def: Stenosis of a peripheral branch of the pulmonary artery.

Name: Ascending tubular aorta aneurysm
Def: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the tubular part of the ascending aorta.
Comment: Aneurysm is considered a severe form of dilatation.
Synonym: Aneurysm of the ascending tubular aorta
Bulging of wall of large artery located above heart

Name: Pulmonary artery hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the pulmonary artery.

Name: Elevated mean arterial pressure
Def: An abnormal increase in the average blood pressure in an individual during a single cardiac cycle.

Name: Coarctation of abdominal aorta
Def: Coarctation of the aorta is a narrowing or constriction of a segment of the abdominal aorta.

Name: Erlenmeyer flask deformity of the femurs
Def: Flaring of distal femur.
Synonym: Erlenmeyer flask deformity of distal femur

Name: Bilateral radial aplasia
Def: Missing radius bone on both sides associated with congenital failure of development.

Name: Metaphyseal sclerosis
Def: Abnormally increased density of metaphyseal bone.
Synonym: Increased bone density in wide portion of long bone

Name: Metaphyseal rarefaction
Def: Reduction in density of metaphyseal bony tissue.

Name: Mesomelic leg shortening
Def: Shortening of the middle parts of the leg in relation to the upper and terminal segments.

Name: Rhizomelic arm shortening
Def: Disproportionate shortening of the proximal segment of the arm (i.e. the humerus).
Comment: This term implies that the ulna and radius are not substantially shortened.

Name: Slender long bones with narrow diaphyses
Def: Reduced diameter of a long bone with a more pronounced reduction of the diameter of the diaphysis of the long bones.
Synonym: Slender long bones with narrow shaft

Name: Multicentric ossification of proximal humeral epiphyses
Recurrent patellar dislocation
Def: Patellar dislocation occurring repeated times.

Name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the capital femoral epiphysis
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
Synonym: Absent/small end part of innermost thighbone
Absent/underdeveloped end part of innermost thighbone

Name: Flattened proximal radial epiphyses
Def: An abnormally flat form of the proximal epiphysis of the radius.

Name: Femoral bowing present at birth, straightening with time
Def: Congenital onset bending or abnormal curvature of the femur that normalizes with age.
Comment: This feature can be diagnosed based on the medical history of congenital femoral bowing with spontaneous improvement.
Synonym: Bowing of thighbone at birth, straightening with time

Name: Dumbbell-shaped humerus
Def: The humerus is shortened and displays flaring (widening) of the metaphyses.
Synonym: Dumbbell-shaped long bone in upper arm

Name: Osteomyelitis leading to amputation due to slow healing fractures
Mesomelic arm shortening
Def: Shortening of the middle parts of the arm in relation to the upper and terminal segments.

Name: Dysplastic distal radial epiphyses
Def: Abnormally developed (dysplastic) distal epiphysis of the radius.

Name: Diaphyseal undertubulation
Def: Tubulation refers to the size and shape of tubular bones. In children and adolescents, the modeling process regulates normal bone growth. Final shaft (tube) diameter depends on appositional bone growth and the equilibrium between periosteal and endosteal bone resorption and formation. Undertubulation refers to a broad, widened form of the shafts (diaphyses) of long bones.
Synonym: Thickening of shaft or central part of long bones

Name: Hypoplastic distal humeri
Def: Underdevelopment of the distal portion of the humerus.

Name: Widened proximal tibial metaphyses
Synonym: Wide innermost wide portion of shankbone bone
Wide innermost wide portion of shinbone bone

Name: Distal ulnar hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the distal portion of the ulna.

Name: Shortening of all phalanges of the toes
Def: Developmental hypoplasia (shortening) of all phalanges of the foot.

Name: Unilateral ulnar hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the ulna on only one side.

Name: Proximal radio-ulnar synostosis
Def: An abnormal osseous union (fusion) between the proximal portions of the radius and the ulna.

Name: Multiple long-bone exostoses
Def: Multiple exostoses originating in long bones.
Synonym: Multiple exostoses of long tubular bones

Name: Irregular capital femoral epiphysis
Def: Irregular surface of the normally relatively smooth capital femoral epiphysis.
Synonym: Irregular end part of innermost thighbone

Name: Proximal humeral metaphyseal irregularity
Def: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of the metaphysis at the proximal end of the humerus (at the shoulder).

Name: Diaphyseal cortical sclerosis
Def: An elevation in bone density of the cortex of one or more diaphyses. Sclerosis is normally detected on a radiograph as an area of increased opacity.

Name: Anterolateral radial head dislocation
Def: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an anterolateral direction.

Name: Metaphyseal spurs
Def: Bony outgrowths that extend laterally from the margin of the metaphysis.

Name: Fragmented, irregular epiphyses
Synonym: Fragmented, irregular end part of bone

Name: Cone-shaped epiphyses fused within their metaphyses
Synonym: Cone-shaped end part of long bone fused within their wide portion of wide bone

Name: Proximal fibular overgrowth
Def: Overgrowth of the proximal part of the fibula.
Synonym: Overgrowth of innermost part of calf bone

Name: Proximal radial head dislocation
Def: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an proximal direction.

Name: Wrist hypermobility
Def: The ability of the wrist joints to move beyond their normal range of motion.

Name: Anterior radial head dislocation
Def: A dislocation of the head of the radius from its socket in the elbow joint in an anterior direction.

Name: Limited knee flexion/extension
Def: A limited ability of the knee joint to perform extension and flexion.

Name: Abnormal metaphyseal trabeculation
Def: An abnormality of the pattern of trabecula (small interconnecting rods of bone) in a metaphyseal region of bone.

Name: Lateral femoral bowing
Def: A lateral bending or abnormal curvature of the femur.

Name: Streaky metaphyseal sclerosis
Def: The presence of streaks (bands) of abnormally increased density of metaphyseal bone.
Synonym: Streak increase in bone density in wide portion of wide bone

Name: Absent proximal radial epiphyses
Def: Absence of the proximal radial epiphysis.

Name: Distal femoral bowing
Def: A bending or abnormal curvature of the distal portion of the femur.

Name: Premature birth following premature rupture of fetal membranes
Synonym: Premature birth following premature rupture of foetal membranes

Name: High-frequency hearing impairment
Def: A type of hearing impairment affecting primarily the higher frequencies of sound (3,000 to 6,000 Hz).
Comment: High frequency hearing impairment often involves loss of ability to hear consonants such as s, f, t, and z, even though vowels can be heard normally.

Name: Cochlear degeneration
Def: Deterioration or loss of the tissues of the cochlea.

Name: Calcification of the auricular cartilage
Def: Ossification affecting the external ear cartilage.

Name: Hypoplastic nasal septum
Def: Underdevelopment of the nasal septum.
Synonym: Decreased size of septum of nose

Name: Abnormal nasal morphology
Comment: This is a category for overall abnormal morphology that may be replaced later with more exact descriptions.

Name: Abnormality of the vertebral endplates
Def: Any abnormality of the vertebral end plates, which are the top and bottom portions of the vertebral bodies that interface with the vertebral disks.

Name: Abnormal sacrum morphology
Def: An abnormality of the sacral bone.
Comment: The sacrum is the large, roughly triangular bone at the base of the verterbal column that is formed by fusion of the five sacral vertebrae S1 to S5.

Name: Abnormal intervertebral disk morphology
Def: Any structural abnormality of the intervertebral disk.
Comment: Any abnormality of the fibrocartilaginous structures that are located between adjacent vertebral bodies.

Name: Abnormality of the Achilles tendon
Def: An abnormality of the Achilles tendon.

Name: Atrial fibrillation
Def: An atrial arrhythmia characterized by disorganized atrial activity without discrete P waves on the surface EKG, but instead by an undulating baseline or more sharply circumscribed atrial deflections of varying amplitude an frequency ranging from 350 to 600 per minute.
Comment: The ventricular response to atrial fibrillation is irregularly irregular because of the large number of atrial impulses that transit the atrioventricular node, making the ventricle partially refractory to further impulses. Atrial fibrillation can cause a number of manifestations including excessive ventricular response with angina pectoris or hypotension in susceptible individuals, syncope, systemic embolization, fatigue, or anxiety. These features should be coded separately.
Synonym: Quivering upper heart chambers resulting in irregular heartbeat

Name: obsolete Dilatation of the ascending aorta
Abdominal aortic aneurysm
Def: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the abdominal aorta.

Name: Aortic arch aneurysm
Def: An abnormal localized widening (dilatation) of the aortic arch.

Name: obsolete Abnormalities of the peripheral arteries
Supraventricular arrhythmia
Def: A type of arrhythmia that originates above the ventricles, whereby the electrical impulse propagates down the normal His Purkinje system similar to normal sinus rhythm.
Comment: Supraventricular arrhythmia includes atrial arrhythmias (atrial tachycardia, atrial flutter, atrial fibrillation), atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia, junctional ectopic tachycardia, atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (Wolf-Parkinson-White Syndrome), orthodromic or antidromic. Supraventricular arrhythmia is distinct from ventricular tachycardia, which originates in the ventricles.

Name: Arterial tortuosity
Def: Abnormal tortuous (i.e., twisted) form of arteries.

Name: Elevated diastolic blood pressure
Def: Abnormal increase in diastolic blood pressure.
Comment: Normal diastolic blood pressure is less than 80 mmHg.

Name: Abnormal cardiac atrium morphology
Def: Any structural abnormality of a cardiac atrium.

Name: Posterior scalloping of vertebral bodies
Def: An excessive concavity of the posterior surface of one or more vertebral bodies.
Comment: The posterior vertebral scalloping sign appears on a lateral radiograph of the spine as an exaggeration of the normal concavity of the posterior surface of one or more vertebral bodies. Neurofibromatosis may be associated with marked scalloping of the posterior borders of the vertebral bodies resulting from intraspinal tumors.

Name: Pericardial constriction
Def: Compression of the heart caused by rigid, thickened, or fused pericardial membranes.

Name: Right ventricular dilatation
Def: Enlargement of the chamber of the right ventricle, which can be defined echocardiographically as a right ventricular to left ventricular ratio greater than 1:1.
Comment: Ventricular dilatation is to be distinguished from ventricular aneurysm, which refers to a diastolic as well as systolic outpouching of the ventricle containing endocardium, epicardium, and thin-wall non-contractile scarred myocardium, which mainly develop in the setting of a full-thickness infarct, replaced by fibrous tissue because of myocardial infarction.

Name: Absence of the pulmonary valve
Def: Refers to the specific combination of defects with a severely dysplastic pulmonary valve and massively dilated branch pulmonary arteries.
Comment: The distinctive feature of APVS is the airway obstruction caused by tracheobronchial compression that results from massive dilatation of the main pulmonary artery (PA) and its first- and second-order branches. Consequential tracheomalacia and bronchomalacia determine the timing and severity of respiratory compromise, as well as the morbidity and mortality of these patients.

Name: Abnormal T-wave
Def: An abnormality of the T wave on the electrocardiogram, which mainly represents the repolarization of the ventricles.

Name: Mitral annular calcification
Def: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) results from progressive calcium deposition along and beneath the mitral valve annulus.
Comment: MAC is a common degenerative process involving the fibrous annulus of the mitral valve, and is generally an incidental finding associated with aging. This term applies if MAC occurs at a substantially younger age than usual.

Name: Anomalous origin of right pulmonary artery from ascending aorta
Def: The right pulmonary artery originates from the ascending aorta in the presence of a pulmonary valve and main pulmonary artery.

Name: Ventricular septal hypertrophy
Def: The dividing wall between left and right sides of the heart, thickens and bulges into the left ventricle.

Name: Coronary artery stenosis
Def: Abnormal narrowing of the coronary artery.

Name: Cardiac valve calcification
Def: Abnormal calcification of a cardiac valve.

Name: Pulmonary valve defects
Def: Any defect in the valve connecting the heart and the pulmonary artery.

Name: Abnormal atrioventricular conduction
Def: An impairment of the electrical continuity between the atria and ventricles.

Name: Preductal coarctation of the aorta
Def: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized proximal to the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the preductal region of aortic arch.
Comment: Blood flow to the aorta distal to the coarctation may be dependent on a patent ductus arteriosus, and hence closure of the ductus arteriosus can lead to serious ischemia of the affected tissues.

Name: Histiocytoid cardiomyopathy
Def: A type of cardiomyopathy characterized pathologically by hamartomatous lesions of cardiac Purkinje cells.
Comment: This HPO term intends to refer to the histological changes that characterize histiocytoid cardiomyopthy. The disease entity Histiocytoid cardiomyopathy is a rare arrhythmogenic disorder characterized by incessant ventricular tachycardia, cardiomegaly, and often sudden death by age 2 years.

Name: Ventricular escape rhythm
Def: A ventricular escape rhythm occurs whenever higher-lever pacemakers in AV junction or sinus node fail to control ventricular activation. Escape rate is usually 20-40 bpm, often associated with broad QRS complexes (at least 120 ms).

Name: Hypoplastic left atrium
Def: Underdeveloped, small left heart atrium

Name: Concentric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Def: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with an symmetrical and concentric pattern of hypertrophy.

Name: Total anomalous pulmonary venous return
Def: Total anomalous pulmonary venous return refers to a congenital malformation in which all four pulmonary veins do not connect normally to the left atrium, but instead drain abnormally to the right atrium.
Comment: Pulmonary veins drain through abnormal connections to the right atrium.

Name: Abnormal left ventricular function
Def: Inability of the left ventricle to perform its normal physiologic function. Failure is either due to an inability to contract the left ventricle or the inability to relax completely and fill with blood during diastole.

Name: Dysplastic pulmonary valve
Def: A congenital malformation of the pulmonary valve characterized by leaflet deformation.

Name: Shortened PR interval
Def: Reduced time for the PR interval (beginning of the P wave to the beginning of the QRS complex). In adults, normal values are 120 to 200 ms long.

Name: Elevated right atrial pressure
Def: An abnormal increase in magnitude of the pressure in the right atrium.
Comment: Elevated mean right atrial pressure (RAP) can be measured by cardiac catheterization.

Name: Complete heart block with broad QRS complexes
Def: A type of third degree heart block in which the escape rhythm arises at a relatively low part of the conduction system (below the atrioventricular node), which produces a wide QRS complex.

Name: Left posterior fascicular block
Def: Conduction block in the posterior division of the left bundle branch of the bundle of His.

Name: Membranous subvalvular aortic stenosis
Def: Subvalvular stenosis is caused by a diaphragm-like membrane. The stenosis is clinically manifested like any other form of aortic stenosis but is often associated with some aortic insufficiency.
Comment: An important feature in the differential diagnosis between valvular and subvalvular aortic stenosis is the fact that no ejection sound is present in the latter.

Name: Dysplastic aortic valve
Def: A congenital malformation of the aortic valve characterized by leaflet deformation.

Name: Premature arteriosclerosis
Def: Arteriosclerosis occurring at an age that is younger than usual.

Name: Complete heart block with narrow QRS complexes
Def: A type of third degree heart block in which the escape rhythm arises at the atrioventricular node, which produces a narrow QRS complex.

Name: Tricuspid regurgitation
Def: Failure of the tricuspid valve to close sufficiently upon contraction of the right ventricle, causing blood to regurgitate (flow backward) into the right atrium.
Comment: This term should not be applied to Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve (see HP:0010316).

Name: Premature coronary artery atherosclerosis
Def: Reduction of the diameter of the coronary arteries as the result of an accumulation of atheromatous plaques within the walls of the coronary arteries before age of 45.

Name: Bicuspid pulmonary valve
Def: The presence of a bicuspid pulmonary valve.
Comment: The pulmonary valve normally has three cusps (flaps), that is, it is normally tricuspid.

Name: Pericardial lymphangiectasia
Def: An abnormal dilatation of lymph vessels in the pericardium.

Name: Prolonged QTc interval
Def: A longer than normal interval (corrected for heart rate) between the Q and T waves in the heart's cycle. Prolonged QTc can cause premature action potentials during late phase depolarizations thereby leading to ventricular arrhythmias and ventricular fibrillations.

Name: Global systolic dysfunction
Def: A reduced ejection fraction and an enlarged left ventricle chamber, the latter by an increased resistance to filling with increased filling pressures. Systolic dysfunction is clinically associated with left ventricular failure in the presence of marked cardiomegaly.

Name: Synovial lining hyperplasia
Def: Synovial hyperplasia involves proliferation of mesenchymal stromal/stem cells and leads to synovial thickening, which can be observed radiographically.
Comment: Synovial hyperplasia is a frequent clinical finding in patients with joint injury and other joint disorders.

Name: Flattened metatarsal heads
Def: Abnormally flat shape of the heads of the metatarsal bones.
Comment: The metatarsal heads articulate with the proximal phalanges of the toes.
Synonym: Flattened head of long bone of foot

Name: Generalized morning stiffness
Def: A sensation of stiffness in the joints that occurs following waking up in the morning.

Name: Stiff interphalangeal joints
Def: Interphalangeal joint stiffness is a perceived sensation of tightness in the interphalangeal joints when attempting to move them after a period of inactivity.

Name: Aplasia of the abdominal wall musculature
Def: Absence of the abdominal musculature.

Name: Helicobacter pylori infection
Def: A recurrent infection of the GI tract with helicobacter pylori, a gram-negative, microaerophilic bacterium usually found in the stomach.
Comment: The bacterial pathogen Helicobacter pylori has co-evolved with humans and colonizes approximately half of the human population, but only causes overt gastric disease in a subset of infected hosts.

Name: Spontaneous esophageal perforation
Def: The occurrence of the full-thickness tear (perforation) of the wall of the esophagus.
Comment: Esophageal perforation can lead to retained gastric contents, saliva, bile, and other substances entering the mediastinum, resulting in mediastinitis, which in turn may lead to sepsis.

Name: Pancreatic pseudocyst
Def: Cyst-like space not lined by epithelium and contained within the pancreas. Pancreatic pseudocysts are often associated with pancreatitis.

Name: Gastric hypertrophy
Def: Hypertrophy of the stomach.

Name: Secretory diarrhea
Def: Watery voluminous diarrhea resulting from an imbalance between ion and water secretion and absorption.

Name: Intrahepatic bile duct cysts
Def: The presence of cyst of the intrahepatic bile duct.

Name: Hypoplastic colon
Def: Underdevelopment of the colon.

Name: Anal mucosal leukoplakia
Def: Leukoplakia is a precancerous dermatosis of mucous membranes analogous Leukoplakia is basically a chronic inflammatory hypertrophy in which anaplasia and malignant dyskeratosis may develop and subsequently advance to an invasive squamous cell cancer. The clinical diagnosis of primary anal leukoplakia is indicated by single or multiple slightly raised,irregular, marginated, grayish-white keratinized' patches in the anal canal. Tissue biopsy is necessary for confirmation.

Name: Pancreatic calcification
Def: The presence of abnormal calcium deposition lesions in the pancreas.

Name: Intestinal obstruction
Def: Blockage or impairment of the normal flow of the contents of the intestine towards the anal canal.

Name: Frequent Giardia lamblia infestation
Def: Increased susceptibility to Giardia lamblia infection of the intestine, as manifested by a medical history of multiple episodes of Giardia lamblia intestinal infection.

Name: Impaired mastication
Def: An abnormal reduction in the ability to masticate (chew), i.e., in the ability to crush and ground food in preparation for swallowing.
Comment: Chewing and swallowing are interrelated. The act of chewing plays a fundamental role in the process of swallowing food. Mastication prepares food for swallowing by breaking it into small particles. Accordingly, loss of teeth has been associated with swallowing difficulties. Chewing difficulties may be caused by loss of teeth, partial dentures, or by tooth pain. Swallowing difficulties, in contrast, are often characterized by difficulties swallowing liquids, reflux, throat spasms, choking on dry food, or dysphagia.

Name: Abdominal organ duplication
Def: A congenital malformation characterized by the development of an additional organ or organ-like structure, i.e., an extra copy of the organ normally located in the abdomen.

Name: Anoperineal fistula
Def: The presence of a fistula (abnormal tunnel) between the anal canal and the perineum.

Name: Absence of intrinsic factor
