The mechanism is currently accepted to be due to cellular interference whereby the two distinct cell populations (those with and without the variant) exhibit abnormal cellular interactions in the mosaic state - in women, who are functionally mosaic due to random X inactivation, or mosaic males. The same mechanism could theoretically be applicable to autosomal genes with a mosaic variant.

Name: Female-limited expression
Def: Used to refer to a monogenic trait linked to an autosomal locus in which the phenotypic effects of allelic differences are expressed only in the female sex.

Name: Mendelian inheritance
Def: A mode of inheritance of diseases whose pathophysiology can be traced back to deleterious variants in a single gene. The inheritance patterns of these single-gene (monogenic) diseases are often referred to as Mendelian in honor of Gregor Mendel.
Comment: Mendelian, or monogenic, inheritance of human diseases refers to patterns of transmission of recognizable disease entities. In many cases variability of clinical manifestations is observed and may be related to variation in other genes, environmental factors, or other unknown causes.

Name: Nesidioblastosis
Def: An abnormality of pancreatic beta cells characterized by a proliferation of abnormal beta cells throughout the entire pancreas, with enlarged islet size and number (hypertrophic islets), increased periductular islets, enlarged beta-cell nuclei and abundant clear cytoplasm. Occasionally beta cells with pleomorphic nuclei, ductuloinsular complexes, and neoformation of islets from ducts are observed.

Name: Greater auricular nerve thickening
Def: Increase in thickness of the great auricular nerve, a cutaneous nerve of the head. It originates from the cervical plexus, with branches of spinal nerves C2 and C3. Thickening may lead to the nerve being palpable or even visible in this region.

Name: Subpulmonary stenosis
Def: A cardiovascular malformation associated with narrowing of the outflow tract of the right ventricle immediately below the pulmonary valve.

Name: Supravalvar pulmonary stenosis
Def: A cardiovascular malformation associated with narrowing at the level of the pulmonary sinotubular junction above the pulmonic valve.

Name: Valvular pulmonary stenosis
Def: A cardiovascular malformation associated with narrowing of the outflow tract of the right ventricle immediately at the level of the pulmonary valve.

Name: Neuromyotonia
Def: Peripheral nerve hyperexcitability manifesting as spontaneous discharges originating from motor axons or their terminals, lead to overactivity of muscles, typically manifesting as twitches, cramps and stiffness.

Name: Bile duct polyp
Def: An elevated growth from the the mucosa of the bile duct.

Name: Appendicular spasticity
Def: A type of spasticity that affects one or more limbs (arms or legs).

Name: Trichoschisis
Def: Transverse fractures through the hair shafts (trichoschisis). Trichoschisis is characterized by a sharp transverse fracture of the hair shaft.
Comment: Hair from individuals with trichothiodistrophy (TTD) exhibits an alternating light and dark (so-called tiger tail) banding pattern with trichoschisis. See figure 2 of PMID:23180925.

Name: White cerebellum sign
Def: On computed tomography of the brain,the white (or dense) cerebellum sign is seen when the cerebellum appears dense with respect to the cerebral parenchyma. The increase in attenuation of cerebellum is in fact a relative hyperdensity caused by decreased attenutation of the brain. It represents anoxic-ischemic cerebral injury, and has a very poor prognosis.
Comment: See figure 30 in PMID:29089832.

Name: Impaired renal tubular reabsorption of low molecular weight protein
Def: Increased loss of low-molecular weight proteins by the kidneys, measured in terms of the fractional excretion (FE). The FE of low-molecular-weight proteins such as beta2-microglobulin can be measured in terms of plasma and urine concentrations, since urinary low-molecular-weight protein concentrations can vary with water reabsorption.
Comment: Urinary proteins are reabsorbed by the renal tubule cells, and increased low molecular weight protein fractional excretion can be a sign of tubular proteinuria.
Synonym: Increased low molecular weight protein excretion

Name: Impaired renal tubular reabsorption of glucose
Def: Increased fractional excretion (FE) of glucose in the urine. The FE of glucose is the percentage of the glucose filtered by the kidney which is excreted in the urine. It is measured in terms of plasma and urine glucose, rather than by the interpretation of urinary glucose concentration alone, as urinary glucose concentrations can vary with water reabsorption.

Name: Impaired renal tubular reabsorption of sodium
Def: Increased fractional excretion (FE) of sodium in the urine. The FE of sodium is the percentage of the sodium filtered by the kidney which is excreted in the urine. It is measured in terms of plasma and urine sodium, rather than by the interpretation of urinary glucose concentration alone, as urinary glucose concentrations can vary with water reabsorption.

Name: Impaired renal tubular reabsorption of phosphate
Def: Increased fractional excretion (FE) of glucose in the phosphate. The FE of glucose is the percentage of the phosphate filtered by the kidney which is excreted in the urine. It is measured in terms of plasma and urine phosphate, rather than by the interpretation of urinary phosphate concentration alone, as urinary glucose concentrations can vary with water reabsorption.

Name: Action myoclonus
Def: A type of myoclonus (arrhythmic muscular jerking) that is induced by voluntary movement. It is made worse by attempts at precise or coordinated movement (intention myoclonus) and may also be provoked by certain sensory stimuli.

Name: Redundant umbilical skin
Def: Greater than normal amount of skin surrounding the umbilicus (belly button) with protrusion of the umbilicus above the plane of the abdomen.
Comment: See Figure 4c of PMID:8944018.

Name: Dull foveal reflex
Def: Reduced brightness of the foveal reflex, which normally is a bright pinpoint of light that is observed to move sideways or up and down in response to movement of the opthalmoscope.
Comment: A dull foveal reflex is an unusual reflex of the foveal region on fundoscopy that may indicate hypoplasia of the fovea.

Name: Corneal pterygium
Def: Corneal pterygium is an ocular surface disease characterized mainly by a wing-shaped growth of limbal and conjunctival tissue over the adjacent cornea.
Comment: In ophthalmological contexts, the word 'pterygium' is frequently used without further qualifiers to denote corneal pterygium.

Name: Fibrofatty replacement of right ventricular myocardium
Def: Replacement of the myocardium of the right ventricular free wall by fat and fibrous tissue.

Name: Elevated circulating alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde concentration
Def: Increased concentration of alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde in the blood circulation.

Name: Fracture blister
Def: Fracture blister is a type of blister that forms following acute bone fractures, typically near the ankle, wrist elbow or foot, where skin adheres tightly to bone with little subcutaneous fat cushioning. The blister that results resembles that of a second degree burn.

Name: Decreased circulating beta-mannosidase activity
Def: Activity of the enzyme beta-mannosidase below the lower limit of normal. Beta-mannosidase is a lysosomal enzyme that catabolizes oligosaccharides.

Name: Urolithiasis
Def: Renal stones are formed within the kidneys, and this is called nephrolithiasis. Urolithiasis is a condition that occurs when these stones exit the renal pelvis and move into the remainder of the urinary collecting system, which includes the ureters, bladder, and urethra.

Name: Decreased level of coenzyme Q10 in skeletal muscle
Def: Reduced amount of coenzyme Q10,a naturally occurring quinone, in skeletal muscle tissue.

Name: Reduced circulating prekallikrein concentration
Def: Reduced concentration of prekallikrein (PK; also known as Fletcher factor) in the blood circulation. PK is the precursor of plasma kallikrein, a serine protease that activates kinins. PK is cleaved to produce kallikrein by activated Factor XII.
Comment: Most cases of prekallikrein deficiency are asymptomatic.

Name: Internal tibial torsion
Comment: Internal twisting of the tibia resulting in the toes of each foot pointing inward (intoeing) .

Name: External tibial torsion
Def: External twisting of the tibia resulting in the toes of each foot pointing outward (outtoeing) .

Name: Trident acetabulum
Def: Abnormal appearance of the acetabulum characterized by spurs at the medial and lateral acetabular margin and in the center of the acetabulum, giving rise to shape resembling a three-pronged spear sadi to resemble a trident.
Comment: See figure 2 of PMID:28744080.

Name: Spherophakia
Def: Spherophakia is a rare congenital condition that presents with weak zonules around a more spherical crystalline lens with an increased anteroposterior thickness of the lens, and highly myopic eye. The lens zonules are developmentally hypoplastic and abnormally weak and due to non-attachment of the posterior zonules to the equatorial zone of the lens, the lens changes its normal shape to spherical.

Name: Atrioventricular valve regurgitation
Def: Regurgitation of a heart valve that controls blood flow from a an atrium to a ventricle, including mitral, tricuspid, or, rarely, single atrioventicular valve.

Name: Single atrioventricular valve regurgitation
Def: Regurgitation of the single atrioventricular valve regurgitation (AVVR) in the context of a congenital heart defect with a single ventricle. Roughly three quarters of patients following Fontan procedure display AVVR.

Name: Urethrovesical occlusion
Def: Blockage of the flow of urine from the bladder into the urethra.

Name: obsolete Vascular granular osmiophilic material deposition
Def: Accumulation of granular osmiophilic material in blood vessel walls. Osmiophilic material becomes black upon staining with osmium tetroxide.

Name: Juvenile type testicular granulosa cell tumor
Def: Juvenile granulosa cell tumor of the testis of neonates and infants is an uncommon lesion frequently associated with abnormal sex chromosome and ambiguous genitalia.

Name: Central nervous system axonal spheroid
Def: Axonal spheroids are bubble-like biological features that form on most degenerating axons. During neurodegeneration, bubble-like swellings form along the length of the axon, a primary and early effect of dynamic axonal deformation. These varicosities, spheroids, or swellings have been described as beads on a string and branches bearing fruit, and they frequently appear on degenerating axons. The focal swellings on degenerating axons, axonal spheroids, are often filled with cellular debris such as organelles, pathological proteins, and disorganized cytoskeletal elements.

Name: Disease remission
Def: A decrease in or disappearance of signs and symptoms typically associated with a disease course.

Name: Elevated circulating biliverdin concentration
Def: Increased concentration of biliverdin, a green tetrapyrrolic bile pigment, in the blood circulation.

Name: Elevated circulating insulin:C-peptide ratio
Def: Increased ratio of insulin to C-peptide in the blood circulation.
Comment: Insulin and C-peptide are secreted into portal vein in equimolar amounts, but the serum ratio is normally from 1:5 to 1:15 due to removal of approximately 50% of insulin from blood during initial passage through the liver.

Name: Abnormal left ventricular endsystolic diameter
Def: A deviation from the normal range of the left ventricular endsystolic diameter.
Comment: The measurement of the left ventricular endsystolic diameter is performed in the parasternal long-axis view, perpendicular to the long axis of the left ventricle at the tips of the mitral valve leaflets. It refers to the transverse (left-to-right) internal (luminal) distance, excluding thickness of walls. The normal range can be taken as 20-40 mm (total 2SD range 17.6-52.3 according to PMID:24451180).

Name: Reduced left ventricular endsystolic diameter
Def: A lower than normal left ventricular endsystolic diameter.

Name: Bacterial encephalitis
Def: Encephalitis caused by bacterial infection.

Name: Hilar lymph node enlargement
Def: Hilar lymphadenopathy is swelling or enlargement of lymph nodes localized in hila, wedge-shaped anatomical structures containing pulmonary vessels, major bronchi, nerves and lymph nodes. Hilar lymph nodes are not visible on chest X-ray if they are not enlarged. Hilar lymph node enlargement can be caused by benign and malignant conditions and can be symmetrical (bilateral) or asymmetrical (unilateral).

Name: Pulmonary vein varix
Def: Pulmonary vein varix (PVV), refers to a localized dilatation of a pulmonary vein. PVV is a rare condition and can be congenital or acquired. PVV typically occur at the confluence of the veins adjacent to the left atrium. PVVs are sometimes classified into three morphological types: saccular, tortuous and confluent.

Name: Decreased CSF glycine concentration
Def: Abnormally decreased levels of glycine in cerebrospinal fluid.

Name: Elbow contracture
Def: A limitation in the passive range of motion of the elbow resulting from loss of elasticity in the periarticular tissues owing to structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules or skin.

Name: Joint contracture
Def: A limitation in the passive range of motion of a joint resulting from loss of elasticity in the periarticular tissues owing to structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules or skin. A contracture prevents movement of the associated body part.
Comment: To assess a joint contracture, the passive or active range of motion (ROM) of a joint with a contracture is assessed by moving the joint through its natural range with no active effort from the individual. The angular distance of the joint motion and the loss of ROM in a contracture is recorded through comparison with the contralateral joint or normative values. Conventionally, a joint contracture is named according to the joint involved and the direction opposite the lack of range. For example, inability to fully extend the knee is referred to as a knee flexion contracture, compared to inability to bend (flex) the knee, which is referred to as a knee extension contracture. Contractures in neuromuscular diseases develop due to intrinsic myotendinous structural changes and extrinsic factors. Known contributing extrinsic factors include decreased ability to actively move a limb through its full range of motion, immobility or static positioning for prolonged periods of time, and agonist antagonist muscle imbalance. Intrinsic muscle tissue alterations in dystrophic myopathies contribute to contracture formation. The most significant histologic changes are those of muscle fiber loss, abnormal residual dystrophic muscle fibers, segmental necrosis of muscle fibers, and increased amounts of adipose tissue, connective tissue, and fibrosis.

Name: Elbow extension contracture
Def: An elbow contracture that limits the ability of the elbow joint to flex (flexion of the the elbow joint refers to bending the elbow joint to bring the hand closer to the shoulder), meaning that the elbow is fixed in an extended (straight) position.

Name: Forearm supination contracture
Def: A contracture that limits the ability of the forearm to stabilize the hand in pronation (pronation refers to a rotation of the forearm that causes the palm and forearm to face downwards), meaning that the palm is fixed in a upward orientation. Restriction of supination/pronation can occur at the elbow (radial-humeral joint), at the wrist (radial-ulnar joint), and anywhere in between.

Name: Forearm pronation contracture
Def: A contracture that limits the ability of the forearm to stabilize the hand in supiation (supination refers to a rotation of the forearm that causes the palm and forearm to face upwards), meaning that the palm is fixed in a downward orientation. Restriction of supination/pronation can occur at the elbow (radial-humeral joint), at the wrist (radial-ulnar joint), and anywhere in between.

Name: Hippocampal malrotation
Def: Hippocampal malrotation, also termed incomplete inversion of the hippocampus or hippocampal malformation, is an increasingly recognized neuroimaging finding of undetermined clinical significance. It is characterized by features including (i) Round or pyramidal shape instead of ovoid shape; (ii) Medial position of the hippocampus on the hippocampal sulcus; (iii) The collateral sulcus is excessively deep or verticalized; (iv) Fimbria located medial to the hippocampus; (v) Small or displaced fornix; (vi) Enlarged temporal horn and empty choroid fissure; (vii) Thickened subiculum; (viii) Reduced upper horizontal portion of the parahippocampal gyrus.

Name: Claw toe deformity
Def: Claw toes are characterized by hyperextension at the metatarsal-phalangeal joints and flexion of the interphalangeal joints.
Comment: Claw teo deformity is commonly seen in neuromuscular disorders.

Name: Toe deformity
Def: Abnormal positioning of toe phalanges. Deformities of the lesser toes often occur gradually, though they can be brought on by trauma. The main adult sagittal plane deformities consist of claw toes, hammer toes and mallet toes. Axial plane deformities include crossover toes.

Name: Prolonged central motor conduction time
Def: Increased duration of the central motor conduction time (CMCT). The CMCT estimates the conduction time of corticospinal fibers between motor cortex and spinal (or bulbar) motoneurons. It includes the times for excitation of cortical cells, conduction via the corticobulbar-corticospinal tract and excitation of the motoneuron sufficient to reach its firing threshold. CMCT is calculated by subtracting the peripheral conduction time from the MEP latency recorded after cortical stimulation.
Comment: The determination of central motor conduction time is a sensitive method to detect myelopathies, and abnormalities may be observed in the absence of radiological changes.

Name: Circumferential skin creases on extremities
Def: Ringed creases of the skin of the extremities related to folding of excess skin.

Name: Atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor
Def: An aggressive malignant embryonal neoplasm arising from the central nervous system. It is composed of cells with a large eccentric nucleus, prominent nucleolus, and abundant cytoplasm. Mutations of the SMARCB1 gene or very rarely SMARCA4 (BRG1) gene are present. The vast majority of cases occur in childhood. Symptoms include lethargy, vomiting, cranial nerve palsy, headache, and hemiplegia.

Name: Rhabdoid tumor of the kidney
Def: A highly aggressive, extremely rare neoplasm of the kidney that is usually seen in children. The term rhabdoid is used because the tumor cells resemble rhabdomyoblasts but lack myogenic markers, and pathologic diagnosis requires familiarity with these microscopic features plus awareness that adult onset is possible. It can be associated with abnormalities of chromosome 22. It is characterized by the presence of cells with a large eccentric nucleus, prominent nucleolus, and abundant cytoplasm.
Synonym: Malignant rhabdoid tumor of the kidney
Malignant rhabdoid tumour of the kidney

Name: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma
Def: A form of T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma in which cytotoxic CD8+ T cells infiltrate adipose tissue forming subcutaneous nodules.

Name: Fungal hyphae in sputum
Def: Presence of hyphae (long, branching, filamentous structures produced by fungi) in sputum.

Name: Enlarged tectum
Def: Increasaed size of the tectum, which is the region of the midbrain posterior to the cerebral aqueduct of Sylvius. The midbrain is the most superior portion of the brainstem.

Name: Reduced circulating 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase concentration
Def: Decreased concentration of 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase in th blood circulation.

Name: Solitary angiokeratoma
Def: A dark, keratotic papule about 2-10 mm in diameter, usually occurring on the lower extremeities. Usually the lesions begin as bright, soft, and nonkeratotic paules which grow larger and change to a firm, blue to black and keratotic stage.
Comment: Solitary angiokeratomas most commonly occur in the third or fourth decade of life but may occur in children.

Name: Fordyce angiokeratoma
Def: A type of angiokeratoma that most commonly occurs on the scrotum of patients who are 40 years old or older. The typical single lesion is a dark red to blue dome-shaped papule 2-4 mm in diameter with a very discrete keratotic surface. Typically, they are multiple and arranged in a line parallel to the raphe mediana of the scrotum. They also occur on the vulva and less commnly on the penis.

Name: Angiokeratoma circumscriptum naeviforme
Def: A type of angiokeratoma that typically presents in childhood as a large, mostly linear and unilateral hyperkeratotic plaque which is composed of confluent keratotic papules. The size ranges from a few centimeters up to a major part of the body surface. Initially the lesions present as multiple reddish macules, clinically similar to a nevus flammeus. Within several years they develop into acanthokeratotic papules that agrregate into plaques which may have a hyperkeratotic surface.

Name: Angiokeratoma of Mibelli
Def: A type of angiokeratoma that typically presents in women on the dorsa of fingers and toes and multiple dark red papules with a slightly verrucous surface, each measuring about 3-5 mm in diameter.

Name: Laryngeal mass
Def: A lump in the region of the larynx. A mass is any lump in the body that can be caused by the abnormal growth of cells, a cyst, hormonal changes or an immune reaction. Typically a mass is an initial finding that will lead to additional workup. Laryngeal masses can be visualized by multiple methods include computed tomography.

Name: Palate mass
Def: A lump in the region of the palate. A mass is any lump in the body that can be caused by the abnormal growth of cells, a cyst, hormonal changes or an immune reaction. Typically a mass is an initial finding that will lead to additional workup.

Name: Thick oral frenulum
Def: Increased thickness of an oral frenulum, flaps of mucous membrane that extend from the midline gingiva to the upper or lower lip.

Name: Tooth avulsion
Def: A type of dental trauma characterized by total dislocation of the tooth from its socket.

Name: Torn oral frenulum
Def: Laceration or tear of an oral frenulum, flaps of mucous membrane that extend from the midline gingiva to the upper or lower lip.

Name: Intraoral laceration
Def: A wound of the mucosa within the oral cavity covering lips, tongue, palate, gingiva, pharynx, or retropharynx.

Name: Erythematous oral mucosa
Def: An erythematous lesion of the oral mucosa may result from a variety of tissue alterations, including inflammation, erythrocyte extravasation, and atrophy or reduced keratinization of the surface epithelium.

Name: Mitral chordae tendinae rupture
Def: Breakage of the chordae tendinae of the mitral valve. This can lead to loss of tension of one of the mitral valve leaflets and mitral regurgitation.
Comment: The chordae provide the critical function of anchoring the mitral leaflets during systole, allowing for symmetric coaptation and preventing prolapse of the leaflets into the left atrium. The chordae are attached to the left ventricle via the papillary muscles.

Name: History of cardiovascular procedure
Def: Indicates that a cardiovascular procedure such as stenting, bypass, catherization was performed on a patient.

Name: Ejection click
Def: A high-pitched sound that occurs at the moment of maximal opening of the aortic or pulmonary valves. They are heard just after the first heart sound. The sounds occur in the presence of a dilated aorta or pulmonary artery or in the presence of a bicuspid or flexible stenotic aortic or pulmonary valve. Ejection clicks may also be called ejection sounds.

Name: Cryofibrinogenemia
Def: Cryofibrinogen is an abnormal protein that forms precipitate only in plasma. consisting of fibrinogen, fibronectin, alpha1-antitrypsin and alpha2-macroglobulin.
Comment: Cryofibrinogenemia (CF) can be detected in both healthy persons and patients with different disorders, including autoimmune diseases, cancer, infections, etc. Cryofibrinogen should be distinguished from cryoglobulin since, unlike the latter, it precipitates only in plasma and not in serum.

Name: triggered by allergens
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to allergens.

Name: Clicking tinnitus
Def: A type of tinnitus that presents as clicks, resembling the noise made by the snapping together of 2 fingers.
Comment: Clicking tinnitus may be caused by conditions including palatal myoclonus, which is characterized by a rhythmic contraction of the palatal muscles including the levator veli palatini and the tensor palatini muscles.

Name: Reduced hair sulfur content
Def: Abnormally low amount of sulfur in hair.
Comment: Normal hair keratin is high in sulfur content.

Name: Chromhidrosis
Def: Secretion of colored sweat.
Comment: While chromhidrosis is a clinical diagnosis, further studies may be needed to ascertain the type and cause of chromhidrosis if not apparent from the history and physical examination. A Wood's lamp will fluoresce green, blue, and yellow apocrine gland secretions yellow, while black and dark brown secretions usually do not fluoresce.

Name: Purulent eye discharge
Def: Secretion of pus-like (purulent) material from the eye, which may caused the eyelids to be matted together.

Name: Megaloblepharon
Def: Disproportionately large eyelids

Name: Bacteria in cerebrospinal fluid
Def: Presence of bacteria in the cerebrospinal fluid, as manifested by visual inspection or bacterial culture results.

Name: Joint crepitus
Def: A popping, clicking or crackling sound that accompaniees movement of a joint.

Name: Intertriginous distribution
Def: Applies to the localization of a skin lesion involving any area of the body where two opposing skin surfaces can touch and rub or chaff.
Comment: The word intertrigo comes from the Latin inter (between) and terere (to rub) and reflects the rubbing together of skin against skin to create maceration and irritation, hence, friction dermatitis or chaffing.

Name: Distributed along skin tension lines
Def: Applies to the localization of a skin lesion that correspond to skin tension lines, which are linear clefts in the skin that indicate the direction of orientation of the underlying collagen fibers. Skin tension lines are also known as Langer's lines or lines of cleavage.

Name: Abnormal communication
Def: Presence of any form of communication (e.g., verbal or non-verbal) that does not align with cultural expectations or developmental level.

Name: Abnormal eye contact
Def: Any abnormality of eye contact behavior. We define eye contact as a form of nonverbal communication between two individuals who are facing each other in which an individual directs the eyes towards the eyes or face of the other individual. Eye contact occurs frequently and voluntarily during face-to-face verbal communication. The duration and frequency of eye contact that is interpreted to be appropriate may follow social and situational norms.

Name: Gaze avoidance
Def: A deliberate avoidance of eye contact.

Name: Excessive eye contact
Def: Tendency to maintain sustained eye contact for an inappropriately long period of time.

Name: Balanitis
Def: Inflammation of glans penis

Name: Instep location
Def: Applies to an abnormality that is situated in the arched middle portion of the foot in front of the ankle joint (i.e., instep).

Name: Ameliorated by ultraviolet light exposure
Def: Applies to a skin lesion that is improved or made more bearable by exposure to ultraviolet light (sunshine or phototherapy).

Name: Decreased circulating aspartic acid concentration
Def: An reduced concentration of aspartic acid in the blood circulation.

Name: Abnormal circulating erythropoietin concentration
Def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of erythropoietin in the blood circulation. Erythropoietin is a glycoprotein hormone produced by the peritubular cells of the kidney that stimulates red blood cell production.

Name: Reduced circulating erythropoietin concentration
Def: Decreased concentration of erythropoietin in the blood circulation. Erythropoietin is a glycoprotein hormone produced by the peritubular cells of the kidney that stimulates red blood cell production.

Name: Abnormal gamma-glutamyltransferase level
Def: Any deviation from the normal level of the enzyme gamma-glutamyltransferase (GGT). GGT is mainly present in kidney, liver, and pancreatic cells, but small amounts are present in other tissues.
Comment: A common reference range for children an adults is between 0 and 30 international units per liter (IU/L).

Name: Reduced gamma-glutamyltransferase level
Def: Decreased level of the enzyme gamma-glutamyltransferase (GGT). GGT is mainly present in kidney, liver, and pancreatic cells, but small amounts are present in other tissues.

Name: Elevated circulating histamine concentration
Def: Increased concentration of histamine in the blood circulation.
Comment: The blood histamine concentration is normally very low but may be increased if released from activated mast cells, for example in an allergic response.

Name: Increased circulating interleukin 18 concentration
Def: An increased concentration of interleukin-18 in the blood circulation.

Name: Abnormal phytanic acid:pristanic acid ratio
Def: Any deviation from the normal ratio of blood phytanic acid concentration to pristanic acid concentration.
Comment: The pristanic acid/phytanic acid ratio is of value for the differential diagnosis of Refsum disease, rhizomelic chondrodysplasia punctata, peroxisome deficiency disorders and isolated peroxisomal beta-oxidation defects.
Synonym: Abnormal phytanic acid to pristanic acid ratio

Name: Increased phytanic acid:pristanic acid ratio
Def: An elevation above the normal ratio of blood phytanic acid concentration to pristanic acid concentration.
Comment: This feature may be observed in diseases such as Alpha-methylacyl-CoA racemase deficiency.
Synonym: Phytanic acid to pristanic acid ratio high

Name: Decreased phytanic acid:pristanic acid ratio
Def: A reduction below the normal ratio of blood phytanic acid concentration to pristanic acid concentration.
Synonym: Phytanic acid to pristanic acid ratio low

Name: Rectovesical fistula
Def: An aberrant, pathological communication between the rectum and the bladder.

Name: Rectoureteral fistula
Def: An abnormal connection (fistula) between the rectum and the ureter.

Name: Hypoplastic umbilicus
Def: Underdevelopment of the umbilicus.

Name: Arachnoid granulation
Def: Arachnoid granulations (AGs) are tufts of arachnoid membrane invaginated into the dural sinuses through which cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) enters the venous system. The lesions are primarily located in the parasagittal region along the superior sagittal sinus, which is occasionally seen at the transverse sinus. Normally dural venous sinus AGs typically range from 2 to 8 mm in size, but may grow enough to expand the dural sinuses, and even the inner table, diploic space and outer table of the skull.

Name: Increased CSF taurine concentration
Def: Increased concentration of taurine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

Name: Elevated circulating glutathione concentration
Def: An abnormally increased level of glutathione in the blood circulation.

Name: Hawkinsinuria
Def: The concentration of hawkinsin in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
Comment: Hawkinsin is a cysteine derivative that is cysteine in which the thiol group is substituted by a [2-(carboxymethyl)-2,5-dihydroxycyclohex-3-en-1-yl]sulfanediyl group.

Name: Elevated urinary phenylpyruvic acid level
Def: An abnormally increased amount of phenylpyruvic acid in the urine.

Name: Ameliorated by lumbar puncture
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by lumbar puncture.

Name: Increased CSF uracil concentration
Def: An increased level of uracil in the cerebrospinal fluid.

Name: Elevated urine kynurenine level
Def: An abnormally increased amount of kynurenine in the urine.

Name: Increased CSF L-alloisoleucine concentration
Def: An abnormally increased concentration of L-alloisoleucine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

Name: Hydroxylysinemia
Def: An increased concentration of hydroxylysine in the blood circulation. Hydroxylysine arises from a post-translational hydroxy modification of lysine and is unique to collagen and proteins containing collagen-like sequences. Elevated concentrations of hydroxylysine may indicate increased bone turnover.

Name: Homocitrullinuria
Def: An increased amount of L-homocitrulline in the urine. L-homocitrulline is an L-lysine derivative that is L-lysine having a carbamoyl group at the N(6)-position. It is found in individuals with urea cycle disorders.

Name: 2-hydroxyadipic aciduria
Def: The concentration of 2-hydroxyadipic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Homoargininuria
Def: An increased amount of homoarginine in the urine. Homoarginine is a nonproteinogenic alpha amino acid.

Name: Increased urinary cysteine level
Def: An increased concentration of cysteine in the urine.

Name: Gastric xanthoma
Def: Gastric xanthomas (also known as xanthelasmas) are are plaque-like red lesions defined by the presence of histiocytic containing lipids.
Comment: Gastrix xanthoma is usually an incidental endoscopic finding of unclear clinical significance.

Name: Decreased stool elastase level
Def: Reduced amount of pancreatic elastase in the stool. This feature may be observed with pancreatic insufficiency.

Name: Elevated stool chloride content
Def: Elevated amount of chloride in the stool.

Name: Increased fecal coproporphyrin III:coproporphyrin I ratio
Def: Abnormal relative increase in the amount of fecal coproporphyrin III as compared to coproporphyrin I in the feces.
Synonym: Coproporphyrin isomer III/I ratio high in stool

Name: Increased fecal harderoporphyrin
Def: Abnormally high concentration of harderoporphyrin in feces.

Name: Increased fecal heptacarboxylporphyrin
Def: Abnormally high concentration of heptacarboxylporphyrin in feces.

Name: Increased fecal pentacarboxylporphyrin
Def: Abnormally high concentration of pentacarboxylporphyrin in feces.

Name: Increased fecal isocoproporphyrin
Def: Abnormally high concentration of isocoproporphyrin in feces.

Name: Positive fecal Clostridium botulinum test
Def: Identification of Clostridium botulinum toxin in the feces.

Name: Perihepatic adhesions
Def: Abnormal union of the membranous surfaces of the liver capsule and the parietal peritoneum due to inflammation or injury. Adhesions may be visualized by laparoscopy and may have a violin string appearance.

Name: Dilated vas deferens
Def: Abnormal increase in diameter (expansion) of the vas deferens.

Name: Enlarged epididymis
Def: Abnormal increase in the size of the epididymis.

Name: Atypical gestures
Def: Spontaneous production of communicative gestures that are perceived as odd or mechanical, or are poorly integrated with other means of communication. This may include inaccurate mimicry of typical gestures.
Comment: Gestures refer to movements of the arms, hand, shoulders, or head and do not include facial expressions.

Name: Bone marrow vacuolated lymphocytes
Def: The presence of lymphocytes with multilple vacuoles (a membrane-bound cell organelle) in the bone marrow.

Name: Spinal cord calcifications
Def: The presence of calcium deposition in the spinal cord.

Name: Neuroepithelial cyst
Def: A benign epithelial-lined cystic lesion that can occur anywhere in the neuraxis. Neuroepithelial cysts are ependymal or epithelial lined fluid collections of unknown etiology within the central nervous system parenchyma with no obvious ventricular or subarachnoid connection. Most cysts are asymptomatic, however, some present with seizures, mass effect, or rarely with movement disorders. On imaging, they present as CSF-like parenchymal cysts with smooth, rounded borders and minimal or no surrounding signal intensity abnormality.

Name: Reduced circulating interleukin 7 concentration
Def: A diminished concentration of interleukin-7 in the circulation.

Name: Increased circulating interleukin 12 concentration
Def: An increased concentration of interleukin-12 in the blood circulation.

Name: Increased circulating interleukin 13 concentration
Def: An increased concentration of interleukin-13 in the blood circulation.

Name: Increased circulating interleukin 2 concentration
Def: An increased concentration of interleukin-2 in the blood circulation.

Name: Increased circulating interleukin 4 concentration
Def: An increased concentration of interleukin-4 in the blood circulation.

Name: Increased circulating interleukin 5 concentration
Def: An increased concentration of interleukin-5 in the blood circulation.

Name: Salpingitis
Def: An inflammation of the fallopian tube.

Name: Tubo-ovarian abscess
Def: A tubo-ovarian abscess (TOA) is a complex infectious mass of the adnexa that forms as a sequela of pelvic inflammatory disease.
Comment: Classically, a TOA manifests with an adnexal mass, fever, elevated white blood cell count, lower abdominal-pelvic pain, and/or vaginal discharge.

Name: Opacified paranasal sinuses
Def: White appearance (radio-opaqueness) of a paranasal sinus on radiography.

Name: Elevated brain glutamine level by MRS
Def: An increased in the level of glutamine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

Name: Abnormal brain glutamine level by MRS
Def: A deviation from normal in the level of glutamine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

Name: Increased urinary hexanoic acid level
Def: The concentration of hexanoic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Hepatic focal nodular hyperplasia
Def: Hepatic focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) is a benign hepatic tumor. FNH develops within hepatic parenchymal tissue that is otherwise histologically normal. Macroscopically, the tumor is characterized by the presence of depressed, grayish-white scar, which is generally (but not always) located at the center of the lesion, with fibrous septa radiating outward, toward the periphery of the tumor. This stellate scar is found in only 50% of all FNH nodules, but its presence is regarded as pathognomonic. The lesion itself is usually lighter in color than the tissue that surrounds it, and it sometimes has a yellowish hue. FNH nodules are generally not capsulated; their margins are well defined, and they are sometimes lobulated.
Comment: FNH is often an incidental finding

Name: Increased bone marrow iron
Def: An increased amount of iron in the bone marrow.
Comment: This feature can be assessed by methods including Prussian blue staining of bone marrow smears.

Name: Glenoid fracture
Def: A fracture of the glenoid fossa, a relatively shallow dish is located on the lateral scapula and is the socket portion of the shoulder joint that meets to articulate the humeral head.

Name: Widened mediastinum
Def: Abnormal increase in the width of the mediastinum, often defined as being greater than 6 to 8 cm.
Comment: This feature can be ascertained by plain chest radiography. A wide mediastinum has many causes which include thoracic aortic aneurysm of the ascending and proximal descending aorta, aortic dissection of ascending and proximal descending aorta, unfolding of the aorta, traumatic aortic rupture, hilar lymphadenopathy, mediastinal masses, mediastinitis, cardiac tamponade, and fractured ribs or thoracic vertebrae.

Name: Narrow mediastinum
Def: Abnormal decrease in the width of the mediastinum.

Name: Ovarian torsion
Def: Ovarian torsion is a twisting of the ligaments that support the adnexa, cutting off the blood flow to the ovary.

Name: Septate gallbladder
Def: Septate gallbladder is characterized by the presence of a septum that divides the gallbladder in two chambers. When the septum dividing the gallbladder lies longitudinally it is called bilobed gallbladder and when there is a transverse septum separating the fundus from the rest of the gallbladder it is called an hour-glass gallbladder.

Name: Gallbladder wall thickening
Def: Abnormal increased in the thickness of the wall of the gallbladder.
Comment: Gallbladder wall thickening is a common yet nonspecific finding that can occur in a wide range of gallbladder diseases and extracholecystic conditions.

Name: Gallbladder enlargement
Def: Abnormal increased in the thickness of the size of the gallbladder.

Name: Gallbladder mass
Def: An abnormal lesion or swelling seen on gallbladder imaging.

Name: Fingerprint bodies
Def: Fingerprint bodies are inclusion bodies located at the periphery of the muscle fibers underneath the sarcolemma (subsarcolemmal), consisting of non-membrane-bound packed lamellae arranged in concentric patterns resembling fingerprints.
Comment: See Figure 2 of PMID:32008911.
Synonym: Muscle biopsy: fingerprint bodies at periphery of muscle fibers
Muscle biopsy: fingerprint bodies at periphery of muscle fibres

Name: Spheroid bodies
Def: An accumulation of myofilamentous material within individual muscle fibers, forming usually round but occasionally elongated bodies ranging from 2 to 15 pm in size. The so-called spheroid bodies stain green with the modified trichrome preparation and are mainly present in the periphery of type 1 muscle fibers, where they may occupy large sectors sharply demarcated from the remainder of the cross-sectioned muscle fiber.
Comment: See Figure 3 of PMID:571956.

Name: Abnormal muscle tissue enzyme activity or level
Def: Any deviation from the normal activity or histological staining of an enzyme in muscle tissue, usually measured in a muscle biopsy specimen.

Name: Reduced muscle aconitase activity
Def: Diminished activity of the enzyne aconitase in muscle tissue.

Name: Transitional-cell carcinoma of the ureter
Def: A cancer of the ureter that most often arises in the distal third of the ureter and is often diagnosed during the sixth and seventh decades of life. The most common presentation is gross hematuria or flank pain.

Name: Increased circulating Interferon-alpha concentration
Def: An elevation in the concentration of interferon alpha measured in the blood circulation.

Name: Liver hamartoma
Def: A benign (noncancerous) tumorlike malformation made up of an abnormal mixture of cells and tissues that originates in the liver.

Name: Ameloblastoma
Def: Ameloblastoma is a benign odontogenic tumor generally present in the jaw bone. The tumor originates from the residual epithelium of the tooth germ, epithelium of odontogenic cysts stratified squamous epithelium and epithelium of the enamel organ.

Name: Ameliorated by ketogenic diet
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by following a ketogenic diet.
Comment: The ketogenic diet is a method of nutrition leading to the increased production of ketone bodies (beta-hydroxybutyrate, acetoacetate and acetone) in the organism and, thus, to a condition of ketosis. This effect comes about by obtaining the greatest energy share from fats and minimizing the consumption of carbohydrates.

Name: Pretibial hyperpigmentation
Def: Darkening of the area of skin that overlies the shin.

Name: Gingival fragility
Def: Gums that are easily damaged.

Name: Muscle fiber fuchsinophilic inclusion bodies
Def: The presence of inclusion bodies within the cytoplasm of muscle cells that react positively with acid fuchsin.

Name: Esophageal myenteric plexus degeneration
Def: Deterioration of the cells of the myenteric plexus (also known as the Auerbach plexus) located between the layers of the muscular propria of the esophagus.

Name: Periorificial hyperkeratosis
Def: Scaling and overgrowth of horny tissue of the skin surrounding body orifices (including peri-auricular, peri-oral, peri-anal areas.

Name: Eosinophilic lymph node infiltration
Def: Presence of an elevated number of eosinophils in a lymph node (usually as demonstrated by lymph node biopsy).

Name: Blood parasite
Def: Detection of a parasitic organism in the blood stream. Blood parasites include malaria plasmodia, microfilaria species, trypanosomes (the causative agents of African sleeping sickness and South American Changas disease) and the causative agents of schistosomiasis of the bladder and the intestine.

Name: Bloodstream trypomastigotes
Def: Presence of trypomastigote parasites in the blood stream. This finding can be demonstrated by the identification of trypomastigote parasites on peripheral blood smear.

Name: Adamantinoma
Def: A primary low-grade, malignant bone tumor that is predominantly located in the mid-portion of the tibia. Histologically, classic adamantinoma is a biphasic tumor characterized by epithelial and osteofibrous components that may be intermingled with each other in various proportions and differentiating patterns.

Name: Abnormal enzyme activity in muscle tissue
Def: Deviation from the normal activity of an enzyme in muscle tissue.

Name: Reduced muscle phosphoglycerate kinase activity
Def: Reduced activity of phosphoglycerate kinase (PGK) in muscle tissue. PGK is a glycolytic enzyme that catalyzes one of the two ATP-producing reactions in the glycolytic pathway, through the conversion of 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate to 3-phosphoglycerate.

Name: Reduced fibroblast type III procollagen synthesis
Def: Diminished production of type III procollagen by cultured skin fibroblasts.
Synonym: Type III procollagen synthesis by fibroblasts low

Name: Reduced muscle myoadenylate deaminase activity
Def: Diminished activity of the enzyme myoadenylate deaminase. Myoadenylate deaminase is the muscle isoform of adenosine monophosphate (AMP) deaminase and catalyzes the deamination of AMP to inosine monophosphate and ammonia.

Name: Bent long bone
Def: A developmental defect of a long bone, such as the femur or the humerus, characterized by a sharply curve deviation located in the diaphysis (shaft) of the bone.

Name: Tracheal rupture
Def: A break or tear in the trachea.

Name: Increased myocardial glycogen content
Def: Elevated amount of glycogen in the myocardium.

Name: Triggered by monoamine oxidase inhibitor
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to a monoamine oxidase inhibitor.

Name: Triggered by serotonin reuptake inhibitor
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to a serotonin reuptake inhibitor.

Name: Ameliorated by acetazolamide
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with acetazolamide.

Name: Ameliorated by exposure to medication
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with a medication. Terms in this subhierarchy are intended to be used for cases in which the fact that a manifestation of a disease responds to a specific treatment can be used in the differential diagnosis.

Name: Ameliorated by vitamin B12
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with vitamin B12.

Name: Ameliorated by thiamine
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with thiamine.

Name: Ameliorated by dantrolene
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with dantrolene.

Name: Ameliorated by biotin
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with biotin.

Name: Reduced bone-marrow megakaryocyte size
Def: Decreased in average size (diameter) of megakaryocytes in the bone marrow. Megakaryocyte diameter can be assessed as using automated cellular imaging systems.

Name: Hairshafts with longitudinal grooves
Def: Long narrow depressions running lengthwise in hairshafts. This feature can be appreciated by scanning electron microsopy.
Comment: See Figure 1 of PMID:11234560.

Name: Mycobacterium bacteremia
Def: Presence of viable mycobacteria in the blood.

Name: Decreased delta-aminolevulinate dehydratase activity
Def: Reduced activity of the enzyme delta-aminolevulinate dehydratase. The enzyme is active in erythrocytes.

Name: Elevated circulating pancreatic secretory trypsin inhibitor activity
Def: Increased activity of the enzyme pancreatic secretory trypsin inhibitor in the blood circulation.
Comment: Pancreatic secretory trypsin inhibitor (PSTI), also known as serine protease inhibitor Kazal type I (SPINK1), binds rapidly to trypsin, inhibits its activity and is likely to protect the pancreas from prematurely activated trypsinogen. The blood concentration of PSTI may be increased in hepatocellular carcinoma and as a part of the acute phase reposnse response to infection, inflammation, tissue damage and other stressors.
Synonym: Elevated circulating serine protease inhibitor Kazal type I

Name: Presence of uterus in 46,XY individual
Def: A developmental anomaly in which an individual with an X chromosome and a Y chromosome (usually 46,XY) has a uterus. The uterus and Fallopian tubes are derived from the Müllerian duct and thus this phenotype is generally also associated with the presence of Fallopian tubes.

Name: Intraluminal meconium calcification
Def: Deposition of calcium in meconium present in the internal cavity of the fetal bowel. This manifestation may be the result of any distal intestinal obstruction.

Name: Portal vein hypoplasia
Def: A developmental defect characterized by underdevelopment of the portal vein.

Name: Adrenal leiomyoma
Def: Adrenal leiomyoma is a rare, benign solid tumor that develops from the smooth muscle of the adrenal vein and its tributaries
Comment: Pheochromocytoma, Cortical Carcinoma, Adrenal leiomyoma present with heterogeneously enhancing masses on different imaging modalities but cannot be differentiated solely based on imaging.

Name: Small intestinal lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate
Def: Infiltration of the wall of the small intestine by lymphocytes and mature plasma cells.

Name: Triggered by neuroleptic medication
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to neuroleptic (also known as antipsychotic) medication.

Name: Abnormal peroxisomal morphology
Def: Structural anomaly of peroxisomes, which are small, membrane-enclosed metabolic organelles with roles in the metabolism of complex lipids and reactive ionic species.

Name: Absence of peroxisomes
Def: Lack of observable peroxisomes. This feature can be observed by immunohistochemical staining of cultured cells (such as fibroblasts) or by electronmicroscopy.

Name: Paucity of peroxisomes
Def: Reduced number of observable peroxisomes per cell. This feature can be observed by immunohistochemical staining of cultured cells (such as fibroblasts) or by electronmicroscopy.

Name: Reduced sulfide:quinone oxidoreductase activity
Def: Reduced activity of the enzyme sulfide:quinone oxidoreductase, which typically is measured in a biopsy specimen from liver or muscle.

Name: Deficit at segmental level
Def: Refers to distribution of neurological deficits that corresponds to a deficit of a specific spinal segment and all segments below it.

Name: Rhabdoid tumor
Def: Rhabdoid tumors are rare aggressive malignancies in infants and young children with a poor prognosis. The most common anatomic localizations are the central nervous system, the kidneys, and other soft tissues.

Name: Rhabdoid tumor of the ovary
Def: A highly aggressive, extremely rare neoplasm of the ovary that is usually seen in children. The term rhabdoid is used because the tumor cells resemble rhabdomyoblasts but lack myogenic markers.

Name: Cardiac rhabdoid tumor
Def: A rare and aggressive neoplasms developing mainly in the kidney but also in cerebral and extra-cerebral tissues and rarely in the heart. Histologically, rhabdoid renal and extrarenal tumors share common characteristics. The cells are polygonal, with eccentric, vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli, eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions. The tumors have an infiltrative growth pattern, necrosis, and high proliferative index. The immunohistochemistry tools of investigation facilitate differential diagnosis by showing loss of INI-1 expression, usually accompanied by germline mutations of the SMARCB1 gene. When INI-1 is still expressed in the affected tissues, a rhabdoid tumor with SMARCA4 mutations should be considered.

Name: Malignant rhabdoid tumor of the bladder
Def: A rhabdoid tumor (a rare aggressive malignancies in infants and young children with a poor prognosis) originating in the urinary bladder.

Name: Malignant rhabdoid tumor of liver
Def: A malginant rhabdoid tumor (MRT) originating in the liver. MRT are best characterized by the presence of round or polygonal cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, typical eosinophilic perinuclear inclusions, vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli. Immunohistochemical expression of vimentin and epithelial markers and lack of staining for S-100, myoglobin and desmin are commonly found, but are non-specific.

Name: Malignant rhabdoid tumor of muscle
Def: A malginant rhabdoid tumor (MRT) originating in muscle tissue.

Name: Neck teratoma
Def: A teratoma located in the neck.

Name: Kidney teratoma
Def: A teratoma located in a kidney.

Name: Elevated urinary 5-amino-4-imidazolecarboxamide-riboside level
Def: Increased amount of 5-amino-4-imidazolecarboxamide(AICA)-riboside in the urine. AICA-riboside is the dephosphorylated counterpart of AICAR, an intermediate of de novo purine biosynthesis.

Name: Aplasia of posterior communicating artery
Def: A developmental anomnaly characterized by the lack of development of the posterior communicating artery.
Comment: The posterior communicating arteries connect the internal carotid artery just proximal to its bifurcation into the anterior cerebral artery and middle cerebral artery with the posterior cerebral artery. The posterior communicating artery is part of the circle of Willis.
Synonym: Absence of both posterior communicating arteries

Name: Optic pit
Def: A developmental anomaloy characterized by congenital excavation of the optic nerve head.

Name: Ameliorated by naloxone
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with naloxone, an opioid antagonist.

Name: Ameliorated by pyridoxal phosphate
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by ingestion of pyridoxal phosphate (activated vitamin B6).

Name: Thickened intrahepatic portal venules
Def: Increased width of the vascular wall of portal venules within the liver.
Comment: The portal vein (PV) is the main vessel of the portal venous system (PVS), which drains the blood from the gastrointestinal tract, gallbladder, pancreas, and spleen to the liver. Once in the liver, the PV ramifies and reaches the sinusoids, forming portal venules.

Name: Ovarian fibrosis
Def: Excessive proliferation of fibroblasts and deposition of extracellular matrix within the ovary.

Name: Pigment incontinence
Def: A process in which melanosomes (melanin granules) are deposited in the dermis. The dermal melanosomes are observed to be mainly in macrophages. This phenomenon of pigmentary incontinence usually follows an inflammatory process with the basic feature of basal cell damage, such as in lichen planus, lupus erythematosus, Riehl's melanosis, incontinentia pigmenti (Bloch-Sulzberger), and fixed drug eruption. Incontinence of pigment, or dropping off of epidermal melanin into the dermis, frequently produces a clinically recognizable and characteristic slate-gray pigmentation.

Name: Reduced epidermal keratin 10 protein expression
Def: Amount of keratin 10 in the epidermis below the lower limit of normal. The findiong is typically ascertained by immunofluorescent microscopy.
Comment: This feature can be assessed antibody staining of a skin biopsy specimen.

Name: Reduced epidermal collagen IV protein expression
Comment: Lower than normal amount of collagen IV in the epidermis.
Synonym: Skin biopsy: collagen IV antibody staining abnormal or absent

Name: Reduced epidermal bullous pemphigoid antigen 1 protein expression
Def: Lower than normal amount of bullous pemphigoid antigen 1 (BP230) in the epidermis.
Synonym: Skin biopsy: BPAG1-e antibody staining abnormal or absent

Name: Reduced epidermal collagen VII protein expression
Comment: Lower than normal amount of collagen VII in the epidermis.
Synonym: Skin biopsy: collagen VII antibody staining abnormal or absent

Name: Reduced epidermal collagen XVII protein expression
Comment: Lower than normal amount of collagen XVII in the epidermis.
Synonym: Skin biopsy: collagen XVII antibody staining abnormal or absent

Name: Reduced epidermal integrin alpha6beta4 protein expression
Comment: Lower than normal amount of integrin alpha6beta4 in the epidermis.
Synonym: Skin biopsy: integrin alpha6beta4 antibody staining abnormal or absent

Name: Reduced epidermal plectin protein expression
Comment: Lower than normal amount of plectin in the epidermis.
Synonym: Skin biopsy: plectin antibody staining abnormal or absent

Name: Bloodstream Trypanosoma cruzi
Def: Presence of Trypanosoma cruzi in the blood stream. Trypanosoma cruzii is the etiological agent of Chagas disease.
Synonym: Trypanosoma cruzi present on peripheral blood smear

Name: Abnormal lymph node cell composition
Def: A deviation from the normal distribution of cell types or their relative proportions in a lymph node.

Name: Lipid-laden lymph node macrophages
Def: Lymph node with increased numbers of macrophages heavily laden with lipids.

Name: Abnormal pancreatic acinus morphology
Def: Structural anomal of pancreatic acinus.
Comment: The exocrine pancreas is structurally analogous to a bunch of grapes; this architecture contains microscopic, blind-ended tubules that are surrounded by polygonal acinar cells and these tubules are organized into lobules called acini. The primary function of the acini is to synthesize and secrete hydrolytic enzymes which empty into the duodenum for the digestion of our daily foodstuff. Each acinus consists of a small cluster of secretory epithelial cells that form a small central lumen, called intercellular canaliculi. Each acinar cell has a round pyramid-like shape.

Name: Cochlear nerve hypoplasia
Def: A developmental defect characterized by underdevelopment of the cochlear nerve.

Name: Glutathionuria
Def: Level of glutathione in the urine above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Nevus psiloliparus
Def: Nevus psiloliparus is a rare fatty tissue nevus that is a marker for encephalocraniocutaneous lipomatosis, a neurocutaneous syndrome with ocular and central nervous system anomalies. Clinically, nevus psiloliparus is often described as a congenital alopecia and appears as an irregularly shaped, circumscribed area of alopecia on the scalp. Histopathology demonstrates a near-complete absence of mature hair follicles with preservation of arrector pili muscles and mature adipocytes within the dermis.

Name: Crypt hyperplasia
Def: Crypt hyperplasia denotes elongation of the length of the crypts of Lieberkuhn, a process that initially precedes villous atrophy. Elongation may be caused by expansion of the lamina propria as a result of the proliferation of stromal cells, an influx of inflammatory cells and tissue remodeling.

Name: Increased circulating dehydroepiandrosterone-sulfate concentration
Def: Concentration of dehydroepiandrosterone-sulfate in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
Comment: Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) is produced in the adrenal glands and to a lesser extent by the ovaries and testes. DHEA is metabolized into DHEA-S in the adrenal glands and liver. Dehydroepiandrosterone-sulfate is a precursor of testosterone and estrogen.

Name: Abnormal circulating thyroxine-binding globulin concentration
Def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG) in the blood circulation.

Name: Decreased circulating thyroxine-binding globulin concentration
Def: A reduction from the normal concentration of thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG) in the blood circulation.

Name: Elevated circulating beta-aminoisobutyric acid concentration
Def: An increased concentration of beta-aminoisobutyric acid in the blood circulation.

Name: Elevated circulating dihydrouracil concentration
Def: An increased concentration of dihydrouracil in the blood circulation. Dihydrouracil is an intermediate in the catabolism of uracil that is also known as 5,6-dihydrouracil.

Name: Elevated circulating dihydrothymine concentration
Def: An increased concentration of dihydrothymine in the blood circulation. Dihydrouracil is an intermediate in the catabolism of thymine.

Name: Elevated circulating N-carbamoyl-beta-alanine concentration
Def: An increased concentrationof N-carbamoyl-beta-alanine in the blood circulation.
Comment: Elevated 3-ureidopropionic acid

Name: Elevated ciculating 5-hydroxymethyluracil concentration
Def: An increased concentration of 5-hydroxymethyluracil in the blood circulation.

Name: Decreased CSF creatinine concentration
Def: Concentration of creatinine in the cerebrrospinal fluid below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urinary creatine level
Def: An increased amount of creatine in the urine.

Name: Decreased circulating biotin concentration
Def: Concentration of biotin in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating thrombopoietin concentration
Def: Concentration of thrombopoietin in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. Thrombopoietin is a glycoprotein hormone produced by the liver and kidney that stimulates the production and differentiation of megakaryocytes.

Name: Decreased circulating C1q concentration
Def: Concentration or activity of the C1q protein in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal. C1q is the first component of the classical pathway and is composed of the C1qA chain, C1qB chain, and C1qC chain, which are encoded by C1qA, C1qB, and C1qC genes.

Name: Decreased circulating apolipoprotein A-II concentration
Def: Concentration of apolipoprotein A-II below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating CA19-9 concentration
Def: Concentration of CA19-9 above the upper limit of normal.
Comment: CA19-9 (carbohydrate antigen 19-9, also called cancer antigen 19-9 or sialylated Lewis a antigen) is the most commonly used and best validated serum tumor marker for pancreatic cancer diagnosis in symptomatic patients and for monitoring therapy in patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
Synonym: Elevated circulating sialylated Lewis a antigen concentration

Name: Elevated circulating DOPA concentration
Def: Concentration of DOPA (3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine) in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated CSF DOPA concentration
Def: Concentration of DOPA (3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine) in the cerebrospinal fluid above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating porphyrin concentration
Def: Concentration of porphyrins or of a specific porphryin above the upper limit of normal. The most commonly tested circulating porphyrins are coproporphyrin, protoporphyrin, and uroporphyrin. Normally protoporphyrin is present in the highest concentration.

Name: Decreased circulating 17-hydroxyprogesterone concentration
Def: Concentration of 17-hydroxyprogesterone in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Decreased circulating transcobalamin II concentration
Def: Concentration of transcobalamin II in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Polychromasia
Def: Increased variation in the color of the erythrocytes (red blood cells), including pale red, normal or dark colors, indicating a highly variable hemoglobin concentration. Typically this indicates the release of immature erythrocytes in states of anemia.

Name: Decreased circulating myo-inositol concentration
Def: Concentration of myo-inositol in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating arabinitol concentration
Def: Concentration of arabinitol in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine arabitol level
Def: Amount of arabitol in the urine above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine erythritol level
Def: Amount of erythritol in the urine above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating erythritol concentration
Def: Concentration of erythritol in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Reduced circulating matrix metalloproteinase 2 concentration
Def: Concentration of matrix metalloproteinase 2 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Abnormal circulating coenzyme concentration
Def: Concentration of a coenzyme (an organic molecule that binds to the active sites of an enzyme to promote the catalysis of a reaction) is above or below the limits of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating S-adenosyl methionine concentration
Def: Concentration of S-adenosyl methionine (SAM) in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. SAM is a cosubstrate involved in methyl group transfers, transsulfuration, and aminopropylation.

Name: Abnormal circulating membrane cofactor protein concentration
Def: Concentration of membrane cofactor protein in the blood circulation outside the limits of normal. Membrane cofactor protein (MCP, CD46) is a cell surface complement regulatory protein which acts as a cofactor for the factor I-mediated cleavage of the activated complement components C3b/C4b.

Name: Decreased circulating membrane cofactor protein concentration
Def: Concentration of membrane cofactor protein in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
Synonym: MCP (membrane cofactor protein) low in blood

Name: Elevated circulating membrane cofactor protein concentration
Def: Concentration of membrane cofactor protein in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Hepatic xanthomatosis
Def: Lipid deposits localized within the liver. Xanthomas are benign but are often an important visible sign of systemic conditions such as familial hypercholesterolemia.

Name: Adrenal xanthomatosis
Def: Lipid deposits localized within the adrenal gland. Xanthomas are benign but are often an important visible sign of systemic conditions such as familial hypercholesterolemia.

Name: Splenic xanthomatosis
Def: Lipid deposits localized within the spleen. Xanthomas are benign but are often an important visible sign of systemic conditions such as familial hypercholesterolemia.

Name: Spinal cord xanthomatosis
Def: Lipid deposits localized within the spinal cord. Xanthomas are benign but are often an important visible sign of systemic conditions such as familial hypercholesterolemia.

Name: Brain xanthomatosis
Def: Lipid deposits localized within the brain. Xanthomas are benign but are often an important visible sign of systemic conditions such as familial hypercholesterolemia.

Name: Pulmonary xanthomatosis
Def: Lipid deposits localized within the lung. Xanthomas are benign but are often an important visible sign of systemic conditions such as familial hypercholesterolemia.

Name: Bone marrow xanthomatosis
Def: Lipid deposits localized within the bone marrow. Xanthomas are benign but are often an important visible sign of systemic conditions such as familial hypercholesterolemia.

Name: Lymph node xanthomatosis
Def: Lipid deposits localized within one or more lymph nodes. Xanthomas are benign but are often an important visible sign of systemic conditions such as familial hypercholesterolemia.

Name: Xanthoma of bone
Def: Xanthoma of bone is an exceedingly rare benign primary bone tumor histologically characterized by mononuclear macrophage-like cells, abundant foam cells, and multinucleated giant cells.
Comment: Because of the aggressive radiographic appearance of bone xanthoma, other primary bone tumors and metastatic lesions need to be ruled out.

Name: Ameliorated by folinic acid
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with folinic acid.

Name: Triggered by succinylcholine anesthetic
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to a succinylcholine anesthetic such as suxamethonium.

Name: Exogenous androgen exposure
Def: History of having been treated with an exogenous androgen medication.

Name: Reduced muscle enolase activity
Def: Diminished activity of the enzyme enolase in muscle tissue. The enzyme enolase catalyzes the interconversion of 2-phosphoglycerate and phosphoenolpyruvate. In adult human muscle, over 90% of enolase activity is accounted for by the beta-enolase subunit, the protein product of the ENO3 gene.

Name: Dopamine antagonist exposure
Def: History of having been treated with a dopamine antagonist including metaclopramide, phenothiazine; haloperidol, chlorpromazine, promethazine, prochlorperazine, ziprasidone, and quetiapine.

Name: Muscle fiber granulofilamentous inclusion bodies
Def: The presence of inclusion bodies within the cytoplasm of muscle cells that contain a mxiture of granules and filaments.
Comment: See Figure 7B of PMID:19181099.

Name: Bone marrow myeloid vacuolization
Def: Formation of vacuoles (a space within a cell that is empty of cytoplasm, lined with a membrane, and filled with fluid) in the cytoplasm of myeloid precursors in the bone marrow.
Comment: See Figure 1 of PMID:33690844.
Synonym: Vacuolization of bone marrow myeloid precursors

Name: Pulmonary cylindroma
Def: A cylindroma located in the lung. Cylindromas are well-circumscribed, smooth, pale pink nodular tumors, often with arborizing vessels visible. The tumors are slow growing and vary in size from a few millimeters to over 5 mm.
Comment: See Figure 1 of PMID:29569226.

Name: Colonic fibrinopurulent exudate
Def: Fluid visible on the colonic surface containing fibrin, inflammatory cells, and cellular debris.

Name: Bloodstream microfilaria
Def: Presence of filaria in the blood stream. Filariasis is a common cause of elephantiasis in Coastal Districts of India. The initial manifestations are repeated episodes of fever with chills and rigor, lymphadenopathy which gradually progress to elephantiasis. In India filarial infestation is commonly caused by W. bancrofti and Brugia malayi, the former responsible for almost 98 percent of all cases.
Comment: Filariasis is an infectious parasitic disease caused by roundworms that belong to the family Filarioidea. These are spread by bloodfeeding insects such as black flies and mosquitoes. Eight known filarial nematodes use humans as their definitive hosts. See Figure 1 of PMID:32313484.

Name: Skin infectious agent
Def: The presence of an infectious agent in the skin.

Name: Dermal microfilaria
Def: Presence of filariae in the skin.

Name: Dermal papillary IgA deposition
Def: Accumulation of immunoglobulin A (IgA) surrounding dermal papillae, which are specialized cells that support the hair follicle.
Synonym: Granular IgA deposits at the dermal papillae

Name: Dermal immune complex deposition
Def: Accumulation of antigen-bound antibody in the skin.

Name: Abnormal liver metabolite concentration
Def: The concentration of a metabolite in the liver is above or below the limits of normal.

Name: Hepatic polyglucosan accumulation
Def: Intracellular accumulation of polyglucosan bodies-containing amylopectinlike polysaccharide-in the liver.
Synonym: Accumulation of polyglucosan bodies in the liver

Name: Urinary bladder neurofibroma
Def: A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) located in the urinary bladder.

Name: Synovial granuloma
Def: An aggregation of macrophages (forming in response to chronic inflammation) localized in the lining of a joint (synovium).

Name: Elevated urine fumaric acid level
Def: The concentration of fumaric acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine N-acetylaspartic acid level
Def: The amount of N-acetylaspartate in the urine, when corrected for urine concentration, is above upper limit of normal. This feature can be measured using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry.
Comment: Although NAA concentration is also elevated in the blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of children with neonatal/infantile (severe) Canavan disease, elevated concentration of NAA in urine is sufficient for diagnosis of affected individuals.

Name: Elevated urine suberylglycine level
Def: Level of suberylglycine in urine above upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine phenylpropionylglycine level
Def: Level of phenylpropionylglycine in urine above upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine octenedioic acid level
Def: The concentration of octenedioic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Monocarboxylic aciduria
Def: Level of a monocarboxylic acid in the urine above the upper limit of normal. A monocarboxylic acid is an oxoacid containing one carboxy group.

Name: Elevated urine octanoic acid level
Def: Amount of octanoic acid in the urine above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine glutaconic acid level
Def: The concentration of glutaconic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine 3-hydroxyglutaric level
Def: The concentration of 3-hydroxyglutaric acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine malonic acid level
Def: The concentration of malonic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine propionylglycine level
Def: Amount of propionylglycine in the urine above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine tiglylglycine level
Def: Amount of tiglylglycine in the urine above upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine 2-methylacetoacetic acid level
Def: Amount of 2-methylacetoacetic acid in the urine above upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine 3-hydroxypropionic acid level
Def: Amount of 3-hydroxypropionic acid in the urine above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine 2-methylcitric acid level
Def: Amount of 2-methylcitric acid in the urine above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine 4-hydroxyisovaleric acid level
Def: Amount of 4-hydroxyisovaleric acid in urine above upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine 2-hydroxy-3-methylvaleric acid level
Def: Amount of 2-hydroxy-3-methylvaleric acid in the urine above the upper limit of normal. 2-Hydroxy-3-methylpentanoic acid or 2-hydroxy-3-methylvaleric acid (HMVA) is an organic acid generated by L-isoleucine metabolism.
Comment: 2-hydroxy-3-methylvaleric acid is elevated in individuals with mapel syrup urine disease.

Name: Shoulder contracture
Def: Lack of full passive range of motion (restrictions in flexion, extension, or other movements) of the shoulder joint resulting from structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and/or skin.

Name: Shoulder extension contracture
Def: Lack of the full expected passive range of flexion of the shoulder joint (Shoulder flexion puts the arms from a resting position at one's sides to straight above the head; thus, with shoulder extension contracture it is not possible to raise the arms above the head fully).

Name: Thumb extension contracture
Def: Movement in the sagittal plane that increases the angle of the thumb joint (straightens the joint); motion involving posterior bending of the vertebral column or returning to the upright position from a flexed position.

Name: Tongue myxoma
Def: A myxoma (benign soft tissue neoplasm characterized by the presence of spindle and stellate cells, lobulated growth pattern, and myxoid stroma formation) localized in the tongue.

Name: Abnormal knee morphology
Def: A structural abnormality of the knee joint or surrounding structures.

Name: Abnormal knee physiology
Def: A functional anomaly of the knee joint.

Name: Knee contracture
Def: Lack of full passive range of motion (restrictions in flexion, extension, or other movements) of the knee joint resulting from structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and/or skin.

Name: Knee extension contracture
Def: A type of knee joint contracture in which the knee lacks full expected flexion, such that the upper and lower leg cannot be brought together.

Name: Abnormal ankle morphology
Def: A structural anomaly of the ankle.

Name: Abnormal ankle physiology
Def: A functional anomaly of the ankle.

Name: Toe joint contracture
Def: Lack of full passive range of motion (restrictions in flexion, extension, or other movements) of a toe joint resulting from structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and/or skin.

Name: Extension contracture of toe
Def: A type of toe joint contracture in which the joint lacks full expected flexion, so that the two bony segments on either side of their connecting joint cannot be brought together.

Name: Finger joint contracture
Def: Lack of full passive range of motion (restrictions in flexion, extension, or other movements) of a finger joint resulting from structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and/or skin.

Name: Extension contracture of finger
Def: A type of finger joint contracture in which the joint lacks full expected flexion, so that the two bony segments on either side of their connecting joint cannot be brought together.

Name: Reduced muscle telethonin level
Def: Amount of telethonin protein expression in muscle tissue below lower limit of normal. Telethonin is a 19-kDa sarcomeric protein, localized to the Z-disc of skeletal and cardiac muscles.
Synonym: Muscle biopsy: telethonin low or absent

Name: Abnormal enzyme concentration or activity
Def: Concentration or activity of an enzyme is above or below the limits of normal.

Name: Abnormal liver enzyme activity or concentration
Def: Concentration or activity of an enzyme is above or below the limits of normal in liver tissue.
Synonym: Abnormal hepatic enzyme activity or concentration

Name: Reduced hepatic urocanase activity
Def: Activity of urocanase in the liver below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Impaired cerebroside sulfate hydrolysis
Def: Reduced hydrolysis (splitting of a bond and the addition of the hydrogen anion of water) of the sulfuric ester linkage in the molecule of cerebroside sulfate, possibly leading to accumuation of cerebroside sulfate.
Comment: This feature can be assayed by cerebroside sulfate loading tests of cultured dermal fibroblasts.

Name: Reduced peroxisomal glutaryl-CoA oxidase activity
Def: Diminished enzyme activity of peroxisomal glutaryl-CoA oxidase, an enzyme that metabolizes glutaryl-CoA (a metabolite of L-lysine, L-hydroxy-lysine and L-tryptophan) by dehydrogenation to glutaconyl-CoA directly followed by decarboxylation of this to crotonyl-CoA.

Name: Reduced sterol 27-hydroxylase activity
Def: Diminished activity of the enzyme sterol 27-hydroxylase, which participates in the degradation of cholesterol to bile acid.
