Sterol 27-hydroxylase catalyzes the first step in the normal oxidation of the steroid side chain, converting cholesterol, as well as different 7a-hydroxylated cholesterol metabolites, to 27-oxygenated steroids.

Name: Reduced short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity
Def: Diminished activity of the enzyme Short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (SCAD), a key enzyme of fatty acid beta-oxidation that catalyzes the first step in mitochondrial beta-oxidation of fatty acids.

Name: Reduced 3-phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase activity
Def: Diminished activity of the enzyme 3-phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PGDH), which catalyzes the first step in the pathway by converting D-3-phosphoglycerate (PGA), an intermediate in glycolysis, to phosphohydroxypyruvate concomitant with the reduction of NAD+.

Name: Elongated mitochondria
Def: Increase in length of mitochondria.
Comment: Mitochondrial elongation can be initiated by a gradual merge of the outer mitochondrial membranes of two individual mitochondria.

Name: Reduced hepatic methionine adenosyltransferase activity
Def: Activity of methionine adenosyltransferase in the liver below the lower limit of normal. Note that there are multiple methionine adenosyltransferase isoezymes.

Name: Substantia nigra dopaminergic neuron loss
Def: Degeneration and loss of neurons in the substantia nigra of the brain.
Comment: Ppigmented neurons in the substantia nigra produce the neurotransmitter dopamine. The loss of these neurons leads to the classical motor symptoms of Parkinson disease. The pigment contained within these neurons, termed neuromelanin because of its similar appearance to cutaneous melanin, is so abundant in the substantia nigra of the human brain that this structure can be seen macroscopically as a darkened area (hence the origin of the name given to this brain region)

Name: Intramuscular lipoma
Def: A lipoma that is located within a muscle.

Name: Cutaneous telangiectasia
Def: Dilated blood vessels on the skin.

Name: Abnormal aromatase activity
Def: Aromatase activity outside of the normal range.
Comment: Aromatase is a specific component of the cytochrome P450 enzyme system responsible for the transformation of androgen precursors into estrogens. This enzyme is encoded by the CYP19A1 gene located at chromosome 15q21.2, that is, expressed in ovary and testis, but also in many extraglandular sites such as the placenta, brain, adipose tissue, and bone. {xref="PMID:21772971"}

Name: Elevated aromatase activity
Def: Enzyme activity of aromatase above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Reduced aromatase activity
Def: Enzyme activity of aromatase below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Corneal amyloidosis
Def: A form of amyloidosis that is located in the cornea.

Name: Abnormal keratinocyte morphology
Def: Any structural anomaly of the keratinocyte. The keratinocyte is the major cell type of the epidermis and is responsible for generating the protective barrier.

Name: Keratinocyte vacuolization
Def: Increased number of vacuoles (membrane-bound organelles that areempty of cytoplasm, lined with a membrane, and filled with fluid) in keratinocytes.

Name: Parotid gland adenocarcinoma
Def: An adenocarcinoma that arises from the parotid gland.

Name: Pulmonary vasculitis
Def: Cellular inflammation, vessel destruction, and tissue necrosis of the blood vessels of the lung.

Name: Reduced hepatic D-glycerate kinase activity
Def: Activity of D-glycerate kinase in the liver below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Lymph-node hemophagocytosis
Def: Phagocytosis of erythrocytes, lymphocytes or other hematopoietic precursors by histiocytes or macrophages in a lymph node.
Comment: See Figure 1 of PMID:16859547.

Name: Superior pubic ramus hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the upper branch of the pubis bone (inferior pubic ramus).

Name: Uterine adenofibroma
Def: A rare benign mullerian mixed tumor of the uterus composed of benign epithelial and mesenchymal components.

Name: Pulmonary hamartoma
Def: A benign malformation of the lung that includes an abnormal mixture of tissue components such as cartilage, epithelium, fat, or muscle which are common to the lung but without preservation of the organ architecture.

Name: Peripheral axonal distension
Def: An abnormal histological finding characterized by an increase in the cross-section area of peripheral nerve axons (up to 20-25 micrometers in diameter).
Comment: In giant axonal neuropathy, distended axons are observed in conjunction with thin myelin sheaths. Distended axons may be filled with masses of neurofilaments. See Figures 4 and 5 of PMID:15897506.

Name: Decreased circulating alpha-mannosidase activity
Def: Concentration or activity of alpha mannosidase below the lower limit of normal in the blood circulation.

Name: Abnormal hepatocyte morphology
Def: A structural anomaly of the hepatocyte, which is the main cell type that makes up the liver perncyhma. Hepatocytes are usually binucleated and appear as sheets in the liver tissue.

Name: Hepatic melanin-like lysosomal pigmentation
Def: Accumulation of dark, coarsely granular pigment localized in lysosomes of centrilobular hepatocytes.

Name: Reduced uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase activity
Def: Activity of the enzyme uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase (UROD; EC 4.1.1.37) below the lower limit of normal.
Comment: Uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase low

Name: Reduced heme oxygenase activity
Def: Activity of the enzyme heme oxygenase below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Swollen achromatic neurons in the cerebral cortex
Def: The presence of enlarged and swollen neurons that lack Nissl bodies (the rough endoplasmic reticulum-achromasia refers to neurons that lack Nissl bodies) in the cortex of the brain.

Name: Vacuolated hepatocytes
Def: Presence of vacuoles (membrane-bound organelles that areempty of cytoplasm, lined with a membrane, and filled with fluid) in hepatocytes, which normally rarely contain vacuoles.

Name: Lack of oocyte pronucleus formation
Def: An abnormality of oocyte maturation characterized by the inability of oocytes to form pronuclei after in vitro fertilization procedures. Oocytes normally show two pronuclei 17 to 20 hours after in vitro insemination.

Name: Self-healing squamous epithelioma
Def: A type of skin tumor that initially presents as a reddish macule and subsequently becomes papular, enlarged, ulcerated and ultimately heals leaving pitted scars.
Comment: Individuals with pathogenic variants in TGFBR1 may present with multiple self-healing squamous epitheliomas. See Figure 1 of PMID:33256177.

Name: Elevated circulating pristanic acid concentration
Def: Concentration of pristanic acid in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Sarcoplasmic bodies
Def: Rounded or oval structures that appeared brown on hematoxylin and eosin and red on the modified Gomori trichrome stain.
Comment: The sarcoplasm is the cytoplasm of a muscle cell.

Name: Elevated CSF hydroxyproline concentration
Comment: Concentration of hydroxyproline in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Reduced CSF cystine concentration
Def: Concentration of cystine in the cerebrospinal fluid below the lower limit of normal. Cystine is sulfur-containing amino acid obtained by the oxidation of two cysteine molecules which are then linked via a disulfide bond.

Name: Abnormal circulating beta-mannosidase activity
Def: Activity of the enzyme beta-mannosidase outside normal limits. Beta-mannosidase is a lysosomal enzyme that catabolizes oligosaccharides.

Name: Elevated circulating beta-mannosidase activity
Def: Activity of the enzyme beta-mannosidase above the upper limit of normal. Beta-mannosidase is a lysosomal enzyme that catabolizes oligosaccharides.

Name: Reduced circulating alpha-L-fucosidase activity
Def: Activity of the enzyme alpha-L-fucosidase below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Abnormal circulating alpha-L-fucosidase activity
Def: Activity of the enzyme alpha-L-fucosidase in the blood circulation outside the limits of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating alpha-L-fucosidase activity
Def: Activity of the enzyme alpha-L-fucosidase above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine concentration
Def: Increased concentration of S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine in the blood circulation.

Name: Elevated circulating S-adenosyl-L-methionine concentration
Def: Concentration S-adenosyl-L-methionine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Exercise-triggered malignant hyperthermia
Def: Malignant hyperthermia that is characterized by exercise-induced life-threatening hyperthermia with a body temperature over 40 degrees C and signs of encephalopathy ranging from confusion to convulsions or coma. Incidence increases with rising ambient temperature and relative humidity. Manifestations may include rhabdomyolysis (presenting with myalgia, muscle weakness, and myoglobinuria), tachycardia, and in severe cases multiorgan failure.

Name: Anesthesic-triggered malignant hyperthermia
Def: Malignant hyperthermia that is characterized by a rapid increase in temperature to 39-42 degrees C in response to inhalational anesthetics such as halothane or to muscle relaxants such as succinylcholine.

Name: Elevated CSF argininosuccinic acid concentration
Def: Concentration of argininosuccinic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated CSF aspartylglucosamine concentration
Def: Concentration of aspartylglucosamine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) above the upper limit of normal.
Comment: Aspartylglucosamine is a derivative of aspartic acid.

Name: Elevated circulating alpha-oxoadipic acid concentration
Def: Concentration of alpha-oxoadipic acid in the blood above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Abnormal erythrocyte metabolite concentration
Def: A deviation from the normal range of a metabolite in red blood cells.

Name: Reduced erythrocyte glutathione concentration
Def: Concentration of glutathione in red blood cells below the lower limit of normal. Glutathione (GSH) is an important redox active biomolecule critical in the maintenance and regulation of cellular and organismal health.

Name: Elevated CSF sarcosine concentration
Def: Concentration of sarcosine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Reduced CSF methionine concentration
Def: Concentration of methionine in the cerebrospinal fluid below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating homoarginine concentration
Def: Concentration of homoarginine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urinary formiminoglutamic acid level
Def: The concentration of formiminoglutamic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated CSF proline concentration
Def: Concentration of proline in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urinary S-sulfocysteine level
Def: Level of S-sulfocysteine high in urine above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating S-sulfocysteine concentration
Def: Concentration of S-sulfocysteine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Sertoli cell hyperplasia
Def: Abnormal increase in the number of Sertoli cells in the testis.
Comment: Sertoli cells are present in the seminiferous tubules of the testes, comprising one of the two types of cells in the germinal epithelium, the other being of spermatogonia lineage. Sertoli cells are one of the most important cells necessary for sperm production in males. They are often identifiable as big, tightly linked cells near the basolateral portion of the seminiferous tubule.

Name: CSF infectious agent
Def: The presence of an infectious agent in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

Name: CSF mycobacteria
Def: Mycobacterium present in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). This feature can be ascertained by CSF microscopy.

Name: Fungal bloodstream infection
Def: Detection of a fungal organism (such as candida or coccidioides) in the blood stream.

Name: Supraclavicular lymphadenopathy
Def: Enlarged lymph node located just above the clavicle (collarbone).

Name: Inguinal lymphadenopathy
Def: Enlarged lymph node located in the inguinal region (groin).

Name: Axillary lymphadenopathy
Def: Enlarged lymph node located in the axillary region (armpit).

Name: Positive Murphy sign
Def: Murphy's sign is elicited in patients with acute cholecystitis by asking the patient to take in and hold a deep breath while palpating the subcostal region. In practice, Murphy's sign is performed by palpating the subcostal region during inspiration. If pain is elicited and the patient suddenly stops their inspiratory effort, a positive Murphy's sign has been elicited.

Name: Bilious emesis
Def: Vomiting whereby the vomit has the color of bile, yellowish-green.

Name: Ameliorated by NSAID
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID).

Name: Fetal exposure history
Def: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to a medication or other substance.

Name: Fetal barbiturate exposure
Def: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to barbiturate medications such as phenobarbital. Barbiturates are used medically as anxiolytics, hypnotics, and anticonvulsants.

Name: Fetal narcotic exposure
Def: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to narcotic medications such as morphine or codeine. Narcotics are used medically to treat moderate or severe pain.

Name: Ameliorated by ethosuximide
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by administration of ethosuximide. Ethosuximide is most often used to treat absence seizures.

Name: Reduced epidermal extracellular matrix protein 1 protein expression
Def: Lower than normal amount of extracellular matrix protein 1 (ECM1) in the epidermis.

Name: Neurofibroma by anatomical location
Def: Neurofibroma categorized according to the anatomical site of origin.

Name: Tongue neurofibroma
Def: A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) localized in the tongue.

Name: Cardiac neurofibroma
Def: A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) localized in the heart.

Name: Gastric neurofibroma
Def: A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) localized in the stomach.

Name: Renal neurofibroma
Def: A neurofibroma (benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor) localized in the kidney.

Name: Muscle fiber polyglucosan inclusion bodies
Def: Accumulation of a poorly branched and poorly spherical amylopectin-like glycogen (polyglucosan) in muscle fibers.

Name: Abnormal rete ridge morphology
Def: Abnormal structure of the rete ridges (also known as rete pegs), which are downward projections of epithelium surrounding the connective tissue papillae in between the dermal papillae.

Name: Rete ridge elongation
Def: Increased length of the rete rdiges of the epidermis.

Name: Pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis
Def: Accumulation of monoclonal CD1a-positive Langerhans cells in the bronchioles and alveolar interstitium that can cause damage to the lungs.

Name: Lumbar hypolordosis
Def: Flattening of a curve in the spine in the lumbar (lower back) region.

Name: Battle sign
Def: Battle sign is bruising over the mastoid process that is typically the result of head trauma. It is retroauricular or mastoid ecchymosis that is typically the result of head trauma. Battle sign typically requires significant head trauma and may indicate significant internal injury to the brain and not just the posterior cranial vault or mastoid.

Name: Decreased skull base length
Def: Reduced anterioposterior dimension of the skull base.

Name: Oscillopsia
Def: A visual disturbance in which objects in the visual field appear to oscillate (jump, jiggle, vibrate).
Comment: Oscillopsia most often results from abnormal eye movements or from impaired vestibulo-ocular reflex.

Name: Decreased blink rate
Def: The frequency with which the eye is blinked is below the lower limit of normal.
Comment: A reduced blink rate may be observed in Parkinson's disease.

Name: Abnormal blink rate
Def: A deviation from the normal frequency of blinking the eye.

Name: Elevated blink rate
Def: The frequecy with which the eye is blinked is above the upper limit of normal.
Comment: An increased blink rate in can be observed in schizophrenia, tardive dyskinesia, Tourette's syndrome and Meige's disease.

Name: Purulent sputum
Def: Sputum contains pus.

Name: Maternal hyperthyroidism
Def: The mother of a fetus or index patient has a history of hyperthyroidism during the corresponding pregnancy.

Name: Perineal
Def: Applies to an abnormality that affects the perineum (the region of skin between the genitals and the anus).

Name: Gadolinium exposure
Def: History of exposure to gadolinium, a contrast medium often used for magnetic resonance imaging.

Name: Purulent parotid gland drainage
Def: Excretion of pus (purulent discharge) from the opening of the parotid duct.
Comment: See Figure 2 of PMID:34952006.

Name: Obstipation
Def: Obstipation is the inability to pass either stool or flatus (gas).
Comment: Obstipation can be a sign of an acute obstruction of the GI tract, either of the small or large bowel.

Name: Posttussive emesis
Def: Vomiting following a coughing spell.
Comment: Individuals with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) will frequently vomit when coughing for a non-GI reason. Vomiting occurs during these coughing spells because the intrabdominal pressure is high from the coughing and the propensity to reflux results in stomach contents emerging as vomit. This is a historical question that allows a parent to impart information suggesting GERD at an age when it is difficult to obtain a reliable GERD history from the child.

Name: Vasculitis by anatomical site
Def: Vasculitis categorized according to the anatomical site where the finding is localized.

Name: Vasculitis by histology
Def: Vasculitis categorized according to type of histological abnormality.

Name: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
Def: A type of vasculitis characterized by the presence of debris of neutrophils within the blood vessel walls.

Name: Accumulation of lipid droplets in small-bowel enterocytes
Comment: The finding can be observed by strong brown cytoplasmic peroxidase staining of enterozytes in a biopsy specimen. See Figure 2 of PMID: 2426307.

Name: Pericardial friction rub
Def: A pericardial friction rub is a grating, to-and-fro sound that occurs in phase with the heart sounds.
Comment: Pericardial friction rubs can be differentiated from pleural friction rubs because they occur independently of breathing. A pericardial rub is highly specific for acute pericarditis. It is generally heard over the left sternal border, it is often louder at inspiration but sometimes can be better heard on forced expiration while the patient bends forward. In most cases, the rub is triphasic (audible in atrial, ventricular systole, and ventricular diastole phases) and is of high frequency.

Name: Abnormal muscle succinate dehydrogenase staining
Def: Any deviation from the normal amount of staining of succinate dehydrogenase in skeletal muscle tissue.
Comment: Succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) is a mitochondrial enzyme complex located in the inner mitochondrial membrane that has dual roles in the oxidation of succinate to fumarate in the Krebs cycle and in electron transport during oxidative phosphorylation.

Name: Increased muscle succinate dehydrogenase staining
Comment: Staining of succinate dehydrogenase in skeletal muscle tissue above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Decreased muscle succinate dehydrogenase staining
Comment: Staining of succinate dehydrogenase in skeletal muscle tissue below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Small intestinal hamartoma
Def: A benign (noncancerous) tumorlike malformation made up of an abnormal mixture of cells and tissues that originates in the small intestine.

Name: Pyriform sperm head
Def: Pyriform spermatozoa consist of a normally shaped acrosomal structure which can be normal in size or enlarged, while the post-acrosomal region shows severe elongation and an acute narrowing to the posterior end, ending in about the same thickness as the connecting mid-piece.

Name: Excess residual spermatozoal cytoplasm
Def: Excess residual cytoplasm is associated with abnormal spermatozoa produced from a defective spermiation process. This abnormal excess cytoplasm should not be confused with more physiological cytoplasmic residues that can be observed in direct microscopy of the ejaculate but not in dried, fixed and stained morphology smears.

Name: Cardiomyocyte hyaline bodies
Def: Subsarcolemmal, eosinophilic glass-like regions within the cytoplasm of cardiomyocytes.

Name: Hepatic hemophagocytosis
Def: Phagocytosis of erythrocytes, lymphocytes or other hematopoietic precursors by histiocytes or macrophages observed in the liver.

Name: CSF hemophagocytosis
Def: Phagocytosis of erythrocytes, lymphocytes or other hematopoietic precursors by histiocytes or macrophages observed in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

Name: Splenic hemophagocytosis
Def: Phagocytosis of erythrocytes, lymphocytes or other hematopoietic precursors by histiocytes or macrophages observed in the spleen.

Name: Urinary bladder granulomatosis
Def: The presence of multiple granulomas in the urinary bladder as based on pathological examination. Granulomas are small 0.5 to 2 mm collections of modified macrophages called epithelioid cells usually surrounded by lymphocytes.

Name: Epidermal necrosis
Def: Death of keratinocytes in the epidermis layer of the skin, which generally manifests as extensive exfoliation (separation of the epidermis from the underlying dermis).

Name: Exacerbated by flexion
Def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is aggravated by (or made more painful by) bending of a limb or joint.

Name: Hemolacria
Def: The presence of blood in tears.

Name: Corneal foreign body sensation
Def: A perception that an object is in contact with the eye.
Synonym: Foreign body sensation in the eye

Name: Buttock pain
Def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the buttock (round fleshy area at the lower rear area of a human trunk).

Name: Vaginal foreign body sensation
Def: A perception that an object located in the vagina.

Name: Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea
Def: Attacks of breathlessness that occur at night and may awaken the sleeping patient.

Name: Eyelid pain
Def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the eyelid.

Name: Abnormal sperm physiology
Def: Abnormality of a sperm function including protection of paternal DNA, traversing the female reproductive tract, oocyte localisation, penetration of the zona pellucida, oocyte activation and centriole deposition.

Name: Small acrosomal area
Def: Reduction in size of the acrosome below the lower limit of normal. The acrosome is a unique membranous organelle located over the anterior part of the sperm nucleus. According to the World Health Organization criteria, the acrosome must be clearly visible, comprising approximately 40-70 percent of the sperm head.

Name: Bent sperm flagella
Def: The proportion of sperm cells whose flagella is sharply curved or has a sharp angle is above normal limits.

Name: Spermiation failure
Def: Spermiation failure is indicated by apparently normal spermiogenesis, but the presence of retained Sd2 spermatids in stages III-V of human spermatogenesis, whereas maturation arrest is indicated by a lack of late Sd1 and Sd2 spermatids in the epithelium.
Comment: It is important to note that multiple spermatogenic abnormalities often occur simultaneously in infertile men, and the helical nature of human spermatogenesis can make it difficult to readily discriminate multiple abnormalities of spermatid development and release.

Name: Hypospermatogenesis
Def: A morphological abnormality visible upon biopsy of the germinal epithelium of the testis in which the cellularity of the germinal epithelium is reduced in general, so that all stages of germ cells (spermatogonia, spermatocytes, and spermatids) are present but reduced in number. This term applies to biopsies with some tubules showing diminished amounts of qualitatively complete spermatogenesis in combination with a vast majority of tubules that lack germ cells.

Name: Conjunctival membrane
Def: Formation of a sheet of tissue by coagulum of exudate over the conjunctiva of the eye that if removed leaves behind a denuded bleeding surface.

Name: Extreme oligozoospermia
Def: A type of oligozoospermia characterized by a total number of more than zero but less than 2 million sperm in the ejaculate or a concentration of more than zero but less than one million sperm per milliliter.

Name: Mild oligozoospermia
Def: A type of oligozoospermia characterized by a total number of more than 30 but less than 39 million sperm in the ejaculate or a concentration of more than 10 but less than 15 million sperm per milliliter.

Name: Moderate oligozoospermia
Def: A type of oligozoospermia characterized by a total number of more than 10 but less than 29 million sperm in the ejaculate or a concentration of more than 5 but less than 10 million sperm per milliliter.

Name: Severe oligozoospermia
Def: A type of oligozoospermia characterized by a total number of more than 2 but less than 10 million sperm in the ejaculate or a concentration of more than 1 but less than 5 million sperm per milliliter.

Name: Iris nodule
Def: The presence of a nodule (small rounded lump of tissue) in the iris.

Name: Koeppe nodules
Def: A type of iris nodule consisting of inflammatory cell precipitates which lie at the pupillary margin.
Comment: Koeppe nodules can be observed in non-granulomaous and granulomatous uveitis.

Name: Bussaca nodules
Def: A type of iris nodule consisting of inflammatory cell precipitates which lie on the iris surface.
Comment: Bussace nodules are considered pathognomonic for granulomatous uveitis.

Name: Decreased CSF copper concentration
Def: Concentration of copper in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Diffuse pulmonary lymphoid hyperplasia
Def: Diffuse lymphoid hyperplasia (DLH) describes the pathological entity that lies between follicular bronchiolitis and lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia (LIP). It is pathologically characterized by a diffuse peribronchiolar proliferation of hyperplastic lymphoid follicles (BALT), extended along the lymphatics to involve the interlobular septa and pleura. Unlike LIP, DHL does not show uniform involvement of the alveolar septa.

Name: Ameliorated by steroid medication
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with a steroid medication such as prednisone.

Name: Triggered by medication exposure
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by administration of a medication.

Name: Triggered by levothyroxin exposure
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by administration of levothyroxin (thyroid hormone).

Name: Reduced muscle laminin alpha-2 chain staining
Def: A decreased amount of laminin alpha-2 chain in muscle tissue. This feature can be shown by immunohistochemistry or Western blotting of muscle tissue.

Name: Adrenal cortical sclerosis
Def: Abnormal thickening of of the outer layer (cortex) of the adrenal gland due to fibrosis.
Comment: See Figure 4 of PMID:4014441.

Name: Reduced hepatic fructose-1,6-phosphate aldolase activity
Def: Concentration or activity of fructose 1,6-bisphosphate aldolase in liver tissue below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Pancreatic hamartoma
Def: A benign (noncancerous) tumorlike malformation made up of an abnormal mixture of cells and tissues that originates in the pancreas.

Name: Liver angiomyolipoma
Def: A benign liver neoplasm composed of fat, vascular, and smooth muscle elements.

Name: Cardiac lipoma
Def: A lipoma that is located within a the heart.

Name: Peripheral nerve polyglucosan inclusion bodies
Def: Accumulation of a poorly branched and poorly spherical amylopectin-like glycogen (polyglucosan) in peripheral nerve fibers.

Name: Cardiac polyglucosan accumulation
Def: Accumulation of a poorly branched and poorly spherical amylopectin-like glycogen (polyglucosan) in myocardial tissue.

Name: Cystic nephroma
Def: A benign cystic neoplasm of the kidney.
Comment: The pathogenesis of cystic nephroma is controversial and there is no generally accepted classification.

Name: Absent dermal elastic fibers
Def: Elastic fibers not demonstrable in skin biopsy.

Name: Cleavage at junction of stratum corneum and stratum granulosum
Def: Splitting of the skin (cell-cell adhesion of keratinocytes) localized to the interface between the stratum corneum and stratum granulosum layers of the epidermis.

Name: Lymphoid hyperplasia
Def: An abnormal bone marrow finding characterized by many poorly circumscribed and occasionally confluent lymphoid nodules. The nodules contain small and uniform lymphocytes with rounded nuclei, clumped chromatin, and without prominent nucleoli.
Comment: The appearance of lymphoid hyperplasia may resemble that of malignant lymphoma, well-differentiated lymphocytic type.

Name: Absence of epidermal lamellar bodies
Def: Lack of lamellar bodies (LBs) inthe epidermis. LBs are specialized organelles that contain pro-barrier lipids imparting a fully lamellar internal structure, but also other cargoes such as enzymes (lipid metabolizing and proteolytic), enzyme inhibitors, and antimicrobial peptides.
Comment: Harlequin ichthyosis is characterized by absence of epidermial lamellar bodies.

Name: Gastrointestinal granulomatosis
Def: The presence of multiple granulomas in the gastrointestinal tract (Pylorus, esophagus, jejunum, ileum, cecum, rectum, perirectal area, esophagus) as based on pathological examination. Granulomas are small 0.5 to 2 mm collections of modified macrophages called epithelioid cells usually surrounded by lymphocytes.

Name: Enlarged sperm head vacuole
Def: Increased size of sperm vacuoles, which are surface concavities typically located at the the tip or middle area of sperm heads. According to the WHO Laboratory Manual for the Examination and Processing of Human Semen, sperm head vacuoles are considered abnormal when exceeding 20% of the cross-sectional area of the head. Vacuoles are found in almost all samples with normal sperm morphology; this term applies if the proportion of sperm with abnormally large vacuoles is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Ureteral hamartoma
Def: A benign (noncancerous) tumorlike malformation made up of an abnormal mixture of cells and tissues that originates in the ureter.

Name: Fetal methimazole exposure
Def: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to methimazole.

Name: Fetal procarbazine exposure
Def: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to procarbazine.

Name: Fetal fluorouracil exposure
Def: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to fluorouracil.

Name: Fetal cytarabine exposure
Def: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to cytarabine.

Name: Fetal tetracycline exposure
Def: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to tetracycline.

Name: Fetal quinine exposure
Def: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to quinine.

Name: Fetal cyclophosphamide exposure
Def: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to cyclophosphamide.

Name: Fetal metronidazole exposure
Def: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to metronidazole.

Name: Fetal phenobarbital exposure
Def: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to phenobarbital.

Name: Fetal phenytoin exposure
Def: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to phenytoin.

Name: Periumbilical
Def: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance are located at or near the umbilicus (belly button).

Name: Maternal obesity during pregnancy
Def: A history of obesity, which can be defined as a body mass index of 30 or greater, in the mother of a fetus or index patient.

Name: Maternal amniocentesis
Def: A history of amniocentesis having been performed in the mother of a fetus or index patient.
Comment: Complications of amniocentesis are rare but include fetal loss, amniotic fluid leak, fetal lung hypoplasia, and fetal injuries like bleeding from the cord, ocular injuries, and postural deformities like talipes equinovarus (clubfoot).

Name: Typified by highly variable age of onset
Def: Description of conditions in which age of onset is highly variable even in family members who share the same disease-associated variant or variants.

Name: Abnormal leukocyte enzyme concentration or activity
Def: Concentration or activity of an enzyme as measured in leukocytes is above or below the limits of normal.

Name: Reduced tissue beta-glucuronidase activity
Def: Concentration or activity of beta-glucuronidase (EC 3.2.1.31) below the lower limit of normal. FECH enzyme can be measured in multiple tissues including cultured fibroblasts and leukocytes.
Synonym: Reduced beta-glucuronidase activity in cultured fibroblasts

Name: Reduced leukocyte alpha-L-fucosidase activity
Def: Concentration or activity of an alpha-L-fucosidase as measured in leukocytes is below the limits of normal.
Comment: This feature is characteristic of fucosidosis.

Name: Reduced leukocyte arylsulfatase B activity
Def: Concentration or activity of an arylsulfatase B as measured in leukocytes is below the limits of normal.
Comment: This finding is characteristic of mucopolysaccharidosis type VI (MPS6). Reduced arylsulfatase activity can also be measured in cultured fibroblasts.

Name: Reduced leukocyte steroid sulfatase activity
Def: Concentration or activity of an arylsulfatase C as measured in leukocytes is below the limits of normal.
Comment: Reduced activity of steroid sulfatase, also called arylsulfatase C, is characteristic of X-linked ichthyosis.

Name: Reduced leukocyte arylsulfatase A activity
Def: Concentration or activity of the lysosomal enzyme arylsulfatase A (EC 3.1.6.8) as measured in leukocytes is below the limits of normal.
Comment: This finding is characteristic of metachromatic leukodystrophy. Reduced activity can also be measured in cultured fibroblasts.

Name: Decreased alpha-galactosidase A activity
Def: Activity of the enzyme alpha-galactosidase outsidebelow the lower limit of normal.
Comment: Fabry disease is a lysosomal storage disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the X-linked GLA (alpha Galactosidase A) gene (Xq22.1).

Name: Positive fecal parasite test
Def: Demonstration of parasite in stool specimen, e.g., Parasites present on wet mount of stool.e
Synonym: Parasites present on wet mount of stool

Name: Positive stool infectious agent test
Def: Any kind of test for an infectious agent in stool positive.

Name: Positive stool giardia antigen
Def: Test for giardia antigen in stool such as immune assay or DFA positive.

Name: Entamoeba histolytica antibody positive in stool
Def: Demonstration of antibody directed against Entamoeba histolytica in stool.

Name: Reduced erythrocyte free porphyrin concentration
Def: Concentration of porphyrin in erythrocytes below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Reduced circulating urocanic acid concentration
Def: The concentration of urocanic acid in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Decreased urinary epinephrine level
Def: The concentration of epinephrine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Decreased CSF epinephrine concentration
Def: Concentration of epinephrine in the cerebrospinal fluid below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Decreased circulating epinephrine concentration
Def: Concentration of epinephrin in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Decreased circulating norepinephrine concentration
Def: Concentration of norepinephrin in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Decreased urinary norepinephrine level
Def: The concentration of norepinephrine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Decreased urinary metaepinephrine level
Def: The concentration of metanephrine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Decreased CSF metanephrine concentration
Def: Concentration of metanephrine in the cerebrospinal fluid below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Decreased circulating metanephrine concentration
Def: Concentration of metanephrin in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Ovarian mass
Def: A swelling or enlargement localized to the ovary. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.
Comment: An ovarian mass may be initially found upon ultrasound, CT, or MRI investigation.

Name: Adrenal mass
Def: A swelling or enlargement localized to the adrenal gland. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

Name: Uterine mass
Def: A swelling or enlargement localized to the uterus. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

Name: Prostatic calculus
Def: Calcium deposits in the prostate gland.
Comment: Most cases of prostatic calculi are not accompanied by symptoms. Therefore, most cases are found incidentally during the diagnosis of BPH using transrectal ultrasonography.

Name: Decreased portal vein velocity
Def: A reduction in the velocity of portal venous flow, generally measured by Doppler ultrasound. Portal venous flow is normally towards the liver with peak systolic velocities in the range of 20-40 cm/s.

Name: Uterine cervix mass
Def: A swelling or enlargement localized to the cervis of the uterus. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

Name: Abnormal urinary uromodulin level
Def: The concentration of uromodulin (also known as Tamm Horsfall protein) in the urine, normalized for usine concentration, is outside the limits of normal.

Name: Decreased urinary uromodulin level
Def: The concentration of uromodulin (also known as Tamm Horsfall protein) in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Increased urine phenylacetylglutamine level
Def: The concentration of phenylacetylglutamine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Decreased urine guanidinoacetic acid level
Def: The concentration of guanidinoacetic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Positive urine infectious agent nucleic acid test
Def: Detection of DNA and RNA originating from an infectious agent (bacteria, viruses, parasites and fungi) in the urine.

Name: Positive CMV urine nucleic acid test
Def: Detection of Cytomegalovirus (CMV) nucleic acid in the urine by a method such as polymerase chain reaction.
Synonym: Positive cytomegalovirus urine nucleic acid test

Name: Positive Neisseria gonorrhoeae urine nucleic acid test
Def: Detection of Neisseria gonorrhoeae nucleic acid in the urine by a method such as polymerase chain reaction.
Synonym: Neisseria gonorrhoeae PCR positive in urine

Name: Positive enterovirus urine nucleic acid test
Def: Detection of enterovirus nucleic acid in the urine by a method such as polymerase chain reaction.

Name: Elevated brain glycine level by MRS
Def: An increase in the level of glycine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

Name: Elevated brain polyol compounds by MRS
Def: An increase in the level of polyol compounds in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

Name: Elevated brain gamma-aminobutyric acid by MRS
Def: An increase in the level of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

Name: History of recent anticoagulant ingestion
Def: Medical history of ingestion of anticoagulants prior to presentation.

Name: Decreased circulating antidiuretic hormone concentration
Def: Concentration of antidiuretic hormone, also known as vasopressin, is below the lower limit of normal in the blood circulation.

Name: Elevated circulating growth hormone-releasing hormone concentration
Def: Concentration of growth hormone-releasing hormone above the upper limit of normal in the blood circulation.

Name: Abnormal amniotic fluid protein concentration
Def: Any deviation of the concentration of a protein in the amniotic fluid from normal limits

Name: Decreased amniotic fluid alpha-fetoprotein concentration
Def: Concentration of alpha-fetoprotein in the amniotic fluid below lower limit of normal.

Name: Increased circulating vitamin E concentration
Def: Concentration of vitamin E in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Abnormal circulating calcitonin concentration
Def: Concentration of calcitonin, a 32-amino acid polypeptide hormone that is produced primarily by the parafollicular cells of the thyroid, in the blood circulation outside of normal limits.

Name: Decreased circulating calcitonin concentration
Def: Concentration of calcitonin, a 32-amino acid polypeptide hormone that is produced primarily by the parafollicular cells of the thyroid, in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Decreased circulating thyrotropin releasing hormone concentration
Def: Concentration of thyrotropin releasing hormone below the lower limit of normal in the blood circulation.
Synonym: Thyrotropin releasing hormone (TRH) low in blood

Name: Elevated circulating uroporphyrin concentration
Def: Concentration of uroporphyrin in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Increased urine pentacarboxylporphyrin level
Def: Concentration of pentacarboxylporphyrin in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Increased urine hexacarboxylporphyrin level
Def: Concentration of hexacarboxylporphyrin in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Increased circulating dehydroepiandrosterone concentration
Def: Concentration of dehydroepiandrosterone in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Increased erythrocyte coproporphyrin concentration
Def: Concentration of coproporphyrin in erythrocytes above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Increased erythrocyte uroproporphyrin concentration
Def: Concentration of uroproporphyrin in erythrocytes above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Decreased circulating apolipoprotein E concentration
Def: Concentration of apolipoprotein E below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating apolipoprotein E concentration
Def: Concentration of apolipoprotein E above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Acrosomal hypoplasia
Def: Reduction in the size of the acrosome of the head of spermatozoa.
Comment: The acrosome is a unique membranous organelle located over the anterior part of the sperm nucleus that is highly conserved throughout evolution. This acidic vacuole contains a number of hydrolytic enzymes that, when secreted, help the sperm penetrate the egg's coats. See Figure 23 of PMID:3311822.

Name: Oocyte maturation arrest
Def: Oocyte maturation arrest (OMA) can manifest as failed in vitro fetilization/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (IVF/ICSI) attempts using affected oocytes.
Comment: Oocyte maturation occurs through a series of molecular and morphological changes. Oocytes are initially arrested at the diplotene stage of prophase I, at which point they are referred to as germinal vesicle (GV) oocytes. Upon a surge in luteinizing hormone, GV oocytes exit prophase I and resume meiosis, and this is followed by chromatin condensation and breakdown of the nuclear envelope. Coupled with spindle formation and chromosome alignment, oocytes enter into meiosis I (when they are referred to as MI oocytes). MI is completed by extrusion of the first polar body. Oocytes then enter into meiosis II (when they are referred to as MII oocytes) but arrest at metaphase of MII until fertilization. In clinical in vitro fertilization (IVF) and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), first polar body (PB1) oocytes are regarded as indicative of MII oocytes, which can be used for fertilization. Oocyte maturation arrest occurs at different stages, including the GV stage and MI, leading to female infertility.

Name: Abnormal anus morphology
Def: A structural anomaly of the anus.

Name: Abnormal anus physiology
Def: A functional anomaly of the anus.

Name: Weak anal sphincter tone
Def: Reduced muscle tone of the sphincter of the anus.

Name: Reduced muscle 2,4-dienoyl-CoA reductase activity
Def: Diminished activity of the enzyme 2,4-dienoyl-CoA reductase in muscle tissue.

Name: Reduced liver 2,4-dienoyl-CoA reductase activity
Def: Diminished activity of the enzyme 2,4-dienoyl-CoA reductase in liver tissue.

Name: Nasal mucosa vasculitis
Def: Inflammation of blood vessels in the mucosa of the nasal cavity.

Name: Pituitary blastoma
Def: Pituitary blastoma is a distinctive anterior hypophyseal tumor of infants
Comment: Pituitary blastoma presents in infants younger than 24 months, most frequently with Cushing syndrome and elevated adrenocorticotropin (ACTH) and occasionally with ophthalmoplegia, signs of increased intracranial pressure, diabetes insipidus, and thyrotropin deficit. An often large solid or cystic/solid mass arises from the sella with extension into the hypothalamus and may encompass the optic chiasm and/or cavernous sinuses. Pathologically, the tumors exhibit arrested pituitary development and uncontrolled proliferation and are composed of Rathke epithelium, folliculostellate cells, small primitive cells, and secretory cells with ACTH or, less often, growth hormone immunoexpression.

Name: Peripheral axon spheroid formation
Def: Axonal spheroids are bubble-like biological features that form on most degenerating axons.
Comment: They often contain cytoskeletal elements and organelles, and, depending on the pathological insult, can colocalize with disease-related proteins such as amyloid precursor protein (APP), ubiquitin, and motor proteins. Initial formation of axonal spheroids depends on the disruption of axonal and membrane tension governed by cytoskeleton structure and calcium levels. Shortly after spheroid formation, the engulfment signal, phosphatidylserine (PS), is exposed on the outer leaflet of spheroid plasma membrane, suggesting an important role for axonal spheroids in phagocytosis and debris clearance during degeneration.

Name: Reduced liver carboxylesterase 1 activity
Def: Activity of the enzyme carboxylesterase 1 in liver tissue below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Abnormal dermis morphology
Def: A structural anomaly of the dermis, the layer of skin that lies beneath the epidermis and above the subcutaneous layer.

Name: Perivascular dermis hyaline deposition
Def: Deposition of a largely amorphous hyaline (transparent and homogeneous) substance around blood vessels in the dermis layer of the skin.
Comment: See Figure 4 of PMID:11298373

Name: Perivascular small intestinal hyaline deposition
Def: Deposition of a largely amorphous hyaline (transparent and homogeneous) substance around blood vessels in the wall of the small intestine.

Name: Large keratohyaline granules
Def: Abnormally large keratohyalin granules (KHG). KHG are typically present in the stratum granulosum of the epidermal layer of the skin (and epithelium of the mucosae). KHG are protein structures found in the keratinocytes of the stratum granulosum.
Comment: The chief function of keratohyaline granules seems to be cross-linking of keratin filaments which creates the tight barrier that is the epidermis.

Name: Decreased muscle lipoic acid content
Def: Reduced amount of lipoic acid in muscle tissue.

Name: Reduced hepatic cystathionine gamma-lyase activity
Def: Activity of cystathionine gamma-lyase in the liver below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Digestive system neoplasm
Def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the digestive system.

Name: Lumbar spondylosis
Def: Arthrosis, i.e., of degenerative joint disease, affecting the lumbar vertebral column.
Comment: When osteoarthritis affects the spine, it is known as spondylosis.

Name: Decreased circulating acid maltase activity
Def: Activity of the enzyme acid maltase (also known as alpha-1,4-glucosidase) below the lower limit of normal.
Comment: This finding is characteristic of Glycogen storage disease II (Pompe disease).

Name: Abnormal circulating 7-dehydrocholesterol concentration
Def: Concentration of 7-dehydrocholesterol in the blood circulation outside the limits of normal.

Name: Decreased circulating 7-dehydrocholesterol concentration
Def: Concentration of 7-dehydrocholesterol in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating lathosterol concentration
Def: Concentration of lathosterol in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
Comment: Lathosterol is an intermeditate in the synthesis of cholesterol.

Name: Elevated circulating desmosterol concentration
Def: Concentration of desmosterol in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Decreased circulating sialic acid concentration
Def: Concentration of sialic acid in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Purulent synovial fluid
Def: The synovial fluid (also known as synovia, i.e., the fluid found in the cavities of synovial joints) contains increased quantities of white blood cells.

Name: Muscle fiber calsequestrin 1-containing inclusion bodies
Def: The presence of inclusion bodies within the cytoplasm of muscle cells that demonstrate immunoreactivity for calsequestrin 1.

Name: Palatine myxoma
Def: A myxoma (A benign tumor composed of myxomatous tissue composed of loosely-arranged spindle, polygonal, and stellate cells) localized to the palate. Clinically, such tumors may present as a sessile nodule on the hard palate.

Name: Vaginal myxoma
Def: A myxoma (tumor of primitive connective tissue) localized in the vagina.

Name: Decreased dermal collagen
Def: Abnormally reduced amount of collagen fibers in the dermis.
Comment: See Figure 4C of PMID:29606302.

Name: Irregularly shaped keratohyaline granules
Def: Abnormal shape of keratohyaline granules in dermal keratinocytes.
Comment: Normal keratohyaline granules demonstrate a stellate and angulated shape See Figure S2 (Electron microscopy of the granular layer) of PMID:29758285.

Name: Tubular shadows
Def: Tubular shadows are characterized by a complete absence of cells in the testicular tubules, meaning that germ cells as well as somatic Sertoli cells are absent. The cells have been replaced by hyalinization.

Name: Multiple eyelid margin cysts
Def: Presence of many apocrine hidrocystoma (cysts) on the margins of the eyelids.

Name: Altered location of the longitudinal column in the fibrous sheath
Def: The fibrous sheath is a structure in the midpiece of the sperm flagellum surrounding the outer dense fibers. It comprises two longitudinal columns and transverse ribs. In case of altered location of the longitudinal column in the fibrous sheath the symmetrical structure is lost, most commonly with the columns not being opposite to each other, which can be visualized by electron microscopy.

Name: Uterine myxoma
Def: A myxoma (tumor of primitive connective tissue) localized to the uterus.

Name: Uterine cervix myxoma
Def: A myxoma (tumor of primitive connective tissue) localized to the the cervix of the uterus.

Name: Typified by complete penetrance
Def: Penetrance describes the proportion of genotype positive individuals that develop disease given a lifespan of 80 years. For example, penetrance of Neurofibromatosis type 1 is close to 100%.
Comment: Description of conditions in which all individuals with a given genotype exhibit the disease within a lifespan of 80 years.

Name: Osteochondromyxoma
Def: A rare benign chondroid and osteoid matrix-producing neoplasm of bone characterized by extensive myxoid changes. OMX originate from bony cortices and have been observed in the nasal region, as well as the tibia and radius.
Comment: Osteochondromyxoma is a rare manifestation of Carney complex.

Name: Gangliocytoma
Def: A low-grade central nervous system tumor composed of dysplastic ganglion cells, usually presenting in children or young adults and located in the cerebral hemispheres.

Name: Duodenal gastrinoma
Def: A gastrinoma, a neuroendocrine tumors characterized by the secretion of gastrin with resultant excessive gastric acid production, that is localized to the duodenum.

Name: Thymic carcinoid tumor
Def: A primary thymic neuroendocrine tumor.

Name: Bone marrow eosinophilia
Def: Count of eosinophils in the bone marrow above the upper limit of normal.
Comment: See Figure 1E of PMID:27684977.

Name: Exacerbated by lithium exposure
Def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by treatment with lithium.

Name: Reduced hepatic glycogen debrancher enzyme activity
Def: Activity of glycogen debrancher enzyme (also known as amylo-1,6-glucosydase, 4-alpha-glucantransferase) in liver tissue below the lower limit of normal.
Comment: Glycogen debrancher enzyme degrades glycogen branches and thereby releases glucose in a two step reaction. Debranching enzyme activity can be measured in either blood cells (leukocytes or erythrocytes), skin fibroblasts, or liver or muscle biopsy.

Name: Asymmetrical insertion of the midpiece into the head
Def: Insertion of the neck and midpiece into the head of a spermatozoon on an axis that diverges from the midline axis of the spermatozoon head. This term applies if the proportion of spermatozoa with this defect is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Bent sperm neck
Def: Sharply angled insertion of the neck and midpiece into the head of a spermatozoon. This term applies if the proportion of spermatozoa with this feature is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine 3,6-epoxydicarboxylic acid level
Def: The concentration of 3,6-epoxydicarboxylic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Gallbladder biliary sludging
Def: Presence of biliary sludge (a mixture of particulate solids that have precipitated from bile) in the gallbladder. Such sediment consists of cholesterol crystals, calcium bilirubinate pigment, and other calcium salts. Sludge is usually detected on transabdominal ultrasonography.

Name: Exacerbated by amiodarone exposure
Def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by treatment with amiodarone.

Name: Ureteral mass
Def: A swelling or enlargement localized to the ureter. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

Name: Wide cavum septum pellucidum
Def: Width of the cavum septum pellucidum above the upper limit of normal, which is defined as a separation of greater than one cm of the leaves of the cavum septum pellucidum.

Name: Hypoplastic trochlear nerve
Def: Underdevelopment of the trochlear nerve, which is the fourth cranial nerve and one of the ocular motor nerves that controls eye movement.

Name: Thymic cyst
Def: A closed sac of tissue (cyst) located in the thymus. Thymic cysts are a rare, benign anomaly, are usually asymptomatic, and mostly occur in the anterior mediastinum .

Name: Uterine cyst
Def: A closed sack of tissue (cyst) located in the uterus.

Name: Urinary bladder mass
Def: A swelling or enlargement localized to the urinary bladder. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

Name: Endosteal scalloping
Def: A series of indentations or erosions on a normally smooth margin of the inner layer of the cortex (i.e. the endosteum) of bones.

Name: Urinary bladder hamartoma
Def: A benign (noncancerous) tumorlike malformation made up of an abnormal mixture of cells and tissues that originates in the urinary bladder.

Name: Peritoneal mass
Def: A swelling or enlargement localized to the peritoneal cavity. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

Name: Fallopian tube mass
Def: A swelling or enlargement localized to the Fallopian tube. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

Name: Aplasia of the pyramids of the medulla oblongata
Def: Congenital absence of the pyramids, that is, of the paired structures located at the medial aspect of the ventral medulla that flank the anterior median fissure.

Name: Bathrocephaly
Def: A deformity of the posterior skull with bulging of the midportion of the occipital bone that is often associated with a benign variant of the mendosal suture.

Name: Occipital horn
Def: Downward pointing exostoses of the occipital bone situated in the tendinous insertions of the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles.
Comment: See Figure 2 of PMID:31336972.

Name: Absent pituitary stalk
Def: A developmental defect characterized by failure to develop of the pituitary stalk. The pituitary stalk, also known as the infundibulum or infundibular stalk, is the connection between the hypothalamus and the pituitary gland.
Comment: See Figure 1 and 2 of PMID:25250085.

Name: Abnormal pituitary stalk morphology
Def: A structural anomaly of the pituitary stalk, also known as the infundibulum or infundibular stalk, is the connection between the hypothalamus and the pituitary gland.

Name: Interrupted pituitary stalk
Def: A developmental defect characterized by a discontinuity of the pituitary stalk. The pituitary stalk, also known as the infundibulum or infundibular stalk, is the connection between the hypothalamus and the pituitary gland.

Name: Facial synkinesis
Def: Unintentional movement in one area of the face produced during intentional movement of another area of the face.
Comment: For instance, facial synkinesis may manifest as hypertonic contractures and synkinetic movements such as eye closure with volitional movement of the mouth or midfacial movement during volitional or reflexive eye closure.

Name: Synkinesis
Def: Unintentional movement in one area of the body produced during intentional movement of another area of the body.

Name: Exposure to birds
Def: History of exposure to birds.

Name: Perianal anethesia
Def: Loss of sensation to the area of buttocks, perianal space and thighs.
Comment: This feature may be observed with cauda equina syndrome as a collection of acute symptoms mostly occurring secondary to a large disk herniations leading to neuropathy of multiple lumbar and sacral nerve roots, or with spinal epidural abscess.

Name: Failure of phenylephrine to induce blanching of eye redness
Def: Instillation of 2.5% phenylephrine drops into the eye does not induce blanching of eye redness. Failure to blanch suggests redness caused by scleral vessel engorgement (e.g., scleritis) or extravascular cause (e.g., hemorrhage), not episcleritis or conjunctivitis.
Synonym: Phenylephrine does not induce blanching of eye redness

Name: Fetal alcohol exposure
Def: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to ethanol (alcohol).
Synonym: Exposure to alcohol in the womb

Name: Reduced cellular cobalamin uptake
Def: Diminished ability of cells to transport cobalamine from the extracellular space to the cytoplasm.
Comment: Cobalamin (Cbl. also known as vitamin B12) plays a role in the recycling of folate for single carbon exchange reactions, purine and pyrimidine synthesis, and methylation of homocysteine for the production of S-adenosylmethionine. The absorption, blood transport and cellular uptake of Cbl are complex processes involving multiple proteins and receptors. Transcobalamine binds to Cbl to protect it from acid degradation in the stomach.

Name: Focal necrotic brainstem lesion
Def: A localized area of cell death, often accompanied by infiltration of inflammatory cells, in the brainstem.

Name: Focal necrotic optic nerve lesion
Def: A localized area of cell death, often accompanied by infiltration of inflammatory cells, in the optic nerve.

Name: Focal necrotic thalamus lesion
Def: A localized area of cell death, often accompanied by infiltration of inflammatory cells, in the thalamus.

Name: Interstitial dermal edema
Def: Accumulation of fluid in the interstitial spaces of the skin. This finding can be appreciated my microscopic examination of a skin biopsy.

Name: Shoulder abduction contracture
Comment: A type of shoulder contracture characterized by decreased adduction movement of shoulder, that is, by a by a chronic reduction in active and passive ability to move the arm via the shoulder joint away from the median plane of the body.

Name: Shoulder external rotation contracture
Def: A type of shoulder contracture characterized by decreased internal rotation of shoulder, that is, by a chronic reduction in active and passive ability to internally rotate the humerus at the shoulder joint (if the arm is flexed at the elbow, Internal rotation of the shoulder rotates the forearm towards the center of the body).
Synonym: External rotation contracture of the shoulder joint

Name: Thumb adduction contracture
Def: A type of thumb contracture characterized by a chronic reduction in active and passive ability of the metacarpal-phalangeal and/or interphalangeal joints of the thumb to bring from medial side to neutral position, where the neutral position for the thumb is when the distal and proximal segments of the thumb joint are in linear alignment.

Name: Reduced tissue fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase activity
Def: Activity of fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase (EC 3.1.3.11) below the lower limit of normal. The activity can be measured in multiple tissues including liver and leukocytes.

Name: Reduced hepatic carbamoylphosphate synthetase 1 activity
Def: Activity of carbamoylphosphate synthetase 1 in the liver below the lower limit of normal.
Comment: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I (EC 6.3.4.16) is the rate-limiting enzyme that catalyzes the first committed step of the hepatic urea cycle by synthesizing carbamoyl phosphate from ammonia, bicarbonate, and 2 molecules of ATP.

Name: Reduced intraepidermal small nerve fiber density
Def: Reduced number of small nerve fibers in the skin.
Comment: Small fibers travel too slowly, and their conduction responses cannot be captured by a nerve conduction study, which is a routine test performed to evaluate large sensory and motor nerve fibers. Therefore, a skin biopsy is often used to assess small sensory nerve fibers in the skin. Skin biopsy is a minimally invasive procedure that may also be used to evaluate intraepidermal nerve fiber density. Skin specimens are typically obtained by a 3 mm punch biopsy at the distal leg and thigh and are then sent for laboratory analysis. Small fiber neuropathy may be diagnosed if the intraepidermal nerve fiber density is less than normal.

Name: Femoral artery duplication
Def: A developmental defect characterized by the presence of a supernumerary femoral artery.

Name: Intracellular accumulation of collagen VII
Def: Collagen VII is the major molecular constituent of anchoring fibrils in the skin. Collagen VII is synthesized as three identical pro-alpha1(VII) polypeptide chains, which are hydroxylated and glycosylated in a coordinated manner and then fold into triple-helical procollagen VII in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Mature collagen VII undergoes a multistep fibril polymerization process to form the anchoring fibrils. Mutant pro-alpha1(VII) polypeptide chains or procollagen VII molecules do not pass the ER quality control and are retained in the ER or designated for ubiquitin-proteasome degradation resulting in reduced amounts of collagen VII in the skin.
Comment: See Figure 2B of PMID:8288900.

Name: Reduced reticular lamina anchoring fibril density
Def: Diminished amount of the anchoring fibrils in the basement membrane zone that normally attach the epithelium to the basement membrane.

Name: Reduced lamina lucida anchoring filament density
Def: Diminished amount of the anchoring filaments that normally bridge the lamina lucida and insert into the lamina densa in the cutaneous basement membrane zone.

Name: Reduced epidermal keratin 5 protein expression
Def: Amount of keratin 5 in the epidermis below the lower limit of normal. The findiong is typically ascertained by immunofluorescent microscopy.

Name: Reduced epidermal keratin 14 protein expression
Def: Amount of keratin 14 in the epidermis below the lower limit of normal. The findiong is typically ascertained by immunofluorescent microscopy.

Name: Reduced epidermal keratin protein expression
Def: Amount of one or more keratins in the epidermis below the lower limit of normal. The findiong is typically ascertained by immunofluorescent microscopy.

Name: Reduced hepatic alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase activity
Def: Activity of alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase in the liver below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Hepatic sinusoidal dilatation
Def: Presence of an increased amount of blood in the hepatic capillaries.
Comment: Sinusoidal dilatation and congestion (SDC) in liver biopsy is often the result of venous outflow impairment. This impairment can occur at the level of the small hepatic veins (veno-occlusive disease), large hepatic veins (Budd-Chiari syndrome), or the heart (right-sided heart failure, tricuspid valve disease, constrictive pericarditis). See Figure in PMID:15270610

Name: Thin spermatozoon midpiece
Def: The cross-sectional size (diameter) of the midpiece of the spermatozoon is below the lower limit of normal. This term applies if the proportion of spermatozoa with this defect is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Thick spermatozoon midpiece insertion
Def: Increased width of the midpiece of the spermatozoon. The midpiece is the structure that is located between the head and the flagella (tail) of the spermatozoon. This term applies if the width of the midpiece increases progressively from the flagella to the head and if the proportion of individual spermatozoa with this anomaly is above the upper limit of normal.
Comment: See Figure 2.10i of the WHO laboratory manual for the examination and processing of human semen, Sixth edition (2021).

Name: Shoulder adduction contracture
Def: A type of shoulder contracture characterized by a chronic reduction in the active and passive ability to abduct the shoulder. This results in the shoulders being closer to midline. The affected individual is not able to position the shoulders away from the body.

Name: Occupational exposure history
Def: Exposure to a substance that results from the performance of an employee's duties.

Name: Occupational silver exposure
Def: A history of exposure to silver that has occurred in relation to performance of job duties.

Name: Abnormal femoral artery morphology
Def: Any structural abnormality of the femoral artey, a large blood vessel that provides oxygenated blood to lower extremity structures and in part to the lower anterior abdominal wall.

Name: Extrahepatic bile duct fibrosis
Def: Accumulation of fibrous connective tissue (collagen) in the extrahepatic bile ducts.

Name: Elevated circulating short-chain acylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of short-chain acylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. Acylcarnitines are classified according to the number of carbon atoms in the acyl-chain. Short chain acylcarnitines have between two and five carbon atoms in the acyl-chain (C2-C5),

Name: Elevated circulating C4 acylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of C4 acylcarnitines in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. C4 acylcarnitines have a four-carbon acyl chain.
Comment: C4 acylcarnitines include butyrylcarnitine (C4:0 acylcarnitine) and isobutyrylcarnitine (C4:1 acylcarnitine).

Name: Elevated circulating medium-chain acylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of medium-chain acylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. Acylcarnitines are classified according to the number of carbon atoms in the acyl-chain. Medium-chain acylcarnitines have between six and twelve carbon atoms in the acyl-chain (C6-C12),

Name: Elevated circulating long-chain acylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of long-chain acylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. Acylcarnitines are classified according to the number of carbon atoms in the acyl-chain. Long-chain acylcarnitines have between thirteen and twenty carbon atoms in the acyl-chain (C13-C20),

Name: Elevated circulating C5 acylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of C5 acylcarnitines in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. C5 acylcarnitines have a five-carbon acyl chain.

Name: Elevated circulating C18 acylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of C18 acylcarnitines in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. C18 acylcarnitines have a eighteen-carbon acyl chain.

Name: Elevated circulating C16 acylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of C16 acylcarnitines in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. C16 acylcarnitines have a sixteen-carbon acyl chain.

Name: Elevated circulating very long-chain acylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of very long-chain acylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. Acylcarnitines are classified according to the number of carbon atoms in the acyl-chain. Very long-chain acylcarnitines have twentyone or more carbon atoms in the acyl-chain (C21 and higher),

Name: Elevated circulating acetylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of acetylcarnitine (C2 acylcarnitine) in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. Acetylcarnitine has a two-carbon acyl chain.

Name: Elevated circulating methylmalonylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of methylmalonylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating 3-hydroxyhexadecanoylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of 3-hydroxyhexadecanoylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating C6 acylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of C6 acylcarnitines in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. C6 acylcarnitines have a six-carbon acyl chain.

Name: Elevated circulating methylglutarylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of methylglutarylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating 3-hydroxyisovalerylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of 3-hydroxyisovalerylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating 3-hydroxyhexanoylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of 3-hydroxyhexanoylcarnitine (C6-OH) in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating carnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of carnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating tiglylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of tiglylcarnitine (C5:1) in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Reduced circulating acetylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of acetylcarnitine (C2 acylcarnitine) in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal. Acetylcarnitine has a two-carbon acyl chain.

Name: Reduced circulating octadecenoylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of octadecenoylcarnitine (C18:1 acylcarnitine) in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Absent pigmentation of chest
Def: Lack of skin pigmentation (coloring) of the chest.
Synonym: Lack of skin coloring on chest
Lack of skin colouring on chest

Name: Aplasia of facial bones
Synonym: Failure of development of facial bones
Failure of development of facial skeleton

Name: Hyperparakeratosis
Def: Abnormal keratinization of the epidermal stratum coreum (horny layer) with increased keratin formation, preservation of the nuclei in the superficial cells, and absence of the stratum granulosum.

Name: Chromosome breakage
Def: Elevated rate of chromosomal breakage or interchanges occurring either spontaneously or following exposure to various DNA-damaging agents. This feature may be assayed by treatment of cultured lymphocytes with agents such as chemical mutagens, irradiation, and alkylating agents.
Synonym: High frequency of chromosome breaks in lymphocytes

Name: Increased activity of mitochondrial respiratory chain
obsolete Radial deviation of the thumb
Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the fifth metatarsal bone
Abnormality of the second metatarsal bone
Synonym: Abnormality of the 2nd long bone of foot

Name: Abnormality of the fourth metatarsal bone
Synonym: Abnormality of the 4th long bone of foot

Name: Onychogryposis of fingernail
Def: Thickened fingernails.

Name: Toenail onycholysis
Def: Painless and spontaneous separation of a toenail from the nail bed.

Name: Aplasia of the eccrine sweat glands
Hypoplasia of the eccrine sweat glands
obsolete Aplasia of the left hemidiaphragm
Macular edema
Def: Thickening of the retina that takes place due to accumulation of fluid in the macula as a nonspecific response to blood-retinal barrier breakdown. Macular edema is a common pathological response to a wide variety of ocular insults, most commonly after intraocular (e.g. cataract) surgery or in association with retinal vascular (e.g. diabetic eye disease, retinal vein occlusion) or inflammatory (e.g. uveitis) disease.

Name: Absent upper eyelashes
Synonym: Failure of development of upper eyelashes

Name: obsolete Abnormal morphology of bones of the upper limbs
obsolete Abnormal morphology of bones of the lower limbs
Abnormal lower limb bone morphology
Synonym: Abnormal morphology of bones of the lower limbs
Abnormal shape of bones of the lower limbs

Name: Abnormal upper limb bone morphology
Synonym: Abnormal morphology of bones of the upper limbs
Abnormal shape of bones of the upper limbs

Name: Abnormal morphology of ulna
Def: Any structural anomaly of the ulna, a bone of the forearm the extends from the elbow to the little finger.

Name: obsolete Abnormal concentration of calcium in blood
Abnormal circulating creatine kinase concentration
Def: Any deviation from the normal circulating creatine kinase concentration.
Synonym: Abnormal levels of creatine kinase in blood

Name: Happy demeanor
Def: A conspicuously happy disposition, characterized by frequent smiling and laughing, which may be contextually inappropriate or unrelated to the situation.

Name: obsolete Toe walking
Def: Toe walking is a pattern of walking in which a person walks on balls of his or her feet, with no contact between the heels and ground. Toe-walking is common in children who are learning to walk, but most children outgrow it around the age of two years. This term refers to the persistence of toe-walking beyond the usual age.

Name: Abnormal circulating renin concentration
Def: A deviation from the normal concentration of renin in the blood, a central hormone in the control of blood pressure and various other physiological functions.

Name: Abnormal blood folate concentration
Def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of folate in the blood circulation.
Comment: Folate is an essential water-soluble vitamin (vitamin B9) that is found in green leafy vegetables, cereals, legumes, and fruit. As a major methyl group donor, it plays an important role in one-carbon metabolism and is involved in DNA, RNA, and protein synthesis, in addition to its significant role in energy production and normal cell division. Low blood folate concentration is associated with an increased risk for neural tube defects during pregnancy.

Name: Abnormal lymphocyte count
Def: Any abnormality in the total number of lymphocytes in the blood.

Name: Abnormal natural killer cell count
Def: Any deviation from the normal overall count of natural killer (NK) cells in the circulation or a deviation from the normal distribution of NK cell subtypes.
Comment: In human peripheral blood, five NK cell subpopulations can be defined on the basis of the relative expression of the markers CD16 and CD56: (1) CD56bright CD16- (50-70% of CD56bright), (2) CD56bright CD16dim (30-50% of CD56bright), (3) CD56dim CD16-, (4) CD56dim CD16bright, and (5) CD56- CD16bright. In healthy individuals, populations (3) and (5) are numerically in the minority.
Synonym: Abnormal number of natural killer cells
Abnormality of natural killer cell count

Name: Abnormal tympanic membrane morphology
Def: Any structural abnormality of the tympanic membrane
Comment: The tympanic membrane is considered to be the border of middle and outer ear.

Name: Asymmetry of the size of ears
Synonym: Asymmetry of the size of ears

Name: Asymmetry of the shape of the ears
Synonym: Asymmetry of the shape of the ears

Name: Asymmetry of the position of the ears
Neoplasm of the outer ear
Def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the outer ear.

Name: Neoplasm of the inner ear
Def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the inner ear.

Name: Neoplasm of the ceruminal gland
Def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the ceruminal gland.

Name: Cutaneous atresia of the external auditory canal
Osseous atresia of the external auditory canal
Cutaneous stenosis of the external auditory canal
Osseous stenosis of the external auditory canal
Abnormal lateral semicircular canal morphology
Synonym: Morphological abnormality of the horizontal semicircular canal
Morphological abnormality of the lateral semicircular canal

Name: Abnormal posterior semicircular canal morphology
Synonym: Morphological abnormality of the posterior semicircular canal

Name: Abnormal anterior semicircular canal morphology
Synonym: Morphological abnormality of the anterior semicircular canal

Name: Absence of the reflex of the tensor tympani muscle
Abnormal Eustachian tube morphology
Def: A structural anomaly of the Eustachian tube (ET). The ET is a biomechanical valve between the nasopharynx and the middle ear. Physiologically, it controls the passive adaptation of the middle ear air pressure to the ambient air pressure primarily via direct muscular actions of the soft palate. In the closed state it protects the middle ear. Inadequate function of the ET causes middle ear ventilation disorders.

Name: Abnormality of the reflex of the tensor tympani muscle
Abnormality of the acoustic reflex
Def: An abnormality in the reflexive contraction of the middle-ear muscles in response to sound stimulation.

Name: Impairment of the the acoustic reflex
Impairment of the reflex of the tensor tympani muscle
Abnormal circulating vitamin B12 concentration
Def: A deviation from the normal concentration of cobalamin (vitamin B12) in the blood. Vitamin B12 is one of the eight B vitamins.

Name: Abnormal sweat homeostasis
