Def: An abnormality of the composition of sweat or the levels of its components.

Name: Abnormal circulating iron concentration
Def: The concentration of iron in the blood circulation is outside the limits of normal.

Name: Abnormal circulating ferritin concentration
Def: A deviation from the normal circulating concentration of ferritin. Ferritin concentration can be measured in serum or plasma.
Comment: Ferritin is an iron storage protein present in all cells of the organism. A small amount is found in plasma and serum, which is a reflection of iron stores in healthy individuals. A low serum ferritin concentration is usually regarded as an indicator of iron depletion, although the interpretation of normal or high serum ferritin values is challenging in the presence of acute or chronic inflammatory processes, as ferritin is increased in iron overload states and inflammation.

Name: Abnormal transferrin saturation
Def: Any abnormality in the serum transferrin saturation, which is calculated by dividing the serum iron level by total iron-binding capacity.

Name: Comedonal acne
Def: A type of acne in which open and closed comedones comprise the majority of the lesions, with substantially fewer papules and pustules.

Name: Mucinous histiocytosis
Def: Multiple subcutaneous non-fragile and skin-coloured papules characterized by interstitial infiltrate of spindle and epithelioid histiocytes, and mucin. There are well circumscribed aggregates of epithelioid histiocytes and mucin in the upper and middle dermis,with the histiocytes arranged between collagen bundles and separated from the epidermis by a Grenz zone.

Name: Lipogranulomatosis
Def: Yellow nodules of lipoid material are deposited in the skin and mucosae. This gives rise to granulomatous reactions.
Comment: Usually caused by a faulty lipid metabolism

Name: Tardive dyskinesia
Comment: the involuntary movements are tardive, meaning they have a slow or belated onset

Name: Reduced circulating 5-oxoprolinase activity
Def: Activity or concentration of 5-oxoprolinase in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal. This enzyme catalyzes the reaction 5-oxo-L-proline + ATP + 2 H(2)O = L-glutamate + ADP + 2 H(+) + phosphate.

Name: Dystopic os odontoideum
Def: Os odontoideum is classified into two anatomic types (orthotopic and dystopic). Os odontoideum is defined as an ossicle that consists of smooth and separate caudal portions of the odontoid process. With orthotopic os odontoideum, the ossicle moves with the anterior arch of the atlas, while the dystopic type consists of an ossicle near the basion, or one that is fused with the clivus

Name: L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria
Def: An increase in the level of L-2-hydroxyglutaric acid in the urine.

Name: Cortical myoclonus
Def: Cortical myoclonus mainly affects the distal upper limbs and face, which reflects the largest cortical representations of these body areas. It is often focal, but may be multifocal, bilateral or generalized, as a consequence of intracortical and transcallosal spreading of abnormal activity. It typically occurs on voluntary action and may affect speech and gait. Cortical myoclonic jerks are stimulus sensitive, typically to touch, but sensitivity to visual stimuli is also described. Most patients with cortical myoclonus have both positive myoclonus and NM, occurring either independently or together as a complex of the two kinds of myoclonus. If cortical myoclonus is prolonged and lasts for hours, days or weeks, it is called epilepsia partials continua and is considered to be a rare form of focal epileptic status. Focal cortical myoclonus almost always points to an underlining lesion of the sensori-motor cortex, which produces hyperexcitability (e.g. vascular, inflammatory or neoplastic).

Name: Woolly scalp hair
Def: The presence of wooly hair on the scalp. The term wooly hair refers to an abnormal variant of hair that is fine, with tightly coiled curls, and often hypopigmented. Optical microscopy may reveal the presence of tight spirals and a clear diameter reduction as compared with normal hair. Electron microscopy may show flat, oval hair shafts with reduced transversal diameter.

Name: Acne inversa
Def: A chronic skin condition involving the inflammation of the apocrine sweat glands, forming pimple-like bumps known as abscesses.

Name: Elevated urinary 3-hydroxybutyric acid
Def: An increased amount of 3-hydroxybutyric acid in the urine.

Name: Elevated urinary carboxylic acid
Def: An increased amount of carboxylic acid in the urine.

Name: Abnormal spaced incisors
Synonym: Abnormality of spacing of front teeth

Name: Orthokeratosis
Def: Formation of an anuclear keratin layer

Name: Lipomas of eyelids
Def: Fatty tumors on the eyelids.
Comment: Eyelid lipomas

Name: Periostitis
Def: Inflammation of the periosteum

Name: Facial papilloma
Comment: A very specific feature of Costello Syndrome

Name: Abnormality of extrinsic muscle of tongue
Platelet-activating factor acetylhydrolase deficiency
Def: Reduced level of platelet-activating factor acetylhydrolase.

Name: Abnormal circulating phospholipid concentration
Def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a phospholipid in the blood circulation.

Name: Chapped lip
Def: Cracking, fissuring, and peeling of the skin of the lips.

Name: Inappropriate sinus tachycardia
Def: Inappropriate sinus tachycardia is a nonparoxysmal tachyarrhythmia characterized by an increased resting heart rate (HR) and/or an exaggerated HR response to minimal exertion or a change in body posture. HR is constantly above the physiological range with no appropriate relation to metabolic or physiological demands.

Name: Maculopapular exanthema
Def: A skin rash that is characterized by diffuse cutaneous erythema with areas of skin elevation. It may evolve to vesicles or papules as part of a more severe clinical entity. Different degrees of angioedema with involvement of subcutaneous tissue may also appear.

Name: Neonatal sepsis
Def: Systemic inflammatory response to infection in newborn babies.

Name: Osteochondrosis
Def: Abnormal growth ossification centers in children. Initially a degeneration/ necrosis followed by regeneration or recalcification.

Name: Scaling skin
Def: Refers to the loss of the outer layer of the epidermis in large, scale-like flakes.

Name: Rectus femoris muscle atrophy
Synonym: Atrophy of the rectus femoris muscles

Name: APUdoma
Def: An endocrine tumor arising from an APUD cell.
Synonym: amine precursor uptake and decarboxylation tumors
amine precursor uptake and decarboxylation tumours

Name: Increased head circumference
Def: An abnormally increased head circumference in a growing child. Head circumference is measured with a nonelastic tape and comprises the distance from above the eyebrows and ears and around the back of the head. The measured HC is then plotted on an appropriate growth chart.

Name: Decreased head circumference
Def: An abnormally reduced head circumference in a growing child. Head circumference is measured with a nonelastic tape and comprises the distance from above the eyebrows and ears and around the back of the head. The measured HC is then plotted on an appropriate growth chart. Microcephaly is defined as a head circumference (HC) that is great than two standard deviations below the mean of age- and gender-matched population based samples. Severe microcephaly is defined with an HC that is three standard deviations below the mean.
Comment: Although HC measures skull size, it typically also reflects overall brain volume and has been described as a widely used proxy of neural growth and brain size. Brain size outside of normal values is an important risk factor for cognitive and motor delay. Microcephaly at birth has been termed primary microcephaly and that acquired after birth is secondary microcephaly.

Name: Mild microcephaly
Def: Decreased occipito-frontal (head) circumference (OFC). For the microcephaly OFC must be between -3 SD and -2 SD compared to appropriate, age matched, normal standards (i.e. -3 SD <= OFC < -2 SD).

Name: Encephalomalacia
Def: Encephalomalacia is the softening or loss of brain tissue after cerebral infarction, cerebral ischemia, infection, craniocerebral trauma, or other injury.

Name: Motor impersistence
Def: The inability to maintain postures or positions (such as keeping eyes closed, protruding the tongue, maintaining conjugate gaze steadily in a fixed direction, or making a prolonged 'ah' sound) without repeated prompts.
Comment: Damage to premotor and prefrontal regions results in motor-intentional disorders that disrupt initiation, maintenance, and termination of volitional movements. Motor impersistence (i.e., failure to maintain movement) more frequently develops following right than left hemisphere lesions. {xref="PMID:17353476", xref="DOI:10.1007/978-0-387-79948-3_2046", xref="https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199"}

Name: Simultanapraxia
Def: A subset of motor impersistence, defined as the inability to perform more than two of the simple voluntary acts simultaneously, such as closing the eyes and protruding the tongue.

Name: Abnormal consumption behavior
Def: Recurrent abnormal consumption of food, liquids, or objects that could have negative consequences for the individual.

Name: Abnormal CSF neopterin concentration
Def: Abnormal concentration of neopterin in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

Name: Elevated CSF neopterin level
Def: Increased concentration of neopterin in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

Name: Decreased CSF neopterin level
Def: Decreased concentration of neopterin in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

Name: Abnormal circulating neopterin concentration
Def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of neopterin in the blood circulation.
Comment: Neopterin can be found to have abnormal level in blood, CSF, or urine.

Name: Abnormal CSF pterin concentration
Def: Abnormal concentration of a pterin in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).
Comment: Pterin is a coenzyme that occurs in various forms, such as biopterin, folic acid, xanthopterin, or methanopterin.

Name: Elevated CSF biopterin level
Def: Concentration of biopterin in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Decreased CSF biopterin level
Def: Concentration of biopterin in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Abnormal circulating biopterin concentration
Def: A deviation from the normal concentration of biopterin in the blood circulation.

Name: Abnormal skin morphology of the palm
Def: An abnormality of the skin of the palm, that is, the skin of the front of the hand.

Name: Risus sardonicus
Def: Fixed sarcastic grimace and anxious expression. Caused by spasms of the masseter and other facial muscles.
Comment: Accompanied by rigidity of neck and trunk muscles and arching of back. Often observed as a sign of tetanus.

Name: Hypopnea
Def: Hypopnea is referring to breathing that is abnormally shallow.
Comment: Not to be confused with Hypoventilation. Hypopnea is distinct from apnea in which there is no breathing.

Name: Abnormal circulating insulin concentration
Def: An abnormal concentration of insulin in the body.

Name: Hypoinsulinemia
Def: A decreased concentration of insulin in the blood.

Name: Elevated hemoglobin A1c
Def: An increased concentration of hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), which is the product of nonenzymatic attachment of a hexose molecule to the N-terminal amino acid of the hemoglobin molecule. This reaction is dependent on blood glucose concentration, and therefore reflects the mean glucose concentration over the previous 8 to 12 weeks. The HbA1c level provides a better indication of long-term glycemic control than one-time blood or urinary glucose measurements.

Name: Reduced natural killer cell count
Def: Less than normal number of natural killer cells, a type of lymphocyte in the innate immune system with an ability to mediate cytotoxicity and produce cytokines after the ligation of a germline-encoded activation receptor.

Name: Absent natural killer cells
Def: Lack of natural killer cells, a type of lymphocyte in the innate immune system that contains cytoplasmic granzymes, i.e., small granules with perforin and proteases that allow natural killer cells to form pores in the cell membrane of the target cell through which the granzymes and associated molecules can enter, inducing apoptosis.

Name: Abnormal size of the dental root
Maternal thrombophilia
Def: An increased tendency towards thrombosis in the mother during a pregnancy.
Comment: Maternal thrombophilia has been linked to an increased incidence of placental abruption, as well as other adverse pregnancy outcomes. It is believed that the increased obstetrical risk is mediated through placental vascular dysfunction. Placental thrombosis can then result in subsequent ischemic complications, such as fetal loss, preeclampsia, and fetal growth restriction. Placental abruption has been identified as being part of the spectrum of ischemic placental disease and is postulated to be a chronic disease process (PMID:25401392).

Name: Pulmonary hemorrhage
Def: Pulmonary hemorrhage is a bleeding within the lungs. Older children and adults may spit blood or bloody sputum. Neonates, infants and young children usually do not spit up blood. Anemia, pulmonary infiltrates, increasingling bloody return on BAL and the presence of hemosiderin-laden macrophages in broncho-alveolar lavage (BAL) fluid or lung biopsy can diagnose lung bleeding. Alveolar macrophages contain phagocytosed red blood cells and stain positive for hemosiderin, a product of hemoglobin degradation, after about 48-72 hours following pulmonary hemorraghe. Previous or recurrent bleeding can thus be distinguished from fresh events. A differentiation into local or diffuse is of importance. Also differentiate if pulmonary hemorrhage is due to a primary lung disorder or a manifestation of a systemic disease.

Name: Abnormality of fibrinolysis
Def: Clinical phenotype characterized by delayed bleeding accelerated break down of blood clot (fibrinolysis)
Comment: requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Decrease in high molecular weight von Willebrand factor Multimers
Def: A decrease in high molecular weight von Willebrand factor multimers.
Comment: Requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium.

Name: Decreased level of heparin co-factor II
Def: An abnormality of coagulation related to a decreased concentration of heparin co-factor II
Comment: Requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Decreased level of histidine-rich glycoprotein
Def: Decrease of these levels result in increased inhibition of fibrinolysis and reduced inhibition of coagulation
Comment: Requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Decreased level of plasminogen
Def: A decreased level of Plasminogen
Comment: Requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Decreased level of thrombomodulin
Def: Thrombomodulin is a cofactor in the thrombin induced activation of Protein C. In the case of deficiency there will be less Protein C and tendency to clot
Comment: Requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Decreased level of tissue plasminogen activator
Def: The tPA protein catalyzes the conversion of plasiminogen to plasmin, and thus break down of clots. When there is a deficiency there will be an increase of thrombosis
Comment: Requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Delayed onset bleeding
Def: Abnormal bleeding related to a procedure or trauma which does not start at the time of the initial insult, but after delay by at least 24 hours.

Name: Factor XIII subunit A deficiency
Def: Deficiency of factor XIII subunit A, leading to a reduced factor XIII activity. Activated Factor XIII cross-links fibrin polymers solidifying the clot.
Comment: Measurement of subunit A or B can be performed by Elisa kits. Adding the more granular term would facilitate mutation analysis as both subunits are encoded by different genes. This is not always performed in the diagnostic workup so 'Reduced factor XIII activity' would sufice. This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Factor XIII subunit B deficiency
Def: Deficiency of factor XIII subunit B, leading to a reduced factor XIII activity. Activated Factor XIII cross-links fibrin polymers solidifying the clot.
Comment: Measurement of subunit A or B can be performed by Elisa kits. Adding the more granular term would facilitate mutation analysis as both subunits are encoded by different genes. This is not always performed in the diagnostic workup so 'Reduced factor XIII activity' would sufice. This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Leukocyte inclusion bodies
Def: The presence of intraceullar inclusion bodies (aggregates of stainable substances, usually proteins) in leukocytes.
Comment: This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Hyperfibrinolysis
Def: Increased degradation of fibrin, associated with clot instability and bleeding
Comment: This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Impaired binding of factor VIII to VWF
Def: Impaired binding of factor VIII to von Willebrand Factor. This is determined using a modified ELISA assay.
Comment: This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium
Synonym: von Willebrand Disease Type II Normandy

Name: Impaired neutrophil chemotaxis
Def: An impairment of the migration of neutrophils towards chemoattractants as part of the innate immune response
Comment: This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Increased plasma vitamin K epoxide after vitamin K supplementation
Def: Increased plasma vitamin K epoxide after vitamin K supplementation is present in VKCFD (vitamin K-dependent clotting factor deficiency) type 2, but not in VKCFD type 1.
Comment: This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Increased ratio of VWF propeptide to VWF antigen
Def: An increased VWF propeptide to VWF antigen indicates that deficiency of VWF is not due to impaired synthesis but due to rapid clearance. The VWF propeptide is measured by ELISA.
Comment: Some forms of von Willebrand Disease Type I (particularly those previously classified as type IC) and Acquired von Willebrand Disease. This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Increased RIPA
Def: Increased platelet agglutination in response to low-dose ristocetin
Comment: Characteristic of type 2B von Willebrand Disease or platelet-type (pseudo) VWD. (NB: this is not the same as enhanced ristocetin coafactor assay activity) This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Muscle hemorrhage
Def: Bleeding occurring within a muscle

Name: Prolonged euglobulin clot lysis time
Def: Abnormally increased length of time required for an in vitro clot to dissolve in the absence of the normal plasmin inhibitors. This test is a clinical assay used to measure fibrinolysis. The euglobulin fraction of plasma is precipitated and used to form clot by addition of thrombin; after clot forms the rate of clot breakdown (fibrinolysis) can be monitored.
Comment: This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Prolonged Russell's viper venom time
Def: Increased time to coagulation in the Russell's viper venom assay
Comment: This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Reduced alpha-2-antiplasmin activity
Def: Reduced activity of alpha-2-antiplasmin. This protein inactivates the protease plasmin that drives fibrinolysis.
Comment: This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Reduced antithrombin antigen
Def: Reduced antithrombin antigen. A reduced level of antithrombin may lead to an increased risk of thrombus formation.
Comment: This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Reduced euglobulin clot lysis time
Def: Abnormally decreased length of time required for an in vitro clot to dissolve in the absence of the normal plasmin inhibitors. This test is a clinical assay used to measure fibrinolysis. The euglobulin fraction of plasma is precipitated and used to form clot by addition of thrombin; after clot forms the rate of clot breakdown (fibrinolysis) can be monitored.
Comment: This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Reduced plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 activity
Def: Reduced activity of plasminogen activator inhibitor 1. This protein down-regulates fibrinolysis in the circulation by inhibiting the two major plasminogen activators: tissue-plasminogen activator and urokinase-plasminogen activator.
Comment: This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Reduced plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 antigen
Def: Reduced level of plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 antigen.
Comment: Added the antigen level as diagnosis with only activity levels is very difficult due to assay problems. Activity levels of control patients also include 0 within the normal limit. This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Reduced prothrombin antigen
Def: Reduced prothrombin antigen as measured by ELISA assay. Prothrombin is a vitamin K-dependent coagulation factor that is proteolytically cleaved to form thrombin.
Comment: This term has been requested and created by members of the BRIDGE consortium

Name: Hand dimple
Def: A cutaneous indentation resulting from tethering of the skin to underlying structures (bone) of the hand.
Comment: Use case: PMC4498842

Name: Aplastic/Hypoplastic nasopharyngeal adenoids
Def: Absence or underdevelopment of the nasopharyngeal adenoids.

Name: Abnormal size of nasopharyngeal adenoids
Def: A deviation in the size of nasopharyngeal adenoids.

Name: Hypoplastic nasopharyngeal adenoids
Def: Underdevelopment of the nasopharyngeal adenoids.

Name: Aplastic nasopharyngeal adenoids
Def: Absence of the nasopharyngeal adenoids as a developmental defect.

Name: Decreased size of nasopharyngeal adenoids
Def: An abnormal decrease in the size of nasopharyngeal adenoids.

Name: Increased size of nasopharyngeal adenoids
Def: An abnormal increase in the size of nasopharyngeal adenoids.

Name: Glue ear
Def: Middle ear is filled with glue-like fluid instead of air.
Comment: In some contexts, glue ear is used interchangeably with otitis media with effusion (OME) (PMID:21653931). Some authors use glue ear to refer to a subtype of OME characterized by thick, glue-like fluid buildup in the middle ear (mucoid otitis media) (PMID:10993548). Serous otitis media is usually responsive to medical treatment, whereas mucoid otitis media is not. This term refers to the mucoid subtype.

Name: Jaw pain
Def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the jaw.

Name: Upper limb muscle hypertrophy
Def: Abnormal increase in muscle size and mass of one or both arms not due to training.

Name: obsolete Recurrent infections of the middle ear
Impaired glucose tolerance
Def: An abnormal resistance to glucose, i.e., a reduction in the ability to maintain glucose levels in the blood stream within normal limits following oral or intravenous administration of glucose.

Name: Hyperintensity of MRI T2 signal of the spinal cord
Def: A region of high intensity (brightness) observed upon magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans of the spinal cord.
Comment: Seen in a wide-ranging variety of spinal cord processes including; simple MR artifacts, congenital anomalies etc. Characterization of the abnormal areas of T2 signal as well as their appearance on other MR imaging sequences, when combined with clinical context and laboratory investigations, will often allow a unique diagnosis, or at least aid in narrowing the differential diagnosis. {xref="PMID:19527360"}

Name: Adenocarcinoma of the intestines
Def: A malignant epithelial tumor with a glandular organization that originates in the intestines.

Name: Adenocarcinoma of the small intestine
Def: A malignant epithelial tumor with a glandular organization that originates in the small intestine.

Name: Adenocarcinoma of the large intestine
Def: A malignant epithelial tumor with a glandular organization that originates in the large intestine.

Name: Frequency
Def: Class to represent frequency of phenotypic abnormalities within a patient cohort.
Comment: Aligned with Orphanet

Name: Obligate
Def: Always present, i.e. in 100% of the cases.

Name: Very frequent
Def: Present in 80% to 99% of the cases.

Name: Frequent
Def: Present in 30% to 79% of the cases.

Name: Occasional
Def: Present in 5% to 29% of the cases.

Name: Very rare
Def: Present in 1% to 4% of the cases.

Name: Excluded
Def: Present in 0% of the cases.

Name: Abnormal axial muscle morphology
Def: A structural anomaly of the muscles of the trunk and head.

Name: Nasogastric tube feeding
Def: The condition of inability to eat normally treated by placement of a thin tube through the nose into the stomach that is then used to carry food.

Name: Cyclic neutropenia
Def: Recurrent episodes of abnormally low levels of neutrophils in the body (neutropenia).

Name: Abnormal location of the eyebrow
Def: Anomalous anatomical placement of the eyebrow.

Name: Preauricular cyst
Def: Preauricular sinus is an occasional finding and most frequently appears as a small pit close to the anterior margin of the ascending portion of the helix. The opening has also been reported along the postero superior margin of the helix, the tragus or the lobule. Preauricular sinus may lead to the formation of a subcutaneous cyst that is intimately related to the tragal cartilage and the anterior crus of the helix.

Name: Decreased circulating free fatty acid level
Abnormal circulating free fatty acid concentration
Def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a free fatty acid in the blood circulation.
Synonym: Abnormal circulating free fatty acid level

Name: Increased urinary glycerol
Def: An increased concentration of glycerol in the urine.

Name: Hyperglycerolemia
Def: Increased concentration of glycerol in the blood.
Comment: In glycerol kinase deficiency, the increased glycerol concentration has been noted to cause false-positive results of hypertriglyceridemia, a phenomenon called pseudohypertriglyceridemia.

Name: Decreased circulating iron concentration
Def: The concentration of iron in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Increased male libido
Def: Increased desire for sexual activity on the part of a male.

Name: Decreased male libido
Def: Reduced desire for sexual activity on the part of a male.

Name: Male sexual dysfunction
Def: A problem occurring during any phase of the male sexual response cycle that prevents the individual from experiencing satisfaction from the sexual activity

Name: Male anorgasmia
Def: Inability of a male to reach orgasm.

Name: Sterile arthritis
Def: An inflammatory arthritis characterized by purulent synovial fluid with neutrophil accumulation, but with negative cultures.
Comment: This form of arthritis is termed 'sterile' because bacetriology returns negative results even though the clinical presentation resembles that of infectious arthritis.

Name: Symmetric polyarthritis
Def: Polyarthritis refers to a joint disease that involves at least five joints. One or more signs of inflammation, including pain, movement restriction, swelling, warmth, and redness, are seen in the joints involved. Polyarthritis is defined as symmetric if at least half of the joints involved are affected in a symmetric (i.e., both right and the left) fashion.
Comment: In the event that pain is the only symptom, it is difficult to differentiate polyarthritis from the causes of polyarticular joint pain, such as fibromyalgia or osteoarthritis.

Name: Oligoarthritis
Def: A type of arthritis that affects up to four joints in the first six months of disease.

Name: Blind vagina
Def: The vagina ends in a blind pouch or sac rather than being connected to the internal genitalia.

Name: Tongue edema
Def: An abnormal accumulation of fluid and swelling in the tongue.

Name: Blue urine
Def: An abnormal blue color of the urine.
Comment: Blue or green urine coloration may be observed due to certain dyes used for tests of kidney and bladder function, some medications, and disorders including familial benign hypercalcemia and urinary tract infections caused by pseudomonas bacteria.

Name: Red urine
Def: An abnormal red color of the urine.
Comment: http://www.health.harvard.edu/newsletter_article/red-brown-green-urine-colors-and-what-they-might-mean

Name: Dark urine
Def: An abnormal dark color of the urine.
Comment: http://www.health.harvard.edu/newsletter_article/red-brown-green-urine-colors-and-what-they-might-mean

Name: Red-brown urine
Def: An abnormal red-brown color of the urine.
Comment: http://www.health.harvard.edu/newsletter_article/red-brown-green-urine-colors-and-what-they-might-mean

Name: Dark yellow urine
Def: An abnormal dark-yellow color of the urine.
Comment: http://www.health.harvard.edu/newsletter_article/red-brown-green-urine-colors-and-what-they-might-mean

Name: Purple urine
Def: An abnormal purple color of the urine.
Comment: http://www.health.harvard.edu/newsletter_article/red-brown-green-urine-colors-and-what-they-might-mean

Name: Eyelid erythema
Def: Redness of the skin of the eyelids, caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin.

Name: Heliotrope rash
Def: In a heliotrope rash, the color of the skin turns to violet, which is the color of the heliotrope flower.
Comment: Heliotrope rash occurs during the initial phase of the idiopathic inflammatory myositis (particularly dermatomyositis). Heliotrope rash is a characteristic symptom of Dermatomyositis.

Name: Bull's eye rash
Def: A cutaneous eruption that consists of multiple (at least two) concentric erythematous rings.

Name: Hypoplasia of the olfactory bulb
Def: Underdevelopment of the olfactory bulb.

Name: Abnormal morphology of the olfactory bulb
Def: An abnormal morphology of the olfactory bulb (bulbus olfactorius), which is involved in olfaction, i.e. the sense of smell.

Name: Focal hyperintensity of cerebral white matter on MRI
Def: An abnormal area of increased brightness (hyperintensity) that is limited to one particular area.

Name: Multifocal hyperintensity of cerebral white matter on MRI
Def: An abnormal area of increased brightness (hyperintensity) that occurs in several distinct areas.

Name: Confluent hyperintensity of cerebral white matter on MRI
Def: Areas of brighter than expected MRI signal in the white matter of the brain whereby individual patches run together.

Name: Focal hypointensity of cerebral white matter on MRI
Multifocal hypointensity of cerebral white matter on MRI
Confluent hypointensity of cerebral white matter on MRI
Purulent rhinitis
Def: Chronic rhinitis accompanied by pus formation.
Comment: An infection of the nasal mucosa associated with pus formation. (Often secondary to a systemic infection, such as measles)

Name: Nipple localization
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is distributed around the nipples or located in the nipples.

Name: Breast microcalcification
Def: The term breast microcalcification is used to define calcium deposits in the breast with a diameter of less than 1 mm.

Name: Architectural distortion of breast
Def: Architectural distortion is defined as an architectural disruption of the normal breast that does not have obvious mass opacities, which may be early signs of breast carcinoma.

Name: Asymmetric thickening of the nipple-areolar complex
Def: Thickening of the skin around the nipple with a distribution that is not equal on all sides.

Name: Perimenopausal
Def: Perimenopause, or the menopausal transition, encompasses that period of time during which physiologic changes mark progression toward a woman's final menstrual period. This phase begins with the onset of menstrual irregularities and continues until a woman reaches menopause, or one year after amenorrhea has occurred. Perimenopause can last for a variable amount of time, the median of which is four years.

Name: Mastitis
Def: Mastitis is defined as an inflammation of the breast and may or may not be accompanied by infection.

Name: Ameliorated by menopause
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by menopause.
Comment: This term may apply to breast fibroadenoma and premenstrual dysphoric disorder.

Name: Fluctuance on palpation
Def: Yielding to alternate pressure by palpating fingers so as to suggest that the area being felt contains fluid.

Name: History of vasectomy
Def: A medical history of having undergone a vasectomy prior to the current presentation.

Name: Pain in penis
Def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the penis.

Name: Left ventricular thrombus
Def: A blood clot (thrombus) localized in the left ventricle. Left ventricular thrombus is a serious complication of acute myocardial infarction and also of non-ischemic cardiomyopathies.

Name: Gelatinous ascites
Def: A type of ascites characterized by copious amounts of mucinous ascites and mucinous peritoneal implants, leading to progressive obliteration of the peritoneal cavity and intestinal obstruction.
Comment: See figures 2 and 3 of PMID:28868432.

Name: Diffuse breast nodularity
Def: Breast tissue with a lumpy or ropelike texture.

Name: Abnormal urinary nitrogen compound level
Def: The amount of a nitrogen compound in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is outside of normal limits.

Name: Decreased urinary biopterin level
Def: The amount of biopterin in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Abnormal urine guanidinoacetic acid level
Def: The concentration of guanidinoacetic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is outside normal limits.

Name: Elevated urine guanidinoacetic acid level
Def: The concentration of guanidinoacetic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Decreased urinary neopterin level
Def: The amount of neopterin in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Abnormal urinary inosine level
Def: The amount of inosine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is outside the limits of normal.

Name: Elevated urinary inosine level
Def: The amount of inosine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Abnormal urinary guanosine level
Def: The amount of guanosine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is outside the limits of normal.

Name: Elevated urinary guanosine level
Def: The amount of guanosine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Abnormal urinary hypoxanthine level
Def: The concentration of hypoxanthine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is outside of normal limits.

Name: Decreased urinary hypoxanthine level
Def: The concentration of hypoxanthine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Absent neutrophil lactoferrin
Def: The absence of lactoferrin in neutrophil granules, which could be caused by either an isolated failure of synthesis of this protein (or the production of an antigenically unrecognizable form of lactoferrin) or a complete deficiency of specific granule production.

Name: Neutrophil nuclear clefts
Def: An abnormality of the nucleus of neutrophils, which presents as either a type I nuclear cleft, where the nuclear cleft may show a transition into a round/oval shape. The second type nuclear cleft, which runs perpendicular to the nuclear surface, and this type of cleft might be related to nuclear lobe formation.

Name: Low neutrophil alkaline phosphatase
Def: An abnormally reduced level of alkaline phosphatase in neutrophils, which could be due to absence of enzyme or the production of defective enzyme.

Name: Increased neutrophil mitochondria
Def: An increased number of mitochondria detected in neutrophils.

Name: Increased neutrophil ribosomes
Def: An increased number of ribosomes detected in neutrophils.

Name: Bladder outlet obstruction
Def: A compression or resistance upon the bladder outflow channel at any location from the bladder neck to urethral meatus, which usually causes lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS).

Name: Decreased expression of GPI-anchored proteins on the cell surface
Def: A decrease in the protein expression of GPI-anchor proteins, such as CD55 and CD59, at the cell surface, which suggests a defect in GPI-anchor biosynthesis.

Name: Starch intolerance
Def: An inability to digest starch.

Name: Renal tubular cyst
Def: Tubular lumnal dilatation/prominence lined by simple layer of cuboidal-to-flat tublar epihelial cells.

Name: Ageusia
Def: A rare condition that is characterized by a complete loss of taste function of the tongue.

Name: Agenesis of putamen
Def: A developmental defect characterized by the absence of the putamen owing to its failure to develop.
Comment: The basal ganglia are symmetrical subcortical gray nuclei at the core of the extrapyramidal system, composed by the striatum (which comprises the putamen, caudate nucleus, olfactory tubercle, and nucleus accumbens), the pallidum, the substantia nigra, and the subthalamic nucleus. Congenital malformations of the basal ganglia deriving from defects of embryogenesis are very rare. The basal ganglia embryologically derive from the prosencephalon (or forebrain), the most rostral of the three vesicles originating from early patterning of the neural tube along the anterior-posterior axis.

Name: obsolete Fractured thoracic segment of trunk
Fractured humerus
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the humerus.

Name: Hot cross bun sign
Def: A cruciform-shaped hyperintensity within the pons found on T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
Comment: It is commonly associated with atrophy of the pons, cerebellum, and putamen in multiple system atrophy (MSA). See figure 15 in PMID:29089832.

Name: Transient decreased circulating IgG4
Def: A temporary reduction beneath the normal level of total immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) in the blood circulation.

Name: Chronic decreased circulating IgG4
Def: A lasting decrease of immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) in the blood.

Name: Chronic (near) absent circulating IgG4
Def: A lasting absence of immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) in the blood, whereby at most trace quantities of IgG4 can be measured.

Name: Chronic partially decreased circulating IgG4
Def: A lasting limited decrease of immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) in the blood.
Synonym: Chronic partially decreased IgG4 in blood

Name: Fractured calcaneus
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the calcaneus.

Name: Transient decreased circulating IgG2
Def: A temporary reduction beneath the normal level of total immunoglobulin G2 (IgG2) in the blood circulation.

Name: Chronic decreased circulating IgG2
Def: A lasting decrease of immunoglobulin G2 (IgG2) in the blood.

Name: Fractured knee
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the knee.

Name: Chronic (near) absent circulating IgG2
Def: A lasting absence of immunoglobulin G2 (IgG2) in the blood, whereby at most trace quantities of IgG2 can be measured.

Name: Chronic partially decreased circulating IgG2
Def: A lasting limited decrease of immunoglobulin G2 (IgG2) in the blood.
Synonym: Chronic partially decreased IgG2 in blood

Name: Transient decreased circulating IgG1
Def: A temporary reduction beneath the normal level of total immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) in the blood circulation.

Name: Chronic decreased circulating IgG1
Def: A lasting decrease of immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) in the blood.

Name: Chronic (near) absent circulating IgG1
Def: A lasting absence of immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) in the blood, whereby at most trace quantities of IgG1 can be measured.

Name: Chronic partially decreased circulating IgG1
Def: A lasting limited decrease of immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) in the blood.
Synonym: Chronic partially decreased IgG1 in blood

Name: Transient decreased circulating IgG3
Def: A temporary reduction beneath the normal level of total immunoglobulin G3 (IgG3) in the blood circulation.

Name: Chronic decreased circulating IgG3
Def: A lasting decrease of immunoglobulin G3 (IgG3) in the blood.

Name: Fractured thoracic vertebra
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the thoracic vertebra.

Name: Chronic (near) absent circulating IgG3
Def: A lasting absence of immunoglobulin G3 (IgG3) in the blood, whereby at most trace quantities of IgG3 can be measured.

Name: Chronic partially decreased circulating IgG3
Def: A lasting limited decrease of immunoglobulin G3 (IgG3) in the blood.
Synonym: Chronic partially decreased IgG3 in blood

Name: Abnormal immunoglobulin level in body fluid
Def: An abnormal deviation from normal levels of immunoglobulins in body fluids, such as mucous.

Name: Increased immunoglobulin level in body fluid
Def: An elevation from normal levels of immunoglobulins in body fluids, such as mucous.

Name: Decreased immunoglobulin level in body fluid
Def: An reduction from normal levels of immunoglobulins in body fluids, such as mucous.

Name: Decreased body fat percentage
Def: The percentage of fat as a part of total body weight below the norm, usually defined as less than 14% for females and less than 8% for males.

Name: Abnormal proportion of exhausted T cells
Def: A deviation from the normal proportion of exhausted T cell relative to T cell in the blood.
Comment: T cell exhaustion is a broad term that has been used to describe the response of T cells to chronic antigen stimulation, first in the setting of chronic viral infection but more recently in response to tumors.

Name: Fractured lower leg
Def: Bone fracture anywhere in the tibia, fibula, or ankle.

Name: Fractured skull
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the skull.

Name: Fractured phalanx
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the phalanx.

Name: Compression-fractured thoracic vertebra
Def: A fracture of the thoracic vertebra that is caused by a loss of bone mass (osteoporosis) that occurs as part of aging.

Name: Compression-fractured vertebra
Def: A fracture of the vertebra that is caused by a loss of bone mass (osteoporosis) that occurs as part of aging.

Name: Compression-fractured cervical vertebra
Def: A fracture of the cervical vertebra that is caused by a loss of bone mass (osteoporosis) that occurs as part of aging.

Name: Compression-fractured lumbar vertebra
Def: A fracture of the lumbar vertebra that is caused by a loss of bone mass (osteoporosis) that occurs as part of aging.

Name: Avulsion fractured humerus
Def: A fractured in which a fragment of the humerus tears away from the main mass of bone as a result of physical trauma.

Name: Avulsion fractured tibia
Def: A fractured in which a fragment of the tibia tears away from the main mass of bone as a result of physical trauma.

Name: obsolete Avulsion fractured pelvic region of trunk
Avulsion fractured epiphysis of femur
Def: A fractured in which the fragment of the epiphysis of femur bone tears away from the main mass of bone as a result of physical trauma.

Name: Emotional hypersensitivity
Def: Heightened emotional reactivity to environmental stimuli, including the emotions of others.

Name: Beau's lines
Def: A nail dystrophy that is preseents as grooved lines that run from side to side on the fingernail or the toenail that may look like indentations or ridges on the nail plate. They are caused by temporary disruption in the growth of proximal nail matrix. Trauma is usually the initiating factor such as infections, severe medical illnesses, major surgery/anesthesia, medication side effects, and autoimmune disease.

Name: Complete tracheal ring
Def: Continuous or nearly continuous configuration of the cartilaginous tracheal ring.
Comment: The trachea is surrounded by 16-20 rings of hyaline cartilage; these rings are incomplete and horseshoe-shaped (C-shaped). In complete tracheal rings, the rings encircle the entire trachea (O-shaped) or nearly the entire trachea. Pulmonary artery sling is a vascular anomaly often seen in CTRD in which the left pulmonary artery (LPA) originates from the right pulmonary artery (RPA) and encircles the distal trachea and right primary bronchus before entering the hilum of the left lung. Pumonary artery sling should be coded separately (HP:0004961).

Name: Decreased middle cerebral artery pulsatility index
Def: Abnormally reduced blood flow pulsatility in in the middle cerebral artery (MCA). The pulsatility index (PI) is calculated using the following equation PI = (peak systolic velocity-end-diastolic velocity)/mean velocity.
Comment: Arterial blood flow pulsatility, as assessed by Doppler, is influenced by many factors, including the differences in resistance between vascular beds upstream and downstream of the artery assessed, intrinsic properties of the artery, fetal heart rate and cardiac output. In the presence of structural heart disease, reduced cerebral oxygen content, abnormal cardiac output, anatomical substrate that impedes cerebral blood flow and differences in systemic and placental vascular resistance may all potentially contribute to changes in middle cerebral artery pulsatility index (MCA-PI). Fetuses with severe left heart obstruction, including hypoplastic left heart syndrome and isolated coarctation associated with retrograde distal arch flow, have altered cerebral blood flow with reduced MCA-PI. These changes in cerebral blood flow potentially contribute to the neurodevelopmental abnormalities frequently observed in affected infants and children.

Name: Fractured metaphysis of femur
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the metaphysis of femur.

Name: Fractured right clavicle
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the right clavicle.

Name: Fractured left clavicle
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the left clavicle.

Name: Fractured lower limb segment
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the lower limb segment.

Name: Fractured upper limb segment
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the upper limb segment.

Name: Fractured metacarpus skeleton
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the metacarpus skeleton.

Name: Fractured epiphysis of fifth metacarpal bone
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the epiphysis of fifth metacarpal bone.
Synonym: bone epiphysis of fifth metacarpal bone

Name: Fractured tibia
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the tibia.

Name: Fractured clavicle bone
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the clavicle bone.

Name: Fractured acetabular part of hip bone
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the acetabular part of hip bone.
Synonym: bone acetabular part of hip bone

Name: Fractured coccyx
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the coccyx.

Name: Fractured epiphysis
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the epiphysis.

Name: Fractured navicular bone of pes
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the navicular bone of pes.

Name: Fractured cuboid bone
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the cuboid bone.

Name: Fractured sternoclavicular joint
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the sternoclavicular joint.

Name: Fractured ankle
Def: A fracture or multiple fractures of one or more of three bones in the ankle joint: the tibia (shinbone), the fibula (outer ankle bone), and the talus (which is the bone that connects your leg to your foot).

Name: Fractured mandible
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the mandible.

Name: Fractured orbit of skull
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the orbit of skull.

Name: Fractured larynx
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the larynx.

Name: Fractured rib
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the rib.

Name: obsolete Fractured pelvic region of trunk
Metatarsal fracture
Def: A partial or complete breakage of a metatarsal bone.

Name: Fractured manual digit
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the manual digit.

Name: Fractured talus
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the talus.

Name: Fractured maxilla
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the maxilla.

Name: Fractured vertebra
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the vertebra.

Name: Fractured cervical vertebra
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the cervical vertebra.

Name: Fractured lumbar vertebra
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the lumbar vertebra.

Name: Fractured fused sacrum
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the fused sacrum.

Name: Fractured metacarpophalangeal joint
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the metacarpophalangeal joint.

Name: Fractured distal phalanx of manus
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the distal phalanx of manus.

Name: Fractured middle phalanx of pes
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the middle phalanx of pes.

Name: Fractured distal phalanx of manual digit 2

Neural tube defect
Def: A neural tube defect arises when the neural tube, the embryonic precursor of the brain and spinal cord, fails to close during neurulation. The cranial region (anencephaly) or the low spine (open spina bifida; myelomeningocele) are most commonly affected although, in the severe NTD craniorachischisis, almost the entire neural tube remains open, from midbrain to low spine.

Name: Aplasia of lymphatic vessels
Def: Aplasia (absence) of the lymphatic vessels.

Name: Abnormal substantia nigra morphology
Def: A structural anomaly of the substantia nigra, which is a midbrain dopaminergic nucleus which has a critical role in modulating motor movement and reward functions as part of the basal ganglia circuitry.

Name: obsolete Abnormal morphology of the radius
Abnormal peripheral nerve morphology by anatomical site
Def: Abnormal morphology of a specific peripheral nerve

Name: Decreased urine bicarbonate concentration
Def: Abnormally decreased concentration of hydrogencarbonate in the urine.

Name: obsolete Elevated serum long-chain fatty acids
Congenital malformation of the left heart
Def: Defect or defects of the morphogenesis of the left heart identifiable at birth.

Name: Narrow palpebral fissure
Def: Reduction in the vertical distance between the upper and lower eyelids.

Name: Abnormal mediastinum morphology
Def: Any structural anomaly of the central compartment of the thoracic cavity.

Name: Microlissencephaly
Def: Severe microcephaly and lissencephaly with granular surfaces with immature cortical plate, reduced in thickness, with focal polymicrogyria and immature small neurons with rare processes, intermingled with a considerable number of glial elements.
Comment: This is a severe phenotype that can be diagnosed at the fetopathological level, by which a diagnosis of lissencephaly can be made by the examination of the 6 layers of the cortex. Examination may show 3 layers or an extremely thin cortical plate consistent with the diagnosis of lissencephaly.

Name: Eosinophilic fasciitis
Def: Inflammation and thickening (localized fibrosis) of the fascia, the tissue under the skin and over the muscle, typically associated with a build up of eosinophils in the muscles and tissues.

Name: Elevated urinary 3-aminoisobutyric acid
Def: An increased amount of 3-aminoisobutyric acid in the urine.

Name: Gastric lymphoma
Def: Lymphoma that originates in the stomach itself.
Comment: An uncommon condition, that accounts for less than 15% of gastric malignancies and about 2% of all lymphomas.

Name: Osteolysis involving bones of the upper limbs
Abnormal circulating lactate dehydrogenase concentration
Def: A deviation from the normal serum concentration/activity of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), which catalyzes the reduction of pyruvate to form lactate.

Name: Reduced circulating lactate dehydrogenase concentration
Def: Concentration of lactate dehydrogenase in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
Comment: Lactate dehydrogenase catalyzes the interconversion of lactate and pyruvate.

Name: Decreased circulating complement C4 concentration
Def: Concentration of the complement component C4 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Decreased circulating complement C4a concentration
Def: Concentration of the complement component C4a in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Decreased circulating complement C4b concentration
Def: Concentration of the complement component C4b in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating acylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of acylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Reduced insulin like growth factor binding protein acid labile subunit concentration
Def: An abnormally decreased concentration of insulin like growth factor binding protein acid labile subunit level in the blood circulation.
Comment: Insulin-like growth factor binding protein, acid labile subunit, also known as IGFALS, is a protein which in humans is encoded by the IGFALS gene. {xref="wikipedia"}
Synonym: Decreased levels of acid labile subunit
Reduced insulin like growth factor binding protein acid labile subunit level

Name: HbS hemoglobin
Def: Presence of an abnormal type of hemoglobin characterized by the substitution of a glutamic acid residue at position 7 following the initial methionine residue by a valine (the mutation causative of sickle cell disease). The mutation promotes the polymerization of the HbS under conditions of low oxygen concentration. HbS can be identified by multiple methodologies including hemoglobin electrophoresis and high-performance liquid chromatography.

Name: Increased HbA2 hemoglobin
Def: An elevated concentration in the blood of hemoglobin A2 (HbA2), which is a normal variant of hemoglobin A that consists of two alpha and two delta chains and is normally present at low levels in adults but may be increased in beta thalassemia.

Name: Abnormal DLCO
Def: An abnormal amount of oxygen passes into the blood from the lungs and/or an abnormal amount of carbon dioxide passes from the blood into the lungs.
Comment: Inhaled CO is used for this test due to its high affinity for hemoglobin (200-250 times that of oxygen). During a ten-second breath-hold, DLCO measures uptake of CO per unit time per mm of driving pressure of CO (cc of CO/sec/mm of Hg).
Synonym: Abnormal transfer factor of the lung for carbon monoxide

Name: Increased DLCO
Def: Increased ability of the lungs to transfer gas from inspired air to the bloodstream as measured by the diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide (DLCO) test.
Comment: Factors that can increase the DLCO include polycythaemia, asthma (can also have normal DLCO) and increased pulmonary blood volume as occurs in exercise. Other factors are left to right intracardiac shunting, and alveolar hemorrhage.

Name: Decreased DLCO
Def: Reduced ability of the lungs to transfer gas from inspired air to the bloodstream as measured by the diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide (DLCO) test.
Comment: DLCO is decreased in any condition which affects the effective alveolar surface area

Name: Abnormality of the brachial nerve plexus
Def: Any abnormality of the brachial nerve plexus.

Name: Abnormality of the lumbosacral nerve plexus
Def: Any abnormality of the lumbosacral nerve plexus.

Name: Brachial plexus neuropathy
Comment: Related to ticket: https://github.com/obophenotype/human-phenotype-ontology/issues/484

Name: Tiger tail banding
Def: An abnormal appearance of hair under polarizing microscopy (using crossed polarizers), whereby hair shafts show striking alternating bright and dark bands, often referred to as tiger tail banding.

Name: Abnormal circulating alpha-fetoprotein concentration
Def: Concentration of alpha-fetoprotein in the blood circulation outside normal limits.

Name: Decreased circulating alpha-fetoprotein concentration
Def: Concentration of alpha-fetoprotein in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Abnormality of the testis size
Def: An anomaly of the size of the testicle (the male gonad).

Name: Hyperkeratotic papule
Def: A circumscribed, solid elevation of skin with no visible fluid, varying in size from a pinhead to less than 10mm in diameter at the widest point that is composed of localized hyperkeratosis (the latter may be demonstrated histopathologically).

Name: Aplasia/hypoplasia involving bones of the extremities
Increased PIVKA-II
Def: Des-gamma carboxyprothrombin (DCP) or pro-thrombin induced by vitamin K absence-II (PIVKA-II) is an abnormal prothrombin protein that is increased in the serum of patients with HCC. Generation of DCP is thought to be a result of an acquired defect in the post- translational carboxylation of the prothrombin precursor in malignant cells.
Comment: PIVKA-II can be measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).
Synonym: Increased prothrombin induced by vitamin K absence-II

Name: Serositis
Def: Inflammation in any serous cavity.

Name: Thin eyebrow
Def: Decreased diameter of eyebrow hairs.

Name: Sparse eyebrow
Def: Decreased density/number of eyebrow hairs.
Comment: Sparseness can be regional (medial, central, lateral) or total.

Name: Distal femoral metaphyseal irregularity
Def: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of the distal metaphysis of the femur.

Name: Decreased proportion of CD3-positive T cells
Def: Any abnormality in the proportion of CD3-positive T cells relative to the total number of T cells.
Synonym: Decreased proportion of CD3+ T cells

Name: Abnormality of body mass index
Def: Anomaly in the weight-to-height squared ratio, calculated by dividing the individual's weight in kilograms by the square of the individual's height in meters and used as an indicator of obesity and underweight compared to averages.

Name: Decreased body mass index
Def: Abnormally decreased weight-to-height squared ratio, calculated by dividing the individual's weight in kilograms by the square of the individual's height in meters and used as an indicator of underweight compared to averages.

Name: Limb myoclonus
Comment: Limb myoclonus was noted in Early myoclonic encephalopathy. See PMID:27789573

Name: Knee joint hypermobility
Def: The ability of the knee to move past its normal range of motion, (knee hyperextension is greater than 10 degrees).

Name: Clinical relevance
Def: Subontology for annotating phenotypic features as distinctive or minor findings in patients. The subontology is intended to be used to annotate subjective clinical impressions of whether a certain finding is important for the differential diagnosis.

Name: Distinctive finding
Def: In clinical parlance, findings are occasionally interpreted as being distinctive or minor, reflecting a subjective clinical impression of the importance of a feature for the differential diagnosis. A minor finding is taken to be one that is likely to have high utility in distinguishing the correct diagnosis from other candidates in the differential.

Name: Minor finding
Def: In clinical parlance, findings are occasionally interpreted as being distinctive or minor, reflecting a subjective clinical impression of the importance of a feature for the differential diagnosis. A minor finding is taken to be one that is unlikely to help distinguish the correct diagnosis from other candidates in the differential.

Name: Anorgasmia
Def: Inability of individual to reach orgasm.

Name: Increased libido
Def: Elevated sexual desire.

Name: Decreased libido
Def: Decreased sexual desire.

Name: Hand pain
Def: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort localized to the hand.

Name: Pain in head and neck region
Bradypnea
Def: Bradypnea is referring to breathing that is abnormally slow.

Name: Abnormal cervical spine morphology
Def: Any morphological abnormality of the cervical vertebral column.

Name: Early onset of sexual maturation
Def: An early onset of puberty, in this case early does not refer to precocious.

Name: Malignant mesothelioma
Def: Malignant mesothelioma is a form of cancer that originates from the cells of the mesothelium, a thin tissue layer surrounding the body's internal organs. Malignant mesothelioma is almost exclusively caused by asbestos exposure, pleural mesothelioma being the most common form, affecting the lining of the lungs called the pleura. Other forms such as perioneal-, percardial- or testicular- mesothelioma are much rarer.

Name: Pleural mesothelioma
Def: A malignant mesothelioma originating from cells of the pleura (the thin layer of mesothelium lining the lungs). Pleural mesothelioma is the most common form of mesothelioma.

Name: Peritoneal mesothelioma
Def: A Malignant mesothelioma originating from cells of the peritoneum (the thin layer of mesothelium lining the abdomen). Peritoneal mesothelioma is the second most common form of mesothelioma after pleural mesothelioma.

Name: Pericardial mesothelioma
Def: A Malignant mesothelioma originating from cells of the pericardium (the thin layer of mesothelium lining the heart).

Name: Testicular mesothelioma
Def: A Malignant mesothelioma of the testis.
Comment: Testicular mesothelioma originates from cells of the tunica vaginalis (the thin layer of mesothelium surrounding the testicles). Testicular mesothelioma is the rarest form of mesothelioma.

Name: Neoplasm of the central nervous system
Def: A neoplasm of the central nervous system.
Synonym: Neoplasia of the central nervous system
Tumors of the central nervous system
Tumours of the central nervous system

Name: Neoplasm of the peripheral nervous system
Def: A benign or malignant neoplasm (tumor) of the peripheral nervous system.
Synonym: Tumor of the peripheral nervous system
Tumour of the peripheral nervous system

Name: Schwannoma
Def: A benign nerve sheath tumor composed of Schwann cells.
Comment: Glial cells are cells that support nerve cells. Schwann cells wrap around the axon to form the myelin sheath. Schwann cells are involved in many important aspects of peripheral nerve biology; the conduction of nervous impulses along axons, nerve development and regeneration, trophic support for neurons, production of the nerve extracellular matrix and presentation of antigens to T-lymphocytes. Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT), Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS), schwannomatosis and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) are all neuropathies involving Schwann cells.

Name: Neoplasm of the eye
Def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the eye.

Name: Neoplasm of the breast
Def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the breast.

Name: Epiretinal membrane
Def: An epiretinal membrane is a thin sheet of fibrous tissue that can develop on the surface of the macular area of the retina and cause a disturbance in vision. An epiretinal membrane area can develop on the thin macular area of the retin. An epiretinal membrane is also sometimes called a macular pucker, premacular fibrosis, surface wrinkling retinopathy or cellophane maculopathy.

Name: Stahl ear
Def: The presence of a supernumerary, i.e. third, crus of the helix in the helix, arising at or above the normal bifurcation of the antihelix.
Comment: The helix is often poorly formed. Four types have been recognized in the surgical literature [Yamada and Fukuda, 1980].

Name: Abnormal mesentery morphology
Def: Folds of membranous tissue (peritoneum, mesothelium) attached to the wall of the abdomen and enclosing viscera. Examples include the mesentery for the small intestine; the transverse mesocolon, which attaches the transverse portion of the colon to the back wall of the abdomen; and the mesosigmoid, which enfolds the sigmoid portion of the colon. Cells of the same embryologic origin also surround the other organs of the body such as the lungs (pleura) or the heart (pericardium).

Name: Capsular cataract
Def: A cataract that affects the capsule of the lens.

Name: Nuclear cataract
Def: A nuclear cataract is an opacity or clouding that develops in the lens nucleus. That is, a nuclear cataract is one that is located in the center of the lens. The nucleus tends to darken changing from clear to yellow and sometimes brown.

Name: Cortical cataract
Def: A cataract which affects the layer of the lens surrounding the nucleus, i.e., the lens cortex. It is identified by its unique wedge or spoke appearance.

Name: Posterior capsular cataract
Def: A cataract which is found in the back outer layer of the lens. This type often develops more rapidly.

Name: Cerebral palsy
Def: Cerebral palsy describes a group of permanent disorders of the development of movement and posture, causing activity limitation, that are attributed to nonprogressive disturbances that occurred in the developing fetal or infant brain. The motor disorders of cerebral palsy are often accompanied by disturbances of sensation, perception, cognition, communication, and behavior, by epilepsy, and by secondary musculoskeletal problems.

Name: Abnormality of movement
Def: An abnormality of movement with a neurological basis characterized by changes in coordination and speed of voluntary movements.
Comment: Movement disorders are characterized by the phenotypic abnormalities including abnormal involuntary movements, akathisia, akinesia, athetosis, ataxia, ballismus, bradykinesia, chorea, dyskinesia, dystonia, and myoclonus tics, tremor, spasms, and stereotypy.

Name: Recurrent hand flapping
Def: A type of repetitive behavior in which the affected individual repeatedly waves the hands and/or arms rhythmically.

Name: Conspicuously happy disposition
Def: An unusually happy demeanor over time, which can also be observed during inappropriate situations that should, for example, cause distress, fear, or anger.

Name: Overfriendliness
Def: A form of hypersociability that presents as mostly inappropriate friendliness towards others.
Comment: In some cases, overfriendliness may be dangerous for affected children, for example, if young children follow strangers without restriction.
Synonym: Excessive eagerness to interact with others

Name: Arteriovenous malformation
Def: An anomalous configuration of blood vessels that shunts arterial blood directly into veins without passing through the capillaries.

Name: Recurrent pancreatitis
Def: A recurrent form of pancreatitis.

Name: Ectopic thyroid
Def: Mislocalised thyroid gland.
Comment: An aberrant or ectopic thyroid gland may occur anywhere along the path of initial descent of the thyroid. A total failure to descend contrasts with the incomplete descent of the thyroid, in which case the resulting final resting point of the gland may be high in the neck or just below the hyoid bone. Apart from an abnormal descent, accessory thyroid tissue can also occur, arising from remnants of the thyroglossal duct anywhere along the path of the thyroglossal duct tract.

Name: Lingual thyroid
Def: An aberrant thyroid gland or Ectopic thyroid located at the base of the tongue, just posterior to the foramen cecum as a result of a failure of the thyroid to descend.
Comment: A lingual thyroid is the most common form of an aberrant thyroid gland.

Name: Accessory ectopic thyroid tissue
Def: Accessory ectopic thyroid tissue arising from remnants of the thyroglossal duct anywhere along the path of the thyroglossal duct tract.
Comment: While the accessory thyroid tissue may be functional, it is generally insufficient for normal function if the main thyroid gland is entirely removed.

Name: Neoplasm of the thyroid gland
Def: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the thyroid gland.

Name: Tics
Def: Repeated, individually recognizable, intermittent movements or movement fragments that are almost always briefly suppressible and are usually associated with awareness of an urge to perform the movement.
Comment: Tics can be invisible to the observer, such as abdominal tensing or toe crunching. Common motor and phonic tics are, respectively, eye blinking and throat clearing. Movements of other movement disorders (for example, chorea, dystonia, myoclonus) must be distinguished from tics. Other conditions, such as autism and stereotypic movement disorder, also include movements which may be confused with tics. Tics must also be distinguished from the compulsions of OCD and from seizure activity. Tics may increase as a result of stress, fatigue, boredom, or high-energy emotions, which can include negative emotions, such as anxiety, but positive emotions as well, such as excitement or anticipation. Relaxation may result in a tic increase (for instance, watching television or using a computer), while concentration on an absorbing activity often leads to a decrease in tics.

Name: Motor tics
Def: Movement-based tics affecting discrete muscle groups.

Name: Phonic tics
Def: Tics are defined as movements or sounds that resemble physiological motor behaviors, but are typically inopportune to social context and appear sudden, repetitive, and often exaggerated. Tic vocalizations commonly termed vocal or phonic tics may include any possible sound (eg, sniffing, coughing, throat clearing, whistling, or grunting), word, or sentence and are most commonly encountered within the spectrum of primary tic disorders, as Tourette syndrome.
Comment: In Tourette syndrome (TS), affected individuals have tics, including phonic and vocal behaviors, that are typically preceded by premonitory urges and can be suppressed voluntarily. Individuals with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) may also present with vocal tics. However, in ASD premonitory urges and overall vocal tic awareness may be reduced compared to people with primary tic disorders and TS. Phonic tics have been described in a variety of other disorders including Klinefelter, fragile X, and Adams-Oliver syndrome, monosomy 9p and trisomy 16p, neurodegenerative syndromes such as Huntington disease. Furthermore, chorea-acanthocytosis because of VPS13A mutations, Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis frontotemporal dementia overlap syndromes, progressive supranuclear palsy, and pantothenate kinase-associated neurodegeneration may present with vocal tics. Neurometabolic disorders such as Wilson's disease or phenylketonuria, focal brain lesions, infectious, and other autoimmune diseases are additional causes of vocal tics. Finally, phonic or vocal tics may also be drug-induced, either directly related to the acute effects of drugs (e.g., cocaine) or as a long-term consequence, such as in tardive tic disorders.

Name: Pseudo-fractures
Def: A band of bone material of decreased density forming alongside the surface of the cortical bone with thickening of the periosteum. Callus formation in the affected area is common and gives the appearance of a false fracture.
Comment: Typical sites of involvement are the axillary margins of the scapula, ribs, pubic rami, proximal ends of the femur and ulna. On x-rays pseudo-fractures appear as a lucent line about 1 -2 cm wide, vertical to the cortex and are pathognomonic of osteomalacia, seen on the concave side and are also seen in Paget disease on the convex side of the bone.

Name: Abnormality of the scalp hair
Def: An abnormality of the hair of head.

Name: Slow-growing scalp hair
Def: Scalp hair whose growth is slower than normal.

Name: Thickened cortex of bones
Def: An Abnormality of cortical bone leading to an abnormal thickness of the cortex of affected bones.

Name: Broad 2nd toe
Def: A broad appearance of the second toe.
Comment: Note that an apparent broad appearance might be due to a hidden duplication.

Name: Broad 3rd toe
Def: A broad appearance of the third toe.

Name: Broad 4th toe
Def: A broad appearance of the fourth toe.

Name: Broad 5th toe
Def: A broad appearance of the fifth toe.

Synonym: Bracket shaped end part of 2nd toe bone

Name: Cone-shaped epiphyses of the 2nd toe
Synonym: Cone-shaped end part of the 2nd toe bone

Name: Enlarged epiphyses of the 2nd toe
Synonym: Enlarged end part of the 2nd toe bone

Name: Fragmentation of the epiphyses of the 2nd toe
Synonym: Fragmentation of the end part of the 2nd toe bone

Name: Irregular epiphyses of the 2nd toe
Synonym: Irregular end part of the 2nd toe bone

Name: Ivory epiphyses of the 2nd toe
Def: Epiphyses of the 2nd toe are hard and dense like ivory. Such an epiphysis has a uniformly dense appearance on radiographs.
Synonym: Increased bone density of end part of the 2nd toe

Name: Small epiphyses of the 2nd toe
Synonym: Small end part of the 2nd toe bone

Name: Stippling of the epiphyses of the 2nd toe
Def: The presence of abnormal punctate (speckled, dot-like) calcifications in the epiphyses of the 2nd toe.
Synonym: Speckled calcifications in the end part of the 2nd toe bone
