Epileptic encephalaopathy is characterized by (1) electrographic EEG paroxysmal activity that is often aggressive, (2) seizures that are usually multiform and intractable, (3) cognitive, behavioral and neurological deficits that may be relentless, and (4) sometimes early death.
Comment: Seizures alone without any underlying neurologic or medical illness can be the sole cause of encephalopathy. Patients with seizures as a cause or consequence of encephalopathy present with a wide variety of neurologic symptoms from mild reduction or alteration of consciousness to coma. Findings on neurologic exam are often nonfocal, nonspecific, and not predictive of the presence of seizures. Patients may or may not have subtle motor findings accompanying the presentation of encephalopathy. Signs range from very focal findings, such as nystagmus, eye flutter, blinking, and eye deviation to more widespread signs, such as myoclonus, tremulousness, and autonomic instability.

Name: Megaloblastic erythroid hyperplasia
Synonym: Bone marrow biopsy shows megaloblastic erythroid hyperplasia

Name: Mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation
Def: An increase of medial mucoid extracellular matrix creating translamellar and/or intralamellar expansions including extracellular pools as noted on an H&E stain and/or a stain to highlight extracellular matrix material (Movat's pentachrome, Alcian blue, etc.).
Comment: MEMA replaces a variety of terms used in the past such as cystic medial necrosis, cystonecrosis, cystic degeneration, mucoid degeneration which, while generally understood by pathologists, are inaccurate. This histopathology can be subclassified and graded according to distribution, severity, and/or whether it crosses over multiple lamellar units as described. The grading should be reported as mild/moderate/severe and the distribution should be reported as focal, multifocal, or extensive.
Synonym: Cystic medial necrosis of the aorta

Name: Neuronal loss in basal ganglia
Def: A reduction in the number of nerve cells in the basal ganglia.
Comment: See Fig. 11 in PMID:13729575.

Name: Abnormal liver function tests during pregnancy
Synonym: Abnormal liver function tests during pregnancy
Abnormal liver function tests during pregnancy, resolves postpartum

Name: CSF lymphocytic pleiocytosis
Def: An increased lymphocyte count in the cerebrospinal fluid.

Name: Increased serum bile acid concentration during pregnancy
Synonym: Increased serum bile acid concentration during pregnancy, resolves

Name: Cutaneous mastocytosis
Def: Multifocal dense infiltrates of mast cells in cutaneous tissue.

Name: Agenesis of lateral incisor
Synonym: Failure of development of lateral incisor

Name: Agenesis of mandibular lateral incisor
Synonym: Failure of development of mandibular lateral incisor

Name: Agenesis of permanent mandibular lateral incisor
Synonym: Absence of adult mandibular lateral incisor
Absence of permanent mandibular lateral incisor
Failure of development of permanent mandibular lateral incisor

Name: Agenesis of primary mandibular lateral incisor
Synonym: Absence of deciduous mandibular lateral incisor
Absence of lower front baby tooth
Absence of primary mandibular lateral incisor
Agenesis of deciduous mandibular lateral incisor
Failure of development of deciduous mandibular lateral incisor
Failure of development of primary mandibular lateral incisor

Name: Agenesis of maxillary incisor
Synonym: Failure of development of maxillary incisor
Failure of development of upper incisor

Name: Agenesis of mandibular incisor
Synonym: Failure of development of mandibular incisor

Name: Tall chin
Def: Increased vertical distance from the vermillion border of the lower lip to the inferior-most point of the chin.

Name: Chin with vertical crease
Def: Vertical crease fold situated below the vermilion border of the lower lip and above the fatty pad of the chin with the face at rest.
Comment: The vertical shape must be distinguished from H-shaped crease of the chin.

Name: Extra concha fold
Def: Folds or ridges within the concha that are distinct from the crus helix.

Name: Focal absence of the external ear
Def: Absence of a localized portion of the ear that cannot be described by a more precise term (e.g., absent ear lobe).

Name: Long ear
Def: Median longitudinal ear length greater than two SD above the mean determined by the maximal distance from the superior aspect to the inferior aspect of the external ear.
Comment: The commonly used term Macrotia is a bundled term comprising increased length and width (surface area).

Name: Short ear
Def: Median longitudinal ear length less than two SD above the mean determined by the maximal distance from the superior aspect to the inferior aspect of the external ear.
Comment: The commonly used term Microtia is a bundled term comprising decreased length and width (surface area).

Name: Polymenorrhea
Def: Frequent menses; menstrual cycles lasting less than 21 days.

Name: Menometrorrhagia
Def: Prolonged/excessive menses and bleeding at irregular intervals.

Name: Abnormal vomer morphology
Def: An abnormality of the vomer.

Name: Abnormality of ophthalmic artery
Def: Abnormality of the first branch of the internal carotid artery.
Comment: The ophthalmic artery (OA) is the first branch of the internal carotid artery distal to the cavernous sinus. Branches of the OA supply all the structures in the orbit as well as some structures in the nose, face and meninges.

Name: Abnormality of the peripheral nervous system
Def: Any abnormality of the part of the nervous system that consists of the nerves and ganglia outside of the brain and spinal cord.
Synonym: Abnormality of the peripheral nervous system

Name: Abnormality of the somatic nervous system
Def: Any abnormality of the part of the peripheral nervous system associated with sensation and skeletal muscle voluntary control of body movements.
Comment: The SoNS consists of afferent and efferent nerves. Afferent nerves are responsible for relaying sensation to the central nervous system; efferent nerves are responsible for stimulating muscle contraction, including all the non-sensory neurons connected with skeletal muscles and skin.

Name: Abnormality of somatic nerve plexus
Def: Any abnormality of the somatic nerve plexus.

Name: Abnormality of masticatory muscle
Def: Any abnormality of the masticatory muscle.

Name: Abnormal mouth floor morphology
Def: Any abnormality of the mouth floor.
Synonym: Abnormality of the floor of mouth

Name: Abnormality of the submandibular region
Def: Any abnormality of the submandibular region, the region between the mandible and the hyoid bone contains the submandibular and sublingual glands, suprahyoid muscles, submandibular ganglion, and lingual artery.

Name: Abnormal ganglion morphology
Def: An abnormality of nerve cell cluster or a group of nerve cell bodies located in the autonomic nervous system.

Name: Abnormal peripheral nervous system ganglion morphology
Def: An abnormality of nerve cell cluster or a group of nerve cell bodies located in the peripheral autonomic nervous system.
Synonym: Abnormality of ganglion of peripheral nervous system

Name: Abnormal cranial ganglion morphology
Def: An abnormality of nerve cell cluster or a group of nerve cell bodies located in the autonomic nervous system of the cranium.

Name: Otitis externa
Def: Inflammation or infection of the external auditory canal (EAC), the auricle, or both.

Name: Recurrent ear infections
Def: Increased susceptibility to ear infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of ear infections.

Name: Epigastric pain
Def: Pain that is localized to the region of the upper abdomen immediately below the ribs.

Name: Fish odor
Def: Body odor characterized by an offensive body odor and the smell of rotting fish due to the excessive excretion of trimethylamine (TMA) in the urine, sweat, and breath of affected individuals.

Name: Musty odor
Def: Pungent body odor.

Name: Vaginal fish odor
Def: A fish odor in the vaginal area, that is characteristic of bacterial vaginosis (BV), and is due to trimethylamine (TMA).

Name: Abnormal distribution of cell junction proteins in buccal mucosal cells
Def: An anomalous amount or location of cell junction proteins such as plakoglobin or Cx43.
Comment: Buccal mucosal cells are harvested from the oral mucosa in the region of the cheek, and can be used as a surrogate tissue to measure cell junction proteins because it is difficult to obtain cells from a tissue of interest such as the myocardium. Cell junction proteins, such as plakoglobin and the major cardiac gap junction protein Cx43 may have an abnormal distribution in diseases such as arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.

Name: Abnormal periodontium morphology
Def: Any abnormality of the periodontium.

Name: Alveolar bone loss around teeth
Def: A decrease in the amount of alveolar bone around the root of a tooth.

Name: Recurrent oral herpes
Def: Recurrent episodes of oral herpes, typically characterized by blisters or ulcers on the gums, lips and/or tongue caused by herpes virus.

Name: Cleft lip
Def: A gap in the lip or lips.

Name: Submucous cleft of soft and hard palate
Def: Soft and hard-palate submucous clefts are characterized by bony defects in the midline of the soft and hard palate that are covered by the lining (ie mucous membrane) of the roof of the mouth.

Name: Unilateral alveolar cleft of maxilla
Def: One sided alveolar cleft of the maxilla.
Comment: Consider adding additional annotations to specify the completeness of the cleft using 'Incomplete cleft maxillary alveolar ridge' (HP:5201007) or 'Complete cleft maxillary alveolar ridge' (HP:5201008).

Name: Bilateral alveolar cleft of maxilla
Def: Nonmidline alveolar cleft of the maxilla.
Comment: Consider adding additional annotations to specify the completeness of the cleft using 'Incomplete cleft maxillary alveolar ridge' (HP:5201007) or 'Complete cleft maxillary alveolar ridge' (HP:5201008).

Name: Abnormal T cell activation
Def: Any abnormality in the activation of T cells, i.e. the change in morphology and behavior of a mature or immature T cell resulting from exposure to a mitogen, cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or an antigen for which it is specific.

Name: Abnormal liver morphology
Def: Any structural anomaly of the bile-secreting organ that is important for detoxification, for fat, carbohydrate, and protein metabolism, and for glycogen storage.

Name: Abnormal neural tube morphology
Def: Any structural anomaly of the hollow epithelial tube found on the dorsal side of the vertebrate embryo that develops into the central nervous system (i.e. brain and spinal cord).

Name: Abnormal radial ray morphology
Comment: An abnormality of the radial ray; the thumb bones and 1st meta carpel. {xref="https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9353-5498"}

Name: Decreased level of 1,5 anhydroglucitol in serum
Def: A decrease in the level of 1,5 anhydroglucitol in the serum. 1,5-Anhydrosorbitol is a validated marker of short-term glycemic control. This substance is derived mainly from food, is well absorbed in the intestine, and is distributed to all organs and tissues.

Name: Increased level of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaric acid in urine
Def: The concentration of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaric acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Increased level of allantoin in serum
Def: An increase in the level of allantoin in the serum.

Name: Elevated circulating gamma-aminobutyric acid concentration
Def: An increase in the level of Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) in the blood circulation.
Comment: Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) is the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter known to counterbalance the action of the excitatory neurotransmitter glutamate.
Synonym: Increased level of GABA in serum
Increased level of gamma-aminobutyric acid in serum

Name: Decreased circulating GABA concentration
Def: A decrease in the level of GABA in the serum.
Synonym: Decreased level of gamma-aminobutyric acid in serum

Name: Decreased level of erythritol in urine
Def: A decrease in the level of erythritol in the urine.

Name: Decreased CSF erythritol concentration
Def: Concentration of erythritol in the cerebrospinal fluid below the lower limit of normal.
Synonym: Decreased level of erythritol in cerebrospinal fluid

Name: Increased level of D-threitol in plasma
Def: An increase in the level of D-threitol in the plasma.
Comment: D-threitol, a C4-polyol, is the main end product of D-xylose metabolism in humans.

Name: Increased CSF D-threitol concentration
Def: The concentration of D-threitol in the cerebrospinal fluid is above the upper limit of normal.
Comment: D-threitol, a C4-polyol, is the main end product of D-xylose metabolism in humans.
Synonym: Increased level of D-threitol in cerebrospinal fluid
Increased level of D-threitol in CSF

Name: Increased level of D-threitol in urine
Def: An increase in the level of D-threitol in the urine.
Comment: D-threitol, a C4-polyol, is the main end product of D-xylose metabolism in humans.

Name: Decreased level of D-mannose in urine
Def: A decrease in the level of D-mannose in the urine.
Comment: D-Mannose is the 2-epimer of glucose.

Name: Increased level of galactitol in plasma
Def: An increase in the level of galactitol in the plasma.

Name: Increased level of galactitol in urine
Def: An increase in the level of galactitol in the urine.
Comment: Galactitol is the reduction product of galactose.

Name: Increased level of galactonate in red blood cells
Def: An increase in the level of galactonate in the red blood cells.
Synonym: Increased level of galactonate in erythrocytes
Increased level of galactonate in RBCs

Name: Increased level of galactitol in red blood cells
Def: An increase in the level of galactitol in the red blood cells.
Synonym: Increased level of galactitol in erythrocytes

Name: Increased level of hippuric acid in blood
Def: An increase in the level of hippuric acid in the blood.
Synonym: Increased level of N-benzoylglycine in blood

Name: Increased level of hippuric acid in urine
Def: An increase in the level of hippuric acid in the urine.
Synonym: Increased level of N-benzoylglycine in urine

Name: Increased level of L-fucose in urine
Def: An increase in the level of L-fucose in the urine.
Comment: Fucose is a hexose deoxy sugar with the chemical formula C6H12O5.

Name: obsolete Increased level of L-glutamic acid in blood
Increased level of propylene glycol in blood
Def: An increase in the level of propylene glycol in the blood.
Synonym: Increased level of propane-1,2-diol in blood

Name: Increased level of ribitol in urine
Def: An increase in the level of ribitol in the urine. Ribotol is a crystalline pentose alcohol (C5H12O5) and is a metabolic end product formed by the reduction of ribose.

Name: Increased CSF ribitol concentration
Def: The concentration of ribitol in the cerebrospinal fluid is above the upper limit of normal.
Synonym: Increased level of ribitol in cerebrospinal fluid

Name: Increased level of ribose in urine
Def: An increase in the level of ribose in the urine.
Comment: Ribose is a pentose monosaccharide.

Name: Increased CSF ribose concentration
Def: The concentration of ribose in the cerebrospinal fluid is above the upper limit of normal.
Synonym: Increased level of ribose in cerebrospinal fluid
Increased level of ribose in CSF

Name: Increased level of xylitol in urine
Def: An increase in the level of xylitol in the urine.

Name: Increased CSF xylitol concentration
Def: The concentration of xylitol in the cerebrospinal fluid is above the upper limit of normal.
Synonym: Increased level of xylitol in cerebrospinal fluid
Increased level of xylitol in CSF

Name: Increased level of L-pyroglutamic acid in urine
Def: An increase in the level of L-pyroglutamic acid in the urine.

Name: Chronic idiopathic urticaria
Def: Urticaria characterized by spontaneously recurring hives for 6 weeks or longer.

Name: Physical urticaria
Def: Urticaria caused by physical agents, such as heat, cold, light, friction.

Name: Cold urticaria
Def: Urticaria may be caused by cold temperatures.

Name: Aquagenic urticaria
Def: A form of physical urticaria, in which contact with water, regardless of its temperature and source, evokes pruritic follicular wheals on the skin.

Name: Solar urticaria
Def: Urticaria in response to exposure to ultraviolet-A (UVA), ultraviolet-B (UVB), visible and rarely infrared light.

Name: Vibratory urticaria
Def: Urticaria in response to dermal vibration, with coincident degranulation of mast cells and increased histamine levels in serum.

Name: Exercise induced anaphylaxis
Def: Anaphylaxis after physical activity.

Name: Abnormal circulating biotinidase concentration
Def: An abnormality in the biotinidase level, an enzyme that releases biotin from biocytin, the product of biotin-dependent carboxylases degradation.

Name: Decreased circulating biotinidase concentration
Def: Concentration of biotinidase in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal. Biotidinase is an enzyme that releases biotin from biocytin, the product of biotin-dependent carboxylases degradation.

Name: Elevated circulating biotinidase concentration
Def: Concentration of biotinidase in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. Biotidinase is an enzyme that releases biotin from biocytin, the product of biotin-dependent carboxylases degradation.

Name: Eosinophilic infiltration in the stomach mucosa
Def: Infiltration of eosinophils in the stomach mucosa, that is diagnosed by an upper endoscopy and microscopy that shows more than 20 eosinophils per high-power field in association with peripheral eosinophilia and the absence of secondary cause of eosinophilia.

Name: Idiopathic anaphylaxis
Def: A rare form of anaphylaxis for which triggers cannot be identified despite a detailed history and careful diagnostic assessment.

Name: Drug-induced anaphylaxis
Def: A form of anaphylaxis that is triggered by intake of drugs or medications.

Name: Eosinophilic infiltration of the esophagus
Def: Infiltration of numerous eosinophils (usually greater than 15 per high power field) into the squamous epithelium of the esophagus, and layering of eosinophils on the surface layer of the esophagus.

Name: Eosinophilic microabscess formation in the esophagus
Def: The formation of small localized collection of eosinophiles (an eosinophilic microabscess) in the esophagus. Usually clusters of greater than or equal to 4 eosinophils are seen, that appear as exudates or white spots or white plaques.
Synonym: Eosinophilic micro-abscess formation in the esophagus
Eosinophilic micro-abscess formation in the oesophagus
Eosinophilic microabscess formation in the esophagus

Name: Increased level of methylsuccinic acid in urine
Def: The concentration of methylsuccinic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
Synonym: Increased level of pyrotartaric acid in urine

Name: Increased level of myristic acid in serum
Def: An increase in the level of myristic acid in the serum.
Synonym: Increased level of tetradecanoic acid in serum

Name: Increased level of N-acetylneuraminic acid in urine
Def: An increase in the level of N-acetylneuraminic acid in the urine.
Comment: N-Acetylneuraminic acid (Neu5Ac or NANA) is the predominant sialic acid found in human cells.
Synonym: Increased level of NANA in urine
Increased level of Neu5Ac in urine

Name: Increased level of N-acetylneuraminic acid in fibroblasts
Def: An increase in the level of N-acetylneuraminic acid in cultured fibroblasts.
Synonym: Increased level of NANA in fibroblasts
Increased level of Neu5Ac in fibroblasts
Increased level of sialic acid in fibroblasts

Name: obsolete Increased urine O-phosphoethanolamine level
Synonym: Increased level of O-phosphoethanolamine in urine

Name: Defective interstrand cross-link repair
Def: A defect in the of the process of interstrand cross-link repair: removal of a DNA interstrand crosslink (a covalent attachment of DNA bases on opposite strands of the DNA) and restoration of the DNA. DNA interstrand crosslinks occur when both strands of duplex DNA are covalently tethered together (e.g. by an exogenous or endogenous agent), thus preventing the strand unwinding necessary for essential DNA functions such as transcription and replication.

Name: Abnormal morphology of the chest musculature
Def: Any abnormality of the chest muscles.

Name: Abnormality of the back musculature
Def: Any abnormality of the back muscles.

Name: Abnormal morphology of the shoulder musculature
Def: Any abnormality of the shoulder muscles.

Name: Hippocampal atrophy
Def: Partial or complete wasting (loss) of hippocampus tissue that was once present.
Comment: The hippocampus is part of the temporal cortex (albeit allocortex rather than neocortex).

Name: Increased cotinine level
Def: Increased concentration of cotinine in urine.
Comment: Cotinine is the main metabolite of nicotine and accumulates in the body as a result of tobacco exposure. In humans, cotinine is excreted in the urine, mainly as trans-3[prime]-hydroxycotinine and glucuronide. This is used as a measure for exposure to tobacco smoke.

Name: Blood xenobiotic
Def: The presence of a xenobiotic in blood.

Name: Increased circulating troponin I concentration
Def: An increased concentration of tropnin I in the blood, which is a cardiac regulatory protein that controls the calcium mediated interaction between actin and myosin. Raised cardiac troponin concentrations are now accepted as the standard biochemical marker for the diagnosis of myocardial infarction.
Synonym: Increased troponin I level in blood

Name: Increased circulating troponin T concentration
Def: An increased concentration of tropnin T in the blood, which is a cardiac regulatory protein that controls the calcium mediated interaction between actin and myosin. Raised cardiac troponin concentrations are now accepted as the standard biochemical marker for the diagnosis of myocardial infarction.
Synonym: Increased troponin T level in blood

Name: Hyperketonemia
Def: An increase in the level of ketone bodies (acetoacetic acid, beta-hydroxybutyric acid, and acetone) in the blood.
Synonym: Increased level of ketone bodies in blood

Name: Abnormal circulating glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase concentration
Def: An anomaly in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase.

Name: Abnormal glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in blood
Def: An anomaly in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in the blood.

Name: Increased glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in blood
Def: An increase in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in the blood.

Name: Decreased glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in blood
Def: A decrease in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in the blood.

Name: Abnormal glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in dried blood spot
Def: An anomaly in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in a dried blood spot.
Synonym: Abnormal G6PD level in dried blood spot
Abnormal glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in DBS

Name: Increased glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in dried blood spot
Def: An increase in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in a dried blood spot.
Synonym: Increased G6PD level in dried blood spot
Increased glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in DBS

Name: Decreased glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in dried blood spot
Def: A decrease in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in a dried blood spot.
Synonym: Decreased G6PD level in dried blood spot
Decreased glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in DBS

Name: Abnormal glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in leukocytes
Def: An anomaly in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in leukocytes.

Name: Abnormal glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in red blood cells
Def: An anomaly in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in red blood cells.
Synonym: Abnormal G6PD level in red blood cells

Name: Abnormal glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in tissue
Def: An anomaly in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in tissue.

Name: Increased glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in tissue
Def: An increase in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in tissue.

Name: Decreased glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in tissue
Def: A decrease in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in tissue.

Name: Decreased glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in red blood cells
Def: A decrease in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in red blood cells.
Synonym: Decreased G6PD level in red blood cells

Name: Increased glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in red blood cells
Def: An increase in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in red blood cells.
Synonym: Increased G6PD level in red blood cells

Name: Decreased glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in leukocytes
Def: A decrease in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in leukocytes.

Name: Increased glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase level in leukocytes
Def: An increase in the level of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase in leukocytes.

Name: obsolete Abnormal uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase level
Abnormal circulating UDP glucose-4-epimerase concentration
Def: An abnormality in uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase level in plasma. Uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase catalyzes the reaction: UDP-glucose = UDP-galactose.
Synonym: Abnormal circulating uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase concentration
Abnormal UDP-glucose 4-epimerase activity level in plasma
Abnormal uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase level in plasma

Name: Increased circulating UDP glucose-4-epimerase concentration
Def: An increase in uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase level in plasma. Uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase catalyzes the reaction: UDP-glucose = UDP-galactose.
Synonym: Increased circulating uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase concentration
Increased uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase level in plasma

Name: Decreased circulating UDP glucose-4-epimerase concentration
Def: A decrease in uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase level in plasma. Uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase catalyzes the reaction: UDP-glucose = UDP-galactose.
Synonym: Decreased circulating uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase concentration
Decreased UDP glucose-4-epimerase level in plasma
Decreased uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase level in plasma

Name: Abnormal erythrocyte UDP glucose-4-epimerase concentration
Def: An abnormality in uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase level in red blood cells. Uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase catalyzes the reaction: UDP-glucose = UDP-galactose.
Synonym: Abnormal erythrocyte uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase concentration
Abnormal UDP-glucose 4-epimerase level in red blood cells
Abnormal uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase level in red blood cells

Name: Increased erythrocyte UDP glucose-4-epimerase concentration
Def: An increase in uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase level in red blood cells. Uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase catalyzes the reaction: UDP-glucose = UDP-galactose.
Synonym: Increased UDP-glucose 4-epimerase level in red blood cells
Increased uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase level in red blood cells

Name: Decreased erythrocyte UDP glucose-4-epimerase concentration
Def: A decrease in uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase level in red blood cells. Uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase catalyzes the reaction: UDP-glucose = UDP-galactose.
Synonym: Decreased erythrocyte uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase concentration
Decreased UDP-glucose 4-epimerase level in red blood cells
Decreased uridine diphosphate glucose-4-epimerase level in red blood cells

Name: Increased CSF urate concentration
Def: Increased concentration of urate in the cerebrospinal fluid.

Name: Positive meconium barbiturate test
Def: Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as phenobarbital in meconium.

Name: Positive hair barbiturate test
Def: Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as phenobarbital in the hair.

Name: Positive stool barbiturate test
Def: Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as phenobarbital in the stool.

Name: Positive gastric fluid barbiturate test
Def: Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as phenobarbital in the gastric fluid.

Name: Increased intestinal transit time
Def: An increase in the length of time required for food to pass through the intestines.

Name: Abnormal circulating nicotinurate concentration
Def: Any deviation from the normal concentration of nicotinurate in the blood.
Comment: Nicotinuric acid is an acyl glycine, which are normally minor metabolites of fatty acids. However, the excretion of certain acyl glycines is increased in several inborn errors of metabolism. In certain cases the measurement of these metabolites in body fluids can be used to diagnose disorders associated with mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation. Nicotinuric acid is the major detoxification product of nicotinic acid. It may serve as a simple quantitative index of hepatic biotransformation of nicotinic acid. {xref="PMID:3243933"}

Name: Increased circulating nicotinurate level
Def: An increased amount of nicotinurate in the blood.

Name: Positive methadone plasma/serum test
Def: Detection of methadone or its metabolite 2-ethylidene-1,5-dimethyl-3,3- diphenylpyrrolidine (EDDP) in plasma or serum.
Comment: Methadone is an opioid drug that is used to treat severe pain or in the treatment of individiuals with opioid dependency.

Name: Positive plasma/serum cotinine test
Def: Detection of cotinine, an alkaloid found in tobacco and the predominant metabolite of nicotine, in plasma or serum.
Comment: Cotinine is used as a biomarker for exposure to tobacco smoke.

Name: Folate deficiency in CSF
Def: A reduced concentration of folic acid, which is also known as vitamin B9 in the cerebrospinal fluid.
Comment: Cerebral folate deficiency is usually measured as low levels of folate in the CSF, in the presence of normal folate metabolism outside the nervous system.

Name: Abnormal cord blood measurement
Def: An abnormality in any umbilical cord measurement performed after birth, such as the blood gas level.

Name: Abnormal blood gas level in cord blood
Hyperoxemia in cord blood
Def: An abnormally high level of blood oxygen in the cord blood.

Name: Hypoxemia in cord blood
Def: An abnormally low level of blood oxygen in the cord blood.

Name: Hypercapnia in cord blood
Def: Abnormally elevated blood carbon dioxide (CO2) level in the cord blood.
Synonym: High cord blood carbon dioxide level

Name: Hypocapnia in cord blood
Def: Abnormally decreased blood carbon dioxide (CO2) level in the cord blood.
Synonym: Low cord blood carbon dioxide level

Name: Abnormal blood 5-methyltetrahydrofolate level
Def: An abnormal concentration of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate in the blood.

Name: Reduced blood 5-methyltetrahydrofolate level
Def: A decreased concentration of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate in the blood.

Name: Hypoplasia of maxilla relative to mandible
Def: Abnormally small dimension of the maxilla (upper jaw) relative to the mandible (lower jaw).
Synonym: Disorder of maxillary and mandibular dental arch relationship

Name: Hypoplasia of mandible relative to maxilla
Def: Abnormally small dimension of the mandible (lower jaw) relative to the maxilla (upper jaw).
Synonym: Disorder of mandibular and maxillary dental arch relationship

Name: Increased anti-dairy protein IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against dairy proteins, including casein, alpha-lactalbumin, beta-lactoglobulin or bovine serum albumin contained in cow, sheep or goat milk and milk products.

Name: Increased anti-animal protein IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against animal proteins, such as albumins that are present in animal hair, dander, shed skin, saliva and urine.
Comment: For animal dander annotations, there is a more specific subclass of this term.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-animal protein IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-seafood IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against seafood, including fish, shrimp, lobster, crab, squid and abalone.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-seafood IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-dust mite IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against dust mites, such as house dust mites.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-dust mite IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-bacteria IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against bacteria.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-bacteria IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-drug IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against a drug or class of drugs, such as antibiotics.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-drug IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-feather IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against feathers, which could be indicative of an allergy against feathers themselves, or mite allergens present in feathers.

Name: Increased anti-food allergen IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against proteins found in foods, such as milk, egg, soy, wheat, peanut, treenut, fish, and shellfish.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-food allergen IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-plant based food allergen IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against a plant based food allergen, including vegetables and fruits.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-plant based food allergen IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-gluten IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against gluten, a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-gluten IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-nut food product IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against nut food products such as peanuts or tree nuts, such as hazelnuts, walnuts, cashews, and almonds.

Name: Increased anti-egg IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against eggs, including egg whites, egg yolks, and egg proteins such as ovoalbumin and ovomucoid.

Name: Increased anti-fungi IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against fungus, such as molds like zygomycota, ascomycota and deuteromycota.

Name: Increased anti-meat allergen IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against meat, such as mammalian meat, including beef or pork, or poultry, like duck or chicken.

Name: Increased anti-parasite IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against parasites, such as helminths (parasitic worms, such as Ascaris lumbricoides, Trichuris trichiura, Ancylostoma duodenalis, Necator americanus, Strongyloides stercoralis) or parasites such as Toxoplasma gondii.

Name: Increased anti-insect IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against antigens from insects such as moths, mosquitos, or cockroaches.

Name: Increased anti-venom IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against venom from insects such as bees, wasps, hornets, yellowjackets.

Name: Increased anti-plant product IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against antigens from plants and products derived from plants, such as wood or pollen.

Name: Positive urine norcotinine test
Def: Detection of norcotinine, a metabolite of nicotine, in urine.

Name: Abnormal circulating IgA concentration
Def: An abnormal deviation from normal levels of IgA immunoglobulin in blood.

Name: Abnormal circulating IgE concentration
Def: An abnormal deviation from normal levels of IgE immunoglobulin in blood.

Name: Abnormal circulating IgG concentration
Def: An abnormal deviation from normal levels of IgG immunoglobulin in blood.

Name: Abnormal circulating IgM concentration
Def: An abnormal deviation from normal levels of IgM immunoglobulin in blood.

Name: Abnormal circulating IgD concentration
Def: An abnormal deviation from normal levels of IgD immunoglobulin in blood.

Name: Decreased circulating IgD concentration
Def: An abnormally decreased level of immunoglobulin D (IgD) in blood.

Name: Increased circulating IgD concentration
Def: An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin D in blood.

Name: Increased anti-animal dander IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against animal dander, tiny scales shed from animal skin or hair, such as from pet dogs or cats.
Synonym: Increased level of anti-dander IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-house dust mite IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against house dust mites, a common allergen.
Synonym: Increased anti-house dust IgE antibody level
Increased level of anti-house dust IgE antibody

Name: Increased anti-alpha-gal IgE antibody level
Def: Increased level of IgE antibody against galactose-alpha-1, 3 galactose (alpha-gal), a carbohydrate found in mammalian meat.
Synonym: Increased anti-galactose-alpha-1, 3 galactose IgE antibody level

Name: Abnormal L-selectin shedding
Def: An abnormality in the cleavage of L-selectin during the process of guiding neutrophils to the site of infection. Proteolytic cleavage of L-selectin results in rapid shedding from the cell surface, which has a role in neutrophil rolling and accumulation at the site of infection.

Name: Chronic neutropenia
Def: Neutropenia with an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) less than 1,500,000,000/L lasting for more than 3 months.

Name: Myeloid maturation arrest
Def: Chornic neutropenia arising from an impaired proliferation and maturation of myeloid progenitor cells in the bone marrow.
Synonym: Myeloid maturation arrest in bone marrow

Name: Cyclic neutropenia in myeloid maturation arrest in bone marrow
Def: Cyclic neutropenia arising from an impaired proliferation and maturation of myeloid progenitor cells in the bone marrow.

Name: Transient neutropenia
Def: A transient reduction in the number of neutrophils in the peripheral blood. Transient neutropenia is most commonly associated with viral infections, but other causes include drugs and autoimmunity.

Name: Infection associated neutropenia
Def: Transient neutropenia caused by an infection, such as with a virus, bacteria or protozoan.

Name: Neutrophilia in presence of infection
Def: An increased number of neutrophils circulating in the blood during an infection, such as with a bacteria, virus or fungus.

Name: Neutrophilia in absence of infection
Def: An increased number of neutrophils circulating in the blood in the absence of an infection. Factors contributing to neutrophilia could include inflammation or congenital disorders.

Name: Hepatopulmonary fusion
Def: Fusion of the liver with the lung.

Name: Asymmetrical gluteal crease
Def: The presence of an asymmetrical gluteal crease, the horizontal crease formed by the inferior aspect of the buttocks and the posterior upper leg.

Name: Wide space between 4th and 5th toe
Def: A widely spaced gap between the fourth toe and the fifth (pinky) toe.
Synonym: Wide space between the 4th and 5th toe

Name: Lower cranial nerve dysfunction
Def: A functional abnormality affecting the lower cranial nerves, which include the paired 9th (glossopharyngeal), 10th (vagal), 11th (accessory) and 12th (hypoglossal) cranial nerves.

Name: Brain imaging abnormality
Def: An anomaly of metabolism or structure of the brain identified by imaging.

Name: Subglottic hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, located in the airway, typically below the vocal chords, that can cause severe obstruction of the airway.

Name: Supraglottic hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, located in the upper part of the larynx (voice box) including the epiglottis; the area above the vocal cords.

Name: Visceral hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma arising from within visceral structures, the internal organs of the body.

Name: Intestinal hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, located in the intestines, which includes the bowel.

Name: Spleen hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the spleen.

Name: Labial hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the upper lip.

Name: Esophageal hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the esophagus.

Name: Laryngeal hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the glottic or supraglottic regions.

Name: Vulvar hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the vulva.

Name: Retropharyngeal hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the retropharyngeal space, the portion of the peripharyngeal space that is located posterior to the pharynx.

Name: Paraspinal hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the paraspinal muscular region, the muscles next to the spine.

Name: Lumbosacral hemangioma
Def: A spinal cord hemangioma located in the lumbosacral spine region.

Name: Supraumbilical raphe
Def: An abnormality of the sternum that presents at birth as a ventral sternal non-union defect, due to an abnormality of the fusion of the layers of the skin. It presents as a scar-like line that extends upward from the umbilicus (belly button).

Name: Sternal pit
Def: A sternal pit is a small indentation or dimple in the skin overlying the sternum of the chest. In some cases, the skin defect can be linear, extending several inches over the sternum.

Name: Pituitary gland cyst
Def: A fluid-filled sacs that develop on or near the pituitary gland.

Name: Atrophic pituitary gland
Def: Partial or complete wasting (loss) of the pituitary gland.

Name: Pediatric onset
Def: Onset of disease manifestations before adulthood, defined here as before the age of 16 years, but excluding neonatal or congenital onset.

Name: Dyspepsia
Def: A heterogeneous group of symptoms that are localized in the epigastric region. Typical dyspeptic symptoms include postprandial fullness, early satiation, epigastric pain and epigastric burning, but other upper gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea, belching or abdominal bloating often occur.

Name: Abnormal circulating amylase concentration
Def: A deviation from the normal concentration of amylase in the blood, an enzyme which helps digest glycogen and starch. It is produced mainly in the pancreas and salivary glands.

Name: Positive blood acetaminophen test
Def: Detection of acetaminophen in the blood.

Name: Positive norpropoxyphene blood test
Def: Detection of norpropoxyphene in the blood, a major metabolite of the opioid analgesic drug dextropropoxyphene.

Name: Positive meconium methadone test
Def: Detection of methadone or its metabolite 2-ethylidene-1,5-dimethyl-3,3- diphenylpyrrolidine (EDDP) in meconium.

Name: Positive blood molindone test
Def: Detection of molindone in the blood, an antipyschotic used for treatment of schizophrenia.

Name: Intrathoracic hemangioma
Def: A hemangioma, a benign tumor of the vascular endothelial cells, that is located in the intrathoracic or chest region.

Name: Hyperamylasemia
Def: Increased level of amylase in the blood, an enzyme which helps digest glycogen and starch. It is produced mainly in the pancreas and salivary glands.

Name: Hypoamylasemia
Def: Decreased level of amylase in the blood, an enzyme which helps digest glycogen and starch. It is produced mainly in the pancreas and salivary glands.

Name: Positive urine norpropoxyphene test
Def: Detection of norpropoxyphene in urine.

Name: Negativism
Def: Opposing or not responding to instructions or external stimuli.

Name: Abnormal isohemagglutinin level
Def: An abnormal level of isohemagglutinin in the blood. An isohemagglutinin refers to the naturally occurring antibodies in the ABO blood group system (i.e., anti-A in a group B person, anti-B in a group A person, and anti-A, anti-B, and anti-A,B in a group O person).
Synonym: Abnormal level of natural antibody to blood group agents
Abnormal natural antibody level to blood group antigens in blood (isohemagglutinin)

Name: Absent isohemagglutinin level
Def: Absent or undetectable level of isohemagglutinin. An isohemagglutinin refers to the naturally occurring antibodies in the ABO blood group system (i.e., anti-A in a group B person, anti-B in a group A person, and anti-A, anti-B, and anti-A,B in a group O person).
Synonym: Absent natural antibody to blood group agents
Complete or near-complete absence of isohemagglutinins

Name: Decreased specific antibody response to protein vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against proteins in vaccines, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Complete or near-complete absence of specific antibody response to tetanus vaccine
Def: The inability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a tetanus antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Complete or near-complete absence of specific antibody response to hepatitis B vaccine
Def: The inability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a hepatisis B antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Partial absence of specific antibody response to tetanus vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a tetanus antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Partial absence of specific antibody response to hepatitis B vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a hepatitis B antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Decreased specific antibody response to polysaccharide vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against polysaccharides in vaccines, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Complete or near-complete absence of specific antibody response to unconjugated pneumococcus vaccine
Def: The inability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a pneumococcus antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Partial absence of specific antibody response to unconjugated pneumococcus vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a pneumococcus antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Decreased specific antibody response to protein-conjugated polysaccharide vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against protein-conjugated polysaccharides in vaccines, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Complete or near-complete absence of specific antibody response to Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine
Def: The inability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Complete or near-complete absence of specific antibody response to meningococcus vaccine
Def: The inability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a meningococcus antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Partial absence of specific antibody response to Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Partial absence of specific antibody response to meningococcus vaccine
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against a meningococcus antigen, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

Name: Positive stool methadone test
Def: Detection of methadone and its metabolites in the stool.

Name: Decreased specific antibody response to infection
Def: A reduced ability to synthesize antibodies against antigens from an infectious agent or pathogen (such as bacteria, viruses, parasites, etc.), as measured by antibody titer determination following infection.

Name: Alpha-aminoadipic aciduria
Def: The concentration of alpha-aminoadipic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Abnormality of neutrophil morphology in CSF
Def: An abnormal form or size of neutrophils in the cerebrospinal fluid.
Synonym: Abnormality of neutrophil morphology in cerebrospinal fluid

Name: Hyposegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in CSF
Def: Hyposegmented (hypolobulated) or bilobed neutrophil nuclei in the cerebrospinal fluid.
Synonym: Hyposegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in cerebrospinal fluid

Name: Hypersegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in CSF
Def: An excessive division of the lobes of the nucleus of a neutrophil in the cerebrospinal fluid.
Synonym: Hypersegmentation of neutrophil nuclei in cerebrospinal fluid

Name: Abnormal urinary 1-methylhistidine concentration
Def: Abnormal concentration of 1-methylhistidine in the urine.

Name: Decreased urinary 1-methylhistidine
Def: Decreased concentration of 1-methylhistidine in the urine.

Name: Increased urinary 1-methylhistidine
Def: Increased concentration of 1-methylhistidine in the urine.

Name: Abnormal urinary 3-methylhistidine level
Def: Abnormal amount of 3-methylhistidine in the urine.
Comment: 3-Methylhistidine is an analog of histidine found mainly in skeletal muscle. The rate of myofibrillar protein breakdown may be estimated from the urinary excretion of 3-methylhistidine. This amino acid is formed by the methylation of peptide-bound histidine in actin and myosin, is excreted in the urine when these proteins are broken down, and is not reused for protein synthesis.

Name: Increased urinary 3-methylhistidine
Def: Increased concentration of 3-methylhistidine in the urine.

Name: Decreased urinary 3-methylhistidine
Def: Decreased concentration of 3-methylhistidine in the urine.

Name: Alpha-gal allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against alpha-gal.

Name: Animal protein allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against animal proteins.

Name: Animal dander allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against animal dander.

Name: Bacteria allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against bacteria.

Name: Drug allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against drugs.

Name: Dust mite allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against dust mites.

Name: Feather allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against feathers.

Name: Dairy allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against dairy.

Name: Egg allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against eggs.

Name: Gluten allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against gluten.
Comment: A gluten allergy is usually distinct from gluten sensitivity or Celiac disease.

Name: Meat allergen allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against allergens contained in meat products.

Name: Nut food product allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against nut food products.
Synonym: Immunoglobulin E-mediated nut food product allergy

Name: Plant based food allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against plant based food allergens.
Synonym: Allergy to plant based food allergens
IgE-mediated plant based food allergen allergy
Immunoglobulin E-mediated plant based food allergen allergy

Name: Seafood allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against seafood.

Name: Fungi allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against fungus.

Name: Insect allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against insects.

Name: Venom allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against insect venom.

Name: Parasite allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against parasites.

Name: Plant product allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against plant products.

Name: Insect bite allergy
Def: Hypersensitivity in form of an adverse immune reaction against insect bites.

Name: Focal epithelial hyperplasia of oral mucosa
Def: The occurrence of multiple or unique whitish or normal in color small papules or nodules in oral cavity, especially on labial and buccal mucosa, lower lip and tongue, and less often on the upper lip, gingiva and palate.
Synonym: Focal epithelial hyperplasia of the lining of mouth

Name: Abnormal circulating heparan sulfate level
Def: An abnormal level of heparan sulfate in the blood.
Synonym: Abnormality of the concentration of heparan sulfate in the blood
Abnormality of the concentration of heparan sulphate in the blood

Name: Increased circulating heparan sulfate level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of heparan sulfate in the blood.

Name: Decreased circulating heparan sulfate level
Def: An abnormal decrease in the concentration of heparan sulfate in the blood.

Name: Shortened O-fucosylated glycan on properdin
Def: Decreased length of O-fucosylated glycans present on properdin.
Synonym: Presence of terminal O-fucose glycans on properdin

Name: Increased urinary polyhexose
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of polyhexose in the urine.

Name: Increased urinary galactosylated oligosaccharide
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of galactosylated oligosaccharides in urine.
Synonym: Increased concentration of galactosylated oligosaccharides in urine

Name: Increased urinary high-mannose-type oligosaccharide
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of high-mannose-type oligosaccharides in the urine.
Synonym: Increased concentration of high-mannose-type oligosaccharides in urine

Name: Increased urinary multiantennary sialylated oligosaccharide
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of multiantennary sialylated oligosaccharides in the urine.
Synonym: Increase concentration of multiantennary sialylated oligosaccharides in urine

Name: Decreased glycosyltransferase O-Fucosylpeptide 3-Beta-N-Acetylglucosaminyltransferase level
Def: An abnormal decrease in glycosyltransferase O-fucosylpeptide 3-beta-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase enzymatic level.

Name: Increased urinary fucosylated oligosaccharide
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of small fucosylated oligosaccharides in the urine.
Synonym: Increased concentration of fucosylated oligosaccharides in urine

Name: Abnormal complex N-glycan level
Def: An abnormal concentration of complex N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Synonym: Abnormal concentration of complex N-glycans on glycoproteins

Name: Increased complex N-glycan level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of complex N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Synonym: Increased concentration of complex N-glycans on glycoproteins

Name: Decreased complex N-glycan level
Def: An abnormal decrease in the concentration of complex N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Synonym: Increased truncated complex N-glycans on glycoproteins

Name: Increased sialylated N-glycan level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of sialylated N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Synonym: Increased concentration of sialylated N-glycans on glycoproteins

Name: Decreased sialylated N-glycan level
Def: An abnormal decrease in the concentration of sialylated N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Synonym: Decreased concentration of sialylated N-glycans on glycoproteins

Name: Abnormal high-mannose N-glycan level
Def: An abnormal concentration of high-mannose N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Synonym: Abnormal high-mannose N-glycans on glycoprotein concentration

Name: Increased high-mannose N-glycan level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of high-mannose N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Synonym: Increased high-mannose N-glycans on glycoprotein concentration

Name: Decreased high-mannose N-glycan level
Def: An abnormal decrease in the concentration of high-mannose N-glycans on glycoproteins.
Synonym: Decreased high-mannose N-glycans on glycoprotein concentration

Name: Abnormal core 1 O-glycan level
Def: An abnormal in the concentration of core 1 O-glycans on glycoproteins.

Name: Increased core 1 O-glycan level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of core 1 O-glycans on glycoproteins.

Name: Decreased core 1 O-glycan level
Def: An abnormal decrease in the concentration of core 1 O-glycans on glycoproteins.

Name: Decreased O-mannosyl glycans on alpha-dystroglycan
Def: Hypoglycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan with O-mannosyl glycans. Alpha-dystroglycan is a functional target of O-mannosyl glycosylation and functional glycosylation of alpha-DG is essential in its interaction with the extracellular matrix.

Name: Increased monosialylated core 1 O-glycan level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of monosialylated core 1 O-glycans on glycoproteins.

Name: Decreased monosialylated core 1 O-glycan level
Def: An abnormal decrease in the concentration of monosialylated core 1 O-glycans on glycoproteins.

Name: Increased disialylated core 1 O-glycan level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of disialylated core 1 O-glycans on glycoproteins.

Name: Increased globoside Gb4 level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of globoside Gb4.

Name: Increased hepatitis A virus antibody level
Def: An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin against hepatitis A virus in the blood.

Name: Increased globoside Gb3 level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of glycolipid globoside Gb3.

Name: Increased hepatitis B virus antibody level
Def: An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin against hepatitis B virus in the blood.

Name: Absence of ganglioside GM3
Def: The absence of ganglioside GM3.

Name: Increased hepatitis C virus antibody level
Def: An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin against hepatitis C virus in the blood.

Name: Increased Tn-antigen level
Def: An abnormal increase in the concentration of Tn antigen on glycoproteins.

Name: Abnormal proportion of naive CD4 T cells
Def: Any abnormality in the proportion of naive CD4 T cells relative to the total number of T cells.
Synonym: Abnormal proportion of naive thymus-derived CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells

Name: Abnormal proportion of naive CD8 T cells
Def: Any abnormality in the proportion of naive CD8 T cells relative to the total number of T cells.

Name: Increased proportion of naive CD4 T cells
Comment: An abnormally increased proportion of naive CD4 T cells relative to the total number of T cells. {xref="PMID:22474485"}
Synonym: Elevated proportion of naive CD4 T cells
Increased proportion of naive thymus-derived CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells

Name: Increased proportion of naive CD8 T cells
Def: An abnormally increased proportion of naive CD8 T cells relative to the total number of T cells.
Synonym: Elevated proportion of naive CD8 T cells
Elevated proportion of naive thymus-derived CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells

Name: Decreased proportion of naive CD8 T cells
Def: An abnormally reduced proportion of naive CD8 T cells relative to the total number of T cells.
Synonym: Reduced proportion of naive CD8 T cells
Reduced proportion of naive thymus-derived CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells

Name: Decreased proportion of naive CD4 T cells
Def: An abnormally reduced proportion of naive CD4 T cells relative to the total number of T cells.
Synonym: Decreased proportion of naive thymus-derived CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Reduced proportion of naive CD4 T cells

Name: Abnormal proportion of CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells
Def: An abnormal proportion of CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CD45RO-positive and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD44-high, and CD122-high.

Name: Abnormal proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells
Def: An abnormal proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. A CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell with memory phenotype is CD45RO and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD44-high, and CD122-high.
Comment: Human CD8+T cells are commonly classified into four subsets based on the surface expression of the leukocyte common antigen isoform CD45RA and the lymph node addressin CCR7. Thereby, naive TN cells (CD45RA+/CCR7+) are separated from central memory TCM (CD45RA-/CCR7+), effector memory TEM (CD45RA-/CCR7-) and TEMRA (CD45RA+/CCR7-) T cells.

Name: Abnormal proportion of central memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: An abnormal proportion of central memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CCR7-positive, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: obsolete Abnormal proportion of effector memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Comment: This term was a duplicate, hence it was obsoleted. https://github.com/obophenotype/human-phenotype-ontology/issues/5696

Name: Abnormal proportion of effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: An abnormal proportion of effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Abnormal proportion of central memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: An abnormal proportion of central memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CCR7-positive, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Decreased proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells
Def: Decreased proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. A CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell with memory phenotype is CD45RO and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD44-high, and CD122-high.

Name: Decreased proportion of CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells
Def: Decresaed proportion of CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CD45RO-positive and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD44-high, and CD122-high.

Name: obsolete Decreased proportion of effector memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Comment: This term was a duplicate, hence it was obsoleted. https://github.com/obophenotype/human-phenotype-ontology/issues/5696

Name: Decreased proportion of central memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: A reduced proportion of central memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CCR7-positive, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.
Comment: An abnormally decreased proportion of central memory CD4+ T cells. These are memory cells that are located in the secondary lymphoid organs. These cells may have a CD3/CD4/CD62L+/CD45RA- phenotype.
Synonym: Decreased proportion of CD4+ central memory cells
Decreased proportion of CD4-positive central memory cells
Decreased proportion of central memory CD4+, alpha-beta T cell
Reduced proportion of CD4+ central memory cells

Name: Decreased proportion of central memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: A reduced proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta central memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Decreased proportion of effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: A reduced proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta effector memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Increased proportion of CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells
Def: An abnormally elevated proportion of CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CD45RO-positive and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD44-high, and CD122-high.

Name: Increased proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells
Def: An abnormally elevated proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CD45RO and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD44-high, and CD122-high.

Name: Increased proportion of central memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: An abnormally elevated proportion of central memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype of CCR7-positive, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.
Comment: These are memory cells that are located in the secondary lymphoid organs. These cells may have a CD3/CD4/CD62L+/CD45RA- phenotype.
Synonym: Elevated proportion central memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Elevated proportion of CD4+ central memory cells
Increased proportion of CD4+ central memory cells
Increased proportion of central memory CD4+, alpha-beta T cell

Name: Increased proportion of effector memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: An abnormally elevated proportion of effector memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Increased proportion of effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: An increased proportion of effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Increased proportion of central memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells
Def: An increased proportion of central memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CCR7-positive, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.

Name: Bronchiolectasis
Def: Saccular dilatation of the terminal bronchioles.

Name: Positive blood lead test
Def: Detection of lead in the blood.

Name: Absent sebaceous glands
Def: Absence of the sebaceous gland, the holocrine gland that secretes sebum into the hair follicles, or in hairless areas into ducts.

Name: Worse in evening
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is exacerbated in the evening as compared to the day.

Name: Abnormal frontal bone morphology
Def: An abnormality of the frontal bone.
Synonym: Abnormality of the bone of the forehead

Name: Abnormal lacrimal bone morphology
Def: An abnormality of the lacrimal bone.

Name: Abnormal palatine bone morphology
Def: An abnormality of the palatine bone.

Name: Abnormal ethmoid bone morphology
Def: An abnormality of the ethmoid bone

Name: Ectopic cilia of eyelid
Def: An eyelash that emerges from the underside (conjunctiva) of the upper or lower eyelid.

Name: Symblepharon
Def: A partial or complete adhesion of the palpebral conjunctiva of the eyelid to the bulbar conjunctiva of the eyeball.
Synonym: Eyelid adhesion to globe of eye

Name: Accessory eyelid
Def: The presence of more than the normal number of eyelids.

Name: Hypoplasia of eyelid
Def: Developmental hypoplasia of the eyelid.

Name: Microblepharia
Def: Abnormal shortness of the vertical dimensions of the eyelids.

Name: Defect of palpebral conjunctiva
Def: An abnormality of the palpebral conjunctiva.

Name: Incomplete ossification of palatine bone
Def: Failure to complete ossification (maturation and calcification) of the palatine bone.

Name: Absent palatine bone ossification
Def: Lack of formation of the palatine bone.

Name: Abnormality of musculature of soft palate
Def: An abnormality of one or more of the five muscles of the soft palate.

Name: Abnormal morphology of musculature of pharynx
Def: An abnormality of any of the muscles of the pharynx.
Synonym: Abnormality of muscles of the pharynx

Name: Abnormality of tensor veli palatini muscle
Def: An abnormality of the tensor veli palatini muscle

Name: Abnormality of uvular muscle
Def: An abnormality of the uvular muscle

Name: Abnormality of nasal musculature
Def: An abnormality of the muscles of the structure of the nose.
Synonym: Abnormality of musculature of the nose

Name: Abnormality of muscle of facial expression
Def: An abnormality of any of the muscles of facial expression, which are innervated by the seventh (VII) cranial nerve and control facial expression.
Synonym: Abnormality of muscle of facial expression
Abnormality of musculature of facial expression

Name: Abnormality of levator labii superioris alaeque nasi muscle
Def: An abnormality of the levator labii superioris alaeque nasi muscle.

Name: Abnormal common carotid artery morphology
Def: An abnormality of the common carotid arteries, which provide the arterial supply to the head and neck and give rise to the internal carotid artery and the external carotid artery.
Synonym: Abnormality of the common carotid artery

Name: Abnormality of the sphenoid sinus
Def: An abnormality of the sphenoid sinus, one of the mucosa-lined, normally air-filled paranasal sinuses of the bones of the skull. The sphenoid sinus is located within the sphenoid bone.

Name: Abnormality of the maxillary sinus
Def: An abnormality of the maxillary sinus, one of the mucosa-lined, normally air-filled paranasal sinuses of the bones of the skull. The maxillary sinus is located within the skeleton of the midface, lateral to the nasal cavity.
Synonym: Abnormality of the antrum of Highmore
Abnormality of the upper jaw sinus

Name: Abnormality of external jugular vein
Def: An abnormality of an external jugular vein of the neck.

Name: Bilateral facial palsy
Def: Two-sided or bilateral weakness of the muscles of facial expression and eye closure.
Synonym: Paralysis of both sides of the face
Weakness of both sides of the face

Name: obsolete Abnormality of the shape of the midface
Hyperplasia of the maxilla
Def: Abnormally increased dimension of the maxilla, especially relative to the mandible, resulting in a malocclusion or malalignment between the upper and lower teeth or in anterior positioning of the nasal base, increased convexity of the face, increased nasolabial angle, or increased width (transverse dimension of the maxilla.

Name: Hyperplasia of the premaxilla
Def: An abnormality of the premaxilla (the embryonic structure that forms the anterior part of the maxilla) causing it to appear relatively large in size compared to the other parts of the maxilla or other facial structures.
Synonym: Hyperplasia of the primary palate bone
Increased size of the primary palate bone

Name: Positive infectious agent test
Def: Any kind of test for an infectious agent in a specimen positive.

Name: Aqueous humor viral DNA positivity
Def: The presence of viral DNA (e.g., cytomegalovirus, herpes simplex virus, or varicella zoster virus) in the aqueous humor of the eye.
Comment: This finding is generally assessed by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of aqueous humor obtained from the anterior chamber of the eye by an aqueous humor tap.

Name: Electronic cigarette exposure history
Def: History of use of electronic cigarettes (vaping).

Name: Gottron sign
Def: Erythematous macules or patches over extensor surfaces of elbows, knuckles, knees, and ankles.

Name: Hypertension resistant to conventional therapy
Def: Resistant hypertension is defined as above-goal elevated blood pressure in a patient despite the concurrent use of 3 antihypertensive drug classes, commonly including a long-acting calcium channel blocker, a blocker of the renin-angiotensin system (angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker), and a diuretic.

Name: Tibiofibular interosseous membrane calcification
Def: Deposition of excess calcium in the interosseous membrane of the leg, which extends between the interosseous crests of the tibia and fibula and separates the anterior and posterior muscles of the lower leg.
Synonym: Calcification of the interosseous membrane of leg
Calcification of the middle tibiofibular joint

Name: Supracondylar elbow fracture
Def: A type of elbow fracture that involves the distal humerus just above the elbow.

Name: Abnormal alcohol consumption
Def: Alcohol abuse or dependence.

Name: Thoracic lordosis
Def: Thoracic lordosis refers to an abnormal curvature of the thoracic spine in which the thoracic spine displays lordosis (inward curve) instead of the normal kyphosis (outward curve).

Name: Radiation into left arm
Def: Refers to pain or discomfort that is perceived to travel from the chest into the left arm.

Name: Radiation into right arm
Def: Refers to pain or discomfort that is perceived to travel from the chest into the right arm.

Name: Small joint hypermobilty
Def: The capability that a small joint (or a group of joints) has to move, passively and/or actively, beyond normal limits along physiological axes. Small joints include metacarpophalangeal joints, proximal interphalangeal joints, \nsecond to fifth metatarsophalangeal joints, and wrists.

Name: Large joint hypermobilty
Def: The capability that a large joint (or a group of joints) has to move, passively and/or actively, beyond normal limits along physiological axes. Large joints include shoulders, elbows, hips, knees, and ankles.

Name: Intracranial calcification
Def: Intracranial calcifications refer to calcifications within the brain parenchyma or vasculature. The five major components of the brain comprise the cerebrum, cerebellum, brain stem, pituitary gland, and hypothalamus.
Comment: pineal gland, choroid plexus, habenula, falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli

Name: Anti-thyroid antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against one or more components on the thyroid.

Name: Bloodstream pathogen-specific antibody positivity
Def: Positive serology for a exposure to an infectious agent (i.e., examining serum for the presence of pathogen-specific antibodies).

Name: Anti-SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus type 2 (SARS-CoV-2).

Name: Anti-West Nile virus antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of the West Nile virus.

Name: Anti-microfilaria antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of a microfilaria (parasite).

Name: Anti-trypanosoma cruzi antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of trypanosoma cruzi.

Name: Anti-chikungunya virus antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of chikungunya virus.

Name: Anti-chlamydia psittaci antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of chlamydia psittaci.

Name: Anti-herpes simplex antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of herpes simplex.
Synonym: HSV antibody titer high in blood

Name: Bloodstream virus-specific antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a virus.

Name: Bloodstream parasite-specific antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a parasite.

Name: Bloodstream antibacterial antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a bacterium.

Name: Anti-Japanese encephalitis virus-specific antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of the Japanese encephalitis virus.

Name: Anti-chlamydia trachomatis-specific antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of chlamydia trachomatis.

Name: Anti-Epstein-Barr virus-specific antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of the Epstein Barr virus (EBV).

Name: Anti-babesia-specific antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of a parasite of the genus Babesia (parasite).

Name: Anti-Zikavirus-specific antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of the Zika virus.

Name: Positive bloodstream nucleic acid pathogen test
Def: Positive (abnormal) result of a test such as polymerase chain reaction that is targeted against a nucleic acid sequence specific for a pathogen.

Name: Positive microfilaria PCR test in the blood circulation
Def: Detection of nucleic acid of a microfilarial parasite in the blood circulation.

Name: Positive JC-virus PCR test in the blood circulation
Def: Detection of nucleic acid of the JC-virus (JC-Polyomavirus, John Cunningham virus) in the blood circulation.
Synonym: JC virus PCR in blood positive

Name: Placenta previa
Def: Implantation of the placenta over or near the internal os of the cervix.
Comment: Placenta previa is the complete or partial covering of the internal os of the cervix with the placenta. It is a major risk factor for postpartum hemorrhage and can lead to morbidity and mortality of the mother and neonate.

Name: Abnormal circulating organic compound concentration
Def: Any deviation of the concentration of an orrganic compound from the normal range. An organic compound is defined as any compound that contains a carbon atom.

Name: Abnormal circulating beta-carotene concentration
Def: Any deviation of the concentration of beta-carotene in the blood circulation from the normal range.

Name: Decreased circulating beta-carotene concentration
Def: The concentration of beta-carotene in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Increased circulating beta-carotene concentration
Def: The concentration of beta-carotene in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Mammary blocked duct
Def: Blocked mammary ducts represent an area of localized milk stasis, typically associated with breast engorgement and resulting in a localized tender breast lump or area of blushed color; the breast may feel hot; and there may be a white, painful bleb on the end of the nipple.

Name: Bloodstream antifungal antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a fungus.

Name: Anti-coccidioidal antibody positivity
