Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of a fungus of the Coccidioides genus.

Name: Anti-cryptococcal antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of a fungus of the Cryptoccous genus.

Name: Anti-mycoplasma antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a mycoplasmal component.
Comment: Mycoplasma is a term used to refer to any of the members of the class Mollicutes which include Mycoplasma and Ureaplasma.

Name: Anti-rickettsial antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of a rickettsial bacterium. Rickettsiae are gram-negative bacteria with an obligate intracellular life cycle circulating between mammalian hosts and hematophagous arthropod vectors

Name: Anti-Bartonella henselae antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of Bartonella.
Synonym: Bartonella henselae antibody titer high in blood

Name: Anti-Dengue virus antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of Dengue virus.
Synonym: Dengue antibody titer high in blood

Name: Anti-arbovirus antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of an Arbovirus.

Name: Anti-lymphocytic choriomeningitis antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV).
Synonym: Lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus antibody titer high in blood

Name: Anti-varicella-zoster antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of Varicella-zoster virus.
Synonym: Varicella-zoster antibody titer high in blood

Name: Anti-rubella antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of rubella virus.
Synonym: Rubella antibody titer high in blood

Name: Anti-cytomegalovirus antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of cytomegalovirus (CMV).
Synonym: CMV antibody titer high in blood

Name: Anti-measles antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of measles virus.
Synonym: Measles antibody titer high in blood

Name: Anti-schistosoma antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of a parasite of the genus Schistosomiasis is a parasitic disease historically known as bilharzia caused by the trematode of the genus Schistosoma. Schistosomiasis is a parasitic disease historically known as bilharzia caused by the trematode of the genus Schistosoma.
Synonym: Schistosoma antibody titer high in blood

Name: Anti-Powassan virus antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of a Powassan virus (POW), which is an arbovirus within the family of Flaviviruses primarily found in the Northeastern United States, Canada, and Russia. It is a zoonotic infection transmitted to humans by several tick species and is the only member of the tick-borne flaviviruses endemic to North America.
Synonym: Powassan encephalitis antibody titer high in blood

Name: Marker expression
Def: Detection of an marker such as a protein by immunohistochemistry or related investigation techniques. The presence or absence of such markers can be used to identify cell types on the basis of a profile of expressed markers. These terms do not imply abnormality and can be used for any cell type or organ.

Name: BCL2 expression
Def: Detection of the presence of BCL2 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-BCL2 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).
Comment: The BCL2 proteins are central regulators of the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway. Overexpression of the BCL2 is associated with a poor prognosis in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

Name: BCL6 expression
Def: Detection of the presence of BCL6 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-BCL6 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).
Comment: BCL6 is a transcriptional repressor which has emerged as a critical regulator of germinal centers (GCs) of lymph nodes. BCL6 is also a frequently activated oncogene in the pathogenesis of human B cell lymphomas, most of which derive from the GC B cells.

Name: CD5 expression
Def: Detection of the presence of CD5 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-CD5 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).
Comment: The CD5 antigen is expressed by most T cells and a subset of B cells. Human CD5 positive B cells are present in fetal lymphoid tissue, their frequency decreasing with fetal age. In adult human tissues, CD5 positive B cells have been reported to be present in the germinal center and mantle zone. Malignancies of CD5 positive B cells include mantle cell lymphoma and chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

Name: CD10 expression
Def: Detection of the presence of CD10 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-CD10 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).
Comment: The CD10 antigen is expressed in acute lymphoblastic leukemia and follicle center cell lymphoma.

Name: CD23 expression
Def: Detection of the presence of CD23 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-CD23 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).
Comment: CD23 is Fc epsilon RII, the low-affinity receptor for IgE. CD23 is found on mature B cells, activated macrophages, eosinophils, follicular dendritic cells, and platelets.

Name: CD38 expression
Def: Detection of the presence of CD38 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-CD38 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).
Comment: CD38 is cyclic ADP ribose hydrolase, a glycoprotein[ found on the surface of many immune cells (white blood cells), including CD4+, CD8+, B lymphocytes and natural killer cells.

Name: CD45 expression
Def: Detection of the presence of CD45 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-CD45 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).
Comment: CD45 is a pan-leukocyte protein with tyrosine phosphatase activity involved in the regulation of signal transduction in hematopoiesis.

Name: Cyclin D1 expression
Def: Detection of the presence of cyclin D1 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-cyclin D1 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).
Comment: Cyclin D1 is an important regulator of the cell cycle and overexpression of this protein by immunohistochemistry is characteristically seen in mantle cell lymphoma and other B-cell neoplasms.

Name: FMC7 expression
Def: Detection of the presence of FMC7 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-FMC7 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).
Comment: FMC7 is a late B cell differentiation marker.

Name: CD19 expression
Def: Detection of the presence of CD19 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-CD19 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).
Comment: In normal cells, CD19 is the most ubiquitously expressed protein in the B lymphocyte lineage. CD19 expression is induced at the point of B lineage commitment during the differentiation of the hematopoietic stem cell, and its expression continues through preB and mature B cell differentiation until it is finally down-regulated during terminal differentiation into plasma cells. CD19 expression is maintained in B-lineage cells that have undergone neoplastic transformation, and therefore CD19 is useful in diagnosis of leukemias and lymphomas using monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and flow cytometry.

Name: CD20 expression
Def: Detection of the presence of CD20 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-CD20 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).
Comment: CD20 is a 33-37 kDa, non-glycosylated phosphoprotein expressed on the surface of almost all normal and malignant B cells.

Name: Past surgical history
Def: information about the patient's previous surgical treatments that might be relevant to the presenting illness or to provide optimal clinical management.

Name: Abnormal superficial temporal artery morphology
Def: Any structural abnormality of a superficial temporal artery, originating from the external carotid artery and passing over the zygomatic process. The superficial temporal artery is located on the superficial parts of the forehead and sides of the head and face.

Name: Skip lesions on temporal artery biopsy
Def: Patchy inflammation of the superficial temporal artery, forming isolated foci of arteritis.
Comment: This feature may be observed in temporal arteritis. The foci are characterized by mononuclear cell infiltrates or a granulomatous process with multinucleated giant cells.

Name: Abnormal brain-evoked potentials
Def: Any anomaly of brain-evoked potentials, defined as potentials generated by exteroceptive stimuli reflect synchronized activity by neuronal and axonal groups in the central nervous system (CNS) resulting from the arrival of nerve impulses after stimulation of a peripheral nerve or its receptors. Depending on the type of stimulus, evoked potentials are categorized as visual (VEP), auditory (AEP), or somatosensory (SSEP). Motor evoked potentials (MEP) occur when the brain's motor area is stimulated. They result from the activation of a sufficient number of motor units.

Name: Sputum infectious agent
Def: The presence of an infectious agent in the sputum, as characterized by sputum culture or other investigation.

Name: Positive Mycobacterium avium sputum culture
Def: Growth of mycobacterium avium in a sputum culture.
Comment: Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare complex (MAC) is a ubiquitous environmental microorganism whose pathogenicity ranges from innocuous colonization to disease, in immunocompetent as well as immunocompromised individuals.

Name: Positive bloodstream infectious agent antigen test
Def: A test result demonstrating the presence of an antigen (marker such as a protein against which an antibody reacts) specific to an infectious agent.

Name: Positive bloodstream Cysticercosis antigen test
Def: Demonstration of an antigen specific to Cysticercosis in the bloodstream.
Comment: Cysticercosis, the infection with the larval stage of Taenia solium, is a cause of neurological symptoms including seizures.

Name: Klazomania
Def: Involuntary attacks of compulsive paroxysmal shouting. The shouting behaviors may be extremely loud and not related to the ongoing mental state of the affected individual. Shouting episodes may occur in bouts and last for several hours.

Name: Coprolalia
Def: Coprolalia denotes the involuntary utterance of obscenities. Intent is an important classifier in coprolalic behaviors, and unfortunately it remains unclear how to objectively distinguish coprolalia from common swearing.
Comment: In Tourette syndrome (TS), the unintended expression of coprolalic behaviors is encountered in about one-fifth of patients. Typical coprolalic behaviors in TS are characterized by the utterance of single short obscenities (e.g., in English, so-called four-letter words) with a different pitch or tone from ongoing speech. There have been only a few reports of patients exhibiting coprolalia in other neurological conditions, such as neurodevelopmental disorders (e.g., Kleine-Levin and fragile X syndrome), neurodegenerative syndromes (e.g., FTD, Alzheimer's disease, and chorea-acanthocytosis), after focal brain lesions, in encephalitis lethargica, or as ictal phenomenon.

Name: Continuous involuntary vocalizations
Def: Continuous groaning, moaning, grunting, and shrieking.
Comment: Continuous involuntary vocalizations are most frequently associated with neurodegenerative diseases. in dementias, such as Alzheimer's disease and Huntington disease, continuous involuntary vocalizations, often labeled as vocally disruptive behavior, are part of a spectrum of behavioral symptoms that correlate with the severity of cognitive impairment and may be exacerbated with emotional arousal. Purposeless noisemaking, for example, groaning or howling in parkinsonism may also be encountered.

Name: Aplasia/hypoplasia of the uterine cervix
Def: Congenital absence or underdevelopment of the uterine cervix.

Name: Cervical hypoplasia
Def: Underdevelopment of the uterine cervix.

Name: Primary peritoneal serous papillary adenocarcinoma
Def: A serous papillary adenocarcinoma that arises from the lining of the peritoneum

Name: Positive skin infectious agent test
Def: Any kind of test for an infectious agent in skin positive.

Name: Positive skin fungus test
Def: A test for fungus, e.g., fungal hyphae, in a skin specimen (usually a skin scraping), demonstrates the presence of fungi. Most commonly, a skin scraping is obtained using a small scalpel blade, the specimen is placed on a clean glass slide, a drop of potassium hydroxide (KOH) is added, and the specimen is examined microscopically for fungal structures such as hyphae or yeast.

Name: Nasal secretion eosinophilia
Def: Count of eosinophils in nasal secretions (for instance, nasal discharge) above the upper limit of normal.
Comment: Nasal eosinophil examinations are routine for patients with continuous nasal discharge symptoms (more than one week), for diagnosing nasal eosinophil-positive rhinitis.

Name: Nasal secretion neutrophilia
Def: Count of neutrophils in nasal secretions (for instance, nasal discharge) above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Seminal vesicle agenesis
Def: A developmental defect characterized by congenital absence of the seminal vesicle.

Name: Head impulse test has corrective saccade
Def: In a patient with nystagmus, The examiner briskly rotates the head of the patient while having the patient fixate on a target. A corrective saccade indicates the patient's eye will move in one direction and quickly return back to neutral position.

Name: Positive CSF infectious agent test
Def: Any kind of test for an infectious agent in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) positive.

Name: Positive CSF toxoplasma gondii nucleic acid test
Def: Detection of Toxoplasma gondii nucleic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) by a method such as polymerase chain reaction.

Name: Elevated circulating plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 activity
Def: The activity or concentration of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Abnormal circulating plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 activity
Def: The activity or concentration of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 in the blood circulation is outside of the limits of the normal range.

Name: Brain localization
Def: The pattern by which a phenotype is localized to or predominant in a part of the brain.

Name: Frontal cortical localization
Def: Localization to or predominance in the frontal cortex of the brain.

Name: Posterior fossa localization
Def: Localization to or predominance in the parts of the brain within the posterior fossa.

Name: Subcortical localization
Def: Localization to or predominance in the subcortical region of the brain.

Name: Parietal cortex localization
Def: Localization to or predominance in the parietal cortex of the brain.

Name: Occipital cortex localization
Def: Localization to or predominance in the occipital cortex of the brain.

Name: Tobacco use history
Def: History of use of tobacco products such as cigarettes.

Name: Bartholin cyst
Def: A fluid-filled sac near the vaginal opening. A Bartholin cyst is usually unilateral, asymptomatic blockage of the Bartholin gland, which may lead to a painless swelling.

Name: Abnormal circulating hepatic transaminase concentration
Def: Any deviation from the normal concentration in the blood circulation of alanine aminotransferase or aspartate aminotransferase.

Name: Reduced circulating aspartate aminotransferase concentration
Def: The concentration of aspartate aminotransferase (AST) in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine succinic acid level
Def: The concentration of succinic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Positive CSF varicella zoster virus nucleic acid test
Def: Detection of Varicella zoster virus nucleic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) by a method such as polymerase chain reaction.
Synonym: Positive CSF varicella zoster virus PCR
Varicella zoster virus PCR in CSF positive

Name: CSF pathogen-specific antibody positivity
Def: Positive serology in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) for a exposure to an infectious agent (i.e., examining CSF for the presence of pathogen-specific antibodies).

Name: Positive CSF nucleic acid pathogen test
Def: Positive (abnormal) result of a cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) test such as polymerase chain reaction that is targeted against a nucleic acid sequence specific for a pathogen.

Name: CSF varicella zoster antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that react against a component of varicella zoster virus.

Name: Reduced circulating interleukin 6 concentration
Def: The concentration of interleukin-6 in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating C12 acylcarnitine concentration
Def: Concentration of C12 acylcarnitines in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. C12 acylcarnitines have a twelve-carbon acyl chain.

Name: Frontalis muscle overactivity
Def: Increased activity of the frontalis muscle, causing a characteristic staring and astonished facial expression.

Name: Nasal dermoid cyst
Def: An ectodermal inclusion cyst containing skin and skin appendages; sebaceous glands, hair follicles, and occasionally sweat glands.

Name: Elevated circulating complement C3 concentration
Def: Concentration of the complement component C3 in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Abnormal circulating inhibin B concentration
Def: The concentration of inhibin B in the blood circulation is outside the limits of normal.

Name: Abnormal circulating lipoprotein(a) concentration
Def: The concentration of lipoprotein(a) in the blood circulation is outside the limits of normal.
Comment: Lipoprotein(a), also known as apolipoprotein(A), is encoded by LPA (HGNC:6667).

Name: Positive blood infectious agent test
Def: Any kind of test for an infectious agent in the blood circulation positive.

Name: Positive respiratory tract infectious agent test
Def: Any kind of test for an infectious agent in the respiratory tract positive.

Name: Body odor
Def: A perceived unpleasant smell given off by the body.

Name: Anal pain
Def: Pain in and around the anus or rectum (perianal region).

Name: Urethritis
Def: Inflammation of the urethra.
Comment: Urethritis is characterized by discharge, dysuria and/or urethral discomfort but may be asymptomatic. Common etiologies include gonococcal urethritis as well as infection by chlamydia trachomatis, mycoplasma genitalium, ureaplasma urealyticum, trichomonas vaginalis, anaerobes, herpes simplex virus, and adenovirus.

Name: Iris flocculi
Def: Multiple cysts along the pupillary margin that appear as spherical or tear-drop-shaped pigmented lesions or wrinkled masses emerging from the pupillary border of the iris.
Comment: Iris flocculi cause little, if any, visual impairment in most cases. However, they are occasionally associated with dissecting aortic aneurysm due to a shared mutation in smooth muscle that affects both the iris and the aorta. {xref="PMID:27843899"}

Name: Cornea verticillata
Def: Golden brown or gray deposits with a clockwise, whorl-like distribution in the inferior interpalpebal portion of the cornea.
Comment: Cornea verticillata can be a feature of Fabry disease and can occur as an adverse effect of mediciations including amiodarone. {xref="https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199"}

Name: Dysplastic gangliocytoma of the cerebellum
Def: It is a rare, slowly growing tumor of the cerebellum, a gangliocytoma sometimes considered to be a hamartoma, characterized by diffuse hypertrophy of the granular layer of the cerebellum.
Comment: Often associated with Cowden syndrome. {xref="PMID:11073535"}

Name: Moon facies
Def: A rounded, puffy face with fat deposits in the temporal fossa and cheeks, a double chin.
Comment: Moon facies can occur in persons treated with high-dose corticosteroids or with Cushing disease.

Name: Abnormal gonadotropin-releasing hormone concentration
Def: A deviation from the normal circulating concentration of the normal gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH). Intermittent GnRH secretion from the hypothalamus acts upon its receptor in the anterior pituitary to regulate the production and release of the gonadotropins, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH).

Name: Lack of gonadotropin-releasing hormone pulsatility
Def: Secretion of gonadotropin-releasing hormone that does not occur in a pulsatile fashion.
Comment: The decapeptide gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) is the master hormone regulating reproduction. GnRH is released from some 1000 neurons within the hypothalamus in a pulsatile manner. Hypothalamic GnRH gene expression occurs intermittently (in a pulsatile fashion). The primary target of hypothalamic GnRH is the anterior pituitary gonadotrope, which responds to stimulation by increasing the synthesis and secretion of the gonadotropins luteinzing hormone (LH) and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH), which in turn regulate gonadal development and function.

Name: Abnormal cardiac test
Def: Abnormal test result of cardiovascular physiology.

Name: Abnormal cardiac MRI
Def: Abnormal results of a MRI for the heart.

Name: Abnormal cardiac catheterization
Def: Abnormal results from the diagnostic tests resulting from cardiac catheterization.

Name: Abnormal cardiac exercise stress test
Def: Abnormal results of exercise on heart function.

Name: Abnormal resting energy expenditure from metabolic cart test
Def: Resting energy expenditure (REE) can be measured with indirect calorimetry using a metabolic cart, which is used to measure the oxygen consumption (VO2) and carbon dioxide production (VCO2).

Name: Abnormal cardiac biomarker test
Def: Abnormal blood test results measuring creatine kinase (CK), CK-MB, troponin (TROPI), myoglobin, and/or cardiac enzymes.

Name: Reduced brain gamma-aminobutyric acid level by MRS
Def: An decreased level of gamma-aminobutyric acid in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

Name: Abnormal circulating dehydroepiandrosterone concentration
Def: A deviation from the normal concentration of dehydroepiandrosterone in the circulation.
Comment: Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), which is produced in the adrenal glands and the gonads, represents the most abundant circulating steroid hormone. It is a metabolic intermediate in the biosynthesis of the androgen and estrogen sex steroids.

Name: Shoulder muscle aplasia
Def: Absence of shoulder muscles.

Name: Aplasia of the musculature of the pelvis
Def: Absence of the musculature of the pelvis.

Name: Hypoplasia of the musculature of the pelvis
Def: Underdevelopment of the musculature of the pelvis.

Name: Aplastic colon
Def: Congenital absence of the colon

Name: Cotton wool plaques
Def: Deposition of large, diffuse cotton wool amyloid plaques (CWPs) lacking a dense core and associated neuritic changes.

Name: Abnormal hepatic glycogen storage
Def: Change in normal glycogen storage content.

Name: Sclerosis of the carpal bones
Def: An elevation in bone density in one or more carpal bones of the hand.

Name: Abnormal neuron branching
Def: Abnormality of the structure and branching of the dendrites of a neuron.

Name: Abnormal natural killer subset distribution
Def: Any abnormality in the proportion natural killer subsets relative to the total number of natural killer cells.

Name: Nasolacrimal sac obstruction
Def: Blockage of the nasolacrimal sac.

Name: Nasolacrimal sac granuloma
Def: A mass of granulation tissue in response to chronic dacryocystitis as polypoid formations or they follow accidental injury, from probing and as a reaction to retained foreign bodies in the sac.

Name: Nasolacrimal sac papilloma
Def: Benign tumor of the nasolacrimal sac.

Name: Nasolacrimal sac epithelial papillary carcinoma
Def: The malignant epithelial neoplasm with papillary growths in the nasolacrimal sac.

Name: Conjunctival cicatrization
Def: An abnormality of the conjuctiva and ocular surface caused by conjunctival inflammation and associated with scarring.

Name: Dermolipoma of the conjunctiva
Def: A benign tumor composed of adipose tissue and dense connective tissue usually located near the temporal fornix.

Name: Myopic astigmatism
Def: A condition where one or both of the two principal meridians focus in the front of the retina when the eye is at rest.

Name: Latent hypermetropia
Def: A term to describe when farsightedness is masked when the accommodative muscles are used to increase the focusing power of the eye.

Name: Eyelid retraction
Def: With the eyes in primary position, the sclera is visible above the superior corneal limbus.

Name: Upper eyelid retraction
Def: An elevation of the eyelid above the normal level in the primary position.

Name: Collier's sign
Def: A unilateral or bilateral eyelid retraction due to midbrain lesions.

Name: Seborrhoeic blepharitis
Def: Inflammation of the eyelid due to overactivity of the sebaceous gland.
Comment: There is some suggestion that yeast bacterial strain called Malassezia furfur may cause seborrhoeic dermatitis. This yeast bacterial strain thrives in the oil of human skin especially in adults. {xref="PMID:10777824"}

Name: Nasolacrimal sac lymphoma
Def: A type of lymphoma that involves the nasolacrimal sac.

Name: Delayed canalization of nasolacrimal duct
Def: A very common condition in which the extreme end of the nasolacrimal duct underneath the inferior turbinate fails to complete its canalization in the newborn period.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity
Def: An avascular or abnormally vascularized retina that occurs in premature infants and can lead to blindness.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 1
Def: The retinal vessels stop and then a linear flat white line is present that usually runs the circumference of the vascular retina.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 2
Def: The accumulating neovascularization thickens and manifests as a linear bump. The neovascularization remains along the surface of the retina and does not extend off the retina into the cortical vitreous.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 3
Def: The neovascularization accumulates at the edge of the vascularized retina and extends into the vitreous (also called extra retinal fibrosis proliferation). In cases of Zone 2 and Zone 3, this may be sausage shaped. In more posterior Zone 1 disease, the stage 3 can appear as a direct extension of the normal retinal vessels but extending tangentially over the avascular retina.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 4
Def: Scar tissue that forms a continuous sheet coming up from the edge of the vascularized retina. This scar tissue can grow toward the vitreous base/posterior lens capsule resulting in traction, distortion, and even detachment.
Comment: Stage 4 can occur after treatment (unlike stages 1-3) and may be accelerated by the absence of vascular endothelial growth factor posttreatment leading to an accelerated cicatricial phase.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 4a
Def: A detachment that involves the peripheral retina that does not extend into the macula.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 4b
Def: A detachment that involves the peripheral retina that involves the macula itself. The detachment usually starts in the temporal periphery although can also involve the nasal retina as well.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 5
Def: Funnel detachment from the retina with generally traction in all four quadrants.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 5a
Def: An open funnel detachment of the retina with generally traction in all four quadrants.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 5b
Def: A closed funnel detachment of the retina with generally traction in all four quadrants.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity zone I
Def: Retinopathy which extends from the center of the optic disc to twice the distance from the center of the optic disc to the center of the macula.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity zone II
Def: Retinopathy which extends centrifugally from the edge of zone I to the nasal ora serrata.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity zone III
Def: Retinopathy which is a residual crescent of retina anterior to zone II.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity plus
Def: Venous dilatation and arteriolar tortuosity of the posterior retinal vessels and may later increase in severity to include iris vascular engorgement, poor pupillary dilatation (rigid pupil), and vitreous haze. This definition has been further refined in the later clinical trials in which the diagnosis of plus disease could be made if sufficient vascular dilatation and tortuosity are present in at least 2 quadrants of the eye.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity pre-plus
Def: As vascular abnormalities of the posterior pole that are insufficient for the diagnosis of plus disease but that demonstrate more arterial tortuosity and more venous dilatation than normal.
Comment: Over time, the vessel abnormalities of pre-plus may progress to frank plus disease as the vessels dilate and become more tortuous. {xref="PMID:16009843"}

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity threshold
Def: A retinopathy with a 50% likelihood of progressing to retinal detachment. Threshold disease is considered to be present when stage 3 retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is present in either zone I or zone II, with at least 5 continuous or 8 total clock hours of disease, and the presence of plus disease.

Name: Retinopathy of prematurity prethreshold
Def: High risk patients who were in Zone 1 (no Plus or stage 3) or Zone 2 with Plus or stage 3 but not both.

Name: Latent myopia
Def: The difference between total and manifest myopia.

Name: Paralytic ectropion
Def: A type of ectropion associated with orbicularis muscle weakness caused by cranial nerve VII palsy.

Name: Conjunctival dermolipoma
Def: A conjuctival lesion composed of adipose tissue and dense connective tissue. Such choristomas of dermal elements are normally found at the outer canthus, and have a gelatinous appearance. Classically, there is an indistinct posterior border (with the lesion frequently extending into the orbit) and a well-demarcated anterior border several millimeters posterior to the limbus.

Name: Absolute eccentric fixation
Def: Eccentric fixation in which the angle of eccentricity equals the objective angle of deviation.

Name: Abnormal ocular alignment
Def: Any deviation from the normal ocular alignment.

Name: Dissociated vertical deviation
Def: An incomitant tendency for an occluded eye to elevate and extort which resolves on uncovering.
Comment: Dissociated vertical deviation (DVD) occurs when the level of illumination received by either eye is reduced sufficiently and as a result eye deviates progressively upwards, but reverts to its original position when the level of illumination returns to normally acceptable levels. It may sometimes be so asymmetrical as to be virtually unilateral and is associated with heterotropia usually of early onset. {xref="https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0986-4123", xref="ISBN-13:978-0199679980"}

Name: Dissociated horizontal deviation
Def: A change in horizontal ocular alignment, unrelated to accommodation, that is brought about solely by a change in the balance of visual input from the two eyes.

Name: Alternating hypertropia
Def: A type of vertical tropia in which, when one eye is fixing, the other eye is deviated upwards.

Name: Alternating hyperphoria
Def: A type of vertical phoria in which, in dissociation, the occluded eye deviates upwards.

Name: Alternating hypotropia
Def: A type of vertical tropia in which, when one eye is fixing, the other eye is deviated downwards.

Name: Alternating hypophoria
Def: A type of vertical phoria in which, in dissociation, the occluded eye deviates downwards.

Name: Pseudophakia
Def: The term pseudophakia refers to having an artificial lens implanted after the natural eye lens has been removed. During cataract surgery the natural cloudy lens is replaced by an pseudophakia intraocular lens (IOL).

Name: Optic nerve gray crescent
Def: Having a characteristic appearance of a slate gray area of pigmentation within the disk margins that commonly appears along the inferotemporal or temporal neuroretinal rim areas.
Comment: This type of disk rim pigmentation can create the impression of neuroretinal rim thinning, and thus lead to the misdiagnosis of glaucoma or "glaucoma suspect" with attendant implications for overtreatment or unnecessary close monitoring of such patients. {xref="PMID:24862768"}

Name: Peripapillary atrophy
Def: Thinning in the layers of the retina and retinal pigment epithelium around the optic nerve.

Name: Foveal depigmentation
Def: Loss of pigment in the fovea centralis.

Name: Optic nerve sheath meningioma
Def: A benign tumor of meningothelial cells of the meninges that usually occurs in middle age. It is typically unilateral and there is an association with neurofibromatosis type 2.

Name: Periocular capillary hemangioma
Def: A capillary hemangioma surrounding the eyeball but within the orbit.

Name: Lymphangioma of the orbit
Def: A hamartoma of lymph vessels that usually presents in childhood. It tends to increase in size with head-down posture and with the Valsalva maneuver. Superficial lesions are visible as transilluminable cystic spaces of the lid or conjunctiva that may also contain blood. Deep lesions may cause gradual proptosis or present acutely with orbital pain and reduced vision due to hemorrhage.

Name: Orbital rhabdomyosarcoma
Def: A mesenchymal tumor that is considered to be the commonest primary orbital malignancy in children. Histologically, it may be differentiated into embryonal, alveolar, and pleomorphic types. It is usually intraconal or within the superior orbit.

Name: Food allergy
Def: Primary food allergies primarily occur as a result (most likely) of gastrointestinal sensitization to predominantly stable food allergens (glycoproteins). A secondary food allergy develops after primary sensitization to airborne allergens (e. g., pollen allergens) with subsequent reactions (due to cross-reactivity) to structurally related often labile allergens in (plant) foods.

Name: Latex allergy
Def: Latex allergy is an IgE-mediated immediate hypersensitivity response to natural rubber latex (NRL) protein with a variety of clinical signs ranging from contact urticaria, angioedema, asthma, and anaphylaxis.

Name: Food-induced anaphylaxis
Def: Food-induced anaphylaxis is a severe, potentially fatal, systemic allergic reaction that occurs suddenly after contact with an allergy-causing food.

Name: Venom-induced anaphylaxis
Def: A form of anaphylaxis that is triggered by exposure to venom.

Name: Stool xenobiotic
Def: Presence of xenobiotic in stool.

Name: Meconium xenobiotic
Def: Presence of a xenobiotic in meconium.

Name: Hair xenobiotic
Def: Presence of xenobiotic in hair.

Name: Plasma/serum xenobiotic
Def: Presence of a xenobiotic in plasma and/or serum.

Name: Gastric fluid xenobiotic
Def: Presence of a xenobiotic in gastric fluid.

Name: Decreased diastolic blood pressure
Def: Abnormal decrease in diastolic blood pressure.

Name: Decreased systolic blood pressure
Def: Abnormal decrease in systolic blood pressure.

Name: Isolated systolic hypertension
Def: Elevated systolic blood pressure without an elevated blood pressure.
Comment: Isolated systolic hypertension or an elevated systolic blood pressure without an elevated diastolic blood pressure is a known risk factor for incident heart failure in older adults. {xref="PMID:21947466"}

Name: Isolated diastolic hypotension
Def: A decrease in diastolic blood pressure (<60 mmHg) without a decrease in systolic blood pressure (> or = to 100 mmHg).
Comment: Isolated diastolic hypotension is a risk factor for incident heart failure. {xref="PMID:21947466"}

Name: Positive urine cocaine test
Def: Detection of cocaine or its major metabolite, benzoylecgonine, in urine.
Comment: Cocaine is an illicit stimulant that has a high potential for abuse and addiction.

Name: Positive urine barbiturate test
Def: Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as Phenobarbital in urine.
Comment: Barbiturates are central nervous depressants. They can reduce heart rate, breathing, and blood pressure. {xref="PMID:26339207"}

Name: Positive urine cannabinoid test
Def: Detection of delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) or other cannabinoid metabolites in urine.
Comment: Cannabis (marijuana, hashish) is the most widely used illegal drug in the world. The primary psychoactive component in cannabis is delta9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), which is rapidly metabolized to equipotent 11-hydroxy-THC (11-OH-THC) and non-psychoactive 11-nor-9-carboxy- delta9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THCCOOH). {xref="PMID:21134021"}

Name: Positive urine benzodiazepines test
Def: Detection of benzodiazepine metabolites, primarily nordiazepam, oxazepam, and temazepam, in urine.

Name: Positive urine amphetamine test
Def: Detection of amphetamine or its metabolites in urine.

Name: Positive urine opioid test
Def: Detection of opioids or opioid metabolites in urine.
Comment: Opiates are the natural or synthetic drugs that have a morphine-like pharmacological action. Medically, opiates are used primarily for relief of pain. Opiates include morphine and drugs structurally similar to morphine (eg, codeine, hydrocodone, hydromorphone, oxycodone).

Name: Abnormal stool urobilinogen concentration
Def: Abnormal concentration of urobilinogen present in the stool.

Name: Increased stool urobilinogen concentration
Def: An increased amount of urobilinogen present in the stool.
Comment: Urobilinogen is formed from the reduction of bilirubin. An increased amount of urobilinogen in the urine may be indicative of liver disease. {xref="https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0736-9199"}

Name: Positive blood barbiturate test
Def: Detection of barbiturate metabolites such as Phenobarbital in blood.

Name: Abnormal glossopharyngeal nerve morphology
Def: Any structural anomaly of the glossopharyngeal nerve, the ninth paired cranial nerve (CN IX).
Comment: The glossopharyngeal nerve originates in the medulla oblongata. It Innervates the oropharynx, carotid body and sinus, as well as the posterior third of the tongue (where it mediates taste sensation), the middle ear cavity and the Eustachian tube. Additionally, it innervates the stylopharyngeus muscle of the pharynx.

Name: Abnormal great auricular nerve morphology
Def: Any structural anomaly of a great auricular nerve.
Comment: The great auricular nerve originates from the cervical plexus and ascends to the posterior inferior region of the parotid gland, where it divides into several small branches. The nerve supplies sensation for an extensive area of the face including the skin over the parotid gland and the mastoid process and the surface of the external ear. The great auricular nerve winds around the posterior aspect of the sternocleidomastoid muscle. After perforating the deep fascia, it ascends upon the sternocleidomastoid muscle beneath the platysma to the parotid gland, where it divides into an anterior and a posterior branch. The anterior branch provides sensory innervation to the skin overlying the parotid gland and communicates with the facial nerve in the substance of the gland. The posterior branch innervates the skin over the mastoid and the posterior surface of the auricle except at its upper part.

Name: Abnormal hypopharynx morphology

Name: Abnormal lacrimal artery morphology
Def: An abnormality of a lacrimal artery.

Name: Abnormal lacrimal sac morphology
Def: An abnormality of a lacrimal sac.

Name: Abnormal lateral cricoarytenoid muscle morphology
Def: Any structural abnormality of a lateral crico-arytenoid muscle, which extends from the lateral cricoid cartilage to the muscular process of the arytenoid cartilage, and can adduct the vocal cords, which closes the rima glottidis and thereby protects the airway.

Name: Abnormality of lateral pterygoid muscle
Def: An abnormality of a lateral pterygoid muscle.

Name: Abnormality of lateral rectus extra-ocular muscle
Def: An abnormality of a lateral rectus extra-ocular muscle.

Name: Abnormality of levator anguli oris
Def: An abnormality of a levator anguli oris.

Name: Abnormality of levator labii superioris
Def: An abnormality of a levator labii superioris.

Name: Abnormal levator palpebrae superioris morphology
Def: An abnormality of a levator palpebrae superioris.

Name: Abnormality of levator veli palatini muscle
Def: An abnormality of a levator veli palatini.

Name: Abnormal lingual artery morphology
Def: Any structural abnormality of a lingual artery.

Name: Abnormal lingual nerve morphology
Def: Any structural anomaly of a lingual nerve.
Comment: The lingual nerve (LN) is one of the two terminal branches of the posterior division of the mandibular nerve. It supplies the general sensation to the mucosa of the anterior two-thirds of the tongue, the sublingual mucosa, the mandibular lingual gingiva and the floor of the mouth.The chorda tympani nerve, a branch of the facial nerve joins this nerve carrying taste fibers from the anterior two third of the tongue and parasympathetic fibers to the submandibular ganglion.

Name: Abnormality of lingual tonsil
Def: An abnormality of a lingual tonsil.

Name: Abnormal mandible condylar process morphology
Def: An abnormality of a mandible condylar process.

Name: Abnormal mandible coronoid process morphology
Def: An abnormality of a mandible coronoid process.

Name: Abnormal mandibular symphysis morphology
Def: A structural abnormality of a mandibular symphysis.

Name: Abnormal cardiac magnetic resonance imaging finding
Def: Abnormal finding by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which uses non-ionizing radiation via a strong magnetic field and radio frequency energy to generate three dimensional images. This term comprises findings that are specific to MRI. Findings such as ventricular spetum defect that can be detected by multiple modalities should be coded separately.

Name: Elevated myocardial native T2
Def: Increased duration of myocardial T2 time without gadolinium contrast. Elevated T2, which can detect myocardial edema.

Name: Myocardial late gadolinium enhancement
Def: Areas of high signal intensity in magnetic resonance imaging of the heart appearing 10 to 15 minutes after injection of the intercellular contrast agent gadolinium.
Comment: LGE can be detected in post-infarct scars, inflammation, as well as non-ischemic CMP, cardiac neoplasm and storage diseases such as amyloidosis.

Name: Pericardial late gadolinium enhancement
Def: Areas of high signal intensity in magnetic resonance imaging of the pericardium appearing around 10 minutes after injection of the intercellular contrast agent gadolinium.
Comment: Late gadolinium enhancement in the pericardium may be observed with pericardial inflammation.

Name: Elevated myocardial native T1
Def: Increased duration of myocardial T1 time without gadolinium contrast. T1 mapping consists of quantifying the T1 relaxation time of a tissue by using analytical expressions of image-based signal intensities. A fundamental principle of MR imaging is that the signal intensity of pixels is based on the relaxation of hydrogen nuclei protons in a static magnetic field. The T1 relaxation times between two tissues vary substantially. Edema, fat infiltration, and fibrosis also cause differences in T1 relaxivity.

Name: Bronchoconstriction
Def: Tightening of smooth muscle surrounding the bronchi and bronchioles with consequent wheezing and shortness of breath.
Comment: Occasionally in the medical literature, the word bronchospasm is interpreted to mean a more sudden narrowing than bronchoconstriction, but this usage is inconsistent and in everyday practice the terms are used as synonyms. We treat the terms as synonyms and recommend using HPO modifiers to denote acuteness or chronicity if needed.

Name: Formation of multiple pronuclei during fertilization
Def: Pronuclei formation is a critical process during fertilization. Normally, there are two pronuclei (2PN), including the paternal pronucleus and the maternal pronucleus, in the zygote after fertilization. It is generally accepted that multiple pronuclei (MPN) formation is due to the abnormal extrusion of the second polar body or to abnormal fertilization with multiple sperm. The MPN therefore can cause infertility and recurrent failure of IVF/ICSI.
Comment: Three pro-nuclei (3PN) prevalence among all pregnancies has been estimated to be approximately 1% to 3%, whereas it accounts for 15% to 18% of cytogenetically abnormal cases among spontaneous abortions.

Name: Kinesiophobia
Def: An excessive, irrational, and debilitating fear of carrying out a physical movement due to a feeling of vulnerability to painful injury or reinjury.

Name: Impaired renal tubular reabsorption of bicarbonate
Def: Decreased renal tubular reabsorption of bicarbonate.

Name: History of congenital HPV infection
Def: A congenital human papillomavirus (HPV) infection of the newborn. Congential HPV infection can manifest as condyloma cuminata in the newborn.

Name: Anti-desmoglein-1 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against desmoglein-1, a dermal cell adhesion molecule.

Name: Anti-desmoglein-3 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against desmoglein-3, a dermal cell adhesion molecule.

Name: Anti-envoplakin antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against envoplakin, a cytoskeletal linker protein that links intermediate filaments to cellular junctions.

Name: Anti-periplakin antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against periplakin.

Name: Anti-desmoplakin I antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against desmoplakin-1.

Name: Anti-desmoplakin II antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against desmoplakin-II.

Name: Anti-BP230 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against BP230.
Comment: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) is an autoimmune disease associated with subepidermal blistering due to autoantibodies directed against BP180 and BP230. BP180 is currently considered as the major pathogenic autoantigen.

Name: Anti-BP180 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against BP180.
Comment: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) is an autoimmune disease associated with subepidermal blistering due to autoantibodies directed against BP180 and BP230. BP180 is currently considered as the major pathogenic autoantigen.

Name: Anti-laminin 332 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against laminin-332.
Comment: Anti-laminin gamma1 pemphigoid (ALG1P) is an autoimmune subepidermal bullous disease characterized by autoantibodies to a 200-kDa acidic noncollagenous glycoprotein of the lower lamina lucida. In contrast, anti-laminin-332 mucous membrane pemphigoid (MMP) is an autoimmune blistering disease characterized by autoantibodies to various subunits of laminin-332 of the basement membrane.

Name: Anti-laminin 6 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against laminin-6.

Name: Anti-laminin gamma1 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against laminin gamma-1.
Comment: Anti-laminin gamma1 pemphigoid (ALG1P) is an autoimmune subepidermal bullous disease characterized by autoantibodies to a 200-kDa acidic noncollagenous glycoprotein of the lower lamina lucida. In contrast, anti-laminin-332 mucous membrane pemphigoid (MMP) is an autoimmune blistering disease characterized by autoantibodies to various subunits of laminin-332 of the basement membrane.

Name: Anti-laminin antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against a laminin. Laminins are major components of the basement membrane.

Name: Anti-integrin antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against an integrin. Integrins are a family of cell adhesion molecules with 24 known integrin heterodimers. Integrins transduce mechanical and biochemical signals from fibrotic extracellular matrix into the cell, activate latent TGFbeta, and subsequently modulate fibroblast adhesion, migration, and growth.

Name: Anti-transglutaminase 6 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against transglutaminase 6.

Name: Anti-LAD-1 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against LAD-1, which is the soluble 120 kDa ectodomain of BP180.
Comment: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) is an autoimmune blistering skin disease characterized by an autoimmune response to type XVII collagen (BP180). The generation of anti-BP180-NC16A IgG autoantibodies is considered to be central to the pathogenesis of BP, in part due to the close correlation between serum concentration and disease activity. However, about 60% of BP patients also generate IgG autoantibodies against LAD-1.

Name: Anti-LABD97 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against LABD97, which is structurally identical to a portion of the extracellular domain of BPAg2. BPAg2, a 180 kDa bullous pemphigoid antigen, is a transmembrane protein important for basement membrane cohesion.

Name: Antigliadin antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against gliadin.

Name: Anti-reticulin antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against reticulin.

Name: Anti-type VII collagen antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against collagen type VII.
Comment: Anti-type VII collagen may be detected in bullous pemphigoid patients at time of relapse.

Name: False perception of self-motion
Def: A perception that one's body is moving or swaying despite lack of motion of the body.

Name: Non-spinning vertigo
Def: A perception of unsteadiness of dizziness that is not characterized bythe spinning sensation of classic vertigo, but rather by an oscillatory perception (rocking, bobbing, or swaying despite the fact that the subject is not moving).
Comment: This feature can be observed in mal de debarquement syndrome and in vestibular paroxysmia.

Name: Infection-associated lymphopenia
Def: Decreased lymphocyte count during infections.

Name: Primary obstructive megaureter
Def: Megaurater associated with obstruction or an adynamic ureteral segment in the ureterovesical junction.

Name: Encysted hydrocele of the cord
Def: A type of hydrocele testis in which both the proximal and distal portions of processus vaginalis get obliterated while the central portion remains patent and fluid accumulates within it.

Name: Congenital hydrocele
Def: Congenital hydrocele occurs when processus vaginalis is patent and communicates with the peritoneal cavity. This communication allows the movement of peritoneal fluid but is too small to allow the intra-abdominal contents to herniate through.

Name: Infantile hydrocele
Def: Infantile Hydrocele is a type pf hydrocele in which the processus vaginalis gets obliterated at the level of the deep inguinal ring. However, the portion distal to it remains patent and allows fluid accumulation.

Name: Reduced proportion of mucosal-associated invariant T cells
Def: A decreased proportion of circulating mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells relative to total T cell count.
Comment: Flow cytometry may identify MAIT cells as CD3+Valpha7+CD161hi or Tet-MR1+CD161hi.

Name: Puerpural onset
Def: Onset of a phenotypic abnormality or a disease during childbirth or in the period immediately following.

Name: AA amyloidosis
Def: Extracellular tissue deposition of fibrils that are composed of fragments of and/or intact serum amyloid A protein, a hepatic acute phase reactant.

Name: Fracture type
Def: Category of fracture. Terms from this subontology can be used together with terms in the subontology that descends from Bone fracture (HP:0020110).

Name: Greenstick fracture
Def: A type of fracture in which the broken bone is not completely separated.

Name: Transverse fracture
Def: A type of fracture in which the break is in a straight line across the bone.

Name: Spiral fracture
Def: A type of fracture in which the break spirals around the bone.

Name: Oblique fracture
Def: A type of fracture in which there is a diagonal break across the bone.

Name: Compression fracture
Def: A type of fracture in which the bone is crushed, causing the broken bone to be wider or flatter in appearance.

Name: Comminuted fracture
Def: A type of fracture in which the break is in three or more pieces and fragments are present at the fracture site.

Name: Segmental fracture
Def: A type of fracture in which the same bone is fractured in two places, so there is a floating segment of bone.

Name: Open fracture
Def: A type of fracture in which there is an open wound or break in the skin near the site of the broken bone.

Name: Closed fracture
Def: A type of fracture in which the broken bone that does not penetrate the skin.

Name: Avulsion fracture
Def: A type of fracture that is localied near to a a tendon or ligament and a small fragment of bone is separated from the main mass of bone as a result of physical trauma.

Name: Displaced fracture
Def: A type of fracture in which the ends of the fractured bone are no longer aligned.

Name: Exanthem
Def: A widespread rash.
Comment: An exanthem may be caused by an infection or represent a reaction to a toxin or an immune response and may be accompanied by symptoms such as fever, malaise and headache.

Name: Intestinal inflammation
Def: A reaction characterizeds by capillary dilatation, leukocytic infiltration, redness, heat, pain, swelling localized to the in the intestinal tract.

Name: Abnormal apoptosis
Def: Any abnormality of programmed cell death (apoptosis), which is defined as the orchestrated collapse of a cell characterized by membrane blebbing, cell shrinkage, condensation of chromatin, and fragmentation of DNA followed by rapid engulfment of the corpse by neighboring cells. Apoptosis is distinguished from death by necrosis by the absence of an associated inflammatory response.

Name: Decreased FasL-mediated apoptosis
Def: A reduced amount of programmed cell death upon stimulation of the FAS receptor, which normally induces caspase-8 dependent apoptosis.

Name: Glomerular proteinuria
Def: A type of proteinuria characterized by increased permeability of the glomerular capillary wall to macromolecules (particularly albumin), whereby protein excretion can reach 20 g/24 h and consists mainly of albumin.
Comment: In contrast to glomerular proteinuria, tubular proteinuria is generally less than 1-2 g/24 h. In tubular proteinuria, although albumin remains a significant component, there is a relatively much greater increase in proteins of smaller than 60 000 Da

Name: Abnormal lung development
Def: A structural defect associated with abnormal development of the lung.

Name: Pancreatic alpha-cell hyperplasia
Def: A diffuse and specific increase in the number of alpha-cells.
Comment: Alpha cells are glucagon-secreting endocrine cells in the pancreatic islets of the pancreas.

Name: 3-4 metacarpal synostosis
Def: A congenital hand malformation characterized by the coalescence of the coalescence of third and fourth metacarpals (i.e., those corresponding to the middle and ring fingers).
Comment: Metacarpal synostosis is best described as a failure of differentiation causing a union between 2 adjacent metacarpals.
Synonym: Middle and ring finger metacarpal synostosis
Synostosis of third and the fourth metacarpal bones

Name: Abnormal iliac artery morphology
Def: Any structural anomaly of the iliac artery.
Comment: The common iliac artery originates from the aorta and divides into the internal and external iliac arteries, supplying oxygenated blood to the lower extremities (via the external iliac artery), the pelvis and its viscera (via internal iliac artery) as well as the peritoneum, psoas major muscle, ureter, and surrounding tissues.

Name: Iliac artery aneurysm
Def: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the iliac artery.

Name: Abnormal interest
Def: Any deviation from normal intensity or subject of a person's interests, which can be defined as a state of giving selective attention to something.

Name: Persistent preoccupation with parts of objects
Def: A type of abnormal interest characterized by a persistent and intense focus on parts of a toy/object. For example, affected individuals may spin the wheels on a toy car rather than drive the toy car.
Synonym: Fixated interest with parts of objects

Name: Fixated interests
Def: Highly restricted, fixated interests that are abnormal in intensity or focus (e.g., strong attachment to or preoccupation with unusual objects, excessively circumscribed or perseverative interests).

Name: Abnormal language feature
Def: The presence of any atypical form of expressive language.

Name: Pronoun reversal
Def: Atypical language features characterized by first vs. second or third person pronoun errors such as using 'you' or 'he/she' in place of 'I'.
Comment: These errors are attested in normal toddlers' spontaneous speech, albeit at varying rates; pronouns typically emerge around 1.5 years of age and reversals are most common before 2.5 years. A higher rate of pronoun reversal may be expected of people with autism spectrum disorder.

Name: Involuntary vocalization
Def: Production of sound done without will or conscious control. Involuntary vocalizations include tics, stereotypies vocalizations as part of dystonia or chorea, continuous vocalizing behaviors such as groaning or grunting, pathological laughter and crying, and others. These vocalizations are not recognized as socially or culturally appropriate.

Name: Reduced frequency of facial expressions
Def: The number of times facial expressions are produced in a given period is lower than expected given the social and cultural context.

Name: Use of another person's body to communicate
Def: Moving another person's hand, body part, or body to communicate a desire, e.g. pushing or pulling someone toward a desired object or placing someone's hand on something.

Name: Fixated interest with abnormal focus
Def: A fixated interest in a specific topic that is atypical for the social context of the individual, such as topics of a non-social nature like fossils or vacuum cleaners.

Name: Fixated interest with abnormal intensity
Def: An abnormally intense interest in a topic or object that is not atypical for the social context of the affected person.
Comment: Typical examples of fixated interests with abnormal intensity include flipping the flag on a mailbox up and down repeatedly for long periods of time, taking a fork or other such objects everywhere, repeatedly lining up toys in the same order, or repeatedly reading information about a favorite topic such as a sports team.

Name: Sensory seeking
Def: Unusual interest in sensory aspects of the environment.

Name: Reduced production of gestures
Def: Diminished use of typical non-verbal conversational gestures such as shaking the head to indicate no or nodding the head to indicate yes.

Name: Reduced cooperative play
Def: Impairment in a child's ability to be able to play in a way that involves peer collaboration. Collaborative play involves things such as verbal and non-verbal communication (e.g., self-initiated interactions), turn-taking, sharing, reciprocity, and collaborative problem-solving. It is often contrasted to parallel play, which involves a form of social play in which two children do similar activities near each other and often mimic each other. Typically developing children develop collaborative play between the ages of 4 and 5.

Name: Lack of interest in peers
Def: Lack of interest in peers of comparable age and social groups is evident when an individual, such as a child, shows more interest in socializing with adults rather than children their own age.
Synonym: Reduced desire to interact with peers

Name: Reduced sharing of interests
Def: An absence or abnormally low frequency of engaging with others to share personal interests or topics. Interest sharing includes offers of information about oneself as a form of social interaction.
Comment: Interest sharing should be assessed in the context of cultural and developmental norms.

Name: Reduced object sharing
Def: An absence or reduction in object sharing. Object sharing is an early emerging social skill in which a child will share objects such as toys, balls, or books with parents or peers during object play.
Comment: This term should not be applied to children younger than one year of life.

Name: Abnormal communicative facial expressions
Def: Abnormal expressions (movements or position of muscles of the face that convey the emotional state of an individual to observers during social interactions) comprising abnormalities of quantity, range, context-appropriateness, and quality.
Comment: This term describes the way facial expressions are used for communicating to other people (social communication). This term does not comprise abnormal facial expressions related to motoric neurological deficits such as hypomimic facies observed in individuals with Parkinson syndrome.

Name: Facial expressions that do not match the context
Def: Production of facial expressions that are misaligned with the social context.

Name: Abnormal quality of facial expression
Def: Spontaneous production of communicative facial expressions that have poor quality or are exaggerated or muted.
Comment: This feature does not include facial motor tics.

Name: Abnormal gesture use
Def: Abnormality in the use of gestures defined as hand, shoulder, and head movements that convey a shared meaning within a culture that replace or supplement verbal communication.
Comment: Gestures refer to movements of the arms, hand, shoulders, or head and do not include facial expressions.

Name: Poor conversational reciprocity
Def: Reduced use of reciprocal (back and forth) conversation, as compared to what would be expected for language level.
Comment: Poor conversational reciprocity may be characterized by deficits in the ability to make comments about discussion topics of others, failure to ask questions, and not building a conversation on comments of others. Affected persons may not know what to say next in a conversation, may not notice if others are bored with a given topic, may conduct a one-sided conversation (talking but not listening), or may veer off topic more than is socially acceptable.

Name: Ectopic tooth eruption
Def: A condition in which the permanent teeth, because of deficiency of growth in the jaw or segment of jaw, assume a path of eruption that intercepts a primary tooth, causes its premature loss and produces a consequent malposition of the permanent tooth.

Name: Corpus cavernosum hypoplasia
Def: A developmental anomaly characterized by undergrowth of the corpus cavernosum.

Name: Elevated circulating thymine concentration
Def: Concentration of the nucleobase thymine in the blood circulation above the normal range.

Name: Positive lactose hydrogen breath test
Def: Elevated hydrogen gas level in exhaled breath following oral administration of lactose. In individuals with lactose intolerance, undigested lactose in the colon will be metabolized by colonic bacteria, releasing hydrogen gas.
Comment: The enzyme lactase phlorizin hydrolase, located at the intestinal brush border, is necessary for the hydrolysis of lactose, the main sugar in milk. Due to the genetically programmed decrease in intestinal lactase activity that occurs post-weaning (lactase non-persistence), a large proportion of the human population loses, in adult age, the possibility to digest and absorb lactose.

Name: Triggered by exposure to medication
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to a medication.

Name: Triggered by allopurinol
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to allopurinol.

Name: Ameliorated by oral zinc supplementation
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by oral zinc supplementation.

Name: Curved dental root
Def: A root of a tooth that is more rounded than normal.

Name: Abnormal four chamber view of the fetal heart
Def: The four-chamber (4Ch) view of the fetal heart is the most widely used screening examination for the detection of structural cardiac abnormalities during routine fetal ultrasonography. In the healthy normal fetus, the apical 4Ch view demonstrates four well-developed chambers, a concordant atrioventricular (AV) connection, unobstructed AV valves (mitral and tricuspid valves), the foramen ovale flap opening into left atrium (LA), and an intact interventricular septum. Additionally, the pulmonary venous opening can be visualized at the LA wall. Any structural deviations from normal anatomy may lead to congenital heart disease that can be determined by the 4Ch view of the fetal heart's ultrasound imaging.

Name: Spleen hamartoma
Def: A hamartomatous lesion (benign focal lesions composed of disorganized tissue elements) localized in the spleen.

Name: Positive lupus band test
Def: Deposits of immunoglobulins and complement components along the dermoepidermal junction.

Name: Bone marrow erythroid vacuolization
Def: Formation of vacuoles (a space within a cell that is empty of cytoplasm, lined with a membrane, and filled with fluid) in the cytoplasm of erythroid precursors in the bone marrow.
Comment: See Figure 1 of PMID:29716882.

Name: Triggered by electromagnetic field
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to an electromagnetic field.

Name: Exposure history
Def: Information about current and past exposure to metals, dust, fibers, fumes, chemicals, biologic hazards, radiation, noise, and/or vibration at work or home.

Name: Asbestos exposure
Def: History of exposure to asbestos, a fibrous mineral with physical and chemical properties that make it resistant to heat and degradation.
Comment: Mesothelioma is an occupational disease occurring as a result of asbestos exposure in the workplace.

Name: Medication history
Def: Information about current or past medications taken by an individual.

Name: Aminoglycoside exposure
Def: History of having taken aminoglycoside antibiotics.
Comment: Aminoglycosides include gentamycin, tobramycin, amikacin, kanamycin, and streptomycin, and may be associated with ototoxicity.

Name: Statin exposure
Def: History of having taken statins, also known as HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors.
Comment: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, or statins, are widely used for hyperlipidemia and cardiovascular disease.

Name: Potassium-sparing diuretic exposure
Def: History of having taken a potassium-sparing diuretic exposure such as amiloride, eplerenone, spironolactone, and triamterene.

Name: Carbamazepine exposure
Def: History of having taken carbamazepine.

Name: Valproate exposure
Def: History of having taken valproate (valproic acid).

Name: Hydralazine exposure
Def: History of having taken hydralazine.

Name: Calcium channel blocker exposure
Def: History of having taken a calcium channel blocker such as amlodipine, nicardipine, nifedipine, verapamil, or diltiazem.

Name: Triggered by nickel
Comment: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure (cutaneous contact) to nickel.

Name: Triggered by poison ivy, poson oak, or sumac
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure (cutaneous contact) to poison ivy, poison oak, and poison sumac. These three plants each contain urushiol. Contact with these plants is the most common causes of clinically diagnosed allergic contact dermatitis.
Synonym: Contact with poison ivy, poison oak, or sumac

Name: History of exclusive breast feeding
Def: A past medical history of having been fed exclusively by breast feeding.

Name: Nutrition history
Def: A part of the past medical history consisting of information about the typical food intake of an individual.

Name: High dietary oxalate intake
Def: A history of ingestion of a relatively high amount of foods containing high levels of oxalate, such as green-leaf vegetables, tea, nuts, chocolate and rhubarb.
Comment: An increased load of dietary oxalate presented to the kidneys has been linked to different kidney-related conditions and injuries.
Synonym: Foods high in oxalate, high intake

Name: Recent honey ingestion
Def: A history of ingestion of honey in recent weeks.

Name: Raw egg-white ingestion
Def: A history of eating raw egg whites.

Name: Exacerbated by sodium channel blocking agent exposure
Def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by administration of sodium channel blocking agents such as phenytoin, carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, lamotrigine, topiramate, and zonisamide.
Synonym: Sodium channel blocking drugs aggravate findings

Name: Addictive nitrous oxide use
Def: Addiction to inhaled nitrous oxide gas (N2O) is a growing concern.

Name: Recent blood transfusion
Def: A past medical history of a recent blood transfusion.

Name: Ameliorated by colchicine
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by administration of colchizine.

Name: Ameliorated by vitamin D
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by administration of vitamin D.

Name: Exacerbated by phenytoin exposure
Def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by administration of phenytoin.

Name: Triggered by angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to anngiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor such as benazepril, captopril, enalapril, fosinopril, and lisinopril.

Name: Prostaglandin E1 exposure
Def: History of having been treateed with prostaglandin E1.

Name: 5-fluorouracil exposure
Def: History of having been treated with 5-fluorouracil.

Name: 6-mercaptopurine exposure
Def: History of having been treateed with 6-mercaptopurine.

Name: Isoniazid exposure
Def: History of having been treateed with isoniazid.

Name: Absent cavum septum pellucidum
Def: The cavum septum pellucidum (CSP) is an important fetal midline forebrain landmark that is normally visible by prenatal sonography. This term refers to the lack of visibility of the CSP on prenatal sonography. The CSP normally can be visualized between 18 and 37 weeks of gestation. Lack of visualization of the CSP in this time period generally requires follow up and may indicate the presence of underlying malformations such as malformations of the corpus callosum. The lack of CSP before 18 weeks or after 37 weeks of gestation (or postnatally) is considered a normal finding.

Name: Fetal abdominal cyst
Def: Fetal abdominal cysts are usually detected during the second trimester anomaly scan or discovered incidentally at later gestations. However, a definitive diagnosis is often not made until postnatal life. The most common etiologies of fetal abdominal cysts are: ovarian, gastrointestinal cystic duplication, liver and choledochal, meconium pseudocysts, mesenteric and adrenal. Following identification of a cyst, careful morphological assessment allows the prediction of their natural history and importantly, the likelihood of surgical intervention being required postnatally.
Comment: Fetal ultrasound cannot always distinguish the origin of a cystic lesion in the abdominal region.

Name: Fetal bowel dilatation
Def: Fetal bowel dilatation is characterized by fluid-filled intestinal loops which measure at least fifteen millimeters long or seven millimeters in diameter. Ultrasonographic image of dilated fetal bowel is a sign of intestinal mechanical or functional obstruction and its prevalence will depend on the underlying condition: bowel atresia or stenosis, malrotation with volvulus, meconium ileus, total colonic aganglionosis, and meconium plug syndrome. The etiology of fetal bowel dilatation is a difficult prenatal diagnosis since ultrasound has limited accuracy for bowel evaluation.

Name: Left ventricular dilatation
Def: Enlargement of the chamber of the left heart ventricle.

Name: Fetal trigonocephaly
Def: A fetal ultrasound finding defined by flattening of the occiput with pointing of the frontal bones and brachycephaly with an increased cephalic index. It is characterized by keel shaped deformity of forehead with midline ridge, bilateral fronto temporal constriction with compensatory biparietal expansion, supra orbital and lateral orbital retrusion and hypotelorism. This finding is said to resemble a strawberry.
Comment: Fetal trigonocephaly can be seen in trisomy 18 (or other chromosomal abnormalities) and monogenic syndromes, particularly also in craniosynostosis syndromes and some skeletal dysplasias.

Name: Abnormal fetal heart outflow tract
Def: A prenatal anomaly of the outflow tract. Fetal ultrasound may not always be able to easily and accurately describe the outflow anomaly, but can detect abnormal anatomy. Often, follow up with a fetal echo is recommended, but fetal ultrasound is limited.
Comment: The left ventricular outflow tract is the anatomic structure through which the left ventricular stroke volume passes towards the aorta. The right ventricular outflow tract is the structure through which the right ventricular stroke volume passes to the pulmonary artery.

Name: Recent past medical history
Def: History of events that precede the current presenting condition and are thought to be of potential relevance, having occurred in the hours, days, or weeks before the current condition.

Name: History of recent viral illness
Def: Medical history of a viral illness in recent weeks.

Name: History of recent dental procedure
Def: Medical history of a dental procedure in recent weeks.

Name: Abnormal hepatic artery morphology
Def: Any structural anomaly of the hepatic artery or its branches.

Name: Hepatic artery hyperplasia
Def: Abnormal increase in size of the hepatic arteries.

Name: Lymph node necrosis
Def: Areas of necrotic tissue within a lymph node.

Name: Multinucleated neuron
Def: Neurons that contain more than one nucleus.

Name: History of recent contralateral injury
Def: A history of an injury that occurred several hours, days, or weeks before the current presenting complaint and is located on the other side of the body relative to the current presenting complaint.

Name: Alternating laterality
Def: Occurring on the left and right in succession. This term can refer to alternating sides of the body (e.g., Alternating hemiplegia) or alternative sides of the visual field (e.g., some migraine auras).

Name: Cervical squamous cell papilloma
Def: A benign tumor arising from the epithelial surface of the cervix and usually caused by Human Papillomavirus infection.

Name: Liver leiomyoma
Def: A benign smooth muscle neoplasm that arises in the liver.

Name: Typified by high penetrance
Def: Description of conditions in which only an incomplete but relatively high proportion of individuals with a given genotype exhibit the disease regardless of age assuming a full lifespan of 80 years. There is no commonly accepted definition for incomplete, but high penetrance, but we suggest that this term be applied if at least 80 percent but less than 100 percent of individuals with the given genotype would manifest the disease with a full lifespan.

Name: Typified by moderate penetrance
Def: Description of conditions in which only a moderate proportion of individuals with a given genotype exhibit the disease regardless of age assuming a full lifespan of 80 years. There is no commonly accepted definition for moderate penetrance, but we suggest that this term be applied if at least 20 percent but less than 80 percent of individuals with the given genotype would manifest the disease with a full lifespan.

Name: Typified by low penetrance
Def: Description of conditions in which only a low proportion of individuals with a given genotype exhibit the disease regardless of age assuming a full lifespan of 80 years. There is no commonly accepted definition for low penetrance, but we suggest that this term be applied if at least some but less than 20 percent of carriers would manifest the disease with a full lifespan.

Name: Decreased Succinyl-CoA 3-ketoacid CoA transferase activity
Def: Decreased activity of the enzyme succinyl-CoA 3-ketoacid CoA transferase.
Comment: Succinyl-CoA: 3-ketoacid CoA transferase (SCOT; EC 2.8.3.5, gene symbol OXCT1) is a mitochondrial homodimer essential for ketone body utilization.

Name: Reduced phytanic acid oxidase activity in cultured fibroblasts
Def: Activity of the enzyme phytanoyl-CoA hydroxylase (PhyH; EC 1.14.11.18) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts. PhyH plays a role in the catabolism of phytanic acid, a branched-chain fatty acid that is a normal constituent of the human diet.

Name: Reduced bifunctional protein activity
Def: Diminished activity of hydroxysteroid 17-beta dehydrogenase 4 (HSD17B4), also known as D-bifunctional protein (DBP), a peroxisomal enzyme that catalyzes multiple steps of beta-oxidation of very long chain fatty acids.

Name: Decreased circulating plasmalogen concentration
Def: Reduced plasmalogen concentration in the blood circulation.
Comment: Plasmalogens are a class of membrane glycerophospholipids that contain a vinyl-ether linked alkyl chain at the sn-1 position of the glycerol backbone and, typically, a polyunsaturated fatty acyl chain at the sn-2 position.

Name: Post-vaccination varicella zoster virus infection
Def: Infection with live, attenuated varicella-zoster virus following vaccination. This is an extremely rare event that may indicate immunocompromise.
Synonym: Varicella zoster virus infection after vaccination

Name: Recent steroid exposure
Def: History of having been treated with corticosteroid medications in recent weeks.

Name: Shark teeth
