Def: Eruption of permanent teeth behind deciduous (baby) teeth before they have fallen out, resulting in a double row of teeth. This phenomen is typically observed between the ages of 5 to 7 years.

Name: Pontine T2 hypointensity
Def: A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the pons.

Name: Anti-platelet antigen antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against antigens present on the surface of thrombocytes such as the glycoproteins GPIIb/IIIa, GPIb/IX, and GPIa/IIa.

Name: Anti-voltage-gated potassium channel antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against a voltage-gated potassium channel.
Comment: Voltage-gated potassium channels represent a family of transmembrane channels responsible for returning the depolarized cell to a resting state after each nerve impulse.
Synonym: Voltage gated potassium channel antibodies in blood

Name: Vegan diet
Def: A history of following a vegan diet characterized by avoidance of food sourced from animals including meet, fish, and dairy products.

Name: History of previous pregnancy with hydrops fetalis
Def: One or more previous pregnancies in which the fetus developed hydrops fetalis.
Synonym: History of hydrops fetalis in newborn offspring

Name: Ameliorated by potassium supplements
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by ingesting a potassium supplement.

Name: Ameliorated by niacin
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by ingesting niacin (vitamin B3).

Name: Aggravated by exposure to medication
Def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by treatment with a medication.

Name: Bleeding ameliorated by vitamin K
Def: Applies to bleeding that is significantly reduced by treatment with vitamin K.
Synonym: Vitamin K treatment reduces bleeding significantly

Name: Anti-retroviral therapy exposure
Def: History of having been treated with an antiretroviral agent.

Name: Potassium-wasting diuretic exposure
Def: History of having been treated with a potassium-wasting diuretic such as thiazide (chlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, hydrochlorothiazide, indapamide, metolazone) and loop (bumetanide, ethacrynic acid, furosemide, torsemide) diuretics.

Name: Tricyclic antidepressant exposure
Def: History of having been treated with a tricyclic antidepressant medication.

Name: Excessive dental attrition
Def: A higher than expected amount of attrition of teeth, as menifested by loss of tooth characteristics including rounding or sharpening of incisal edges, loss of cusps, and fracturing of teeth, to an extent that is deemed more than would be expected at a given age.
Synonym: Excessive wear and tear on teeth

Name: Positionally dependent pain
Def: Pain improves or worsens with changes in body position.

Name: Abnormal erythrocyte adenosine triphosphate concentration
Def: Concentration of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in red blood cells (erythrocytes) outside of the normal range.

Name: Reduced erythrocyte adenosine triphosphate concentration
Def: Concentration of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in red blood cells (erythrocytes) below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Elevated erythrocyte adenosine triphosphate concentration
Def: Concentration of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in red blood cells (erythrocytes) above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Spermatogonial maturation arrest
Def: A type of spermatogenesis maturation arrest in which the block of developmental occurs in the spermatogonial stage. Testicular histology shows seminiferous tubules with Sertoli cells and spermatogonial cells but no further differentiated cells like spermatocytes or round spermatids.

Name: Elevated circulating neuron-specific enolase concentration
Def: Concentration of neuron-specific enolase above the upper limit of normal in the blood circulation.
Comment: Neuron-specific enolase (NSE) is an important tumor marker in the serum of patients with lung cancer. Elevated serum NSE levels are also associated with neuroblastoma, neuroendocrine neoplasms, renal cell carcinoma, multiple myeloma, brain trauma, Guillain-Barre syndrome, and other diseases.

Name: Reduced leukocyte alpha-mannosidase activity
Def: Concentration or activity of an alpha-mannosidase as measured in leukocytes is below the limits of normal.

Name: Increased circulating alpha-mannosidase activity
Def: Concentration or activity of alpha mannosidase above the upper limit of normal in the blood circulation.

Name: Reduced leukocyte cathepsin D activity
Def: Concentration or activity of cathepsin D as measured in leukocytes is below the limits of normal. The reduction in cathepsin D activity can also be measured in fibroblasts.

Name: Reduced leukocyte N-sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase activity
Def: Concentration or activity of N-sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase as measured in leukocytes is below the limits of normal.

Name: Pseudohyperkalemia
Def: Pseudohyperkalemia describes a falsely elevated potassium level upon measurement of the serum electrolyte concentration due to disruption of cells during the collection or processing of the sample.
Comment: Pseudohyperkalemia is an elevation of potassium in the serum that results during collection, storage, or handling of a blood sample, and is not representative of the potassium level in vivo. Pseudohyperkalemia can result from increased tourniquet tension, increased pressure from a patient's fist being clenched, or mechanical lysis of hematocytes during pneumatic tube delivery of samples to the laboratory or the centrifugation process.

Name: Abnormal enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts
Def: Concentration or activity of an enzyme is above or below the limits of normal in cultured fibroblasts. Fibroblasts are easy to grow in culture and are the main cell type involved in producing extracellular matrix. They are used as a convenient model system for measuring enzyme activity for enzymes that are not expressed in blood cells. Usually, the test is done in fibroblasts for convenience rather than for the investigation of a pathophysiology specific to fibroblasts.

Name: Reduced heparan-alpha-glucosaminide N-acetyltransferase activity in cultured fibroblasts
Def: Concentration or activity of N-sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

Name: Reduced N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfate sulfatase in cultured fibroblasts
Def: Concentration or activity of N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfate sulfatase as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

Name: Reduced acetylglucosamine-6-sulfate sulfatase activity in cultured fibroblasts
Def: Concentration or activity of N-acetylglucosamine-6-sulfatase (EC 3.1.6.14) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal. N-acetylglucosamine-6-sulfatase hydrolyzes heparan sulfate and keratan sulfate.

Name: Reduced erythrocyte porphobilinogen deaminase activity
Def: Activity or concentration of in the level of porphobilinogen deaminase (EC 4.3.1.8) in erythrocytes below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Reduced holocarboxylase synthetase activity in cultured fibroblasts
Def: Concentration or activity of holocarboxylase synthetase (EC 6.3.4.10) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

Name: Abnormal circulating alpha mannosidase activity
Def: Concentration or activity of alpha mannosidase outside of the limits of normal in the blood circulation.

Name: Reduced tissue alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase activity
Def: Concentration or activity of alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase (EC 3.2.1.49) is below the limits of normal. The activity can be measured in multiple tissues including cultured fibroblasts.

Name: Reduced erythrocyte arginase activity
Def: Activity or concentration of arginase (EC 3.5.3.1) in red blood cells below the lower limit of normal. Arginase catalyzes the last step of the urea cycle.

Name: Reduced mitochondrial acetyl-CoA acetyltransferase activity in cultured fibroblasts
Def: Concentration or activity of mitochondrial acetyl-CoA acetyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.9) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.
Comment: Mitochondrial acetyl-CoA acetyltransferase is a short-chain-length-specific thiolase that is encoded by the ACAT1 gene.

Name: Reduced tissue beta-mannosidase activity
Def: Concentration or activity of beta-mannosidase (EC 3.2.1.25) below the lower limit of normal. Beta-mannosidas enzyme can be measured in multiple tissues including leukocytes and cultured fibroblasts.
Comment: Beta-mannosidase is a lysosomal enzyme that catalyzes the final exoglycosidase step in the degradation pathway for N-linked oligosaccharide moieties of glycoproteins.
Synonym: Reduced beta-mannosidase activity in cultured fibroblasts

Name: Reduced 3-methylcrotonyl CoA carboxylase activity in cultured fibroblasts
Def: Activity of 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase (EC 6.4.1.4) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

Name: Reduced branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase activity in cultured fibroblasts
Def: Activity of branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex (EC 1.2.4.4) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.
Comment: Branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex is an inner-mitochondrial enzyme complex that catalyzes the oxidative decarboxylation of the branched-chain alpha-ketoacids derived from isoleucine, leucine, and valine.

Name: Reduced erythrocyte galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase activity
Def: Activity or concentration of in the level of galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase (GALT; EC 2.7.7.12) in erythrocytes below the lower limit of normal.
Comment: Galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase is the second enzyme in the galactose metabolic pathway.

Name: Abnormal erythrocyte adenosine deaminase activity
Def: Activity of adenosine deaminase in red blood cells outside the limits of normal.

Name: Reduced isovaleryl CoA dehydrogenase activity in cultured fibroblasts
Def: Activity of isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase (EC 1.3.99.10) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

Name: Reduced glycerol kinase activity in cultured fibroblasts
Def: Activity of glycerol kinase (EC 2.7.1.30) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

Name: Increased circulating vitamin A concentration
Def: Concentration of vitamin A above the upper limit of normal in the blood circulation.

Name: Elevated circulating hyaluronic acid concentration
Def: Concentration of hyaluronic acid in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Diminished breath sounds
Def: A reduction in the intensity of the breath sound as ascertained by auscultation of the lung.

Name: Anti-AK5 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against anti-adenylate kinase 5 (AK5).

Name: Anti-AMPAR antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against anti-alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor (AMPAR).

Name: Anti-Amphiphysin antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Amphiphysin.

Name: Anti-ARHGAP26 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Rho GTPase-activating protein 26 (ARHGAP26).

Name: Anti-CARP VIII antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Carbonic anhydrase-related protein VIII (CARPVIII).

Name: Anti-CASPR2
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against contactin-associated protein-like 2 (CASPR2).

Name: Anti-CV2/CRMP5 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against CV2/CRMP5. Anti-CV2/CRMP5 autoantibody is the most commonly detected anti-neuronal autoantibody. Patients with typical paraneoplastic chorea show fully developed chorea in the course of weeks to months with acute inflammation in the striatum.

Name: Anti-DPPX antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against dipeptidyl-peptidase-like protein 6 (DPPX).

Name: Anti-FGFR3 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against FGFR3.

Name: Anti-GABA(A)R antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against gamma-aminobutyric acid A receptor, i.e., GABA(A)R.
Synonym: Anti-gamma amino butyric acid type A receptors antibody

Name: Anti-GABA(B)R antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against gamma-aminobutyric acid B receptor, i.e., GABA(B)R.

Name: Anti-GAD65 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against glutamic acid decarboxylase 65 (GAD65).

Name: Anti-Gephyrin antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Gephyrin.

Name: Anti-GFAP antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP).

Name: Anti-GlyR antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Glycine receptor (GlyR).

Name: Anti-Homer-3 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Homer-3.

Name: Anti-Hu antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Hu.

Name: Anti-Iglon5 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against immunoglobulin-like cell adhesion molecule 5 (IgLON5).

Name: Anti-ITPR1 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor 1 (ITPR1).

Name: Anti-Kelch like protein 11 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against kelch-like protein 11 (KLHL11).

Name: Anti-LGI1 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against leucine-rich glioma-inactivated 1 (LGI1).

Name: Anti-Ma antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ma.

Name: Anti-Ma2 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ma2.

Name: Anti-Ma1 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ma1.

Name: Anti-mGluR1 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against metabotropic glutamate receptor 1 (mGluR1).

Name: Anti-mGluR5 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5).

Name: Anti-neurexin-3alpha antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against neurexin-3alpha.

Name: Anti-P/Q-type VGCC antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channels (VGCCs).

Name: Anti-MAP1B antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against microtubule-associated protein 1B (MAP1B).

Name: Anti-PKCgamma antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against protein kinase Cgamma.

Name: Anti-Ri antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ri, an antineuronal antibody.

Name: Anti-Septin-5 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Septin-5.

Name: Anti-SEZ6L2 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against seizure-related 6 homolog like 2 (SEZ6L2).

Name: Anti-SOX1 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against SOX1. Anti-SOX1 antibodies, also known as antiglial nuclear antibody (AGNA), are specifically found in paraneoplastic neurological disorders. Since SOX1 is expressed in neuronal precursor cells in the developing central nervous system, it has been used as an early marker of neural stem cells.
Synonym: Anti-Sry-like high mobility group box (SOX) 1 antibody

Name: Anti-Tr/DNER antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Tr/DNER. Anti-Tr antibodies are directed against cerebellar Purkinje cells (termed anti-Tr or PCA-Tr). Anti-Tr autoantibodies are frequently associated with Hodgkin lymphoma (HL). Anti-Tr antibodies are defined by a specific staining pattern in cerebellar tissue that is characterized by punctate immunoreactivity in both the dendritic tree and soma of Purkinje cells but not in their axons. This characteristic pattern is indicative of the presence of anti-Tr antibodies. The Delta/Notch-like epidermal growth factor-related receptor (DNER) was identified as the target antigen of anti-Tr.
Synonym: Anti-delta/notch-like epidermal growth factor-related receptor antibody

Name: Anti-TRIM46 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against the axon initial segment protein tripartite motif 46 (TRIM46).

Name: Anti-TRIM9/TRIM67 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against TRIM9/TRIM67.

Name: Anti-Yo antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Yo.

Name: Anti-titin antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against titin.

Name: Anti-Zic4 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Zic family member 4 (ZIC4).

Name: Anti-Sj/ITPR1 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Sj/inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor.

Name: Anti-D2 R antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against dopamine-2 receptor.

Name: Anti-GluK2 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against glutamate kainate receptor subunit 2 (GluK2).

Name: Anti-Lrp4 antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against low-density lipoprotein receptor (Lrp4).

Name: Anti-ryanodine receptor antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against ryanodine receptor.

Name: Anti-Kv1.4 antibody
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against the voltage-gated potassium channel Kv1.4.

Name: Selective mutism
Def: Voluntary failure to use spoken language (at whatever level attained) in selective social contexts over a period of time.

Name: Limited repertoire of facial expression
Def: An abnormally limited range of facial expressions demonstrated by a lack of nuance of facial expression to match specific social situations or an inability to demonstrate a normal range of emotions with one's face.

Name: Excessive interest in others
Def: A strong desire to interact and engage with others that is perceived to be inappropriate or excessive in the context of cultural norms.

Name: obsolete Reduced response to another's attempt to get direct attention
Abnormal pitch
Def: Persistently abnormally high or low-pitched vocalization or speech than is considered the norm for the context of social situation or significantly different from baseline of the individual.
Comment: Pitch refers to the frequency of sound waves (measured in Hertz).

Name: Disjointed sentences
Def: Persistent abnormalities in the sentence structure in speech, phrases may not be logically connected to each other, gives the impression of rambling. This may be a characteristic feature of the individual or may be a change from the norm of the affected individual.
Comment: Loose association is highly correlated with flight of ideas and for which it is the speech-based expression. Typically it is very difficult to follow the logic in the expressed speech. The affected individual's speech is characterized by expressions in speech that have weak (e.g. tangential/circumstantial) connections between ideas.

Name: Neologism
Def: Consistent use of an invented word that is unique to an individual.

Name: Overly formal/pedantic language
Def: Use of language that is overly formal, precise, detailed, or pedantic for the social context.
Comment: This term may apply to a persistent and ongoing feature of the affected individual or to a change from baseline.

Name: Midline hand movements
Def: Hand stereotypies within the medial plane of the body.

Name: Abnormal Intonation
Def: Abnormal rise and fall of the voice in speech and vocalization for the context and cultural situation.

Name: Abnormal speech rate
Def: Speech that is abnormally fast or slow as compared to the perceived cultural norm.
Comment: The term Abnormal speech rate can also be used for a comparison at the individual level, speech that is faster or slower compared to the baseline of the individual.

Name: Abnormal speech rhythm
Def: Speech with persistent abnormal rhythm or pattern for the context and cultural situation. This may occur constantly throughout conversations with the person or may occur in periodic bursts lasting several minutes to hours.

Name: Ambiguous facial expression
Def: Spontaneous production of communicative facial expressions that have poor quality or are perceived as odd or mechanical. This may include inaccurate mimicry of typical facial expressions. These expressions may be difficult to interpret for someone who is not familiar with the individual making the expression.

Name: Exaggerated facial expression
Def: A tendency to make facial expressions that are exaggerated and a failure to make subtle facial expressions in a social context when a subtle expression is more appropriate.

Name: Muted facial expression
Def: A tendency to produce facial expressions with decreased intensity or expressivity which appear muted or flat.

Name: Abnormal peer relationships
Def: The state of having abnormal relationships with others. This does not describe specific aspects of one's social aptitudes but rather a state which may come about from these aptitudes, such as lacking peer relationships or lacking close friends.

Name: Steroetypic movements of face and head
Def: Abnormal movements of face and head.

Name: Steroetypic upper-extremity movements
Def: Abnormal movements of the upper extremities.

Name: Stereotypic whole-body movements
Def: Abnormal movements of the whole body.

Name: Abnormal interest in others
Def: A social interest in others that is abnormal given the social context. This can include an increased interest with another person or an abnormal lack of interest in other people.

Name: Reduced social insight
Def: A lack of awareness of social rules in multiple social settings, which are simple or intuitive to others in the same social setting.

Name: Reduced awareness of convention
Def: Reduced awareness of expected conventions, which are normal and expected for particular social settings or interactions.

Name: Abnormal relationship
Def: The state of having abnormal relationships with others. This does not describe specific aspects of one's social aptitudes but rather a state which may come about from these aptitudes, such as lacking peer relationships, lacking close friends, or having a relational network that is abnormal given one's cultural context.

Name: Impaired social imitation
Def: Reduced use of imitation of tasks or movements of others in play or learning.
Comment: The ability to imitate others is common in children during early cognitive development (4-5 years old) and can be abnormal in children with developmental delay.

Name: Infrequent social initiations
Def: Social initiation refers to the ability to begin interactions with other people. This term refers to a reduction in the frequency with which an individual attempts to begin interactions. The term should only be used for individuals who are assessed to have sufficient intellectual and language skills to interact with others.
Comment: Social interactions can be begun by eye contact, nodding with the head, saying hello, or otherwise capturing the attention of another person with the intention of starting an interaction. The failure of a person to initiate social interactions with others can be observed when the examiner assesses that the person has had the opportunity to initiate interactions but did not do so for an extended period. Additionally, the interaction must be spontaneous and not prompted by another individual. This can be observed in individuals with long-standing social deficits, such as those with autism, as well as in episodic disorders like severe depressive episodes.
Synonym: Infrequent attempts to direct the attention of another person
Reduced attempt to get or direct the attention of another person

Name: Reduced responsiveness to social cues
Def: A tendency to display responces to social cues that are interpreted (e.g., by family members, peers, or caregivers) as diminished compared to what would be expected based on the developmental stage and cultural context of an individual.
Comment: This term describes a behavioral abnormality and does not apply if the lack of response is assessed to be due to hearing impairment or intellectual disability.
Synonym: Lack of response to verbal cues

Name: Social disinhibition
Def: A tendency to violate social norms because of a failure to resist temptations or urges in social settings.
Comment: A tendency to social disinhibition can be acquired after traumaticbrain injury and may be described as insensitivity to others. Manifestions of social disinhibition may include (1) insertion of poorly considered utterances including insensitive remarks,overly intimate information, sexual references, and swear words, (2) failure to adhereto the rules of discourse leading to poor turn-taking, excessive side tracks, off topics,and talking too much, and (3) speaking from an egocentric perspective, that is,lacking concern, selfishness, childishness, arguing, not getting along with others.

Name: Diminished integration of verbal and non-verbal communicative behavior
Def: A communicative abnormality where one's nonverbal and verbal communication are poorly integrated. This may occur when verbal and nonverbal communication are intact alone but are abnormal when used together, or an abnormality in the use of typically integrated communication such as the use of beat gestures during speech.

Name: obsolete Reduced immediate imitation of others
Reduced cooperative imaginative play
Def: Failure of a child to engage with peers games that involve creating imaginary scenarios or narratives, for instance, in which children pretend to be characters or act out adventurous scenarios.

Name: obsolete Reduced responsiveness to verbal cues
Lack of expressed empathy
Def: This term refers to the observation that an affected person tends not to provide situationally appropriate responses to other people in times when these people are in emotional need. For instance, failure to provide comfort to a person who is sad or crying.
Comment: Empathy can be defined as the ability to explain, predict and interpret behavior by attributing mental states such as desire, beliefs, intentions and emotions to oneself and to other people. Empathy cannot be directly observed.

Name: Bradylalia
Def: Speech that is abnormally slow as compared to the perceived cultural norm.
Comment: Bradylalia can also be used for speech that is slower compared to the baseline of the individual.

Name: Excessively loud speech
Def: Speech which is persistently abnormally and noticeably loud or high volume for the social and cultural context and is not due to a structural or muscular abnormality. Those around the person often consider them to be shouting.

Name: Excessively quiet speech
Def: Speech which is persistently abnormally quiet, or of low in volume for the social and cultural context. This includes persistent and inappropriate whispering. It is not due to a medical or surgical condition that results in hoarseness, nor structural or muscular abnormality that results in low speech volume.

Name: Abnormal speech volume
Def: Speech that is abnormally loud or quiet for the social and cultural context in which it is spoken. It is clinically noted by others, including family, friends, or clinical providers.

Name: Reduced attention regulation
Def: An abnormality in one's ability to control their attention towards a specific subject or task can include difficulties in changing or maintaining attention.

Name: Reduced impulse control
Def: Reduced ability to control, or a failure to resist a temptation, urge, or impulse.

Name: Sensory behavioral abnormality
Def: Abnormal sensory behavior, including avoiding or seeking sensory input or difficulty modulating sensory stimuli.

Name: Idiosyncratic gesture
Def: When one uses gestures that are unique to them and have no apparent meaning to others.

Name: Atypical sorting
Def: Atypical focus on arranging, balancing, or positioning objects; may be atypical in focus or intensity.

Name: Excessive checking
Def: Checking behavior that is excessive for the situational context.

Name: Excessive hand washing
Def: Hand washing behavior that is excessive for the situational context.

Name: Resistance to trivial environmental changes
Def: Distress in response to minor changes in one's environmental expectations.
Comment: Typical examples of resistance to trivial environmental changes include distress when receiving the wrong color cup or when furniture is moved.

Name: obsolete Reduced nonverbal responsiveness to verbal cues
obsolete Reduced verbal responsiveness to verbal cues
Reduced co-speech gestures
Def: Reduced use of speech-integrated gestures such as the use of beat gestures.

Name: Limited head nodding or shaking
Def: Absence or reduction in the use of head nodding to indicate agreement or head shaking to indicate disagreement.

Name: Limited pointing
Def: Absence or reduction in the use of pointing to request or direct another's attention.

Name: Sensory hypersensitivity
Def: A decreased tolerance to sensory stimuli that triggers emotional and/or physical distress.

Name: Sensory hyposensitivity unexplained by sensory deficit
Def: Increased tolerance to sensory stimuli due to diminished sensory ability.

Name: Auditory hypersensitivity
Def: Hyperresponsive to sound that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

Name: Tactile hypersensitivity
Def: A decreased tolerance to physical touch.

Name: Auditory sensory seeking
Def: Pursuit of specific sounds or noises that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

Name: Gustatory sensory seeking
Def: Pursuit of a particular taste that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

Name: Olfactory sensory seeking
Def: Pursuit of specific scents, smells, or fragrances that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

Name: Tactile sensory seeking
Def: Pursuit of a specific texture that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

Name: Vestibular sensory seeking
Def: Pursuit of vestibular stimulation that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

Name: Visual sensory seeking
Def: Pursuit visual stimulation by looking at specific sights, images, and/or colors that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.

Name: Socially inappropriate questioning
Def: A tendency to ask questions that are overly personal or otherwise inappropriate in the social situation in which they are asked.

Name: Spinning
Def: An excessive frequency of spinning one's body.

Name: Delayed Echolalia
Def: Repetition of borrowed words or phrases outside of the context in which they were originally heard. E.g., scripting from TV shows or movies.

Name: Immediate Echolalia
Def: Immediate repetition of another person's speech.

Name: Excessive cleaning
Def: Excessive cleaning of surfaces, living space, or environment that is excessive for the situational context.

Name: Facial expressions not directed to others
Reduced social smiling
Def: Reduced production of smiles during engagement with an interactive parent, caregiver, or peer.
Comment: In typical development, smiling is one of the most commonly observed social behaviors during the first 6 months of life. Most babies begin to smile by the age of about 2 months.

Name: Abnormal play
Def: An abnormality in a child's ability play.
Comment: Does not apply to the presence of abnormal play. The presence of abnormal play should be specified under atypical repetitive behaviors.

Name: Reduced imaginative play skills
Def: Reduced or lack of pretending in play (does not assign abstract properties to objects, use invisible objects, or use objects in nonliteral ways other than their intended purpose in play).

Name: Nonfunctional or atypical use of objects in play
Def: Use of objects in atypical, unimaginitive ways other than for which they are intended (banging, throwing, shaking, sorting, lining up, spinning).

Name: Infrequent social engagement with peers
Def: Social engagement refers to the interaction of an individual with others in a contextually appropriate manner. This term refers to a lower than typical number of attempts to engage peers in conversation, play, or other interactions.

Name: Avoidance of emotional intimacy
Def: An atypically high tendency to avoid interpersonal exchanges characterizing by sharing of personal feelings, expressions of understanding, affirmation, and demonstrations of caring.

Name: Failure to offer information to initiate social interaction
Def: An atypically low tendency to offer information as a means to initiate or sustain social interactions or direct another's attention.
Comment: This term refers specifically to offering information in order to initiate social interactions and should not be applied to a person who is reluctant to offer information when prompted.

Name: Difficulty understanding nonliteral meaning of conversation
Difficulty recognizing another's emotions
Def: A difficulty in being able to understand the emotions of other people. This can range from recognizing emotions from facial expressions to an inability to empathize with others when they describe their feelings

Name: Abnormal social emotional interactions
Def: Social emotional interactions refer to the exchange of feelings during social interactions by means of a wide range of communicative behaviors including facial expressions, body language, and verbal communication. This term refers to an atypically low production of emotion social communication by an individual.

Name: Objectification of others
Def: A tendency to interact with others as if they are objects with functional purpose rather than engaging in social/emotional interactions.

Name: Indifference to social norms
Def: Failure to follow social norms (shared standards of acceptable behavior) even though one has awareness of these norms and the ability to follow them. This is characterized by an indifference to the consequences of breaking social norms.

Name: Aggression towards others
Def: Aggression that is directed towards other individuals, as opposed to oneself.

Name: Aggression towards caregivers
Def: Aggression that is directed towards caregivers.

Name: Aggression toward non-caregivers
Def: Aggression that is directed towards non-caregivers.

Name: obsolete Deficit applying language skills across context
Abnormal rituals
Def: Insistence on rituals which are self-imposed on a person's environment including directing the behavior of those around them.

Name: obsolete Reduced use of language for social purposes
Jumping
Def: An excessive frequency of jumping in place.

Name: Delay in the acquisition of cooperative play skills
Def: Failure to acquire the ability to play cooperatively, a type of play in whichchildren work together towards a common goal and in which a child displays interest both in the play and in the the other child or children involved in playing. This ability is observed in neurotypical children from the age of 3 to 6 years.

Name: Reduced social reciprocity with peers
Def: Reduced back and forth interactions with others compared to what would be expected for the developmental level.

Name: obsolete Infrequent social engagement with peers
Olfactory hallucination
Def: Perception of smell without olfactory stimulus.

Name: Gustatory hallucination
Def: Perception of taste without gustatory stimulus.

Name: Abnormal interpretation of external stimuli
Def: Abnormal perception of reality is characterized by an abnormal or inaccurate experience of external stimuli.

Name: Proprioceptive hallucination
Def: A type of hallucination that involves the perception of distorted or abnormal sensations related to one's body position or movement.

Name: Disturbed perception with a stimulus
Def: A perceptual experience in which an individual's perception of sensory stimuli is altered or disrupted in some way, resulting in abnormal or distorted sensory perceptions despite the presence of actual external stimuli.

Name: Illusions
Def: Perceptual experiences that involve misinterpretations or distortions of sensory stimuli.

Name: Inattentiveness illusion
Def: Instances in which individuals fail to perceive or notice salient or significant stimuli in their visual field due to a lack of attention.

Name: Illusions due to affect
Def: Perceptual distortions or misinterpretations of sensory information arise as a result of the individual's emotional or affective state.

Name: Pareidolia
Def: Apophenia is a psychological phenomenon in which individuals perceive familiar patterns or meaningful images in random or ambiguous stimuli, such as clouds, shadows, or inanimate objects.

Name: Autoscopy
Def: A phenomenon in which an individual perceives themselves from an external perspective, as if they are observing their own body or self from a location outside of their physical body.

Name: Subjective eidetic images
Def: A mental phenomenon is when an individual can vividly visualize or recall visual information from memory with exceptional detail and accuracy. These images are experienced subjectively by the individual, meaning they are not physically present or visible to others.

Name: Amplification of social interactions
Def: A increase in the tendency of a person to seek or maintain social connections or interactions with others compared to previous norms for an individual.

Name: Diminishment of emotional responsiveness
Def: A reduction in the tendency of a person to display emotional responsiveness or empathy towards others during interpersonal interactions as compared to that person's previous norm.
Comment: This feature may be reported by family members, friends, or peers.

Name: Somatic hallucination
Def: A type of hallucination that involves the perception of sensory experiences related to the body or its internal organs, systems, or processes. It is a hallucinatory experience that primarily affects bodily sensations rather than external sensory perceptions.

Name: Visceral hallucination
Def: A type of hallucination that involves the perception of internal bodily sensations or processes that do not actually exist.

Name: Abnormal perceptual state
Def: Temporary alteration of the awareness of reality or self-perception.

Name: Depersonalization
Def: A psychological experience or symptom characterized by a sense of detachment or estrangement from oneself or one's surroundings.

Name: Derealization
Def: Depersonalization is a subjective experience in which an individual feels a sense of detachment or estrangement from their surroundings, leading to a distorted perception of the external world. It is characterized by a feeling of unreality or unfamiliarity with one's environment, as if things are dreamlike, artificial, or lacking in significance.

Name: Decreased facial expression mirroring
Def: Diminished mirroring or reflection of facial expressions in another person during social interactions.
Comment: Automatic mirroring of affective gestures and expressions refers to the unconscious imitation of gestures and expressions of other people during conversation. This term refers to the assessment that the affected person does not imitate gestures and expressions as much as typically expected in age-matched children.

Name: Diminishment of comfort with casual physical contact
Def: A reduction in the tendency of a person to accept casual physical contact with others as compared to that person's previous norm.
Comment: For instance, an individual may choose to stand farther apart from others in conversations or decline physical contact when offered during social interactions.This feature may be reported by family members, friends, or peers.

Name: Thought blocking
Def: The experience of sudden cessation of the thought/thinking process, the person often describes the mind going blank and there is frequently a period of silence that is accompanied by a perplexed state, not understanding what transpired. Some may describe the experience as an abrupt emptying of the mind or the belief that an external force removed their thoughts from their head.

Name: Maladaptive fear-related cognitions
Def: Threat-based cognitive biases result in a skewed perception, experience, or processing of internal or external stimuli.

Name: Hypervigilance
Def: A heightened alertness is characterized by a broad awareness and/or excessive scanning of environmental stimuli.

Name: Phobia
Def: Extreme, irrational, and persistent fears of certain objects, situations, activities, or persons can impede functioning in day-to-day life.

Name: Anticipatory anxiety
Def: A state characterized by future-oriented worry, accompanied by negative affect and autonomic arousal.

Name: Flight of ideas
Def: Successive thoughts and speech are easily diverted by external stimuli or internal superficial associations. Unable to maintain a constant train of thought and lose themselves in side issues, losing the thread and are unable to recover it. Superficial connections appear to drive the subject matter.

Name: Recurrent maladaptive behavior
Def: A repeating behavior that is either immediately unproductive or has negative long-term consequences. This includes harmful coping mechanisms such as addictive behavior and failure to control impulses and compulsions.

Name: Cognitive distortion
Def: A cognitive distortion is a maladaptive, exaggerated, or irrational thought pattern.
Comment: Cognitive distortions are often involved in the onset or perpetuation of psychopathological states, such as depression and anxiety.

Name: Abnormal change in social behavior
Def: An alternation in the habits and emotional tendencies of an individual with a change in behavior that is typically noticed by family members or peers.
Comment: Changes in behavior may be observed as a disease such as dementia progresses and may manifest in increased or decreased amounts of passivity, depressive affect, anxiety, self-centeredness, wandering, agitation, paranoia, and so on.

Name: Abnormal demeanor
Def: An anomaly in demeanor, which refers to the outward behavior, manner, or conduct of a person. It encompasses how an individual presents themselves to others in terms of attitude, posture, and general comportment.
Comment: Demeanor can be assessed by observation of an individual's posture, gestures, facial expressions, overall mannerisms, or other behavioral manifestations.

Name: Abnormally increased volition
Def: An excessive increase in motivated and goal directed as well as non-goal directed behaviors that are usually accompanied by elevated energy and interest that allows individuals to get started, be energized to perform a sustained and directed action. The increase is often disruptive and typically results in unfavorable consequences.

Name: Pressured speech
Def: Speech pattern that is excessive and intense that often imparts a sense of urgency, the individual appears to be driven to communicate with many words that are spoken very quickly and may run into each other. The person is frequently difficult to interrupt and appears to not respond to social cues for the conversational partner(s) to take their turn in speaking.
Comment: Pressured speech manifests as an increase in the amount of spontaneous speech, which is generally continuous, rapid, loud, and difficult to interrupt. Pressured speech may sometimes be incoherent and continue even when no one is listening.

Name: Laeden paralysis
Def: The sensation of having heavy arms and legs, or feeling a heaviness in the limbs.

Name: Grandiosity
Def: Persistently exaggerated feelings and thoughts of an inflated sense of self-importance, superiority, uniqueness, or invulnerability. The affected individual may project arrogance with a dismissive behavioral pattern towards others the individual deems inferior.

Name: Hopelessness
Def: Persistent and excessive feelings of despair with an overwhelming lack of hope. While hopelessness is primarily a personal experience, the sense of hopelessness becomes pervasive and affects most aspects of the personal experience in relation to the world. For example the person may communicate a sense of hopelessness for family and friends (who themselves do not experience hopelessness), as well as the world in general.

Name: Abnormal sadness
Def: Experience of intense or excessively negative feelings that may include profound unhappiness, feeling low, down, or sorrowful and are beyond cultural or societal norms. Commonly associated with a low self-attitude and grim outlook.

Name: Decreased need for sleep
Def: There has been a noticeable decrease in the need for sleep, where individuals feel refreshed even with minimal or no sleep.

Name: Sleep-related breathing disorders
Def: Conditions of abnormal and difficult respiration during sleep, including chronic snoring and sleep apnea.

Name: Bruxism during sleep
Def: Bruxism is a condition in which you grind, gnash, or clench your teeth while asleep.

Name: Nightmare disorder
Def: Nightmare disorder is defined by the repeated occurrence of nightmares that cause clinically significant distress or impairment in social, occupational or other important areas of functioning, which are not attributable to the physiological effects of a substance (e.g. drug abuse or medication) and which cannot be adequately explained by coexisting mental and medical disorders.

Name: Sleep-related eating disorder
Def: Eating while asleep can be problematic, as it may involve potentially harmful behaviors like overeating or consuming raw meat.

Name: Microsleep
Def: Sudden onset of extreme drowsiness or falling asleep during the day for a short period of time.

Name: Exploding head syndrome
Def: Sleep disorder in which one hears a loud noise or explosive crashing sound in their head. The sound is not real or heard by anyone else. The episode typically happens suddenly, either when beginning to fall asleep or when waking up during the night.

Name: REM sleep behavior disorder
Def: REM Sleep Behavior Disorder (RBD) is a chronic sleep condition characterized by dream enactment and loss of REM atonia.
Comment: Normally during rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, the body experiences temporary paralysis (REM atonia) of most of the body's muscles while the brain is active and dreaming.
Synonym: Rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder
Rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder

Name: Non-restorative sleep
Def: Perception of feeling unrefreshed after sleep.

Name: Disturbance during transitions between sleep and wake states
Def: A group of parasomnias that occur during the transition from wakefulness to sleep or from one sleep stage to another. Rhythmic Movement Disorder, Sleep Starts, Sleep Talking, and Nocturnal Leg Cramps - these four disorders belong to Sleep-Wake Transition Disorders in the International Classification of Sleep Disorders.

Name: Sexsomnia
Def: Unintentional sexual behavior during sleep, such as masturbation, initiation of sex, or making sexual noises, is known as sexsomnia. Sexsomnia predominantly occurs during NREM sleep.

Name: Periodic limb movements
Def: Repetitive limb movements during sleep can affect the quality of your sleep.
Comment: It often occurs alongside Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS). Treatment for RLS may also help with PLMS.

Name: Abnormal hypnagogia
Def: Abnormal transition of consciousness from wakefulness to sleep.

Name: Abnormal hypnopompia
Def: Abnormal transition of consciousness from sleeping to wakefulness.

Name: Abnormal sleep architecture
Def: Interruptions during the various stages of sleep.

Name: REM parasomnia
Def: Parasomnia occurs during REM sleep.

Name: Abnormal movement during sleep
Def: Periodic Limb Movement Disorder, also known as Sleep-Related Myoclonus Syndrome or Nocturnal Myoclonus Syndrome, refers to the periodic and stereotypic movements of the legs or upper limbs during sleep.

Name: Short N1 sleep
Def: Decreased duration of phase N1 of nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.
Comment: N1 sleep may be delayed or disrupted by a number of sleep disorders, including insomnia, hypersomnia, and movement disorders such as restless legs syndrome.

Name: Paradoxical insomnia
Def: Paradoxical insomnia is a condition in which individuals with a normal or near-normal sleep macrostructure tend to severely underestimate the quantity and quality of their sleep.
Synonym: Disturbance in perception related to sleep

Name: Short N2 sleep
Def: Decreased duration of phase N2 of nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.
Comment: In the N2 sleep stage, muscles begin to relax, breathing and heart rate slow, and body temperature drops slightly. During this stage of the sleep cycle, your brain activity also slows down to help maintain sleep.

Name: Short N3 sleep
Def: Decreased duration of phase N3 of nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.
Comment: On an electroencephalogram (EEG), N3 sleep is characterized by a distinct pattern of synchronized brain waves. These brain waves give N3 the moniker "slow-wave sleep.

Name: Diminishment of social interactions
Def: A reduction in the tendency of a person to seek or maintain social connections or interactions with others compared to previous norms for an individual.
Comment: This feature may be reported by family members or peers. This feature is distinct from (but may be accompanied by) loneliness, which can be defined as a perceived discrepancy between one's actual and desired social relationships.
Synonym: Reduced, declined or lessened social interactions

Name: Amplification of interpersonal communication
Def: An increase in the tendency of a person to share information or emotions compared to that person's previous norms.
Synonym: Heightened, amplified social expression and social connectedness

Name: Amplification of relationship seeking
Def: Increased frequency or duration in social outings and interactions as part of relationship-seeking or maintenance compared to the previous norms of an individual. May be considered to be overfamiliar and have a tendency to engage strangers in a presumptive manner.

Name: Diminishment of interpersonal communication
Def: A reduction in the tendency of a person to share information or emotions compared to that person's previous norms.
Comment: This feature may be reported by family members, friends, or peers if the affected person begins to share less information or emotions than previously.
Synonym: A decline or reduced social expression and social connectedness

Name: Diminishment of relationship seeking
Def: A reduction in the tendency of a person to seek new interpersonal relationships or maintain existing relationships.
Comment: The affected person may begin to avoid social outings or interactions.

Name: Amplification of sexual behavior
Def: An abnormal increase of libido (sexual desire), typically accompanied by a higher frequency of sexual activity compared to from a person's previous norm.
Comment: Engaging in riskier sexual practices, experiencing a significant increase in frequency, having multiple sexual partners, or spending excessive time on sexual activities can become disproportionate to other aspects of a person's life.

Name: Amplification of emotional expression
Def: An increase in the tendency of a person to express emotions compared to that person's previous norm.
Comment: Examples of emotional behaviors include crying, laughing, and smiling.

Name: Amplification of emotional responsiveness
Def: An increase in the tendency of a person to display emotional responsiveness or emotional empathy towards others during interpersonal interactions as compared to that person's previous norm. May be considered to be overreactive or over-engaged with interpersonal situations that may take on a persistent preoccupation and would appear to be relatively unrelated to the person, and beyond the expression of normal empathy.
Comment: This feature may be reported by family members, friends, or peers.

Name: Amplification of comfort with casual physical contact
Def: An increase in the tendency of a person to be comfortable with physical contact with others compared to that person's previous norm. Often considered to be intrusive and encroaching on personal space of others less known to the person, frequently causing discomfort and may result in argument or altercation.
Synonym: Increase in comfort with casual physical contact

Name: Diminishment of sexual behavior
Def: A reduction of libido (sexual desire), typically accompanied by a reduction in the frequency of sexual activity , and/or activity compared to the affected individual's previous state.

Name: Diminishment of emotional expression
Def: A reduction in the tendency of a person to express emotions that is typically noticed as a change in behavior by family members or peers.
Comment: Reduced frequency or subdued emotional behaviors like crying, laughter, and smiling, making the individual appear apathetic or disinterested.

Name: Problematic alcohol consumption
Def: Impaired ability to stop or control alcohol use despite adverse social, occupational, or health consequences.

Name: Suicide behaviors
Def: Suicide attempts or preparations
Comment: Suicidal thoughts, ideations, or perseveration should be labeled as HP:0031589.

Name: Addictive sedative use
Def: Misuse and/or abuse of sedative drugs.

Name: Addictive non-substance behaviors
Def: Uncontrolled use or problematic behaviors of dependency without the use of drugs or substances can be detrimental.

Name: Addictive spending behavior
Def: An uncontrollable urge to shop and spend money can lead to distress or impairment.

Name: Addictive gambling behavior
Def: The act of taking chances or engaging in behaviors without restraint, typically involving the wagering of something valuable, in pursuit of acquiring something of higher value.

Name: Addictive sex behavior
Def: Inability to control or manage sexual urges, fantasies, or behaviors that impair one's ability to function.

Name: Addictive video game use
Def: The inability to regulate persistent gaming behavior is characterized by a heightened prioritization of gaming activities over regular daily tasks and responsibilities.

Name: Compulsive stealing
Def: Irresistible impulses to take easily affordable items.

Name: Excessive fire setting
Def: The inability to control urges of deliberately setting fires for pleasure and gratification, without any criminal intent.

Name: Self-cutting
Def: Deliberate harm to one's body, in the form of cutting that results in tissue damage, without a conscious intent to die.

Name: Addictive cannabis use
Def: A persistent and compulsive need to use cannabis, despite negative consequences.

Name: Autophagia
Def: The habitual action of inflicting pain upon oneself by biting and/or devouring portions of one's body.

Name: Hypnagogic sleep paralysis
Def: Sleep paralysis that occurs when falling asleep.
Comment: During sleep paralysis, a person often hallucinates sounds or sensations, such as the presence of a person in the room or even on their chest. If sleep paralysis and these hallucinations occur as a person is falling asleep, they are considered hypnagogic hallucinations.
Synonym: Inability to move while falling asleep

Name: Hypnopompic sleep paralysis
Def: Sleep paralysis that occurs when waking up from sleep.

Name: Sleep onset rapid eye movement period
Def: Entering REM sleep immediately upon falling asleep.
Comment: The NREM stages of sleep are not skipped.

Name: Prolonged N1 sleep
Def: Increased duration of phase N1 of nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.

Name: Prolonged N2 sleep
Def: Increased duration of phase N2 of nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.

Name: Prolonged N3 sleep
Def: Increased duration of phase N3 of nonrapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.

Name: Abnormal judgment
Def: Beliefs that deviate from what is considered rational or within the range of normal human judgment and belief formation.

Name: Overvalued idea
Def: A solitary belief that may be held by others in the society that is maintained by the person to an abnormal and morbid degree and overtly drives behaviors that are considered unhealthy, intrusive, or illegal. This includes fads and cults that the person may adhere to and practice to a morbid degree. The content may vary and ranges from religion, health, romance, or politics.
Comment: An overvalued idea is held strongly, with less than delusional intensity, usually preoccupies the individual's mental life, compared to many delusions, is ego-syntonic, the content is usually regarded as abnormal compared to the general population (but not bizarre as some delusions), could progress to a delusion and may be associated with a high degree of affect (e.g. anxiety or anger when there is a threat to the loss of their goal or object of the belief).

Name: Time agnosia
Def: The inability to perceive the passage of time is usually due to a disorder involving the temporal area of the brain.

Name: Olfactory agnosia
Def: The inability to recognize certain smells or types of odors that you previously recognized.

Name: Tactile agnosia
Def: The inability to recognize objects by touch is called tactile agnosia.

Name: Topographical agnosia
Def: The inability to rely on visual cues to guide one's direction is due to the inability to recognize objects.

Name: Delusional memory
Def: Delusional memory is a memory that is false or fantastically distorted, but held with firm and irrefutable conviction despite evidence to the contrary. It is often seen in psychiatric conditions such as delusional disorders, schizophrenia, and sometimes in severe mood disorders. These memories can be completely fabricated or have a basis in an actual event that has been grossly misinterpreted or altered by the individual's mind.

Name: Auditory agnosia
Def: The condition is characterized by the inability to recognize spoken languages and/or nonverbal environmental sounds and music, despite having adequate hearing. However, spontaneous speech, reading, and writing abilities remain intact.

Name: Gustatory agnosia
Def: People cannot identify tastes, even though they can experience them.

Name: Allesthesia
Def: Referral of a sensory stimulus from one side of the body to the other.

Name: Autotopagnosia
Def: The loss of the ability to localize, recognize, or identify specific parts of one's body.

Name: Persecutory delusion
Def: False beliefs (or judgements) that are held with extraordinary conviction and subjective certainty that are impervious to other experiences or counterarguments and the content is generally considered impossible for the context and circumstance. Delusional beliefs may arise meaningfully from personal or social experiences, yet are impossible, held with conviction, and irrefutable; more commonly they may be psychologically irreducible, appearing with no logical or meaningful connection to the individual experience.
Comment: Persecutory delusions are differentiated from paranoia by the intensity and fixation of the persecutory delusion. Paranoia may be a diffuse or vague suspicion of untoward intent that may be reasoned with, whereas the persecutory delusion is more likely to be specific and impervious to logic.

Name: Morbid jealosy
Def: A disorder of delusional content wherein the affected individual believes they are a victim of their partner's infidelity. It is often based on delusional evidence of an erotic or romantic nature. There may be an affective (mood related) component or may be associated with substance use disorders. It may also occur on its own. There may be associated behaviors to monitor or gather evidence of the perceived infidelity.

Name: Grandiose delusion
Def: Delusional beliefs of a fantastical, expansive, or supernatural quality related to power, ability, wealth, or station. They are often related to origin (aristocratic lineage, royal birth, being raised as a foster child), possessions (owning vast estates, castles, etc., which are withheld through intrigue), abilities (being great inventors, discoverers, artists, possessors of special wisdom, gifted with inspiration), and status (adviser to prominent diplomats, the true director of political destinies). Grandiose delusions may be related to affective states, substance use, or may occur independently.

Name: Folie à deux
Def: Delusional beliefs are transmitted from one individual to another.

Name: Disorder of thought control
Def: A false belief that another person, group of people, or external force controls one's general thoughts, feelings, impulses, or behaviors.

Name: Delusion of love
Def: A delusional belief that the person is secretly loved by another individual who is often of recognized fame or authoratative significance. There is typically no overt evidence and the delusional belief may be driven by falsely perceived indicators. Often there is a blend of erotic delusions and morbid infatuation.

Name: Nihilistic delusion
Def: A delusion that elements of the self, body, or world no longer exist. The person typically recognizes that the entity did in fact exist at one time, but has ceased to exist. The cause of which may be related to disease, decay, or may have been removed or taken by unknown forces.

Name: Cotard delusion
Def: A false belief that you or your body parts are dead, dying, or do not exist.

Name: Abnormal experience of reality
Def: Subjective phenomena or perceptions that deviate from what is considered correct or are outside the range of normal human experiences.
Comment: Abnormal experiences of reality can range from rare perceptions, such as hallucinations or delusions, to more common experiences, such as subtle misinterpretations of events, like cognitive distortions.

Name: Delusional perception
Def: A true perception, to which a patient attributes a false and usually bizarre meaning or interpretation. It is often a revelatory experience that is sudden and is a profound realization of the delusional belief. It often occurs in the context of delusional mood or atmosphere wherein vague and mysterious hunches or concerns with nebulous meaning evolve into clear, delusional observations, and expresses delusions of reference.

Name: Hypochondriac delusion
Def: Delusion quality to belief that one is suffering from an illness despite reassurances based on medical examination and testing. The person may (or not) express pain or discomfort that they attribute to the disease. They are frequently treatment seeking, but do not induce illness features (which is termed Munchhausen syndrome).

Name: Delusions of infestation
Def: A persistent belief that a person is infested with living or non-living pathogens, such as parasites, insects, or bugs, when no such infestation is present.
Comment: This may occur in conjunction with tactile hallucinations of bugs or insects crawling on one's skin and is related to substance use disorders (delirium tremens).

Name: Delusional atmosphere
Def: A persistent sense or a hunch that something is different in an imperceptible manner. Typically the perception is one of a sinister, portentous , uncanny, mysterious, or peculiar sense of foreboding in an indefinable way. There is an innate sense of inexplicable self-relevance to the person. There is often a feeling of anticipation, sometimes even excitement, that soon the mystery may be revealed and all the separate parts of their experience will fit together to reveal something immensely significant. The duration of this experience may vary, lasting from hours to days. It may be intermittent over an extended period of time (months to years).

Name: Delusional misidentification
Def: A group of complex, monothematic delusional phenomena in which subjects hold a belief that the identity of a familiar person, object, location, or self has been altered or replaced. The majority of misidentifications are spouses or first degree relatives, i.e. someone well-known to the person.

Name: Religious delusion
Def: Delusions with a religious content that are considered delusional in nature based on how the belief is held and the evidence offered to support it, which is generally considered impossible or fantastical in the cultural setting of the person. It differs from unusual beliefs that are held with tenacity or conviction and are typically associated with other phenomena consistent with mental illness.

Name: Abnormal psychotic pattern
Def: Any abnormal pattern of psychotic experiences, where an individual has significant disturbances in their thoughts, perceptions, emotions, and behavior, resulting in a loss of touch with reality.

Name: Incomplete unilateral cleft lip
Def: Unilateral cleft lip cleft that starts from the bottom of the upper lip but does not reach the nasal cavity.
Comment: Please use this term only when the cleft lip is unilateral, ie occurring only on one side.

Name: Complete unilateral cleft lip
Def: Unilateral cleft lip cleft that starts from the bottom of the upper lip and reaches the nasal cavity.
Comment: Please use this term only when the cleft lip is unilateral, ie occurring only on one side.

Name: Microform unilateral cleft lip
Def: Notch, groove, or scar of the upper lip without noticeable rupture of the lip. Microforms are sometimes associated with disruption of the continuity of the orbicularis oris muscle.
Comment: Please use this term only when the cleft lip is unilateral, ie occurring only on one side.

Name: Complete cleft hard palate
Def: Cleft hard palate in which the cleft goes through the entire length of the hard palate, ie. from the incisor foramen to the anterior border of the soft palate.

Name: Incomplete cleft hard palate
Def: Cleft hard palate in which the cleft does not go through the entire length of the hard palate, ie. the cleft does not go from the incisor foramen to the anterior border of the soft palate.

Name: Complete cleft soft palate
Def: Cleft soft palate in which the cleft goes through the entire length of the soft palate, i.e. from the posterior border of the hard palate until the uvula.

Name: Incomplete cleft soft palate
Def: Cleft soft palate in which the cleft does not go through the entire length of the soft palate, i.e. the cleft does not go from the posterior border of the hard palate until the uvula.

Name: Incomplete cleft maxillary alveolar ridge
Def: Cleft maxillary alveolar ridge in which the cleft does not go through the entire length of the maxillary alveolar ridge.

Name: Complete cleft maxillary alveolar ridge
Def: Cleft maxillary alveolar ridge in which the cleft goes through the entire length of the maxillary alveolar ridge.

Name: Complete cleft of the upper lip
Def: Cleft of the upper lip that starts from the bottom of the upper lip and reaches the nasal cavity.
Comment: If the cleft lip is on only one side, use 'Complete unilateral cleft lip' (HP:5201001). This term was created to be used in association with a left (HP:0012835) or right (HP:0012834) modifier to annotate completeness of a cleft lip.

Name: Microform cleft of the upper lip
Def: Notch, groove, or scar of the upper lip without noticeable rupture of the lip.
Comment: If the cleft lip is on only one side, use 'Microform unilateral cleft lip' (HP:5201002). This term was created to be used in association with a left (HP:0012835) or right (HP:0012834) modifier to annotate completeness of a cleft lip.

Name: Complete bilateral cleft lip
Def: Bilateral cleft lip in which the cleft lip on both sides is complete, i.e. start from the bottom of the upper lip and reach the nasal cavity.

Name: Incomplete bilateral cleft lip
Def: Bilateral cleft lip in which the cleft lip on both sides are incomplete (i.e. start from the bottom of the upper lip but do not reach the nasal cavity), or the cleft lip on one is incomplete and a microform on the other side.

Name: Microform bilateral cleft lip
Def: Bilateral cleft lip in which the cleft lip on both sides are microform, i.e. a notch, groove, or scar without noticeable rupture of the lip.

Name: Asymmetric bilateral cleft lip
Def: Bilateral cleft lip in which the cleft lip on one side is complete (i.e. starts from the bottom of the upper lip and reaches the nasal cavity), and the one on the other side is incomplete (i.e. starts from the bottom of the upper lip but does not reach the nasal cavity) or microform (i.e. a notch, groove, or scar without noticeable rupture of the lip).
Comment: Consider making additional annotations to specify the type of cleft lip on each side using 'Complete cleft of the upper lip' (HP:5201009), 'Incomplete cleft of the upper lip' (HP:0011340), and/or 'Microform cleft of the upper lip' (HP:5201010).

Name: Craniofacial cleft
Def: Congenital abnormality with cleft (gap or opening) in the craniofacial bones. Craniofacial cleft includes facial cleft, orofacial clef, and cleft of the jaw.

Name: Submucous cleft palate
Def: A cleft of the muscular portion of the palate that is covered by mucous membrane.

Name: Left-right disorientation
Def: A tendency to mix up left and right in one's own body space, typically elicited by asking a person to perform a two-stage command involving specified lateralized anatomy.
Comment: Some suggest that a tendency to mix up left and right of an examiner's body space is a more reliable feature sensitive.

Name: Elevated circulating DNAJB9 protein concentration
Def: Concentration of DnaJ homolog subfamily B member 9 (DNAJB9) in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
Comment: DNAJB9 is a proteomic tissue biomarker for fibrillary glomerulonephritis.
Synonym: DNAJB9 protein level in serum elevated

Name: Olecranon fracture
Def: A partial or complete break in the olecranon,which is the proximal articular portion of the ulna and makes up part of the elbow.
Comment: The olecranon is the proximal articular portion of the ulna. Along with the coronoid process, it forms the greater sigmoid (semilunar) notch which articulates with the humerus to provide flexion and extension of the elbow.

Name: History of mastectomy
Def: Past medical history of surgical breast removal.

Name: Lymphangiosarcoma
Def: A malignant neoplasm arising from the endothelial cells of the lymphatic vessels.

Name: Exposure to inhaled lipids
Def: Aspiration or inhalation of lipid-containing products.
Comment: Exogenous lipoid pneumonia is caused by aspiration or inhalation of lipid-containing products. In the past, the most common agents included mineral oil-based laxatives and nasal decongestants. Other causes include inhalation of petroleum jelly used as a lubricant, e.g., tracheostomy care. The incidence of exogenous lipoid pneumonia is growing exponentially in all age groups secondary to the phenomena termed vaping.

Name: Holster sign
Def: Symmetric poikiloderma of hips and lateral thighs below the greater trochanter.
Comment: The Holster sign may indicate dermatomyositis.

Name: Salivary basal cell adenoma
Def: A rare neoplasm consisting of a monomorphic population of basaloid epithelial cells, and it accounts for approximately 1-2% of all salivary gland tumors.
Comment: Thee most frequent location of basal cell adenoma (BCA) of the salivary gland is the parotid gland. It usually appears as a firm and mobile slow-growing mass. Histologically, isomorphic cells in nests and interlaced trabecules with a prominent basal membrane are observed. In contrast to pleomorphic adenoma, it tends to be multiple and its recurrence rate after surgical excision is high.

Name: Hemidiaphragm elevation
Def: Elevated Hemidiaphragm is a condition where one portion of the diaphragm is higher than the other. Elevated hemidiaphragm occurs when one side of the diaphragm becomes weak from muscular disease or loss of innervation due to phrenic nerve injury.

Name: Cerebriform connective tissue nevus
Def: The cerebriform connective tissue nevus (CCTN) is one of the most characteristic skin findings. It commonly occurs on the soles of the feet, and frequently causes problems because of pain, pruritus, infection, bleeding,exudation, odor, and walking impairment.
Comment: The cerebriform connective tissue nevus is frequently observed in patients with Proteus syndrome and it is an important specific criterion for diagnosis.

Name: Linear Hyperpigmentation along Blaschko's lines
Def: Linear streaks and swirls of macular hyperpigmentation along the lines of Blaschko.
Comment: Blaschko's lines are attributed to the migration lines of epidermal cells during embryogenesis and are characterized by a V-shaped pattern on the posterior midline, S-shape on the abdomen, and spiral on the posterior scalp.

Name: Excessive guilt
Def: Excessive guilt is an internal feeling that is intense and considered clinically to be beyond normal range, out of proportion for the act or offense; excessive guilt is typically based on an incorrect judgment of responsibility for an unfavorable outcome. Excessive guilt is typically pervasive and enduring, i.e. it is not fleeting or a temporary thought associated with a specific action.
Comment: Here we define guilt as the negative feeling that accompanies the belief that one is responsible for a negative outcome or event. Excessive guilt is distinct from self-blame (a cognition/wrong judgment), and rather is defined as excessive given one's perceived responsibility, whether or not the perceived responsibility is accurate.

Name: Mediastinal shift
Def: A deviation of the mediastinum from its normal position in the midline of the thoracic cavity. The mediastinum is a compartment of the thoracic cavity that contains the heart and its blood vessels, the esophagus, trachea, thymus, as well as nerves and lymph nodes.
Comment: Since the pleural cavity is confined by the rib cage, large pleural effusion may push the structures in the thoracic cavity to the opposite side resulting in a shift of the upper and lower mediastinum. Other etiologies are also observed. See Figures 1 and 2 of PMID:35990927 or Figure 1 of PMID:37680422.

Name: Bendopnea
Def: Dyspnea as a result of bending forward while not holding one's breath; dyspnea or shortness of breath onset within 30 seconds of bending forward.
Comment: Bendopnea is mediated by increased ventricular filling pressure during bending, which exacerbates an already high filling pressure in patients with heart failure.

Name: Pain worse when lying flat
Def: Refers to pain that is worse when the affected individual lies down (flat).

Name: Tympanic membrane hypermobility
Def: Abnormally increased ability to move of the tympanic membrane.
Comment: In Stickler syndrome, hypermobility is sometimes associated with thin, visibly hyperflaccid tympanic membranes, which is a common and otoscopically detectable sequela of chronic or recurrent otitis media and/or previous tympanostomy tubes. Hypermobility may also be found with normal appearance tympanic membranes.

Name: Elevated circulating vitamin B12 concentration
Def: Concentration of vitamin B12 in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
Comment: Elevated levels of serum cobalamin may be a sign of a serious, even life-threatening, disease. Hematologic disorders like chronic myelogeneous leukemia, promyelocytic leukemia, polycythemia vera and also the hypereosinophilic syndrome can result in elevated levels of cobalamin.

Name: Elevated circulating soluble FASL concentration
Def: The concentration of soluble FASL in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal. The first apoptosis signal receptor (FAS) pathway regulates apoptosis and is critical for proper development and functioning of the immune system. FAS ligand (FASL) can bind to FAS receptors.

Name: Internal anal sphincter achalasia
Def: A disorder of the internal anal sphincter (IAS) in which the IAS fails to relax that manifests clinically as intractable constipation.
Comment: The internal anal sphincter, which is a specialized smooth muscle continuation of the circular muscle layer of rectum, plays a significant role in the maintenance of anorectal continence and in the pathophysiology of incontinence and constipation. Internal anal sphincter achalasia is a clinical condition with presentation similar to Hirschsprung disease but with the presence of ganglion cells on suction rectal biopsy.

Name: Anthracycline exposure
Def: History of treatment with an anthracycline chemotherapy agent.

Name: Binge drinking
Def: A pattern of episodic heavy alcohol use characterized by the consumption of a high number of drinks per occasion.
Comment: The World Health Organization defines binge drinking (BD) based on a cut-off of six drinks (i.e., 60g of alcohol) or more per occasion. The National Institute on Alcoholism and Alcohol Abuse (NIAAA) defines BD as a pattern of drinking that brings blood alcohol concentration (BAC) levels to 0.08 g/dL, which typically occurs after 4 drinks (i.e., 56 g of alcohol) for women and 5 drinks (i.e., 70 g of alcohol) for men in about 2 hours.

Name: Decreased circulating thrombopoietin concentration
Def: Concentration of thrombopoietin in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal. Thrombopoietin is a glycoprotein hormone produced by the liver and kidney that stimulates the production and differentiation of megakaryocytes.

Name: Collagenoma
Def: A rare hamartomatous malformation characterized by the predominant proliferation of normal collagen fibers and normal, decreased, or increased elastic fibers. Collagenomas may be solitary or multiple, sporadic, acquired or inherited.

Name: Lack of sufficient daily physical activity
Def: Physical activity levels less than those required for optimal health and prevention of premature death.

Name: Synesthesia
Def: A phenomenon whereby stimulation of one sensory or cognitive pathway leads to automatic, involuntary experiences in a second sensory or cognitive pathway.
