Solitary gastric carcinoids have a greater chance for the development of malignancy and metastasis as compared to multiple gastric carcinoids due to hypergastrinemia.

Name: Posiitve skin scabies test
Def: Identification of scabies by means of an examination of the skin such as microscopic identification of scabies mites, eggs, or feces from obtained scales by skin scraping.
Comment: Human scabies is a neglected tropical disease of the skin that affects all age groups. It is a highly contagious skin infection that presents as generalized pruritus and is caused by the Sarcoptes scabiei (S scabiei) var. hominis mite, which is a constrained ectoparasite that lives in the epidermis. Classic scabies is expressed by erythematous papular eruptions, burrows, and pruritus.

Name: Positive mumps virus PCR test in the blood circulation
Def: Detection of nucleic acid of the mumps virus in the blood circulation by a method such as polymerase chain reaction (PCR) or reverse transcriptase (RT)-PCR.

Name: Positive bloodstream tuberculosis-induced T-cell-based interferon-gamma release assay
Def: Detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in the bloodstream by means of detection of interferon-gamma secreted by T cells in response to specific antigens from Mycobacterium tuberculosis, commonly 6kD early secretory antigenic target-6 and 10kD culture filtrate protein-10.
Synonym: Positive T-SPOT-tuberculosis test in the bloodstream

Name: Positive blood Neisseria gonorrhoeae culture
Def: Growth of Neisseria gonorrhoeae in a culture derived from circulating blood.

Name: Anti-mumps antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of Mumps virus.

Name: Positive Vibrio cholerae stool culture
Def: Growth of Vibrio cholerae in a culture derived from a feces sample.

Name: Positive cutaneous varicella zoster virus nucleic acid test
Def: Detection of mucocutaneous varicella zoster virus nucleic acid in the skin by a method such as polymerase chain reaction. The sample is usually obtained by swab from skin or mucous membranes.

Name: Positive bloodstream cryptococcus culture
Def: Growth of Cryptococcus in a culture derived from a blood sample.

Name: Positive bloodstream Borrelia miyamotoi nucleic acid test
Def: Detection of nucleic acid of Borrelia miyamotoi in the blood circulation by a method such as polymerase chain reaction (PCR).

Name: Positive bloodstream Coxsackievirus nucleic acid pathogen test
Def: Detection of nucleic acid of Coxsackievirus in the blood circulation by a method such as polymerase chain reaction (PCR).

Name: Positive stool Cryptosporidium antigen test
Def: Fecal analysis for Cryptosporidium antigen is abnormal. Tests include direct fluorescent-antibody (DFA), which detects intact organisms, and enzyme immunoassays (EIAs), which detect soluble stool antigens.

Name: Diminished tissue alpha-L-iduronidase activity
Def: Concentration or activity of alpha-L-iduronidase (IDUA; EC 3.2.1.76) below the lower limit of normal. FECH enzyme can be measured in multiple tissues including cultured fibroblasts and leukocytes.

Name: Reduced tissue neuraminidase activity
Def: Activity of neuraminidase (EC 3.2.1.18)in tissues below the lower limit of normal. The activity can be measured in multiple tissues including culutured fibroblasts. Neuraminidase is also known as lysosomal sialidase.

Name: Nummular keratitis
Def: Nummular keratitis consists of multiple scattered small round anterior corneal superficial stromal infiltrates.
Comment: Nummular means coin-shaped.

Name: Swelling of inguinal region
Def: Bulging in the area of the lower abdomen, just above the thigh and near the groin.

Name: Single lesion
Def: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance are solitary and localized to a part of the skin, a tissue or an organ that differs from the surrounding healthy tissue.

Name: Dysorthography
Def: A specific disorder of spelling. A score on a standardized spelling test is at least two standard errors of prediction below the level expected on the basis of the child's chronological age and general intelligence in the context of scores on reading accuracy and comprehension and on arithmetic that are within the normal range (within two standard deviations from the mean).

Name: Echogenic fetal colon
Def: A type of echogenic fetal bowel in which the hyperechogenicity is strictly limited to the colon.

Name: Bone marrow edema
Def: Accumulation of excess fluid in the bone marrow.
Comment: This condition is typically detected using magnetic resonance imaging, where it appears as an area of increased signal intensity on fluid-sensitive sequences.

Name: Transverse terminal upper limb defect
Def: A congenital anomaly that appears as an amputation at different levels of the arm, e.g. humerus, proximal forearm, wrist or finger. The limb is missing the terminal (distal) segment(s), with preservation of all the segment(s) proximal to the missing segment.

Name: Trousseau sign
Def: After inflating a blood pressure cuff from 10 mm Hg to 20 mm Hg over the patient's systolic blood pressure, the Trousseau sign is considered positive if carpal spasm develops, with flexion of the thumb and adduction of the finger within 3 minutes. However, this can be painful, so the time should be noted, and the cuff should be deflated once the test is positive.

Name: Craniocervical junction constriction
Def: Congenital or acquired abnormalities of the occipital bone, foramen magnum, or first two cervical vertebrae that decrease the space for the lower brain stem and cervical cord. These malformations can lead to cranial nerve compression, vertebral artery compression, and obstructive hydrocephalus.

Name: Fibular torsion
Def: Excessively rotated (also called torsion) position of the fibula (calf bone). An increased external rotation of the fibula in the incisura tibiofibularis of more than 5 degrees may lead to an increased pressure and will negatively affect the cartilage.

Name: Abnormal finger phalanx ossification
Def: Any abnormal process of ossification of the phalangeal bones, which normally are ossified from the body and proximal extremity. Ossification of the body commences during the eighth week of fetal development. Ossification of the proximal extremity commences in the bones between the third and fourth years.

Name: Positive bloodstream EBV monospot test
Def: The monospot test is a latex agglutination test which utilizes equine erythrocytes as the primary substrate and tests for specific heterophile antibodies produced by the human immune system in response to EBV infection. When these specific antibodies are present in the patient's blood specimen, exposure to equine erythrocytes will lead to clumping of the sample, thus signaling a positive agglutination reaction.

Name: Positive CSF Toxoplasma gondii antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that react against a component of Toxoplasma gondii.

Name: Positive tuberculin skin test
Def: A positive result of the tuberculin skin test suggesting previous expouse or infection with mycobacterium teberculosis. A standard dose of five tuberculin units (TU) (0.1ml) is injected intradermally (into the skin) and read 48 to 72 h later. A person who has been exposed to the bacteria is expected to mount an immune response in the skin containing the bacterial proteins. The volar aspect of the forearm is the preferred site of test. The basis of reading is the presence or absence of induration, which may be determined by inspection (from a side view against the light as well as by direct light) and by palpation. For standardization, the diameter of induration should be measured transversely to the long axis of the forearm and recorded in millimeters.
Comment: The tuberculin most widely used is purified protein derivative (PPD), which is derived from cultures of M. tuberculosis.

Name: Anti-Treponema pallidum antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that react against a component of Treponema pallidum.
Synonym: Positive Fluorescent treponemal antibody absorption test
Treponemal antibody titer high in blood

Name: Positive CSF Borrelia burgdorferi antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that react against a component of Borrelia burgdorferi.

Name: Positive CSF JC-virus antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that react against a component of JC-virus (also known as JC-polyomavirus and John Cunningham virus).

Name: Neutralizing anti-rabies virus antibody positivity
Def: The presence of antibodies in the blood circulation that act against the rabies virus function by blocking the binding of the glycoprotein to a receptor or preventing the membrane fusion process.

Name: Impaired hepatobiliary scintigraphy tracer uptake
Def: An abnormal reduction in the amount of radioactive tracer uptake upon hepatobiliary scintigraphy.
Comment: A normal HBS shows rapid clearance of the radio-tracer from the blood pool. Prompt and uniform hepatic uptake is reached within 5 min, functional visualization of the gall bladder is seen as early as 10 min and bowel activity by 30 to 40 minutes. The presence of tracer in the bowel confirm patency of biliary channels and excludes biliary atresia.

Name: Calcified pulmonary nodule
Def: A pulmonary nodule with calcium deposits. On radiography, these nodules appear dense.
Comment: Calcification in a pulmonary nodule (PN) on imaging indicates a high probability that the lesion is benign. But not all calcified PN are benign and the differential considerations include a primary central lung carcinoid, metastasis and a primary bronchogenic carcinoma.

Name: Postprandial exacerbation
Def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is more severe following a meal.

Name: Koebner Phenomenon
Def: The appearance of new skin lesions on previously unaffected skin secondary to trauma. This phenomenon is also termed the isomorphic (from Greek, equal shape) response, given the fact that the new lesions that appear are clinically and histologically identical to the patient's underlying cutaneous disease.
Comment: The Koebner phenomenon is typically associated with preexisting skin disease. Clinical entities that commonly display the Koebner phenomenon include psoriasis, vitiligo, lichen planus. The incidence of Koebnerization ranges broadly within these entities; estimates of the prevalence of the Koebner phenomenon are approximately 11 to 75% in psoriasis and 21 to 62% in vitiligo.

Name: Glenoid dysplasia
Def: Glenoid dysplasia is a developmental anomaly of the scapula that is characterized by a bony deficiency of the posteroinferior glenoid and the adjacent scapular neck.
Comment: Glenoid dysplasia may occur as a primary isolated condition or in association with various syndromes. It is thought to be related to defective ossification of the inferior glenoid precartilage. Radiographs typically demonstrate bilateral, symmetric dysplasia of the scapular neck with a range of associated bony changes. Glenoid dysplasia has been associated with instability and premature glenohumeral arthritis, although the clinical presentation is highly variable. Symptoms are delayed or mitigated as a result of compensatory glenoid labral hyperplasia.

Name: Prolonged retraction of penile foreskin
Def: A past medical history of recently having retracted the penile foreskin for a prolonged period of time. Paraphimosis commonly occurs iatrogenically, when the foreskin is retracted for cleaning, placement of a urinary catheter, a procedure such as a cystoscopy, or for penile examination. Failure to return the retracted foreskin over the glans promptly after the initial retraction can lead to paraphimosis.
Comment: This can be a risk factor for paraphimosis, a urologic emergency that occurs in uncircumcised males when the foreskin becomes trapped behind the corona of the glans penis.

Name: Thickened cortex of the clavicle
Def: Abnormal thickening of the cortex of the clavicle.

Name: Thickened cortex of the mandible
Def: Abnormal thickening of the cortex of the mandible.

Name: Thumb hypoplasia grade 1
Def: Minor hypoplasia (developmental undergrowth) of the thumb, whereby all musculoskeletal and neurovascular components of the digit are present, just small in size (Blauth classification).

Name: Thumb hypoplasia grade 2
Def: A type of developmental undergrowth of the thumb, whereby all of the osseous structures are present (may be small), and there is metacarpophalangeal joint ulnar collateral ligament instability and thenar hypoplasia.

Name: Thumb hypoplasia grade 3A
Def: A type of developmental undergrowth of the thumb, whereby there are musculotendinous and osseous deficiencies with the carpometacarpal (CMC) joint intact. Absence of active motion at the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) or interphalangeal (IP) joint.
Synonym: Hypoplasia of the thumb grade IIIA

Name: Thumb hypoplasia grade 3B
Def: A type of developmental undergrowth of the thumb, whereby there are musculotendinous and osseous deficiencies characterized by basal metacarpal aplasia with deficient carpometacarpal (CMC) joint, and absence of metacarpophalangeal (MCP) or interphalangeal (IP) joint.
Synonym: Hypoplasia of the thumb grade IIIB

Name: Thumb hypoplasia grade 4
Def: A type of developmental undergrowth of the thumb characterized by attachment to the hand only by the skin and digital neurovascular structures.
Synonym: Hypoplasia of the thumb grade IV

Name: Femoral osteopoikilosis
Def: Multiple multiple, small, well-defined radiodense foci of cortical-like bone in the medullary space parallel to the trabeculae located in the femur. The loci correspond to condensations of the lamellar trabeculae on histology.

Name: Carotidynia
Def: Pain or tenderness in the region of the carotid artery.
Comment: Fay Syndrome is characterized by carotidynia and manifests as an atypical facial neuralgia characterized by an unusual neck pain extending towards the head and associated with carotid artery tenderness. Diagnostic criteria include neck tenderness, elevated carotid pulse without anatomical abnormalities, and neck distension.

Name: Asymmetric blood pressure between arms
Def: A substantial difference in blood pressure (e.g., 20 mmHg) between the right and left arms.

Name: Transverse terminal lower limb defect
Def: A congenital anomaly that appears as an amputation at different levels of the leg, e.g. femur, foreleg, ankle or toe. The limb is missing the terminal (distal) segment(s), with preservation of all the segment(s) proximal to the missing segment.

Name: Hemimelia of lower leg
Def: A developmental defect leading to a transverse deficiency with absence of the lower leg (eg tibia and fibula), ankle and foot.

Name: Hemimelia of forearm
Def: A developmental defect leading to a transverse deficiency with absence of the forearm (eg ulna and radius), wrist and hand.

Name: Sodium glucose transport inhibitor exposure
Def: History of having been treateed with a sodium glucose transport inhibitors such as dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, canagliflozin, sglt-i, SGLT2, bexagliflozin, ertugliflozin, sotagliflozin, jardiance, invokana, forxiga, brenzavvy, steglatro, inpefa.
Comment: May be a risk factor for SGLT-2i induced diabetic ketoacidosis.

Name: Breath-holding spell
Def: A benign paroxysmal nonepileptic disorder occurring in healthy children 6 to 48 months of age. The episodes start with a provocation such as emotional upset or minor injury, and might progress to breath holding, cyanosis, and syncope.

Name: Flared proximal tibial metaphysis
Def: The presence of a splayed (i.e.,flared) metaphyseal segment of the proximal tibia.

Name: Delayed toe phalanx ossification
Def: Delayed maturation and calcification of any of the toe phalanges.

Name: Sorbitol ingestion
Def: A history of ingestion of a relatively high amount of foods containing sorbitol.

Name: Positive peritoneal fluid bacterial culture
Def: Growth of bacteria in a culture dervied from ascites fluid.

Name: Ocular cystine crystal deposition
Def: Accumulation of cystine crsytals in the eye. Patients present with crystal accumulation affecting the cornea and conjunctiva, but crystals can also be deposited in the iris, ciliary body, choroid and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), and lens capsule. Corneal crystal deposition starts in infancy in the anterior periphery of the cornea, and progresses centrally and posteriorly. The crystals, which have a fine, uniform needle-shaped structure, are diffusely distributed within the corneal tissues.

Name: Exuberant granulation tissue
Def: A manifestation of abnormal wound healing in which there is formation of excessive granulation tissue, with the granulation tissue rising above the level of surrounding skin and creating a raised, reddish, moist, and bumpy surface.

Name: Oral mucosal papule
Def: A small (less than 5 mm in diameter), elevated, circumscribed, solid, palpable mass located in thte mucosa of the oral cavity.

Name: Excessive piloerection
Def: Abnormally increased degree of goose bump formation, that is, of involuntary formation of bumps on a person's skin at the base of body hairs.
Comment: Excessive piloerection can be a feature of opioid withdrawal.

Name: Scalp edema
Def: A palpable swelling in the scalp caused by an increase in interstitial fluid volume (excess fluid).

Name: Serpiginous burrow
Def: A slightly raised and often reddish serpentine or curvilinear path in the skin.
Comment: Serpiginous refers to the wavy path of the burrows that is said to resemble the tracks of a snake. These lesions are characteristic of scabies and some other infections.

Name: Positive brain-tissue rabies nucleic acid test
Def: Detection of rabies nucleic acid in brain tissue by a method such as polymerase chain reaction.

Name: Positive respiratory tract Bordetella pertussis nucleic acid test
Def: Detection of Bordetella pertussis PCR nucleic acid in in nasopharyngeal secretions by a method such as polymerase chain reaction.

Name: Demonstration of acid-fast bacilli in wound tissue
Def: Demonstration of acid-fast bacilli by microscopic examination of wound tissue. Acid fastness is a physical property that gives a bacterium the ability to resist decolorization by acids during staining procedures.
Comment: Bacteria displaying acid fastness include: Mycobacterium leprae, M. tuberculosis, M. smegmatis, M. Avium complex, M. kansasii, Nocardia brasiliensis, N. cyriacigeorgica, N. farcinica, and N. nova.

Name: Positive tissue encapsulated budding yeast test
Def: Identification of encapsulated budding yeasts in smears of body fluids, secretions, exudates, or other specimens.
Comment: In fixed-tissue specimens, encapsulated yeasts may also be identified and confirmed as cryptococci by positive mucicarmine or Masson-Fontana staining. This finding may suggest a diagnosis of cryptococcosis.

Name: Positive tissue coccidioidomycosis culture
Def: Growth of coccidioidomycosis in a culture derived from skin or an organ.

Name: Diminished tissue dihydropteridine reductase activity
Def: Concentration or activity of dihydropteridine reductase (EC 1.6.99.7) below the lower limit of normal. This enzyme can be measured in multiple tissues including leukocytes and erythrocytes.

Name: Decreased circulating transcobalamin I concentration
Def: Concentration of transcobalamin I in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
Synonym: Decreased circulating R vitamin B12 binder protein concentration

Name: Diminished circulating cationic trypsinogen concentration
Def: Concentration of cationic trypsinogen in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
Comment: Cationic trypsinogen is one of the several isoforms of trypsinogen. Serum cationic trypsinogen when low, is known to be associated with reduced pancreatic exocrine function in a number of disorders, including Shwachman's syndrome and type 1 diabetes mellitus.

Name: Diminished circulating hyaluronidase activity
Def: The activity or concentration of hyaluronidase in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Diminished sulfotransferase activity in cultured fibroblasts
Def: Rate of proteoglycan sulfation (sulfotransferase activity) is below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

Name: Elevated tissue alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase activity
Def: Concentration or activity of alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase (EC 3.2.1.50) above the upper limit of normal. This enzyme can be measured in multiple tissues including leukocytes and cultured fibroblasts. It is also known as alpha-acetylglucosaminidase, N-acetyl-alpha-D-glucosaminidase, N-acetyl-alpha-glucosaminidase, and alpha-D-2-acetamido-2-deoxyglucosidase.

Name: Abnormal tissue alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase activity
Def: Concentration or activity of alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase (EC 3.2.1.50) outside of the limits of normal. This enzyme can be measured in multiple tissues including leukocytes and cultured fibroblasts. It is also known as alpha-acetylglucosaminidase, N-acetyl-alpha-D-glucosaminidase, N-acetyl-alpha-glucosaminidase, and alpha-D-2-acetamido-2-deoxyglucosidase.

Name: Elevated circulating trihydroxycholestanoic acid concentration
Def: The concentration of trihydroxycholestanoic acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated circulating glyoxylic acid concentration
Def: The concentration of glyoxylic acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated CSF sepiapterin concentration
Def: Concentration of sepiapterin in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Intrahepatic inclusion bodies
Def: Nuclear or cytoplasmic aggregates of stainable substances within hepatocytes.

Name: Muscle vacuoles
Def: Presence of abnormal vacuoles (membrane-bound organelles) in the sarcolemma. The vacuoles are often associated with cytoplasmic and occasionally intranuclear eosinophilic inclusions.

Name: Nonrimmed muscule vacuoles
Def: Presence of abnormal vacuoles (membrane-bound organelles) in the sarcolemma. On histological staining with hematoxylin and eosin, non-rimmed vacuoles lack the prominent dark border (rim) seen in rimmed vacuoles.

Name: Reduced hepatic glycogen phosphorylase activity
Def: Activity or concentration of glycogen phosphorylase L in the liver below the lower limit of normal.

Name: Bone marrow hemophagocytosis
Def: Phagocytosis of erythrocytes, lymphocytes or other hematopoietic precursors by histiocytes or macrophages observed in the bone marrow.

Name: Splenic granulomatosis
Def: Splenic inflammation involving a granulomatous response, i.e., a non-specific inflammatory response involving granulomas, defined as a compact organized collection of mature mononuclear phagocytes including epithelioid and giant cells.

Name: Immediate detumescence of penis at time of symptom onset
Def: Loss of erection at the time point of pain or other symptom onset.

Name: History of aortic valve replacement
Def: History of having received a surgical replacement of the aortic valve.

Name: Coved type ST segment elevation
Def: An ST-segment elevation of at least 2 mm in at least one right precordial lead (V1 to V3), followed by an r'-wave and a concave or straight ST segment. The descending ST segment crosses the isoelectric line and is followed by a negative and symmetric T-wave.
Comment: This finding is highly suggestive of Brugada syndrome.

Name: Saddle-back type ST segment elevation
Def: An ST-segment elevation of at least 0.5 mm (generally at least 2 mm in V2) in at least one right precordial lead (V1 to V3), followed by a convex ST. The r'-wave may or may not overlap the J point, but it has a slow downward slope. The ST segment is followed by a positive T-wave in V2 and is of variable morphology in V1.
Comment: ECG anomaly is only suggestive of Brugada syndrome.

Name: Substantially elevated circulating ethanol concentration
Def: A blood concentration of ethanol that is consistent with alcohol intoxication, generally assumed to be 0.0800 g/dL or higher.

Name: Tortuous appearance of the stomach
Def: Abnormal twisting or winding of the stomach.
Comment: This feature can be seen with gastric volvulus and cam imply that it is difficult to reach the pylorus with gastric endoscopy.

Name: Cochlear nerve aplasia
Def: A developmental defect causing an absence of the cochlear nerve resulting in sensorineural hearing loss.

Name: Slit-like lateral ventricle
Def: Abnormally small lateral ventricle with a slit-like appearance.

Name: Fetal methamphetamine exposure
Def: A history of exposure during pregnancy (including during the period of conception) of the mother of a fetus or child to methamphetamine.

Name: Elevated circulating 4-hydroxybutyric acid concentration
Def: Concentration of 4-hydroxybutyric acid in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urinary 2,4-dihydroxybutyric acid level
Def: The amount of 2,4-dihydroxybutyric acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Pupillary hypersensitivity to parasympathomimetic agents
Def: A higher than normal tendency of parasympathomimetic agents to induce miosis.
Comment: Topical administration of methacholine 2.5% or pilocarpine 0.0625% has no observable effect on the normal pupil but causes miosis after approximately 20 minutes in almost all individuals with familial dysautonomia.

Name: Lack of pupillary response to hydroxyamphetamine
Def: 4-hydroxyamphetamine is used in eye drops to dilate the pupil, e.g.., to induce mydriasis for fundus examinations. This term refers to a lack of response of the pupil to topical application of 4-hydroxyamphetamine.

Name: Subcortical U fiber lesion
Def: Abnormal morphology of subcortical U fibers, typically as assessed by abnromal intensity on magnetic resonance imaging of the brain.
Comment: Subcortical U-fibers are special types of short association fibers located in the superficial white matter (SWM). In contrast to the SWM, the U-fibers only connect the adjacent gyri. Since U-fibers have a rich blood supply from long perforating arteries and short perforating arteries that span the white matter (WM) and adjacent cortex, they are usually unaffected in chronic ischemic WM disease. Anatomically, U-fibers originate from pyramidal neurons of layer 6 of the cerebral cortex and provide local integration of different sites of the same gyrus or immediately adjacent gyri. Developmentally, U-fibers do not fork until the second half of gestation when gyration and sulcation of the cerebral cortex occur. As a result, U-fibers are not readily involved in diseases of myelin metabolism, such as adrenoleukodystrophy and metachromatic leukodystrophy. However, in demyelinating diseases with normal myelin and oligodendrocyte dominance, including multiple sclerosis and progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, U-fibers are commonly involved Pathologic processes that involve the white matter typically appear hyperintense on T2/FLAIR images.

Name: Intraspinal extradural lipoma
Def: A lipoma (a benign encapsulated mass with lobulated mature adipose tissue enclosed by fibrous tissue) located within the spine but outside of the dura mater.

Name: Intranasal mass
Def: An abnormal enlargement or swelling localized to the nasal cavity. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

Name: Liver rupture
Def: Subcapsular hepatic rupture is characterized by the development of a hematoma, often quite large, beneath the liver capsule. An interval of days or hours may elapse between the time of injury and the first appearance of symptoms. A history of injury may be entirely lacking, or may be so unremarkable that it is elicited only by diligent interrogation. The hematoma tends to increase in size.

Name: Elevated urinary mandelic acid
Def: The amount of mandelic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine malic acid level
Def: The amount of malic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine 3-hydroxysebacic acid level
Def: The amount of 3-hydroxysebacic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urinary vanillactic acid level
Def: The amount of vanillactic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine 4,5-dihydroxyhexanoic acid level
Def: The amount of 4,5-dihydroxyhexanoic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine hydroxyphenyllactic acid level
Def: The amount of hydroxyphenyllactic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
Comment: Hydroxyphenyllactic acid or 4-hydroxyphenyllactate (the L-form) is a tyrosine metabolite. The level of L-hydroxyphenyllactic acid is elevated in patients with a deficiency of the enzyme p-hydroxyphenylpyruvate oxidase (EC 1.14.2.2).

Name: Positive gastric CMV intranuclear inclusions
Def: Demonstration of the presence of cytomegalovirus in the stomach by means of a method such as in-situ hybridization.

Name: Elevated urine dihydroxycholestanoic acid level
Def: The amount of dihydroxycholestanoic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urinary bile alcohol level
Def: The amount of bile alcohol in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Elevated urine glucose tetrasaccharide level
Def: The amount of glucose tetrasaccharide in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Increased urine 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate level
Def: The amount of 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Inability to protrude lips
Def: Lack of ability to purse or pucker the lips.
Comment: The anomaly can be related to abnormalities of the muscles, nerves, or structure of the face.

Name: Wet voice
Def: Wet voice is a perceptual vocal quality that is gurgly or liquid sounding and is due to the voice being produced through moisture. It is commonly used as an indicator of penetration and/or aspiration in clinical swallowing assessments and bedside screening tests.

Name: Erythema marginatum
Def: An erythematous (pink-red, depending on the skin color of the affected individual) macule that spreads peripherally and coalesces to form polycyclic or serpentine patches or plaques. Lesions occur in crops over days to weeks and are evanescent. The rate of migration is 2 to 12 mm over a period of a few hours. Erythema marginatum tends to affect the trunk more than the extremities and to not be accompanied by pruritus.

Name: Mechanic's hands
Def: Mechanic's hands are fissured, erythematous, hyperkeratotic eruptions on the hands, resembling the type of occupational dermatosis said to resemble the hands of a manual laborer. The lesions are classically on the lateral edges of the fingers and thumbs, largely sparing the palmar, and dorsal aspects of the digits.
Comment: This feature can be observed in antisynthetase syndrome (ASyS), an autoimmune disease clinically manifested most often by interstitial lung disease, myositis, and arthritis.

Name: Hiker's feet
Def: Hyperkeratotic scaly fissured plaques on the fingers/palms or soles, generally more evident on the lateral aspect of index fingers.
Comment: Hiker's feet is a finding that is analogous to mechanic's hands with similar hyperkeratotic eruptions on the toes and feet, and is a manifestation of antisynthetase syndrome.

Name: Anti-HLA-DQ antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against a human leukocyte antigen (HLA-DQ). DQ is one of several antigens involved in antibody-mediated rejection of organ transplants.

Name: Inappropriate normal or low erythropoietin
Def: Erythropoietin is produced and released into the blood by the kidneys in response to hypoxemia, and would normally be expected to increase with decreasing hemoglobin levels. This term applies if the increase fails to occur, as may be seen in conditions including chronic kidney disease.

Name: Rapid gastric emptying
Def: A condition in which food moves through the stomach into the small intestine at an abnormally fast rate.
Comment: Dumping is the effect of alteration in the motor functions of the stomach, including disturbances in the gastric reservoir and transporting function. Anatomic and physiologic changes introduced by gastric surgery result in clinically significant dumping syndrome in approximately 10% of patients. Gastrointestinal hormones play an important role in dumping by mediating responses to surgical resection. Treatment options of dumping syndrome include diet, medications, and surgical revision.

Name: Mediastinal lymph node calcification
Def: Abnormal deposition of calcium in mediastinal lymph nodes.
Comment: Lymph node calcifications most often result from prior granulomatous infections, especially tuberculosis and histoplasmosis. Other, less common, causes are sarcoidosis, silicosis, amyloidosis, and calcifications secondary to the treatment of lymphomas (radiation therapy or chemotherapy).

Name: Eggshell calcification of lymph nodes
Def: Eggshell calcification refers to fine calcification seen at the periphery of a mass and usually relates to lamellar lymph node calcification.
Comment: Eggshell calcification, commonly occurs in patients with silicosis and coal-worker's pneumoconiosis. Sarcoidosis, postirradiation Hodgkin disease, blastomycosis, and scleroderma are other reported causes. Eggshell calcification has more rarely been observed in amyloidosis and histoplasmosis.

Name: Knee joint effusion
Def: Abnormal accumulation of fluid within the knee joint or around the knee. Symptoms maye include, pain, swelling, and stiffness.
Comment: Increased intra-articular amount of (synovial) fluid is not specific for a particular disorder, as can occur in a variety of settings but draws attention to the presence of a joint disorder, such as knee osteoarthritis, or rheumatoid arthritis.

Name: Subcutaneous emphysema
Def: Skin emphysema/Subcutaneous emphysema occurs when gas or air accumulates and seeps under the skin, where normally no gas should be present. While the presence of air in subcutaneous or mediastinal tissue is not dangerous in itself, prompt recognition of the underlying cause is essential.
Comment: Subcutaneous emphysema can be caused by medical procedures and medical conditions that cause the pressure in the alveoli of the lung to be higher than that in the tissues outside of them. Its most common causes are pneumothorax or a chest tube that has become occluded by a blood clot or fibrinous material. It can also occur spontaneously due to rupture of the alveoli, with dramatic presentation. When the condition is caused by surgery it is called surgical emphysema. The term spontaneous subcutaneous emphysema is used when the cause is not clear.

Name: Elevated bone scintigraphy uptake
Def: Bone scintigraph is performed with technetium 99m-labeled diphosphonates. The uptake of these radiopharmaceuticals depicts osteoblastic activity and regional blood flow to bone.
Comment: Bone scintigraphy is frequently performed as part of the routine staging of patients with a wide variety of primary malignancies. Although it is a sensitive imaging modality, it is relatively nonspecific, and there are many potential causes of increased isotope uptake that can mimic metastatic disease.

Name: Diminished long-chain-enoyl-CoA hydratase activity in cultured fibroblasts
Def: Concentration or activity of long-chain-enoyl-CoA hydratase (EC 4.2.1.74) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

Name: Diminished acetyl-CoA C-acyltransferase activity in cultured fibroblasts
Def: Concentration or activity of acetyl-CoA C-acyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.16) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal. This enzyme catalyzes the reaction acetyl-CoA + an acyl-CoA = a 3-oxoacyl-CoA + CoA. It is also known as 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase and beta-ketothiolase.
Synonym: Reduced 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase activity in cultured fibroblasts

Name: Pathological inclusion body
Def: Pathological inclusion bodies are are composed of glycogen, proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, hemosiderin, and calcium, that accumulate as metabolic by-products, catabolic products of macromolecular complexes, or in the context of cell injury.

Name: Reduced epidermal collagen IV alpha 5 chain staining
Def: Diminished or absent collagen alpha5(IV) chain staining pattern in the epidermal basement membrane.

Name: Diminished glomerular basement membrane collagen IV alpha 3 chain staining
Def: Abnormal reduction in the amount of the alpha 3 chain of collagen IV in the basement membrane of the glomeruli of the kidney.

Name: Diminished glomerular basement membrane collagen IV alpha 4 chain staining
Def: Abnormal reduction in the amount of the alpha 4 chain of collagen IV in the basement membrane of the glomeruli of the kidney.

Name: Diminished glomerular basement membrane collagen IV alpha 5 chain staining
Def: Abnormal reduction in the amount of the alpha 5 chain of collagen IV in the basement membrane of the glomeruli of the kidney.

Name: Cystine nephrolithiasis
Def: Deposition of cystine crystals in kidney tissue. Cystine crystals display a pathognomic hexagonal shape.

Name: Hepatic cystine accumulation
Def: Accumulation of cystine in the liver.
Comment: Cystine crystal accumulation activates Kupffer cells and secreted vasoactive substances cause vasoconstriction in microcirculation resulting in portal hypertension

Name: Bone marrow cystine accumulation
Def: The presence of cystine crystals in bone marrow cells as demonstrated in a fresh bone marrow aspiration sample.

Name: Desmoid tumor
Def: Desmoid tumors are rare, locally aggressive, fibroblastic soft-tissue tumors that are characterized by infiltrative growth and tendency to recur. Desmoid tumors do not metastasize but can arise in any part of the body: extra-abdominal (appear in the head and neck, chest, extremities), and abdominal wall or intra-abdominal (originating in tissue that connects abdominal organs).

Name: Tubular jejunal duplication
Def: A segment of the jejunum that runs parallel to the normal jejunum and communicates with the jejunal lumen at one or both ends.

Name: Left ventricular rupture
Def: A full thickness tear or breakage of the myocardium of the left ventricle.

Name: Punctate pontine perivascular enhancement
Def: Multiple punctate (speckled, patchy spot-like) and/or curvilinear areas of gadolinium enhancement distributed around blood vessels in the pons.
Comment: The lesions may extend into adjacent CNS structures, caudally to the medulla oblongata or the cervicothoracal spinal cord, rostrally to the midbrain, and even involve supratentorial regions such as the thalami, capsula interna, basal ganglia, corpus callosum and cerebral white matter. See Figure 1 of PMID:24028073.

Name: Intestinal worm
Def: Presence of one or more adult worms in the intestine as demonstrated by sonography or passage of a worm in the stool. On sonography, worms may appear as linear, echogenic structures within the intestines.

Name: Scrotal worm
Def: Demonstration of one or more worms in the scrotum. This finding can be appreciated by sonography, where echogenic, linear structures could be seen moving within the scrotum.

Name: Small intestinal adenoma
Def: A small bowel tumor with adenomatous epithelium.
Comment: Grossly and histologically, adenomas arising in the mucosa of the small intestine are similar to the adenomas found in the colon.

Name: Maternal retinal mottling
Def: Mottling (spots or blotches with different shades) of the retinal pigment epithelium in the mother of the index patient. Retinal mottling may indicate a mosaic X-linked inactivation state in the mother.

Name: Twisted gallbladder pedicle
Def: A stretched conical-shaped structure found at the gallbladder neck with several linear echoes converging towards its tip. This finding is demonstrated by sonography and can indicate gallbladder volvulus.
Synonym: Conical structure at the gallbladder neck

Name: Cholecyst-enteric fistula
Def: Fistula between the gallbladder and the intestine.

Name: Dyschronometria
Def: Impaired ability to accurately measure or estimate time intervals.
Comment: Common signs of dyschronometria are often generic to cerebellar ataxia, including a lack of spatial awareness, poor short term memory, and inability to keep track of time. For example, when asked to wait for thirty seconds, or tap every second that has gone by, those affected will be able to perform the task for a short time and then become derailed. This can result from a loss of focus, however, more often than not the individual affected can no longer tell what they are doing and they become disoriented. This often takes form in forgetting basic time keeping unless a timer is set, such as when cooking for example. Dyschronometria does not affect the 24-hour circadian rhythm, which is sustained by a different biological process.

Name: History of recent intermittent breastfeeding
Def: History of recently intermittent breastfeeding an infant (i.e., on and off).
Comment: Recent on and off breastfeeding can be a risk factor for galactocele and breast abscess.

Name: Breast cyst
Def: A benign, fluid-filled sac in the breast.

Name: Circumscribed
Def: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance are well-defined and localized to a specific area.

Name: Lobulated
Def: Applies to an abnormality that displays ultiple indentations and/or elevations producing an irregular surface contour.

Name: Spiculated
Def: Applies to an abnormality with irregular, radiating, or spiky edges.
Comment: A spiculated mass is a centrally dense lesion seen on mammography with sharp lines radiating from its margin. The spicules can vary greatly in length, from a few millimeters to several centimeters. In malignant lesions, spicules represent a mixture of tumor cells and fibrosis invading the normal tissue surrounding the lesion.

Name: Whorled
Def: Applies to an abnormality whose distribution and appearance resembles series of a concentric circles or spirals.

Name: Delta brush pattern on EEG
Def: Delta brushes are transient patterns characterised by a slow delta wave with superimposed fast activity.
Comment: Delta brushes are the hallmark of the EEG of premature infants.

Name: Tibiotalar synostosis
Def: Fusion of the junction between the distal tibia, fibula and the talus.

Name: Vertebra plana
Def: he term given when a vertebral body has lost almost its entire height anteriorly and posteriorly, representing a very advanced compression fracture.

Name: Intoeing
Def: An abnormal gait caused by a rotational variation anywhere in the lower extremity that causes the foot to point inward, instead of pointing straight ahead or outward, when walking or running.
Comment: The three major causes of pediatric in-toeing are metatarsus adductus, internal tibial torsion, and femoral anteversion.

Name: Palpable thrill on extremity
Def: A vibration felt upon palpation of a blood vessel over an extremity.
Comment: This feature can be due to an arteriovenous malformation.

Name: Out-toeing
Def: The feet turn excessively outward when walking, caused by a rotational variation in the leg.

Name: Ankle dislocation
Def: An abnormal separation between the talo-tibial joint.

Name: Anti-neuronal intermediate filament antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against neuronal intermediate filament.

Name: Anti-DREBRIN antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against dendritic spine scaffolding protein Drebrin.

Name: Anti-lipoprotein lipase autoantibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against anti-lipoprotein lipase.

Name: Anti-apolipoprotein CII autoantibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against apoCII.

Name: Eosinophilic neuronal inclusion bodies
Def: The presence of intracellular inclusion bodies (aggregates of stainable substances, usually proteins) in neurons that stain with eosin, a red or pink dye.

Name: Sweaty foot-like odor
Def: A characteristic smell said to resemble the odor of dirty socks.
Comment: This feature is characteristic of isoveleric acidemia.

Name: Anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody positivity
Def: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against acetylcholine receptor.
Comment: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (AChR) are ligand-gated cation channels that are present throughout the nervous system. The muscle AChR mediates transmission at the neuromuscular junction; antibodies against the muscle AChR are the cause of myasthenia gravis. The ganglionic (alpha 3-type) neuronal AChR mediates fast synaptic transmission in sympathetic, parasympathetic, and enteric autonomic ganglia. Impaired cholinergic ganglionic synaptic transmission is one important cause of autonomic failure.

Name: Hair shaft lesion
Def: Applies to an abnormality that is located on hair shafts.

Name: Prolonged use of tightly fitting footwear
Def: History of use of tightly fitting shoes for a long period of time.
Comment: This may be a risk factor for tinea pedis.

Name: Triggered by high protein intake
Def: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about ingestion of high quantities of protein.
Comment: Metabolic triggers for late-onset urea cycle disorders include excessive protein intake.

Name: Thickened tricuspid valve cusp
Def: An abnormally increased thickness of a leaflet of the tricuspid valve.

Name: Displaced anterior fontanelle
Def: Abnormal shifting of the anterior fontanelle fropm its normal central position.
Comment: This feature can be related to an abnormality of the cranial sutures, mostly craniosynostosis.

Name: Subdural hygroma
Def: Accumulation of cerebral spinal fluid in the subdural space.

Name: Incus ankylosis
Def: Incus ankylosis refers to congenital or acquired fixation of the incus, which is associated with conductive hearing resulting from impairment of the sound-conduction mechanism (the external auditory canal, tympanic membrane, and/or middle-ear ossicles).

Name: Excessive diet restriction
Def: A tendency to reject a variety of foods and/or to eat a restricted range of foods.

Name: Left ventricular apical dyskinesis
Def: Dyskinesis is used to describe ventricular muscle segments that bulge outside the left ventricular cavity during systole, as opposed to contracting inwards with the rest of the segments.

Name: Longitudinal erythronychia
Def: A longitudinal red band extending from the proximal nail fold or lunula to the distal nail plate.

Name: Exacerbated by exposure to sunlight
Def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by exposure to sunlight.

Name: Exacerbated by heat
Def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is made worse by exposure to heat (high ambient temperatures).

Name: Exacerbated by excessive sweating
Def: Applied to a sign or symptom that is made worse by excessive sweating.
Comment: High temperatures, high humidity, excessive sweating can exacerbate cutaneous wounds.

Name: Malignant pleural effusion
Def: The accumulation of a significant amount of exudate in the pleural space, accompanied by the presence of malignant cells or tumour tissue.

Name: Inappropriately low urine osmolality following challenge
Def: In diabetes insipidus, affected individuals produce large quantities of dilute urine. In nephrogenic DI, the kidneys do not respond to vasopressin. In a water deprivation test or with administration of exogenous vasopressin, the osmolaltiy of the urine does not increase as normally.

Name: Reduced urine retrahydrocortisol plus 5-alpha-THF to tetrahydrocortisone ratio
Def: Abnormally low ratio of tetrahydrocortisol (THF) plus 5-alpha-THF to tetrahydrocortisone (THE).
Comment: In cortisone reductase deficiency-2, the ratio of tetrahydrocortisol (THF) plus 5-alpha-THF to tetrahydrocortisone (THE), which in CORTRD patients is typically less than 0.1 (reference range, 0.7 to 1.2).

Name: Elevated urinary 2,4-dihydroxyglutarate level
Def: The amount of 2,4-dihydroxyglutarate in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

Name: Abnormal urine D-xylose test
Def: An abnormal result of the xylose absorption test that is used to assess the ability of the intestines to absorb D-xylose. D-xylose is a five-carbon monosaccharide found in some plants. The patient drinks a solution containing a specific amount of D-xylose and the concentration of xylose is measured in the blood circulation and then in the urine. A low amount of D-xylose indicates reduced small intestinal absorbtion.
Comment: The standard 25-g D-xylose test in adults, based on analysis of a 5-h urine collection and a 1-h serum sample, discriminates between normal subjects and patients with proximal small intestinal malabsorption with X5% specificity and sensitivity.

Name: Cerebral hemisphere mass lesion
Def: An abnormal growth or accumulation of tissue in a hemisphere of the cerebrum. Typically a mass is an initial finding that will lead to additional workup.

Name: T2-hyperintense putaminal rim
Def: Increased signal on T2 magnetic resonance imaging characterized by a linear region of high signal surrounding the lateral aspect of the putamen at 1.5 Tesla.

Name: Posterior fossa mass lesion
Def: An abnormal growth or accumulation of tissue in the posterior fossa, affecting the cerebellum or fourth ventricle. Typically a mass is an initial finding that will lead to additional workup.

Name: Irregular RR interval
Def: Abnormal increased variability in the timing between consecutive R-waves on an electrocardiogram.
Comment: Sinus arrhythmia is a variation of normal sinus rhythm that characteristically presents with an irregular rate in which the change in the R-R interval is greater than 0.12 seconds.

Name: Irregular P-P interval
Def: Abnormally increased variability in the timing between consecutive P-waves on an electrocardiogram.

Name: Fungal hair infection
Def: Demonstration of fungi growing on hair by a method such as microscopy of hairs mounted on slides with 10% potassium hydroxide.

Name: Long hairstyle
Def: A past medical history of having long, full hair.

Name: Conjunctival subepithelial fibrosis
Def: fine white linear scars under intact conjunctival epithelium. This scarring appears in areas of previous conjunctival ulceration or pseudomembrane formation, weeks to months after the insult is healed.
Comment: Subepithelial fibrosis can be a manifestation of ocular graft-versus-host disease (oGVHD), but can also be found after epidemic keratoconjunctivitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and chemical burns.

Name: Conjunctival fornix foreshortening
Def: Abnormal reduction in depth of the fornix of the conjunctiva. The fornix is the area where the conjunctiva folds back upon itself, thereby creating a recessed space.

Name: Strong ultraviolet light exposure
Def: History of exposure to ultraviolet light, such as may be encountered with outdoor activities, living near equator, radiation.

Name: Exposure to vaginal douching
Def: A history of intravaginal cleansing with a liquid solution for personal hygiene or aesthetic reasons.
Comment: Douching represents a risk factor for bacterial vaginosis.

Name: Exposure to oily lotions or creams
Def: A history of applying oily lotions or creams to the skin.
Comment: This may be a risk factor for tinea versicolor.

Name: Elevated circulating pristanic acid concentration following branched-chain fatty acid ingestion
Def: Concentration of pristanic acid in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. This finding can be observed in Zellweger syndrome. Note that branched-chain fatty acid accumulation depends on dietary intake of phytanic acid, which is minimal in formula- and breast-fed infants. Thus, phytanic and pristanic acid levels are normal in a neonate with Zellweger spectrum disorder.

Name: Decreased T-cell ZAP-70 protein expression in CD4-positive T cells
Def: Reduction in the level of ZAP-70 protein CD4-positive T cells.
Comment: Testing of CD4+ T cells reveals absence or near absence of ZAP-70 protein in most individuals affected by ZAP70-related combined immunodeficiency.

Name: Dorsal flexion contracture of the ankle
Def: A type of contracture in which the dorsal flexion muscles of the ankle are contracted.
Comment: Dorsiflexion of the ankle is the movement of the top of the foot towards the leg in an upward motion. With dorsal flexion contracture, the ability to passively or actively move the tip of the toe away from the leg is limited.

Name: Metaphyseal undermodelling
Def: Lack of the normal diaphyseal constriction (thinning of long bones toward the midshaft area) giving the submetaphyseal areas an abnormally wide appearance.

Name: Iliac vein compression
Def: Compression of the common iliac vein against the spine by the contralateral common iliac artery.
Comment: Pulsations of the overriding artery cause shear stress and endothelial changes in the vein, resulting in the formation of fibrous bands or spurs. Over time, the affected area forms a stricture, causing impaired venous return and, in some circumstances, deep venous thrombosis. Common iliac vein compression can be ascertained by Doppler sonography.

Name: Positive serum amyloid P scintigraphy
Def: Detection of abnormal amyloid deposits in the body by 123I-labeled serum amyloid P component (SAP) scintigraphy.

Name: crossed brainstem sign
Def: Motor and/or sensory cranial nerve findings ipsilateral to the lesion, and at the same time motor and/or sensory findings on the contralateral side of the body.

Name: Inability to puff cheeks
Def: Reduced ability to inflate the cheeks by blowing air into them while keeping the lips closed.
Comment: This feature may be related to facial muscle weakness as well as to cranial nerve VII lesions.

Name: Entoptic phenomenon
Def: Visual sensations caused by changes within the eye itself, rather than by the normal light stimulation process. Entoptic phenomena are classified in the syndrome as floaters, blue field entoptic phenomenon, photopsia and self-light of the eye.

Name: Abnormal vestibulo-spinal reflex
Def: An abnormality of the vestibulospinal (VS) reflexes, which contribute to the control of postural orientation. In this task, they continuously collaborate with reflexes elicited by stimulation of visual and somatosensory receptors. Labyrinthine receptors are sensitive to modifications (i) of the head position with respect to the earth vertical or (ii) of the angular/linear velocity of head motion in space. This information can be used to monitor deviations from the maintained body position.

Name: Positive probe-to-bone test
Def: An abnormal result of the probe-to-bone (PTB) test. The PTB test is performed by inserting a sterile, metal surgical probe into the ulcer and is positive if a hard, gritty surface is felt inside. For large wounds, this may require gentle exploration of the wound with the probe.
Comment: The basis behind the PTB test is that if a probe can reach bone, so can bacteria.

Name: Exposure to repetive hand impact
Def: A history of exposure to repetitive impact on palm or hand, such as working with a jackhammer.
Comment: This history can be a risk factor for carpal tunnel syndrome.

Name: Fractured scaphoid bone
Def: A partial or complete breakage of the scaphoid bone.

Name: Local anesthetic ineffectiveness
Def: Resistance to the effects of local anaesthesia, with delayed onset or failure of local anesthetics to incude numbness or relieve pain.
Comment: This feature has been reported in individuals with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

Name: Palmoplantar location
Def: Applied to lesions whose distribution is confined or restricted to the palms of the hands and soles of the feet.

Name: Oral mucosa plaque
Def: A raised, flat-topped lesion with a diameter of one centimeter or more that is located in the mucosa of the mouth.

Name: Positive saliva rabies nucleic acid test
Def: Detection of rabies nucleic acid in saliva by a method such as polymerase chain reaction.

Name: Elevated tissue arylsulfatase A activity
Def: Activity of arylsulfatase A (EC 3.1.6.8) above the upper limit of normal. The activity can be measured in multiple tissues including culutured fibroblasts and leukocytes or in the blood circulation.

Name: Elevated circulating methysterol concentration
Def: The concentration of a methysterol in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
Comment: This group of compounds includes thje 4-alpha-monomethyl sterols and 4,4-prime-dimethyl sterols.

Name: Elevated urinary adipic acid
Def: The amount of adipic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal. Adipic acid is an alpha,omega-dicarboxylic acid that is the 1,4-dicarboxy derivative of butane.
